3d-wall-art.title: 3D / relief wall art and sculptural paintings
3d-wall-art.full: 3D / relief wall art and sculptural paintings (Rafael Martin-type spotlight reliefs, Guillaume Azoulay, Park West mixed media, Agam agamographs, decorator workshops)
3d-wall-art.money: listed artists' sculptural works (Azoulay, Agam agamographs, Rotman) $200–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
3d-wall-art.fakes: Park West-type editions are produced in large runs; "original" claims are frequently overstated. Many decorator pieces carry invented signatures. Authentication for listed artists usually means provenance/COA, which Dyla
3d-wall-art.buy: Most are decorator art that does not fit the car or ship economically; pass unless small (≤ 24×28 framed), signed by a recognised artist, and ≤ 1/4 of realistic sold value.
tells: Lenticular / kinetic prints (Agam agamographs): flat, but the image changes as the viewer moves; not relief.
Agam: image changes with viewing angle, hand signature and number in the margin, Agam name on labels.

Tourist relief paintings from Spain/Latin America (1970s–80s): mixed media on masonite with raised figures (women with baskets or umbrellas, street scenes), often signed and dated on the back with a place (e.g. Marbella 1985). Small sizes (about 11×15") exist

8mm-movie-cameras.title: 8mm movie cameras
8mm-movie-cameras.full: 8mm movie cameras (Kodak / Cine-Kodak, Bell & Howell, Keystone, Revere, Bolex, Canon, Nizo, Beaulieu, Elmo, Nikon)
8mm-movie-cameras.money: good-brand Super 8 (Canon 310XL/514XL, Nizo, Bolex, Nikon R8/R10, Beaulieu) tested $150–600+
8mm-movie-cameras.fakes: None to worry about. New-production Super 8 (Kodak Super 8 camera 2023, Logmar) are modern and expensive, never on Craigslist for cheap.
8mm-movie-cameras.buy: Pass on every wind-up Regular-8 and generic Super 8; only a recognisable pro Super 8 body (Canon 814/1014 XL-S, Nizo S/Professional, Beaulieu 4008/6008, Nikon R10, Leicina) at ≤ $60 and only if the seller shows it running, since untested electronics are off-li
tells: Super 8 (1965–1980s): pistol grip with batteries in the handle, plastic body, square cartridge door, zoom lens. Cheap ones: Kodak Instamatic M-series/XL, Bell & Howell 1970s, Sears, GAF, Keystone, Chinon, Sankyo, Minolta Autopak, Yashica. Better: Canon 310XL,

Regular 8 / Double 8 (1932–1960s): boxy metal body, wind-up key or crank on the side, no battery door, turret of 1–3 lenses or a single lens. Kodak models carry a red Kodak badge, a "Cine-Kodak" lens and an exposure-guide plate on the side (Brownie, Reliant, M
Junk to recognise instantly: film reels and reel cans (e.g. a "SAV-ON" drugstore-branded aluminium reel can lid), splicers, viewers, light bars, plain projectors.

acoustic-guitar-amps.title: Acoustic guitar amplifiers
acoustic-guitar-amps.full: Acoustic guitar amplifiers (Roland AC, Fishman Loudbox, AER)
acoustic-guitar-amps.fakes: No fakes known to matter. Reissues/revisions (AER Compact 60/2, /3, /4) differ in features; state the revision (general knowledge, verify).
acoustic-guitar-amps.buy: Working AER Compact 60 < $250, Roland AC-90/100 < $80, Fishman Artist/Performer < $120; pass anything with a described fault.

acoustic-guitars.title: Acoustic guitars
acoustic-guitars.full: Acoustic guitars (Martin, Gibson, Guild, Taylor, Yamaha, Takamine, Alvarez, Washburn, Ovation; budget: Esteban, Rogue, First Act; vintage Japan: Yairi, Aria, Ibanez, Takamine lawsuit era)
acoustic-guitars.fakes: Chinese counterfeit Martins/Gibsons ("Chibson") exist; check serials and construction. - Counterfeit tells: flat untapered Martin headstock, ink-stamped (not burned/stamped) neck block, wrong font, sanded area around ser
acoustic-guitars.buy: Skip TV-brand guitars; target 1970s Japanese and US-made brand guitars at ≤ 1/3 sold — but only playable ones with no cracks or neck issues (no repairs).
tells: Where the ID is: Martin — "C.F. Martin & Co, Nazareth PA" burned/stamped and serial stamped on the neck block (look through the sound hole toward the neck), model stamped there too on most post-1930 guitars; Gibson — label or ink-stamped serial inside, logo in

Body shapes: dreadnought (big square shoulders, Martin D), jumbo (round lower bout, Gibson J-200), slope-shoulder (Gibson J-45), 000/OM and parlor (smaller, narrow waist), round-back (Ovation bowl), 12-string (twelve tuners, wide headstock).

Solid vs laminate top in a photo: look at the sound-hole edge — a solid top shows the same grain running through the edge; a laminate shows layered plies or a different-coloured edge, and grain on top that does not continue (Andertons).

adding-machines.title: Adding machines and mechanical calculators
adding-machines.full: Adding machines and mechanical calculators (Victor, Burroughs, Felt & Tarrant Comptometer, Monroe, Marchant, Friden, Curta, Odhner, Brunsviga, Addometer, Remington Rand, Sundstrand, Allen-Wales)
adding-machines.fakes: Curta replicas/3D-printed copies exist; otherwise none.
adding-machines.buy: Pass bulky crank adders; buy Curta, Golden Gem or glass-sided early Burroughs only with clear photos and ≤ 1/4 comps.

advertising-china.title: Advertising china
advertising-china.full: Advertising china (beef-extract and tonic mugs: Armour's Vigoral, Cudahy's Rex/Soma, Liebig, Bovril; calendar and premium plates; Old Sleepy Eye; railroad, airline and restaurant ware with logos; Buster Brown and brand-character china)
advertising-china.money: Old Sleepy Eye Monmouth/Western Stoneware and rare railroad patterns $200–1,000+ (heavy reproduction) (triage + general knowledge, verify)
advertising-china.fakes: Old Sleepy Eye (pitchers, mugs, steins) heavily reproduced since the 1950s–2000s; B&O Centenary and other railroad patterns reproduced (Shenango reissues and fakes with spurious marks); fake airline and Coca-Cola restaur
advertising-china.buy: Single beef-extract mugs and calendar plates only at ≤ $8; look instead for top-marked railroad dining-car china or authentic Old Sleepy Eye under $40; kill anything with racist caricature imagery (policy).
tells: Old Sleepy Eye: Sleepy Eye Milling Co. (Minnesota) premiums made by Weir/Western Stoneware/Monmouth, blue-on-grey salt glaze with an Indian chief's profile, c.1899–1937 (general knowledge, verify).

Beef-extract and tonic mugs (c.1890–1915): small handled porcelain mugs or cups-and-saucers from Bavaria/Austria printed with a brand — Armour's Vigoral (Chicago, 1890s), Cudahy's Rex / Soma, Liebig Company's Extract of Meat, Bovril. Sold or given with the pro
Calendar plates (c.1906–1929, peak 1909–1912): a year calendar printed around a central scene, with a local merchant's name — US potteries and German blanks.

advertising-collectibles-coca-cola.title: Coca-Cola advertising collectibles
advertising-collectibles-coca-cola.full: Coca-Cola advertising collectibles (signs, trays, thermometers, coolers, clocks, calendars, bottles, carriers, chairs, placemats)
advertising-collectibles-coca-cola.money: porcelain signs, pre-1940 trays and calendars $200–5,000+.
advertising-collectibles-coca-cola.fakes: Extremely common: fake porcelain signs from India/China ("distressed"), reproduction trays (1970s–90s), placemats. Repros carry recent copyright dates. - Only two of the 21 red rim tray issues (1934 and 1937) have been r
advertising-collectibles-coca-cola.buy: Pass on anything with "since 1904/1886" nostalgia graphics or post-1970 copyright; only authentic pre-1960 tin/porcelain trays, thermometers and small signs at ≤ $50 — with photos of the maker's tagline and date code.
tells: Authentic: pre-1960 trays with "Drink Coca-Cola" and copyright line on the rim edge, maker (e.g. "American Art Works, Coshocton O."), date; porcelain signs (heavy, glossy, chip edges with black steel); thermometers with "Robertson" maker marks.

Nostalgia reproductions (1970s–2000s): "Hilda Clark" or Victorian-lady images, laminated placemats, large tin signs with "©19xx The Coca-Cola Company" and "Advertising for Coca-Cola since 1904" lines. Low value.
Furniture: red metal Coca-Cola stacking/folding chairs (mostly 1990s–2000s licensed retro), 1950s ice-cream parlour chairs (wire), coolers (Westinghouse, Cavalier).

advertising-giveaways.title: Advertising giveaways and promotional items
advertising-giveaways.full: Advertising giveaways and promotional items (tape measures, rulers, flasks, wastebaskets, pocket items; Barlow, Lufkin, Whitehead & Hoag, Bastian Bros, Parisian Novelty, Brown & Bigelow, oil and tire companies)
advertising-giveaways.money: rare figural celluloid tapes and early lithographed tin with strong graphics $150–500+.
advertising-giveaways.fakes: - Reproduction tin signs, trays and wastebaskets for Coca-Cola, Texaco, Harley and similar (1980s–present, thin, very glossy, often marked "Ande Rooney" or with a modern copyright) are common. Be wary of any "old" petrol
advertising-giveaways.buy: Only buy pre-1940 celluloid or figural pieces, or big-name petroliana tin with bright graphics, at ≤ 25% of the estimated sold price; pass on 1960s+ chrome/enamel tapes, rulers, flasks and anything still made.
tells: Celluloid tape measures, 1890s–1930s: a round drum about 1.5" across with printed pictures on both faces, often a cloth tape and a small pull tab. Figural versions are shaped like pigs, apples, clocks, flatirons or people. Makers' names are printed on the rim:

Metal-cased "pocket tape" with a domed enamel or epoxy face, 1950s–1980s: a chromed square or round case like the Eagle Powerstrand pair, a steel blade marked "Made in USA", often in a gold-foil gift box. Makers are Barlow, Lufkin and Rose. These were made by
Rulers: 1920s–50s pieces are wood or celluloid with litho graphics. 1950s–70s pieces are painted steel or aluminium, 12" or 30 cm, with a hanging hole, like the Goodyear diamond-logo ruler.

advertising-glassware.title: Advertising glassware
advertising-glassware.full: Advertising glassware (root beer mugs, fast-food and soda promo glasses; A&W, Hires, Dad's, Frostie, Coca-Cola, Pepsi, McDonald's, Burger King, Pizza Hut, Libbey and Federal promos)
advertising-glassware.money: rare Pepsi/Warner character glasses and pre-war Coca-Cola syrup-line glasses $25–150+ (general knowledge, verify).
advertising-glassware.fakes: A&W and Coca-Cola reissued retro designs repeatedly; Coca-Cola syrup-line glasses are reproduced. Fast-food glasses are rarely faked.
advertising-glassware.buy: Pass on 1970s+ promo glasses and common A&W mugs; buy only pre-1950 embossed syrup-line glasses or rare character glasses at ≤ 25% of sold.
tells: Fast-food character glasses: Pepsi/Warner Bros Looney Tunes (1973–76), Star Wars Burger King (1977), McDonald's Garfield, etc.
Coca-Cola: pre-1930 flare "syrup line" glasses are valuable; modern bell glasses are common.

A&W dating (general knowledge, verify): 1950s–60s "bullseye and arrow" logo (A&W in orange circle with arrow); 1970s "US map" logo with A&W in brown oval on orange map (a 1976-ish bicentennial-era design); 1980s–90s plain brown/orange oval logo. Embossed-only

advertising-oil-cans.title: Petroliana – motor oil & grease cans, gas-station signs
advertising-oil-cans.full: Petroliana – motor oil & grease cans, gas-station signs (Archer, Mohawk, Sinclair, Polly, Pennzoil, Shell)
advertising-oil-cans.money: big porcelain signs and one-piece globes $800–20,000+.
advertising-oil-cans.fakes: Reproduction tin signs are everywhere ("metal reproduction advertising", thin, Chinese) – $5–20. Reproduction globes $50–100. Fake porcelain signs (often from India) exist with artificially aged chips (general knowledge,
advertising-oil-cans.buy: Graphic quart/5-lb cans < $30, Archer/Mohawk/Polly pails < $60, porcelain sign < $150 with enamel-to-steel chips; never repro or plastic.
tells: Graphics with an image (Indian head – Archer, Mohawk, Red Indian; Sinclair dinosaur; Polly Gas parrot; Flying A; Frontier buffalo; Musgo; Harbor Petroleum) are worth 3–10x plain-text cans (Pennzoil, Quaker State, Havoline, Valvoline, Texaco – $15–60).

Archer Lubricants (Omaha, NE): Indian archer graphic; quart cans $40–120, 5-lb/10-lb/25-lb grease pails $100–300 depending on graphic version and condition; paper-label versions and salesman sample kits $100–250.
Condition grades: rust, dents, fading knock 50–80% off; "full" or "NOS" adds a little; 25 lb pails are shipping-expensive.

advertising-prints.title: Advertising premium prints
advertising-prints.full: Advertising premium prints (Northern Paper Mills / Northern Tissue, Maxfield Parrish Edison-Mazda, Coca-Cola, Brown & Bigelow, Gerber, Cream of Wheat, Fisk Tire etc.)
advertising-prints.money: Maxfield Parrish Edison-Mazda calendars and original-size advertising lithos $200–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
advertising-prints.fakes: Heavy reproduction of Parrish, Coca-Cola and Cream of Wheat. Northern prints were reissued in the 1960s–70s and are cheap anyway.
advertising-prints.buy: Only buy complete, uncut early (pre-1935) advertising calendars and Parrish/Rockwell/Elvgren originals; pass on 1950s–60s mail-in premium prints.

advertising-signs.title: Advertising signs
advertising-signs.full: Advertising signs (porcelain, tin, plastic, neon, street signs)
advertising-signs.money: big porcelain Shell/Texaco/Mobil and dealer signs $1,000–20,000.
advertising-signs.fakes: Repros flood the market, especially porcelain Shell/Texaco/Harley signs. Reproduction tin signs are thin and printed; fake porcelain (often imported) has overly uniform colours, artificial chips without the layered shelf
advertising-signs.buy: Porcelain pump plate/small sign ≤ $150 with clean gloss, porcelain street sign ≤ $30; pass plastic, tin repros and neons.

advertising-thermometers.title: Advertising thermometers
advertising-thermometers.full: Advertising thermometers (Coca-Cola, Pepsi, Dr Pepper, Texaco, Mobil, Prestone, Royal Crown, Orange Crush, Mail Pouch, Hills Bros; makers Taylor, Stout Sign Co., Robertshaw, Ohio Thermometer Co., Pam Clock)
advertising-thermometers.fakes: Very high repro risk — petroliana and Coke are the most faked advertising categories. Ande Rooney and "Old Time Signs" style repros flood the market. - Licensed Coca-Cola reissues from the 1980s–90s are dated in small pr
advertising-thermometers.buy: Pass anything plastic, “Made in USA” small reproduction style or with a printed “clean rest rooms” novelty slogan; buy only embossed tin or porcelain originals with weathering ≤ 1/4 of comps.
tells: History: advertising thermometers appeared in the 1900s and were widespread in the US by the 1920s; the earliest were tin and wood, later ones porcelain like porcelain signs; they were made to hang outside (Collectors Weekly).
Forms: round dials with clock-style hands; vertical rectangular or die-cut (bottle-shaped) signs with a tube in the middle (Collectors Weekly).

Very large porcelain examples exist (e.g. a Mail Pouch porcelain thermometer 19 × 73 with wood frame, RM Sotheby's); anything over about passenger-seat length is excluded by the size rule. The common Mail Pouch is the 39 in. size.

advertising-tins.title: Advertising & decorative tins
advertising-tins.full: Advertising & decorative tins (pocket tobacco, coffee, tea, biscuit, toffee/candy, spice, lard; makers Somers Bros., Ginna, Hasker & Marcuse, American Can, Tindeco, Hudson Scott, Huntley Boorne & Stevens, Barringer Wallis & Manners)
advertising-tins.money: vertical pocket tobacco, figural biscuit and rare-brand store tins $200–5,000.
advertising-tins.fakes: - 1970s–80s "Fake-Antique" lithographed nostalgia tins (often by Cheinco, Ballonoff, or labelled "Collector Series") – worth $2–8. - Coca-Cola, Planters, Prince Albert, Folgers, Hills Bros. official reissue tins (1980s–2
advertising-tins.buy: Buy only pre-1950 lithographed tins with images (people, animals, vehicles) – pocket tobacco, 1-lb coffee, figural/novelty biscuit tins – at ≤ $25 each; pass all Christmas, reproduction "nostalgia" and 1980s commemorative tins and any rusted lot.
tells: Paper label on plain tin (example 7935128376) – 1880s–1920s bulk/lard pails or later home use; worthless without a readable label.

Stencilled/japanned (painted) tin 1860s–1890s; offset lithography on tin from the 1870s–80s, mass after 1895. Pre-1900 litho has slightly muted colours and fine detail; post-1960 litho is bright, photographic, with a UPC barcode (post-1974), nutrition facts bo
Construction: soldered side seams and hinged lids with wire pins = old; lock-seamed, rolled-edge, slip-lid cookie tins with printed "Made in England/Hong Kong/China" = 1960s+.

african-masks.title: African masks
african-masks.full: African masks (Cameroon Grassfields/Bamileke/Bamum, Dan, Baule, Punu, Fang, Chokwe, Yoruba Gelede, Kuba; tourist "airport art" vs. tribal-used)
african-masks.fakes: Most masks are made to look old. The fake-patina industry is very large. Authentication requires collection history, a specialist dealer, or published provenance. Provenance that predates the large-scale reproductions of
african-masks.buy: Treat almost all Craigslist African masks as decorative (resale $30–150); buy only at ≤ $30 for decorative pieces. "Authentic tribal-used" claims need professional authentication, which is out of scope.

akro-agate-glass.title: Akro Agate Glass
akro-agate-glass.full: Akro Agate Glass (Akro Agate Co., Clarksburg WV 1914–1951; also Vitro Agate, Westite, Houze, Imperial slag)
akro-agate-glass.fakes: Akro doll dish reproductions by others; Westite and Imperial slag confused with Akro. - Married sets assembled from loose pieces are more common than outright fakes (Kovel column advice to check matching).
akro-agate-glass.buy: Buy boxed children's dish sets and rare-color pieces under ~$40; pass single ashtrays and unmarked "slag" that may not be Akro.
tells: Company: organized in Akron, Ohio, in 1911; moved to Clarksburg, West Virginia, in 1914 for glass sand and cheap natural gas; first a marble maker (over 2 million marbles a week during the 1930s–40s Chinese checkers craze); pressed glassware (vases, flowerpots

The crow mark sits as a raised moulded logo on the base (concave bases of teapots, creamers, sugars and plates on the CMOG set); lids are usually unmarked (CMOG). Some pieces are unmarked, and some carry "J.P." for J. Pressman Co., a toy company Akro made sets

Children's dish patterns (Kovel column; CMOG; eBay titles): Stippled Band, Ribbed (Concentric Ring/Rib), Raised Daisy, Chiquita, Interior Panel, Octagonal, and the "H"-panel pattern of the Little American Maid sets. Sets came in large and small sizes.

aluminum-serving-ware.title: Aluminum serving ware , Russel Wright aluminum, Farberware, Cellini Craft, Federal Silver, Keystone Ware, World Hand Forged)
aluminum-serving-ware.full: Aluminum serving ware (hand-wrought and hammered aluminum: Arthur Armour, Wendell August Forge, Everlast, Continental Silverlook, Buenilum, Rodney Kent, Palmer-Smith, Cromwell, Kensington (Alcoa), Russel Wright aluminum, Farberware, Cellini Craft, Federal Silver, Keystone Ware, World Hand Forged)
aluminum-serving-ware.money: Russel Wright and Kensington design pieces $60–400.
aluminum-serving-ware.fakes: Wendell August continues production (newer pieces lower than early forge pieces). Little faking otherwise.
aluminum-serving-ware.buy: Pass on all unmarked/common aluminum; buy only Arthur Armour, Wendell August Forge (deep relief scenes) or Russel Wright pieces at ≤ $15.

american-art-pottery.title: American art pottery
american-art-pottery.full: American art pottery (Rookwood, Roseville, Weller, Van Briggle, Newcomb, Grueby, Teco, Fulper, Cowan, Hull, McCoy, Gonder, Shawnee, Haeger, Red Wing, Frankoma, Bauer, Pisgah Forest, North State, Jugtown)
american-art-pottery.money: Arts & Crafts studio/early (Rookwood artist-signed, Grueby, Newcomb, Teco, Fulper early, Marblehead, Van Briggle pre-1920) $300–5,000+.
american-art-pottery.fakes: - **Chinese Roseville fakes** (1990s–today) are everywhere: blurry molds, garish wrong colors, raised "Roseville U.S.A." mark on the wrong patterns, often too light. Also fake Weller and fake Rookwood marks. - Van Briggl
american-art-pottery.buy: Buy only marked Roseville/Weller/Rookwood/Van Briggle/Fulper/Grueby/Newcomb/Teco forms at ≤ 30% of sold median, undamaged; never buy Gonder/McCoy/Hull/Haeger singles unless rare glaze or form and ≤ $10.
tells: Arts & Crafts high end: thick matte glazes (green "Grueby green", Teco green, Van Briggle "Persian Rose"/"Mulberry"/"Ming Blue"), hand-incised or carved floral decoration (Newcomb: bayou moss, oaks, moon, in blues/greens), Rookwood "Standard Glaze" (brown with

Roseville: molded floral patterns in named lines (Pinecone, Futura, Blackberry, Sunflower, Baneda, Morning Glory, Ferrella, Wisteria, Jonquil = high; Freesia, Zephyr Lily, Snowberry, Magnolia, Bittersweet, Apple Blossom, Clematis, Columbine, Peony, Gardenia =
Weller: Louwelsa (brown standard glaze), Hudson (artist-painted matte), Coppertone (frogs), Woodcraft. Ink stamp or impressed "Weller".

american-belleek.title: American Belleek porcelain
american-belleek.full: American Belleek porcelain (Ott & Brewer, Willets, CAC/Lenox, Ceramic Art Co.)
american-belleek.money: Ott & Brewer and large signed vases $600–3,000+.
american-belleek.fakes: No widespread fakes known (general knowledge, verify). The real risk is confusing Lenox wreath-mark or Irish Belleek pieces with the early American makers, and amateur-decorated blanks with factory work.
american-belleek.buy: Palette, snake or crescent mark visible: decorated ≤ $60, O&B or artist-signed ≤ $150; pass Lenox wreath, Irish Belleek, damage.
tells: Ott & Brewer 1883–1892: crescent with "BELLEEK" and "O&B" – rarest, highest.
Willets Manufacturing 1880–1909: snake coiled into a "W" over "BELLEEK".

Ceramic Art Company (CAC) 1889–1906: artist's palette with brushes, "CAC" monogram, "BELLEEK" below – this is early Lenox. Red/lavender palette = decorated at the factory; green = sold as blank for home decoration.

american-dinnerware.title: American dinnerware, 1900–1970
american-dinnerware.full: American dinnerware, 1900–1970 (Homer Laughlin, Hall, Taylor Smith & Taylor, Knowles, Harker, Sebring/Limoges China Co., Scio, Salem, Paden City, US Pottery, Red Wing, Franciscan, Bauer, Vernon Kilns, Blue Ridge, Russel Wright, Marcrest)
american-dinnerware.money: rare Fiesta/Harlequin colours and forms, Bauer ring-ware big pieces, Vernon Kilns Rockwell Kent, Blue Ridge figural pitchers $150–800.
american-dinnerware.fakes: - Post-1986 Fiesta (Homer Laughlin, now Fiesta Tableware Co.) in vintage-like colours – check backstamp and colour list. - Harlequin was reissued (1979 for Woolworth) in the old shape. - "Hall" teapots reissued (China Sp
american-dinnerware.buy: Never buy decal-floral or gold-filigree single plates/platters; buy only solid-colour Art Deco ware (Fiesta/Harlequin/Bauer/Russel Wright) and rare forms (pitchers, vases, casseroles, figural) at ≤ $30.
tells: Solid-colour glazes: Fiesta (1936–73; post-1986 revival), Harlequin, Riviera (Homer Laughlin), Bauer ring ware (1932–62), LuRay pastels (TS&T), Russel Wright American Modern (Steubenville, 1939–59) and Iroquois Casual.
Hand-painted underglaze: Blue Ridge (1930s–57), Red Wing (1940s–60s), Purinton, Stangl, Franciscan Apple/Desert Rose (embossed and hand-painted).

Decals (transfers) of florals and roses, often with silver/platinum or gold trim; embossed scroll shapes (Homer Laughlin "Virginia Rose" shape 1929–1970s – embossed scrolls at four points on the rim, e.g. example 7975237695; Knowles "Deanna", Taylor Smith & Ta

american-pocket-watches.title: American pocket watches
american-pocket-watches.full: American pocket watches (Waltham, Elgin, Hamilton, Illinois, Hampden, South Bend, Rockford, Howard, Ball; dollar watches Ingersoll, Ingraham, Westclox, New Haven)
american-pocket-watches.fakes: - Cheap Chinese "Railroad"/"Train" skeleton pocket watches with fake vintage styling – no American maker, quartz or crude mechanical. - Fake private-label dials, redials and repainted dials (crisp new paint on an old mov
american-pocket-watches.buy: Buy running gold-filled hunter-case or 17j+ open-face American watches at ≤ $40–50; ask for case marks – any solid 10K/14K/18K case bought ≤ $200 is a strong buy; pass dollar watches over $15 and non-running watches over $25.
tells: Case style: hunter (hinged front cover over the dial – examples 7969348839, 7974975384) vs open face (crystal only). Hunters pre-date about 1915 mostly; open faces dominate after.
Dial: white enamel (fired glass, glossy, may show hairlines) = older/better; painted metal dials = later/cheap. Railroad dials: bold Arabic numerals, "Montgomery" (each minute numbered) dials.

Movement (inside the back cover): maker name, grade, jewel count, serial number engraved on the plates; nickel with damaskeening (wavy engraved patterns) = mid-to-high grade (example 7974975384 Elgin "Safety Pinion", damaskeened 3/4 plate). Dollar watches have

american-precious-metal-marks.title: American precious-metal marks
american-precious-metal-marks.full: American precious-metal marks (US karat gold and plumb marks; gold-filled, RGP, GE and HGE; coin silver and sterling; Tiffany, Gorham, Whiting, Unger Bros, Kerr, Shiebler, Kalo, Jensen USA, Roycroft, Marie Zimmermann; modernists Ed Wiener, Sam Kramer, Art Smith, Paul Lobel, Ruth Roach; Native hallmarks Loloma, Kenneth Begay, Preston Monongye, Lee Yazzie; mid-century gold houses Tiffany, Cartier NY, Verdura, David Webb, Seaman Schepps, Trabert & Hoeffer-Mauboussin; Balfour, Jostens and Herff-Jones)
american-precious-metal-marks.money: Loloma and top Native makers, Verdura, Webb, Schepps, Zimmermann $3,000–100,000+ (Bonhams/Witherell's Loloma $8,338–11,475).
american-precious-metal-marks.fakes: - **Fake karat stamps** on plated base metal, especially "14K" on imported chain and on "Italy 14K" rope chains; a karat stamp with no trademark is the first warning (MJSA). - **"Tiffany & Co" fakes:** heart-tag bracelet
american-precious-metal-marks.buy: Read the stamp before the photo: a karat or STERLING/COIN mark with a weight lets you pay ≤ 50–80% of melt with no expertise; pay over melt only for a named maker mark from the golden-egg list whose sold comps clear profit ≥ max($50, price); GF, RGP, GE, HGE,

american-shelf-clocks.title: American shelf clocks
american-shelf-clocks.full: American shelf clocks (Seth Thomas, E.N. Welch, Brewster & Ingrahams, E. Ingraham, Waterbury, Ansonia, Gilbert, New Haven / Jerome & Co., Chauncey Jerome, Atkins, Birge & Fuller, Sperry & Shaw, Forestville)
american-shelf-clocks.money: Eli Terry pillar & scroll and wagon-spring Atkins $800–3,000+.
american-shelf-clocks.fakes: Mid-20th-c Seth Thomas, New Haven, Howard Miller and Waltham "colonial" steeple and beehive reproductions with stamped-plate or electric movements (printed dials, printed lower pictures, no paper label or a modern one).
american-shelf-clocks.buy: Buy only 19th-c. case clocks with original label and tablet, movement visible and complete, at ≤ $40 for 30-hour and ≤ $80 for 8-day beehive/double-steeple; pass on 1950s+ reproductions and anything with a replaced label or missing pendulum.
tells: Sharp gothic / steeple (1840s–1900s): pointed case with two turned finials on side columns; rosewood or mahogany veneer; lower glass tablet (reverse-painted, stencilled or transfer) and paper label inside on back board. "Steeple-on-steeple" (double steeple) is

Round gothic / beehive (1840s–1860s): rounded arch, bezel round dial, often ripple moulding; Brewster & Ingrahams, Chauncey Jerome, Sperry & Shaw (NY retailer). Etched/frosted lower glass with basket or urn motif is typical.
Ogee (OG) (1840s–1910s): rectangular wall/shelf case with S-curve moulding, weight-driven 30-hour; very common.

anamorphic-projection-lenses.title: Anamorphic projection lenses
anamorphic-projection-lenses.full: Anamorphic projection lenses (Kowa, Sankor, Isco, Bell & Howell)
anamorphic-projection-lenses.fakes: No fakes known. Modern cheap camera anamorphics (Sirui, Great Joy) compete with and have softened prices of the vintage units; they are not passed off as vintage.
anamorphic-projection-lenses.buy: Kowa 8-Z/16-H < $300, 16-D < $120, Iscorama < $800; pass big theatre units and any haze.

angel-figurines.title: Angel figurines
angel-figurines.full: Angel figurines (Roman Inc. Seraphim Classics, Willow Tree/Demdaco, Goebel/Hummel, Lladró, Hallmark, Lenox, Josef Originals, Precious Moments, Boyds, Sonny Angel, Napco, Lefton)
angel-figurines.fakes: Asian Lladró-lookalikes (glossy porcelain, no blue mark). Sonny Angel fakes are common. Seraphim are not usually faked, but copied in style by unmarked gift-shop resin.
angel-figurines.buy: Pass on resin angel lots; only Lladró/Goebel porcelain or Sonny Angel rarities priced as junk, ≤ $20.

anniversary-clocks.title: Anniversary clocks
anniversary-clocks.full: Anniversary clocks (400-day torsion clocks: Kundo / Kieninger & Obergfell, Schatz, Kern, Koma, Herr, Haller, Jahresuhrenfabrik, Gustav Becker; quartz "anniversary" clocks: Rhythm, Seiko, Howard Miller, Bulova, Elgin)
anniversary-clocks.money: pre-WWII Gustav Becker, Jahresuhrenfabrik, Badische Uhrenfabrik disc-pendulum and early "Plato"-style pieces $100–600
anniversary-clocks.fakes: Not faked. Quartz clocks imitating 400-day look; check for battery compartment.
anniversary-clocks.buy: Pass on quartz and common post-war German 400-day clocks; only pre-1930 German clocks with disc pendulums and original domes, or Kundo/Schatz miniatures, at ≤ $25 — and they're fragile.
tells: Mechanical 400-day: brass plate movement, keyhole in the back, four-ball (or disc/pinwheel) rotating pendulum, white/silver dial with baton or Arabic numerals; dome on a round or oval wood/brass base.
Quartz "anniversary" clocks (1980s–2000s): AA battery, often "Quartz" on dial, rotating pendulum driven by a motor, sometimes musical with dancers/carousel (Rhythm, Japan). Low value.

anri-woodcarvings.title: ANRI and Italian/Alpine woodcarvings
anri-woodcarvings.full: ANRI and Italian/Alpine woodcarvings (ANRI mechanical bottle stoppers, Big Mouth toothpick/match holders, Ferrandiz and Sarah Kay figures, Black Forest and Swiss carvings)
anri-woodcarvings.money: large Ferrandiz/Disney limited editions and Black Forest bears $150–1,000+.
anri-woodcarvings.fakes: Japanese composition copies (see above). Modern Chinese resin "carved look" stoppers and toothpick holders. ANRI made resin figures from the 1990s — lower value than wood.
anri-woodcarvings.buy: Mechanical stoppers ≤ $4 each in lots and only lots of 10+ with working levers; Big Mouth holders ≤ $5 each; buy large ANRI Disney/Ferrandiz limited editions at ≤ 25% of sold.
tells: ANRI figurines (1960s–2000s): Juan Ferrandiz (children and animals), Sarah Kay (Australian illustrator), Disney characters, nativities, Kristin; marked "ANRI" with an artist's name, sometimes a limited edition number.
Black Forest (1860s–1920s): carved bears, hall stands, nutcrackers — much more valuable but larger.

Mechanical bottle stoppers (1940s–70s): a cork base on top of which a carved figure moves when a lever or string at the back is pressed — man tips his hat, couple kisses, drinker raises a glass, woman beats a man with a broom, man lifts a woman's skirt (risqué

antique-baskets.title: Antique & vintage baskets
antique-baskets.full: Antique & vintage baskets (Hawkeye/Burlington Basket Co., Shaker, Nantucket lightship, Native American, Longaberger, splint/egg/bushel)
antique-baskets.money: signed Nantucket lightship, Shaker, early painted splint, Native American (Cherokee, Pomo, Apache, Tlingit) $200–2,000+
antique-baskets.fakes: - Imported "antique" splint and egg baskets (1980s–present, China/Philippines) with faux-age stain and chippy paint – sold as "primitive". - Wire egg baskets are widely reproduced (decor stores); "French oyster basket" d
antique-baskets.buy: Only buy small (≤ 14 in) baskets with old-patina native-material tells – lightship mould bottom/wooden base, Shaker swallowtail/kitten-head, Native American coiled or dyed-cane work, paint over old splint – at ≤ $40; pass every bushel, decor, Longaberger and r

antique-bottles.title: Antique and vintage bottles
antique-bottles.full: Antique and vintage bottles (Coca-Cola and soda, Clorox, medicine/apothecary, poison, milk, whiskey/Jim Beam decanters, bitters, inks)
antique-bottles.money: rare colours/shapes (cobalt and amber figural poisons, bitters, early sodas, rare towns) $100–600+.
antique-bottles.fakes: - Reproduced: bitters, historical flasks, Coca-Cola amber and straight-sided bottles, poison bottles, apothecary jars, milk bottles. Many are marked on the base (e.g., "Wheaton", "Made in Italy", "Taiwan"). - Coca-Cola c
antique-bottles.buy: Pass on anything machine-made after ~1915 unless it's a known rarity; buy only pre-1910 hand-finished bottles in strong colour (cobalt, emerald, amber poisons, bitters) or rare-town Coca-Cola at ≤ 30% of sold median.
tells: Age tells visible in photos:
Mould seams: a seam that stops below the lip = mouth-blown, finished by hand (pre-c.1915). A seam running through the top of the lip = machine-made (after c.1905–1920).
Lip ("finish"): applied/tooled lips, uneven drips = old; screw threads and perfect crown tops = 20th century.

antique-canning-jars.title: Antique canning / fruit jars
antique-canning-jars.full: Antique canning / fruit jars (Ball, Atlas, Kerr, Mason's Patent 1858, Lightning, Drey, Root, Hazel-Atlas, Kilner; colours aqua, cornflower, amber, cobalt, olive)
antique-canning-jars.money: rare named jars and true amber/cobalt/odd-closure jars $150–2,000+.
antique-canning-jars.fakes: Ball's own 2010s Heritage Collection coloured "Perfect Mason" (blue, green, purple, amber, rose) are widely sold as "vintage" – check for "Heritage Collection" and the modern Ball logo and lack of mould seams over the li
antique-canning-jars.buy: Pass common aqua/clear Ball, Atlas and Kerr jars; buy only true off-colour (amber, olive, cobalt, milk glass) or odd-closure / small-maker embossed jars at ≤ $20, and verify with the Red Book.

antique-clothes-wringers.title: Antique clothes wringers
antique-clothes-wringers.full: Antique clothes wringers (American Wringer Co. – Horse Shoe Brand, Eureka, Bicycle, Anchor; Lovell Mfg. – Anchor/Lovell; Universal; Keystone; Superior)
antique-clothes-wringers.money: folding wringer benches/tub stands with wringer $100–250 local only
antique-clothes-wringers.fakes: Few fakes; Amish-made new hand wringers exist (Lehman's), and modern repro "décor" wringers. Steel Lehman's wringers are user tools, not antiques.
antique-clothes-wringers.buy: Pass by default: heavy (15–25 lb), bulky to ship, and décor-driven; buy only a clean stencilled wood-frame clamp-on wringer under $25 for a local décor flip, never wringer benches.

antique-coin-purses.title: Antique coin purses
antique-coin-purses.full: Antique coin purses (squeeze/kiss-lock frame purses, mesh purses, chatelaine purses, advertising giveaway purses; makers Whiting & Davis, Mandalian, Prince Gardner, Buxton, Rolfs, Amity, Hickok)
antique-coin-purses.money: Victorian beaded, sterling, chatelaine and miser's purses $50–500+.
antique-coin-purses.fakes: Modern Chinese "vintage-style" beaded and kiss-lock purses; Whiting & Davis continued making mesh into the 1980s–2000s (newer tags, lighter weight). Advertising repros are rare (low value).
antique-coin-purses.buy: Pass plain and generic coin purses; buy enamelled Mandalian/Whiting & Davis mesh, sterling-frame, and fine beaded Victorian purses at ≤ 25% of the ladder; local-advertising purses only at ≤ $5 unless a well-known brand or graphic.
tells: Victorian: miser's purse (long crocheted tube with rings), beaded, sterling hinged, chatelaine purses hung from a belt.
Kiss-lock / frame purses (1880s–1970s): metal frame with two balls that click; leather, vinyl, beaded, tapestry. Double-frame (two compartments) and squeeze-spring types.

Advertising giveaways (1900s–1970s): leather/vinyl with gold-stamped business name and phone numbers (short local numbers like "500", "270" indicate pre-1960s rural exchanges, before 7-digit dialing in the 1950s–60s). The example lists 3-digit local numbers –

antique-door-hardware.title: Antique door hardware
antique-door-hardware.full: Antique door hardware (pocket/sliding door hangers, mortise locks, knobs, hinges, escutcheons; Russell & Erwin, Sargent, Corbin, P&F Corbin, Yale & Towne, Reading, Branford, Lane, Richards-Wilcox, National Mfg, Stanley, Coburn)
antique-door-hardware.fakes: Large repro industry for Victorian knobs/plates (Mexico, India, Taiwan) and "cast iron" barn hardware from China. Hangers are not faked — too cheap. Also: modern UV-treated "amethyst" glass knobs sold as sun-purpled anti
antique-door-hardware.buy: Pass utilitarian hangers/rollers; buy only cast-bronze Victorian knob/escutcheon sets with crisp named patterns at ≤ 1/4 of comps.
tells: Ornamental pocket door hangers also exist: 19th-century cast-iron brackets with foliate scrollwork and grooved spoked rollers that ran on a wood track — e.g. Wilcox Mfg. Co., Aurora IL, patent-dated, about 9 × 6 × 2½ in each, from an 1880s Chicago building (Ur

Knob/plate sets: knob pair + spindle + two rosettes or backplates (backplates run about 5–12 in; long plates and deep backsets suggest entry doors — Appraisily) + mortise lock with faceplate and strike, sometimes with keyhole escutcheons.
Mortise locks: steel box set into the door edge; the maker's name is often cast or stamped on the case side, so it shows only when removed (Appraisily).

antique-figural-scissors-and-sewing-tool.title: Antique figural scissors and sewing tools
antique-figural-scissors-and-sewing-tool.full: Antique figural scissors and sewing tools (D. Peres Solingen, Henckels, Wiss, Gorham/Unger/Webster sterling; Simons Bros, Ketcham & McDougall, Waite-Thresher, Stern Bros thimbles; needle cases, tape measures, stork scissors)
antique-figural-scissors-and-sewing-tool.money: gold thimbles (scrap $150–600 by weight), sterling figural scissors/chatelaines, Victorian etuis, German figural tape measures and Art Nouveau sterling sewing sets $80–500+ (general knowledge, verify)
antique-figural-scissors-and-sewing-tool.fakes: Modern stork scissors and "Victorian style" figural scissors are reproduced en masse; Chinese "sterling" thimbles not actually silver; reproduction chatelaines. Test sterling with mark checks and magnet.
antique-figural-scissors-and-sewing-tool.buy: Buy gold thimbles at ≤ 50% of melt and sterling thimbles/needle cases in lots at ≤ $8 each; Solingen figural scissors and figural tape measures only at ≤ $20; pass on modern stork scissors and souvenir thimbles.

antique-flatware.title: Antique flatware and serving pieces
antique-flatware.full: Antique flatware and serving pieces (bone/ivory/celluloid-handled steel, coin and sterling silver, silverplate; Gorham, Reed & Barton, Wallace, Towle, Rogers, Sheffield cutlers)
antique-flatware.money: rare figural/Aesthetic-movement sterling (Gorham, Whiting, Tiffany) $200–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
antique-flatware.fakes: Little faking at this level; fake hallmarks on "silver" from Asia exist.
antique-flatware.buy: Only buy pieces marked STERLING / COIN / 925 below melt, or named sterling serving pieces in figural patterns at ≤ $40; pass on plate and bone/steel.

antique-framed-prints.title: Antique framed prints
antique-framed-prints.full: Antique framed prints (chromolithographs, photogravures, hand-coloured engravings and fashion/costume plates; Knapp Co., Prang, Currier & Ives, Kellogg, Taber-Prang, Gibson, Maxfield Parrish, Wallace Nutting, Bessie Pease Gutmann, Haigh-Wood photogravures; 19th-c. French costume plates)
antique-framed-prints.money: Currier & Ives large folios, rare originals $500–10,000+.
antique-framed-prints.fakes: Halftone reproductions of Currier & Ives and Parrish are everywhere (often titled "antique"). Modern "costume plate" reproductions printed on aged-look paper. Re-framed modern prints in old frames.
antique-framed-prints.buy: Pass on most; only buy original Currier & Ives (check the publisher line and title vs. the catalogue), period Parrish/Gutmann with publisher line, or a strong original ornate gesso frame alone worth ≥ $150, at ≤ 1/3 resale; large frames rarely pass the shippin
tells: Currier & Ives (1835–1907): hand-coloured lithographs with "Currier & Ives, 152 Nassau St. N.Y." line.

Chromolithographs (1870s–1910s): layered colour printing with a fine stippled dot texture (no regular halftone grid); publishers like Knapp & Co. (NY), L. Prang (Boston), Gray Lithograph; romantic or genre subjects (Romeo and Juliet, cherubs, maidens); frequen

Photogravures and hand-tinted photographic prints (1890s–1920s): smooth continuous tone, sometimes hand-coloured; Edwardian ladies in parlours, "Haigh-Wood" style genre scenes; frames often oak or gilt with applied crest.

antique-glassware-lots.title: Antique glassware lots
antique-glassware-lots.full: Antique glassware lots (mixed estate lots: pressed glass, Depression glass, cut crystal, art pottery strays)
antique-glassware-lots.money: signed art glass (Steuben, Loetz, Fenton early, Tiffany), vaseline/uranium, EAPG rarities $50–1,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
antique-glassware-lots.fakes: Depression glass reproductions (Cherry Blossom, Madrid/"Recollection"), fake Heisey marks, Fenton reissues of EAPG patterns.
antique-glassware-lots.buy: Mixed lots only pay off when one identifiable "hit" (signed art glass, uranium/vaseline, rare Depression colour or form) is visible; otherwise pass, since shipping kills lot value.

antique-gold-jewelry.title: Antique gold jewelry
antique-gold-jewelry.full: Antique gold jewelry (Victorian, Edwardian, Art Nouveau gold; gold-filled and rolled gold)
antique-gold-jewelry.money: Etruscan revival, signed makers, mourning pieces with hair, large lockets $300–3,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
antique-gold-jewelry.fakes: Lots of reproduction "Victorian" jewelry; fake karat stamps on plated pieces. Testing (acid or XRF) is needed, which is a professional-verification issue for high-value pieces. Single contradictory clues (rollover catch
antique-gold-jewelry.buy: Never buy from photos unless the karat mark is visible and price ≤ melt + small margin; tiny earrings/studs never clear the $50 profit bar.

antique-grease-lamps.title: Antique grease, betty and early oil lamps
antique-grease-lamps.full: Antique grease, betty and early oil lamps (betty lamps, crusie/phoebe lamps, tin spout lamps, miners' tin "teapot" lamps, Scandinavian iron fire lighters)
antique-grease-lamps.money: signed/dated or brass-decorated betties and rare forms $300–1,500 (general knowledge, verify)
antique-grease-lamps.fakes: Betty lamps were widely reproduced in the 20th century (colonial-revival tin and iron, Williamsburg reproductions) — these have stamped parts and uniform rust. Fake "aged" miners' lamps exist.
antique-grease-lamps.buy: Pay ≤ $20 only for genuine hand-forged iron betty/crusie lamps (hinged lid, hanging hook, wick channel); pass on tin cans with wicks.
tells: Betty lamp: shallow iron/tin pan with an inner wick channel and hinged lid, hanger + pick on a chain; hand-forged rivets.
Crusie/Phoebe: two stacked open pans with pinched spout, a hanger; Scottish/Scandinavian.
Miners' "teapot" cap lamps: small tin/brass oil-wick lamp with a spout and hook to clip onto a cap (1850–1910s), brands like Dewar, Wolf; mostly 3–4" tall.

antique-hand-saws.title: Antique hand saws
antique-hand-saws.full: Antique hand saws (Henry Disston & Sons, Simonds, E.C. Atkins, Wheeler Madden & Clemson, Spear & Jackson, Harvey Peace, Warranted Superior, Sears Craftsman)
antique-hand-saws.fakes: No meaningful faking. Watch for re-handled saws (a period handle on a different plate) and "married" medallions. Modern reproduction makers (Lie-Nielsen, Veritas) sell new premium saws: they are not fakes but are not ant
antique-hand-saws.buy: Buy only straight, unpitted saws with crisp wheat-carved apple handles and legible etch (Disston No. 12/16/D-12, early No. 7 with nib, back saws), at ≤ $10 each; pass on rusty lots, crosscut logging saws and meat saws.
tells: Handle: carved wheat on apple wood = premium line (Disston No. 12, No. 16, D-12, Atkins 400, Simonds No. 71/72). Plain beech = No. 7/D-7. Thumbhole "covertop/let-in" handle = D-8/D-23. Plastic (Tenite) or plywood = later, cheap.
Nut count: 4–5 nuts on full-size premium saws; 3 on cheap ones.
Blade back: straight back (No. 7, 12, 16, D-12) vs skewback (D-8, No. 120 Acme).

antique-horseshoes.title: Antique horseshoes and pitching horseshoes , Ohio Horseshoe Co., Giant Grip, St. Pierre, Gordon Spin-On, Lattore, "Ringer", Royal, Allen)
antique-horseshoes.full: Antique horseshoes and pitching horseshoes (farrier shoes, draft horse shoes; pitching shoes by Diamond Calk (Duluth), Ohio Horseshoe Co., Giant Grip, St. Pierre, Gordon Spin-On, Lattore, "Ringer", Royal, Allen)
antique-horseshoes.money: early drop-forged pro pitching shoes (Gordon Spin-On, Ohio O, Lattore) $40–150 per pair (Gordon Terapeak median $69).
antique-horseshoes.fakes: - Cast-iron decorative "antique" horseshoes from China for crafts. - Some makers (Gordon, St. Pierre) remained in production for decades, so a "vintage" name does not guarantee age; check old company names, wear and pain
antique-horseshoes.buy: Pass — heavy, cheap; only boxed early pro-model sets ≤ $20.
tells: Pitching shoes: ~7–7.5 in. long, ~2.5 lb; NHPA limits are max 2 lb 10 oz, max 7-5/8 in. long, max 7-1/4 in. wide, opening max 3-1/2 in. (used shoes 3-5/8), no part over 1 in. high (NHPA). Cast or forged, with "calks" (toe points/heel hooks) and a brand cast or
Farrier shoes: nail holes, worn, uneven; set in a crease (fullering) along the branches; toe clips and calks on draft shoes.

Hand-forged vs machine-made farrier shoes: Henry Burden's 1835 machine (Troy NY) made 60 shoes a minute and supplied the Union Army, so mass-made "keg shoes" date from the mid-19th c. on; hand-forged shoes show uneven branch thickness, hammer marks and irregul

antique-keys.title: Antique keys
antique-keys.full: Antique keys (skeleton/barrel/bit keys, padlock keys, railroad switch keys, jail and hotel keys; makers Yale & Towne, Corbin, Russell & Erwin, Sargent, Eagle Lock, Slaymaker, Adlake, Fraim)
antique-keys.money: rare jail, prison, castle, and early named railroad keys $100–800.
antique-keys.fakes: Railroad switch keys are heavily faked (cast copies with soft details, wrong hallmarks, fresh brass). Craft "skeleton key" bags (Michaels, Amazon) are sold as vintage everywhere. Fake "jail keys" and "Titanic" keys. High
antique-keys.buy: Pass ordinary skeleton key bunches and craft/repro keys; buy only railroad switch/signal keys with stamped road initials, hand-forged large keys over 5", or advertising hotel fobs, at ≤ $10 each.
tells: Hand-forged (pre-1850): uneven bow, hammer marks, iron, often 4–8" long, decorative bows.
Cast/stamped (1870–1940): uniform, iron or brass/bronze; maker names stamped on bow ("Corbin", "R&E", "Sargent", "Yale & Towne", "Eagle"), numbers on bit.

Railroad switch keys (1870s–1970s): brass, flat bow stamped with railroad initials (e.g. "PRR", "CB&Q", "ATSF") and maker (Adlake, Fraim, Slaymaker, Wilson Bohannan) and serial; barrel shank with hole.

antique-lamp-shades.title: Antique lamp shades, glass
antique-lamp-shades.full: Antique lamp shades, glass (GWTW / student / hurricane / Aladdin / Handel / Pairpoint / art glass)
antique-lamp-shades.money: signed art glass (Steuben, Quezal, Tiffany, Handel, Pairpoint) $200–3,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
antique-lamp-shades.fakes: Huge volume of 1960s–90s GWTW-style reproductions (L.G. Wright, Fenton, Asian imports). Fake "Tiffany"/"Steuben" signatures on modern iridescent shades. "Antique" in a title rarely means anything for pink frosted decal s
antique-lamp-shades.buy: Only buy cased or acid-cut student shades, signed art glass, or Victorian hand-painted globes; pass on decal-flower 1970s–90s shades.
tells: Art glass tulip shades for 2 1/4" fitters (Steuben Aurene, Quezal, Lustre Art, Tiffany Favrile): iridescent, signed on the fitter rim.
Reverse-painted shades (Handel, Pairpoint, Jefferson, Moe Bridges): painted on the inside, signed near the rim.
Art glass tulip shades are small (Quezal examples at Corning are about 11–13 cm high, 11–13 cm wide) and mould-blown, with a polished fitter rim (CMOG).

antique-light-fixtures.title: Antique light fixtures
antique-light-fixtures.full: Antique light fixtures (gas/electric "gasolier" fixtures, Arts & Crafts lanterns, Spanish/French brass chandeliers, sconces, coach lanterns; makers incl. Mitchell Vance, Cornelius, Handel, Gill Brothers, Jefferson, Virden, Lightolier, Stiffel, Progress)
antique-light-fixtures.money: pre-1930 slip-shade, Arts & Crafts and gas/electric fixtures $150–1,500
antique-light-fixtures.fakes: Rejuvenation and others reproduce period fixtures; Chinese "antique style" crystal chandeliers flood the market. Shades are often married to fixtures. - Reproductions use modern sockets and UL-listed wiring from the fact
antique-light-fixtures.buy: Pass on chandeliers (too big, need rewiring = repairs) and modern brass coach lanterns; only small pre-1930 sconces or single shades with signed art glass at ≤ $60 qualify.
tells: 1910s–30s Arts & Crafts / slip-shade: cast-iron or brass with polychrome paint; shades slip into cups; schoolhouse globes; "Virden", "Lincoln", "Moe Bridges", "Riddle" fixtures.
Pre-1920 gas/electric combination: arms pointing up (gas) and down (electric), cast brass, often with acid-etched or art-glass shades on 2¼-in fitters.

Combination fixtures were used from the 1880s into the early 20th century so electric light could be used with gas as a backup (Ingenium). Gas tells: a small decorative gas key (often openwork) on each gas arm, a gas burner tip or candle-slip socket, and a hol

antique-maps.title: Antique maps
antique-maps.full: Antique maps (atlas leaves: Mitchell, Colton, Johnson, Tanner, Meyer, Stieler, Black, Johnston, Arrowsmith; separately issued maps; reproductions)
antique-maps.money: separately issued pocket/wall maps and early Texas/West $300–5,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
antique-maps.fakes: Many "antique" maps are 20th-c. reproductions (Rand McNally facsimiles, Hammond, National Geographic reprints, decorator prints on parchment paper). Reproductions often come pre-framed in sets of 2–3 matching frames — ch
antique-maps.buy: Buy lots of genuine (plate-marked or letterpress-backed, foxed, hand-coloured) atlas leaves at ≤ $3–5 per map, or any single genuine American state/Texas map ≤ $40; never pay for prints.
tells: Plate mark (IMCoS): copper and steel engravings leave a continuous indented line around the image that you can feel; early plate marks hug the image, later ones can sit up to 1 cm outside it. A plain groove with the paper equally high on both sides is a faking
Atlas guard/stub: atlas leaves often keep a paper guard or glue traces along one edge where they were bound; folded maps show wear at fold crossings.

Paper: pre-1800 laid paper shows chain and laid lines to the edge when held to light; post-1800 wove/wood-pulp paper is smoother with no lines. A map with no blemishes at all is unlikely to be antique (IMCoS).

antique-meat-grinders.title: Antique meat grinders
antique-meat-grinders.full: Antique meat grinders (Enterprise, Universal/Landers Frary & Clark, Chop-Rite, Keystone, Griswold, Hussmann, Alexanderwerk, Spong)
antique-meat-grinders.money: early decorative Enterprise/coffee-mill crossovers and complete store models $150–400 (general knowledge, verify)
antique-meat-grinders.fakes: Asian cast-iron repros of decorative Enterprise coffee mills exist; for grinders, Chop-Rite reissues and modern Porkert/Chinese clones (light, rough castings, no patent dates).
antique-meat-grinders.buy: Buy only large-number (#22/#32) or decorative early store grinders under ~$40 that a car seat can hold; common clamp-on choppers are a pass.

antique-milk-cans.title: Antique milk cans
antique-milk-cans.full: Antique milk cans (dairy transport cans: Cherry-Burrell, Buhl, Davis, Superior, Mojonnier, Sturges; dairy-stamped cans; copper/brass cream cans; hand-painted tole cans)
antique-milk-cans.money: embossed dairy-name cans and small cream cans (1–2 qt to 1 gal) $40–150
antique-milk-cans.fakes: Small decorative replica cans (Asian imports) and new "farmhouse" cans with fake stencilling.
antique-milk-cans.buy: Pass on full-size 5–10 gallon cans (25 in tall, 15–25 lb, $40+ to ship); only small embossed cream cans or copper cans at ≤ $20.

antique-natural-history-prints.title: Antique natural history prints
antique-natural-history-prints.full: Antique natural history prints (Brehm, Naumann, Audubon, Gould, Lizars, Buffon, Meyers, Keulemans chromolithographs)
antique-natural-history-prints.fakes: Countless modern reproductions; 1940s–80s Audubon prints (Macmillan, Amsterdam Audubon). Use a loupe for dot patterns; check verso text.
antique-natural-history-prints.buy: Buy hand-colored (not chromolith) large plates or Gould/Audubon octavo with visible plate numbers ≤ $40; framed German book chromolithographs are pass above ~$25.
tells: Modern offset reproductions: rosette dot pattern, bright white paper, often "Audubon" — low value.
Hand-colored engravings/lithographs (pre-1870): watercolor washes on black-line prints; colors slightly overlap lines; plate mark (embossed rectangle) for engravings.

Chromolithographs (1870s–1910s): printed color from multiple stones; dot/grain pattern under magnification; uniform colors; German books (Brehms Tierleben, Naumann "Naturgeschichte der Vögel Mitteleuropas" 1896–1905, Meyers Konversations-Lexikon) produced vast

antique-oil-cans.title: Antique oil cans, lamp fillers and kerosene cans
antique-oil-cans.full: Antique oil cans, lamp fillers and kerosene cans (hand-made tin fillers, Eagle, Dandy, Winfield, Delphos, Wedco, railroad cans, advertising motor-oil and household-oil tins)
antique-oil-cans.money: rare graphic 1910s–30s brand cans (Mobiloil Gargoyle early, Polarine, Indian, Harley-Davidson, Wolf's Head) $200–2,000+.
antique-oil-cans.fakes: - Reproduction advertising oil cans and "aged" decorator cans (Texaco, Harley, Indian) are abundant — modern lithography, spot welds, too-even rust. - Decorator "primitive" tin pitchers and fillers made in India/China, a
antique-oil-cans.buy: Plain unmarked cans never clear the rule; buy only strong-graphic advertising tins or rare brand quarts with ≥ 80% litho surviving, where the sold median clears profit ≥ max($50, price).
tells: Advertising tins: lithographed graphics and logos (Texaco star, Sinclair dinosaur, Mobil Pegasus/Gargoyle, Shell), cone-top household oil "Handy Oilers," quart motor-oil cans.

Hand-made tin lamp fillers (19th c.): coffee-pot or conical body of tinned sheet iron, soldered seams, strap handle, long tapering spout often stiffened by a wire/strap brace, hinged or cap lid with a knob, dark asphaltum (japanned) finish worn to rust/patina.

Kerosene cans: 1–5 gallon, round or square, bail handle with wooden grip, screw fill cap and spout with a cap on a chain; painted red (gas) or blue/green (kerosene) or plain galvanized. Makers' names embossed on the base or top (Eagle, Winfield "Polo," Delphos

antique-open-back-banjos.title: Antique open-back 5-string banjos
antique-open-back-banjos.full: Antique open-back 5-string banjos (1880s–1920s) (S.S. Stewart, Fairbanks, Vega, Bacon, Cole, Dobson, Washburn)
antique-open-back-banjos.fakes: No significant fakes. Later reissue Whyte Laydie/Tubaphone models (e.g. Vega/Deering-era) exist – check the dowel stick stamp and serial (general knowledge, verify). Married parts (replacement necks) are the main risk.
antique-open-back-banjos.buy: Stamped Fairbanks/Vega/Stewart/Cole/Bacon < $300 with straight neck; unmarked with engraved rim or tone ring < $100; pass plain unmarked > $60.

antique-portraits.title: Antique portraits
antique-portraits.full: Antique portraits (crayon/charcoal and pastel enlargements, painted ancestor portraits, tintypes, ambrotypes, daguerreotypes, convex glass portraits, chromolithograph "lady" prints)
antique-portraits.money: occupational, Civil War, African-American and named-artist painted portraits $200–5,000+.
antique-portraits.fakes: Modern prints on aged paper in old frames; "antique tintypes" made today (tintype revival) or Civil War fakes on old plates; reproduction daguerreotype cases. Fake named-sitter labels.
antique-portraits.buy: Buy only small cased images (occupational, military, outdoor, ethnic subjects) and small signed/painted portraits at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on large framed crayon enlargements and prints — they ship big and sell cheap.
tells: Crayon / solar enlargements (1860s–1920s): a photograph enlarged onto paper (solar camera, later bromide) and overdrawn in charcoal, crayon or pastel by studio artists (Chicago Portrait Co., Pan-American Portrait Co., traveling salesmen). Typically 16x20" in d
Convex (bubble) glass portraits (1890s–1920s): photo enlargements in oval frames behind convex glass.

Prints of pretty women (1900s–1930s): chromolithograph or photomechanical prints (Harrison Fisher, Philip Boileau, Maud Humphrey-type "lady" pictures) in oval gilt-gesso frames (like the $1 profile in our sweep).

antique-print-advertisements.title: Antique Print Advertisements
antique-print-advertisements.full: Antique Print Advertisements (magazine ads and covers 1890–1950: Ladies' Home Journal, Saturday Evening Post, Delineator, Collier's, Life)
antique-print-advertisements.money: illustrator-signed (Parrish, Leyendecker, Rockwell, Coles Phillips) or auto/Coca-Cola $30–150 (general knowledge, verify)
antique-print-advertisements.fakes: Modern reprints/posters of famous ads; "vintage ad" prints on blank-back stock. Check reverse.
antique-print-advertisements.buy: Buy lots of pre-1930 full-page color ads/covers at ≤ $2 per page, especially Leyendecker/Parrish/Phillips/Rockwell and auto/tire/soda ads; pass single common ads.

antique-scales.title: Antique and vintage scales , Hanson, Pelouze, American Family, Chatillon, Triner)
antique-scales.full: Antique and vintage scales (Toledo, Detecto/Jacobs Bros., Fairbanks, Howe, Computing Scale Co. (Dayton), Hanson, Pelouze, American Family, Chatillon, Triner)
antique-scales.money: restored or early Toledo "Honest Weight" fan scales and computing scales $150–1,100.
antique-scales.fakes: - Decorative "antique" cast-iron balance scales, brass apothecary scales and "Toledo-style" candy scales are made new in Asia. - Reproduction decals and badges exist for Toledo; check for overly crisp decals on a worn bo
antique-scales.buy: Only Toledo/Computing-Scale fan or candy scales and complete baker's scales with pan, scoop and weights, at ≤ 30% of sold median, and only if they ride in a passenger seat (most counter scales weigh 15–40 lb, so shipping is the killer).
tells: Fan/candy scales (Toledo "No Springs Honest Weight", Computing Scale Co., Dayton): tall enamel housing with a fan-shaped or arched chart and a pan or scoop on top; 1900s–1960s; store counter pieces. Toledo model 405 (antique, pendulum "No Springs") and 3111 (1

Counter/baker's/dough scales (Detecto, Fairbanks, Howe): black cast-iron base with a beam and sliding poise, loose slotted weights, and a tin or brass scoop. Detecto (Jacobs Bros., Brooklyn) cast "DETECTO" on the base plate.

Postal scales: Pelouze (Evanston/Chicago, IL) spring scales with rate charts dated by postal rates (e.g., "rates effective May 1971"); Fairbanks cast-iron and brass beam postal balances (1870s–1920s).

antique-tennis-rackets.title: Antique tennis rackets
antique-tennis-rackets.full: Antique tennis rackets (lopsided/tilt-head 1870s–80s; flat-top and fishtail 1880s–1900s; Spalding, Wright & Ditson, Draper & Maynard, Slazenger, F.H. Ayres, Feltham, Malings, Tate, Bancroft, Dayton steel, Birmal, Dunlop Maxply, Wilson)
antique-tennis-rackets.money: lopsided/tilt-head lawn tennis rackets c.1874–c.1885 $500–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify
antique-tennis-rackets.fakes: Decorative "antique style" rackets made for interior decor; occasional re-shaped or fake-stamped frames. A lopsided head that looks too clean, light or nylon-strung is suspect.
antique-tennis-rackets.buy: Check head symmetry first: a lopsided head under $150 is a buy; symmetric convex-wedge rackets only at ≤ $15; pass on 20th-century wood rackets unless a rare model (Dayton steel, Birmal) is ≤ $15.
tells: Lopsided / tilt-head / teardrop (c.1874–c.1885): head tilted to one side, flattened on top, like a real-tennis racket; heavy ash frame, concave wedge often stamped with maker and weight (F.H. Ayres example: "13oz ¼, Warranted, London"), thick gut, sometimes tr
Flat-top / square-top (c.1880s–1890s): symmetric but with a flattened top edge.

Symmetric oval with a convex wedge (c.1890–1910s): a solid wood "wedge" filling the throat, bulging outward; corrugated or scored handle, sometimes a fishtail (flared) butt. Spalding "18 oz Hand Made" stamps are typical — the common tier (triage).

antique-wall-shelves.title: Antique wall shelves
antique-wall-shelves.full: Antique wall shelves (Victorian carved oak clock shelves, Eastlake, Black Forest, mirrored shelves, spice/curio shelves)
antique-wall-shelves.money: Black Forest carved, Aesthetic Movement and fine Eastlake pieces $200-600+ (general knowledge, verify)
antique-wall-shelves.fakes: Large volume of reproductions, and AI-staged / AI-enhanced listing photos now appear (see sweep note: the example's photo looks generated - styled clock, "HOROLOGY" book, matching decor). Always ask for unedited phone ph
antique-wall-shelves.buy: Buy only verified-old carved shelves ≤ 30" wide at ≤ $60 after getting real (not staged) photos; resale must reach ~$175.

antique-washboards.title: Antique washboards
antique-washboards.full: Antique washboards (National Washboard Co., Columbus Washboard Co., Dubl Handi, Maid-Rite, Brass King, glass and enamel boards)
antique-washboards.money: cobalt glass, enamel ("granite") or all-wood/early patented boards $60–200.
antique-washboards.fakes: Columbus Washboard Co. still makes Dubl Handi and Maid-Rite; decor-store fake "antique" boards with distressed paint and invented brand names exist.
antique-washboards.buy: Pass on zinc/galvanized boards; only cobalt/blue glass, enamelware or hand-made all-wood boards at ≤ $20 are worth a look, and even those only clear profit when locally cheap.

antique-wooden-boxes.title: Antique and vintage wooden boxes
antique-wooden-boxes.full: Antique and vintage wooden boxes (tea caddies, writing slopes, document/jewelry boxes, Tunbridge, Chinese export, folk art)
antique-wooden-boxes.money: Georgian tea caddies, writing slopes, Tunbridge mosaic, tramp art $150–1,500+
antique-wooden-boxes.fakes: Many modern "antique-style" tea caddies and writing boxes from India/China (artificially aged, often with brass "campaign" corners). Tell: machine dovetails, new screws, uniform distressing, no wear where hands touch. -
antique-wooden-boxes.buy: Buy Georgian/Victorian tea caddies, writing slopes, Tunbridge ware or tramp art (visible dovetails, inlay, brass escutcheons, period locks) at ≤ 1/3 of sold; souvenir/import boxes are pass.
tells: Georgian tea caddies (1760–1840): sarcophagus or rectangular, mahogany/rosewood/satinwood veneer, inlaid stringing, lidded compartments and mixing bowl inside, lion-mask ring handles.
Tunbridge ware (Kent, 1830–1900): wood mosaic pictures of castles/flowers made of tiny tesserae.

Typical documented example: early 19th-c. rosewood veneer with satinwood inlay, inlaid escutcheon, ring handle, ball feet, red leather interior, two lidded tea compartments (originally tin/lead/foil-lined) flanking a central well with a blown-glass mixing bowl

antiquities-and-reproductions.title: Antiquities and reproductions
antiquities-and-reproductions.full: Antiquities and reproductions (Roman/Holy Land terracotta oil lamps, Egyptian ushabti/scarabs, pre-Columbian figures, "Persian"/"Luristan"/"Gandhara" carved stone and bronze, museum-shop replicas, tourist-market fakes)
antiquities-and-reproductions.money: genuine better pieces (figural Roman discus lamps, bronze lamps, Egyptian faience) $200–2,000+ but legally and authentically fraught.
antiquities-and-reproductions.fakes: This category is mostly fakes. "Ancient" coins, lamps, scarabs, and pre-Columbian figures sold by private owners are overwhelmingly souvenirs. Genuine pieces require provenance documentation (pre-1970 UNESCO) and profess
antiquities-and-reproductions.buy: Pass – genuine antiquities need provenance and authentication (excluded by Dylan's rules, plus legal/eBay-policy risk) and the reproductions are worth $5–30; never buy items sold as "ancient" from private sellers.
tells: Genuine ancient oil lamps: mould-made or wheel-made fired clay (terracotta, buff/orange/red slip), 2.5–4" long, wick nozzle, fill hole, soot blackening at the nozzle, root marks and calcified mineral deposits, worn relief. Stone lamps exist but are rare and pl

Reproductions: crisp moulded detail, uniform grey/black colour with applied white wash or "dirt" in recesses, no soot at nozzle, resin feels warm/light, plaster chalky; motifs mixed from different cultures (fish + crowned deity + scales in a lozenge = invented
Museum replicas: marked on base ("MMA", "© British Museum", "Alva Museum Replicas", "Israel Museum").

aramith-pool-balls.title: Pool balls and billiard accessories
aramith-pool-balls.full: Pool balls (Aramith) and billiard accessories (Aramith Crown, Premium, Super Pro, Tournament, Black)
aramith-pool-balls.fakes: Generic sets in the same colours sold as "Aramith" – check for the logo on the cue ball and the Aramith moulded box.
aramith-pool-balls.buy: Super Pro/Tournament < $60; Premium only at ≤ ~$20 (see buy rule note); pass Premium at $75.

architectural-salvage.title: Architectural salvage
architectural-salvage.full: Architectural salvage (door hardware: Russell & Erwin, Sargent, Yale & Towne, Corbin, P&F Corbin, Reading Hardware; stained/leaded glass; terra cotta and plaster ornament; corbels, finials, balusters, register grates, glass knobs)
architectural-salvage.money: exceptional stained glass and named-building terra cotta $500–5,000+.
architectural-salvage.fakes: Large volumes of reproduction cast-iron and brass Victorian hardware (Asian imports) with fake rust; resin corbels; new barley-twist spindles; reproduction "salvaged" stained glass. Real hardware has makers' marks on the
architectural-salvage.buy: Buy only compact ornate Victorian/Arts & Crafts hardware (cast-bronze/brass knobs, backplates, hinges in named patterns) at ≤ 1/3 sold median; pass heavy stone/terra cotta, oversize glass, plain or reproduction spindles.
tells: Door hardware: knobs (cast bronze/brass with patterns – Eastlake, Aesthetic, Japanesque), backplates/escutcheons, hinges with decorative leaves and ball/steeple tips, mortise locks. Pattern names catalogued (e.g., Russell & Erwin "Windsor", Sargent "Lorraine",

Glazed architectural terra cotta: egg-and-dart, bead-and-reel, dentil cornice blocks, crazed white or cream glaze over buff clay, hollow cellular backs (example 7942248064) – very heavy (15–40 lb per block).
Turned wood: balusters/spindles, newel posts, finials. Retail reproduction barley-twist spindles (example 7942251853 photo is a retailer's stock photo with "THESE SOLD OUT") are new.

art-backs-labels-and-printmaking-marks.title: Art backs, labels and printmaking marks — reading guide
art-backs-labels-and-printmaking-marks.full: Art backs, labels and printmaking marks — reading guide (canvas colourmen stamps: Winsor & Newton, Reeves, Rowney, Roberson, Newman, Lefranc, Bourgeois, Lechertier Barbe, Blanchet, Prud'homme, Fredrix, Devoe, Schneider & Co, Weber; stretchers; gallery, exhibition, customs, framer and auction labels and stencils; paper watermarks; printer chops and blindstamps; edition annotations; estate stamps; photograph versos)
art-backs-labels-and-printmaking-marks.money: The back of a picture is evidence, not decoration: a pre-1882 "Winsor & Newton, 38 Rathbone Place" stamp or a 1892–1953 Macbeth Gallery label turns a $40–150 "decor painting" into a researchable American/British period work ($300–5,000+ when the artist traces), a Carrig-Rohane or Newcomb-Macklin fra
art-backs-labels-and-printmaking-marks.fakes: - **Moved labels:** gallery and exhibition labels are steamed off and stuck on other frames or stretchers. Check the label sits on aged wood with matching dirt and that title/size match. - **Forged colourman stamps:** ra
art-backs-labels-and-printmaking-marks.buy: Always ask for a full photo of the back and close-ups of every stamp, label and blindstamp; buy a cheap "decor" painting only when a period colourman stamp or a recorded dealer/exhibition label supports a period date and the artist (or frame) has sold comps cl
tells: Labels: gallery, dealer, exhibition, framer, shipper and customs labels on the stretcher bars, crossbar, backing board, or the back of the frame (frame labels belong to the frame, not necessarily the picture).

Canvas stamp (colourman's stamp): on the back of the canvas itself, usually centred or in the lower half, in black, blue or red ink; an oval, shield, rectangle or royal-arms cartouche with the supplier's name and address. On a lined (relined) canvas it is hidd
Stretcher stamp: a smaller ink or burned stamp on the top or side bar of the stretcher, or on the crossbar.

art-deco-glass.title: Art Deco glass
art-deco-glass.full: Art Deco glass (Czech/Bohemian Tango and enamelled glass, Moser, Loetz late wares, Lalique, Sabino, Verlys, Phoenix/Consolidated, Fostoria/Cambridge/Fenton/Imperial Deco lines, English Davidson and Bagley, Sowerby)
art-deco-glass.money: Lalique pre-1945 R.LALIQUE, Ruba Rombic, Loetz/Moser signed $300–5,000+.
art-deco-glass.fakes: Lalique: fake "R. LALIQUE" signatures added to post-war or other-maker pieces (wrong font, wrong place, sand-blasted signature on a piece that should be moulded). Sabino: 1960s–70s reissues from the same moulds. Czech Ta
art-deco-glass.buy: Buy only signed or unmistakable makers (R.LALIQUE, Moser, Ruba Rombic, Czech acid stamp on a strong Tango form) at ≤ 1/3 of the low tier; pass on unsigned pairs priced over $40.
tells: American Deco: Consolidated "Ruba Rombic" (1928–32, cubist, very valuable), Phoenix and Consolidated sculptured vases (frosted/pastel backgrounds), Fostoria, Cambridge Statuesque/"Nude stem" (Cambridge Crown Tuscan, Carmen, Royal Blue), New Martinsville, Paden
Enamelled Czech/Bohemian glass: black-enamel rims, painted florals and birds on frosted or coloured glass (Harrach, Moser-Karlsbad, Loetz late period, many unnamed Novy Bor/Kamenicky Senov studios).

French frosted/opalescent: René Lalique (moulded "R.LALIQUE" pre-1945; "Lalique France" after), Sabino (opalescent with blue-gold glow, "Sabino Paris"), Etling, Hunebelle, Verlys (French and later Heisey/Holophane US), Marius-Ernest Sabino.

art-glass-vases.title: Art glass vases , Steuben, studio glass; decor-brand imports like Palmero, Global Views, Pier 1)
art-glass-vases.full: Art glass vases (Kosta Boda, Orrefors, Holmegaard, Riihimäki, Blenko, Fenton, Pilgrim, Viking, Hartley Wood, Mdina, Krosno, Bohemian/Czech (Loetz, Kralik, Welz), Steuben, studio glass; decor-brand imports like Palmero, Global Views, Pier 1)
art-glass-vases.money: Loetz phenomenon, Tiffany Favrile, Gallé cameo, Lalique $500–10,000 (authentication needed).
art-glass-vases.fakes: Fake Loetz, Tiffany Favrile and Gallé signatures on Chinese/Romanian glass are common; modern Fenton reissues; "Blenko" attribution to any colourful vase. Decor brands imitate mid-century and Murano styles.
art-glass-vases.buy: Pass on unsigned swirl/optic vases and decor-brand glass; buy only signed Scandinavian/studio pieces or Czech iridescent/Loetz-type at ≤ $30 with base photos, or a recognisable Blenko/Mdina form at ≤ $15.
tells: Bohemian/Czech iridescent (1890s–1930s): Loetz, Kralik, Pallme-König, Rindskopf; oil-slick iridescence, applied threads, polished pontil.
Depression-era optic glass (1920s–40s): thin, mould-blown green/pink with spiral optic ribs, crimped rim; Fenton, Imperial, Hazel-Atlas; $10–30.

Cased/opaline with trailing: white or coloured cased glass with applied trails or pulled swirls; Kralik/Welz Czech (1920s–30s, often with polished pontil), Hartley Wood (UK), modern Polish Krosno, Asian decor glass.

art-nouveau-poster-reproductions.title: Art Nouveau poster reproductions
art-nouveau-poster-reproductions.full: Art Nouveau poster reproductions (Mucha, Cappiello, Metlicovitz, Dudovich, Chéret, Toulouse-Lautrec, Steinlen reprints; Wine Spectator, Portal, Bernard Picture, Dover, Mucha Trust and museum reprints; original period lithographs)
art-nouveau-poster-reproductions.fakes: The category itself is reproduction. Danger: reprints sold as "vintage original lithograph"; giclées on canvas; Lens matching reprints to original-auction values (e.g., $3,750) — always a bust for these examples.
art-nouveau-poster-reproductions.buy: Pass on reprints; only flag possible originals (thick linen-backed stone lithograph with printer's imprint, period size, visible litho dot-free colour) for "ask seller" and specialist review — outside Dylan's no-authentication rule unless priced ≤ $25.
tells: Reprint tells: halftone dot rosette under magnification (offset printing), glossy or uniform paper, modern margin text ("The Wine Spectator", "© Mucha Trust", "Printed in USA"), fold lines from magazine inserts, small or standardised sizes (11×14, 24×36), mech

Original tells: stone lithography (solid, layered colour, no dot pattern), large sizes (e.g., Bitter Pastore c.1913 ~140×100 cm), printer's imprint in the margin (e.g., "G. Ricordi & C. Milano", "Imp. F. Champenois Paris"), linen backing, period tears and repa
Menus/ephemera using Mucha line art (e.g., restaurant menus) are modern printing, usually 1970s–90s.

artist-prints-vs-originals.title: Regional artist "originals" that are usually prints
artist-prints-vs-originals.full: Regional artist "originals" that are usually prints (Campanelli, Kinkade, Gaston Bussière, Putt)
artist-prints-vs-originals.money: listed artists with $5k+ records not our lane.
artist-prints-vs-originals.fakes: The core risk of this type: prints sold as "originals". Also canvas transfers and hand-embellished prints passed off as paintings, and forged signatures on decorative oils (general knowledge, verify).
artist-prints-vs-originals.buy: Buy only visible brushwork, signed, artist with auction records, ≤ 20% of low estimate; pass anything matted under glass.

asian-art-seals-signatures-and-box-inscr.title: Asian art seals, signatures and box inscriptions — reading guide , Meiji bronze signatures, "Dai Nippon", netsuke; Korean celadon; Southeast Asian bronzes)
asian-art-seals-signatures-and-box-inscr.full: Asian art seals, signatures and box inscriptions — reading guide (Chinese painting seals, woodblock-print vs painted, hardwood and jade tells; Japanese tomobako/hakogaki, kakejiku, ukiyo-e censor and date seals, Watanabe seal eras, Satsuma/Kutani/cloisonné marks (Ando, Namikawa), Meiji bronze signatures, "Dai Nippon", netsuke; Korean celadon; Southeast Asian bronzes)
asian-art-seals-signatures-and-box-inscr.money: Reading the seal or box is the whole edge: a printed "Qi Baishi" scroll is $20–80, a printed famous-name woodblock print $50–300, but a Watanabe-sealed first-edition Hasui sells $1,500–18,900 (Christie's 2024), a Namikawa-signed vase bought for £3 sold £6,300 (Canterbury 2022), an Ando-marked vase €
asian-art-seals-signatures-and-box-inscr.fakes: - **Chinese painting:** printed and hand-copied famous names with printed or carved seals; added "imperial" collector seals; Rongbaozhai prints sold as originals. - **Reign marks:** see ceramic-and-glass-marks-that-multi
asian-art-seals-signatures-and-box-inscr.buy: Never pay for a seal or signature you can't read in a sharp close-up; buy when the mark, the material and the technique agree (real seal paste on paper, kiri box signed by the same artist as the base, Watanabe seal of the right era, silver-wire cloisonné with

asian-paintings.title: Asian paintings
asian-paintings.full: Asian paintings (Chinese scrolls and silk paintings, porcelain plaque paintings, export decorator paintings, Japanese works)
asian-paintings.fakes: - Printed paintings with added hand-applied seals or a few added brush strokes ("over-painted prints"). - Famous-name forgeries, including old forgeries sold in the 1980s. - Modern porcelain plaques signed with Republic-
asian-paintings.buy: Pass on souvenir scrolls and signed-in-English decorator paintings; any "famous master" attribution needs professional authentication = pass; only Republic-period porcelain plaques (small, hand-enamelled) at ≤ $40 are worth an ask.
tells: Porcelain plaque painting: a flat glazed porcelain slab painted in overglaze famille-rose enamels, framed like a picture. Modern Jingdezhen workshops make large square/rectangular plaques (lady in a lotus boat with a Li Bai "Picking Lotus Song" 采莲曲 poem is a s

Tourist/export hanging scroll (1970s–today): bright white paper or brocade mounting, plastic or lacquered-wood roller knobs, a wire hanger, a short title in calligraphy (e.g. 寒梅 "winter plum") plus a cyclical date and one or two red seals. Plum blossoms, bambo
Framed silk landscape: misty mountains, pines, pavilions; the silk has a regular woven grid; signed with two characters and one seal; brocade mat. 1960s–90s Taiwan/Hong Kong/PRC export.

austrian-porcelain-fish-plates.title: Austrian, Bavarian and Limoges porcelain fish and game plates , Victoria Carlsbad, Carlsbad , Haviland, Limoges , Bavaria , Royal Doulton/Minton hand-painted, Pickard, Stouffer)
austrian-porcelain-fish-plates.full: Austrian, Bavarian and Limoges porcelain fish and game plates (MZ Austria (Moritz Zdekauer), Victoria Carlsbad, Carlsbad (Pirkenhammer), Haviland, Limoges (various), Bavaria (Hutschenreuther, Rosenthal, Z.S. & Co.), Royal Doulton/Minton hand-painted, Pickard, Stouffer)
austrian-porcelain-fish-plates.money: Haviland/Limoges decorated sets with large platter $300–900
austrian-porcelain-fish-plates.fakes: Modern Chinese "Limoges" marks on decals; reproductions of Royal Doulton/Minton fish painting rare. "Hand painted" stamped on backs of transfer-decorated plates (overpainted transfers) is common and misleading.
austrian-porcelain-fish-plates.buy: Pass on transfer-printed MZ/Bavaria plates unless a complete set of 8–12 with platter for ≤ $40; buy only hand-painted signed Limoges/English sets with platter at ≤ 1/3 resale.
tells: Limoges (France): hand-painted fish in water with seaweed, often signed by decorators (e.g. "Dubois", "Max", "Luc", "R.K."); Elite, T&V, J.P.L. blanks; heavy gilt rococo rims; sets of 12 + platter.
Haviland & Co.: fish sets designed by Félix Bracquemond (Japonisme), etc. — collectible.

MZ Austria (Moritz Zdekauer, Altrohlau near Carlsbad, 1884–1909; then C.M. Hutschenreuther): "MZ Austria" with crown/shield mark in green; scalloped gilt-rim plates, transfer printed fish or birds often over-painted, coloured borders (green, pink, cream).

auto-accessories.title: Vintage auto accessories
auto-accessories.full: Vintage auto accessories (trunk/ski racks, luggage racks, spotlights, hood ornaments, tissue dispensers, dealer accessories; makers Barecos, Sears Allstate, J.C. Whitney, Unity, Appleton, Moto Meter, Thule/Barrecrafters)
auto-accessories.money: Unity/Appleton spotlights, Lalique-era mascots and original radiator caps $100–2,000+.
