auto-accessories.fakes: Reproduction hood ornaments and Lalique-style glass mascots are common; reproduction NOS boxes exist for popular GM parts.
auto-accessories.buy: Pass on generic racks; buy only boxed NOS dealer accessories, chrome spotlights or pre-1950 mascots under ~$40 that fit the seat.

autoharps.title: Autoharps
autoharps.full: Autoharps (Oscar Schmidt, Zimmermann, Chromaharp/Rhythm Band, Orthey, Fladmark, d'Aigle)
autoharps.money: luthier harps (Orthey, Fladmark, d'Aigle, Daigle) $800–2,500 (general knowledge, verify)
autoharps.fakes: No fakes as such. Reissue OS models (2000s Asian "OS 21" etc.) look like vintage ones; check "USA" on the label and the serial number. Ignore "Antique" claims for 1970s harps.
autoharps.buy: Buy luthier harps and high-end OS models (Appalachian, Centurion, Festival, Ozark, signature) under ~$150; pass on common 15/21-chord models above ~$40.

automotive-diagnostic-scopes.title: Automotive diagnostic scopes & engine analysers
automotive-diagnostic-scopes.full: Automotive diagnostic scopes & engine analysers (Snap-on Counselor, Sun, Allen)
automotive-diagnostic-scopes.fakes: None for the cabinets. Cloned scan tools exist in the modern market (general knowledge, verify) – not relevant to vintage units.
automotive-diagnostic-scopes.buy: Hand-held Snap-on scanners ≤ $60 tested only; all cart/cabinet units are bigger than a passenger seat – excluded.

automotive-gauges.title: Vintage automotive and motorcycle gauges , Stewart-Warner, Sun Tach, AutoMeter, Smiths, VDO, Jaeger)
automotive-gauges.full: Vintage automotive and motorcycle gauges (Nippon Seiki (Honda/Yamaha/Kawasaki/Suzuki OEM), Stewart-Warner, Sun Tach, AutoMeter, Smiths, VDO, Jaeger)
automotive-gauges.money: Sun Super Tach II, Stewart-Warner Wings, Smiths chronometric for British classics $100–400.
automotive-gauges.fakes: Large volume of aftermarket reproduction Honda gauges (made in Taiwan/China) with near-identical faces; tells: lighter case, generic back without part number, different font, cheaper chrome.
automotive-gauges.buy: Pass unless the exact model fitment is identified, it's mechanical (cable-drive) and the seller shows it works or it's a known-high model; never pay > 40% of the model's sold median.

avon-figural-bottles.title: Avon figural bottles pre-1939 bottles)
avon-figural-bottles.full: Avon figural bottles (Avon Products 1960s–1980s aftershave/cologne decanters; Avon Cape Cod 1876 ruby glass; California Perfume Co. (CPC) pre-1939 bottles)
avon-figural-bottles.money: rare items (pre-1939 CPC bottles, 1960s Avon "Bay Rum" kegs, test/prototype pieces, full boxed sets) $30–200.
avon-figural-bottles.fakes: Not faked; Avon reissued many shapes.
avon-figural-bottles.buy: Pass on all 1960s–80s Avon figurals and Cape Cod; only CPC (California Perfume Company, pre-1939) bottles with labels at ≤ $15.

bakelite-and-mid-century-radios.title: Bakelite and mid-century tube radios
bakelite-and-mid-century-radios.full: Bakelite and mid-century tube radios (Zenith, Philco, RCA, Emerson, Motorola; Catalin)
bakelite-and-mid-century-radios.fakes: General knowledge, verify: reproduction "nostalgia" radios (Crosley, Thomas, Spartus) styled like old cathedral/bakelite sets; replacement reproduction knobs and backs; Catalin cabinets with repaired cracks or re-polishe
bakelite-and-mid-century-radios.buy: Pass brown bakelite > $40 and anything untested.

bakelite-buttons.title: Bakelite and early plastic buttons , Rich Art, Schwanda, Lucky Strike; carved, laminated, polka-dot and reverse-carved apple juice)
bakelite-buttons.full: Bakelite and early plastic buttons (Bakelite/phenolic, Catalin, celluloid, galalith/casein, lucite; realistic/figural buttons 1930s–40s by B. Blumenthal "La Mode"/"Le Chic" (Marion Weeber designs), Rich Art, Schwanda, Lucky Strike; carved, laminated, polka-dot and reverse-carved apple juice)
bakelite-buttons.money: rare realistics (Rich Art sets, B. Blumenthal Le Chic/La Mode) $100–500 per set (estimate
bakelite-buttons.fakes: "Fakelite" — modern cast resin realistics and polka dots (1990s–present, often from Asia); "Bakelite" claims on any old plastic. Fakelite often fails Simichrome and lacks oxidation. - Some fakes are washed or treated so
bakelite-buttons.buy: Buy only tested Bakelite realistics/figurals or full button jars ≤ $20 when they visibly contain carved/dot Bakelite; pass on pairs of novelty buttons over $10.
tells: Cards: original cards carry the brand name (La Mode, Le Chic, B.G.E. Originals, Rich Art, Schwanda, etc.), and the card is the best maker evidence. Off the card, maker attribution of realistics is usually a guess.
Size: coat buttons 1–1.5 in., dress buttons 5/8–7/8 in.; realistics usually 3/4–1.5 in. Collectors measure diameter in inches (or NBS "lines").

Shanks: Bakelite/Catalin buttons usually have a self-shank (drilled through a moulded or carved boss on the back) or a metal loop set into the back. Two- and four-hole sew-throughs are common on cheaper plastic. Realistics often have an inserted wire loop or a

bakelite-flatware.title: Bakelite-handled flatware & kitchen tools
bakelite-flatware.money: carved/figural or Art Deco fitted-box sets $250–500.
bakelite-flatware.fakes: "Fakelite" (modern resin imitating bakelite) exists mainly in jewellery; in flatware the risk is plastic/lucite sold as bakelite – sellers often hedge ("says bakelite online") (general knowledge, verify).
bakelite-flatware.buy: 24+ pc marbled or red/green set ≤ $25; pass 12-pc butterscotch at $25+.

bakelite-jewelry.title: Bakelite / Catalin jewelry
bakelite-jewelry.full: Bakelite / Catalin jewelry (cast phenolic bangles, brooches, dangles; vs Lucite, celluloid, resin and "Fakelite")
bakelite-jewelry.money: "Philadelphia" bracelets, Shultz-signed modern-era pieces and rare colours (true red, cobalt, "end-of-day" multicolour) $500-5,000. Lucite/celluloid/resin look-alikes $3-15.
bakelite-jewelry.fakes: "Fakelite" reproductions of cherries, dangles, dot bangles, Scottie pins and Philadelphia bracelets have been made since the 1990s in resin and even in new-cast phenolic (which passes Simichrome — the test is not definit
bakelite-jewelry.buy: Only buy when the seller confirms a hot-water/Simichrome test or the photo shows the carving, patina and oxidised colour of phenolic; never pay Bakelite money for untested "plastic".

balalaikas.title: Balalaikas
balalaikas.full: Balalaikas (Soviet factories: Lunacharsky Leningrad, Shikhovo, Moscow Experimental, Bobrov; modern Russian/Ukrainian makers)
balalaikas.money: master-built concert balalaikas and contrabass $500–3,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
balalaikas.fakes: None in the usual sense. Modern Chinese/Russian souvenir models are sold as "vintage USSR".
balalaikas.buy: Pass on student prima balalaikas above ~$30; buy only master-built/concert (labelled maker, multi-piece ribbed back, fine tuners) at ≤ 1/3 of resale, and only prima/secunda sizes.

bamboo-fly-rods.title: Bamboo fly rods
bamboo-fly-rods.full: Bamboo (split-cane) fly rods (Heddon, Granger, South Bend, Montague, Orvis, Leonard, Payne)
bamboo-fly-rods.fakes: Re-stamped or "upgraded" rods with forged maker names are rare but possible on top makers; mismatched (married) tips from another rod are more common – check matching serials (general knowledge, verify).
bamboo-fly-rods.buy: Named Granger/Heddon/Phillipson/Orvis/Winston rod with all tips ≤ $120–150; any Leonard/Payne/Thomas ≤ $200; always get the butt stamp photo first.

bandai-and-japanese-toys-vintage.title: Vintage Japanese toys
bandai-and-japanese-toys-vintage.full: Vintage Japanese toys (Popy/Bandai chogokin, Jumbo Machinder, Mattel Shogun Warriors, post-war tin: Alps, Yonezawa, Nomura, Masudaya, Marusan, Linemar)
bandai-and-japanese-toys-vintage.money: boxed pieces and tin robots $200–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
bandai-and-japanese-toys-vintage.fakes: - Repro **Shogun Warriors fists, missiles, swords and stickers** (3D-printed or recast) – common; they lower value if not disclosed. Tells: lighter plastic, slightly different color, rough mold lines. - **Chinese tin rob
bandai-and-japanese-toys-vintage.buy: Buy 24 in Shogun Warriors/Jumbo Machinders ≤ $60, Popy/Bandai die-cast robots with fists/missiles ≤ $40, friction (non-battery) tin cars/robots ≤ $40; pass battery-op tin unless sold as untested display at ≤ $20, and pass all reissues.
tells: Chogokin ("super alloy") die-cast robots, 1974 onward: Popy GA-series (GA-01 Mazinger Z, 1974), Bandai later. Heavy die-cast metal torsos, plastic limbs, spring-launched fists/missiles. Markings: "POPY" or "BANDAI", "Made in Japan", ©Dynamic Planning / ©Toei,
Jumbo Machinder (Popy, 1973–): ~24 in hollow blow-molded polyethylene robots with launching fists.

Shogun Warriors (Mattel import line, 1976–1980): Popy chogokins and Jumbo Machinders sold in the US with Mattel boxes. 24 in figures: Great Mazinga, Raydeen, Gaiking, Dragun, Combatra, Daimos, Poseidon, Godzilla (19 in, with launching hand and rolling tongue),

bank-bags.title: Bank bags
bank-bags.full: Bank bags (canvas coin and deposit bags; small-town national banks, savings and loans, Federal Reserve, US Mint, casino and armoured-car bags)
bank-bags.fakes: Novelty "money bag" props and decor reproductions exist; Federal Reserve style bags are reproduced as decor. Small-town bank bags are not faked.
bank-bags.buy: Buy lots at ≤ $2 per printed canvas bag and only if most are small-town or defunct banks; sell singly. Pass on vinyl zipper bags.
tells: Collectors value small-town and defunct banks, bags with building pictures or logos, old "Member Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation" wording, and state-specific names (Wyoming, Montana, New Mexico draw regional collectors).
Federal Reserve and US Mint canvas bags (with "$1000" or coin denominations stenciled) are a separate, popular category.

barware.title: Vintage barware
barware.full: Vintage barware (cocktail shakers, ice buckets, decanters, glass sets, trays; Dorothy Thorpe, Georges Briard, Culver, Fred Press, Cera, Libbey, Napier, Chase, Revere, Kromex, Irvinware, Tiffany & Co., Baccarat, beer trays)
barware.money: Tiffany/Baccarat/Lalique crystal, Napier penguin, early Coca-Cola/beer trays $100–500+.
barware.fakes: - Coca-Cola and pre-Prohibition beer trays are widely reproduced (thin steel, bright, a modern copyright line). - Napier penguin shakers have been reproduced. An original has the Napier mark under the beak flap and a hea
barware.buy: Buy only signed or figural pieces (Napier penguin or bell shakers, Chase/Revere chrome, Culver/Briard full sets, acid-etched Tiffany/Baccarat crystal) at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on unsigned glass, 1960s+ beer trays, woodgrain ice buckets, novelty glasses.
tells: Ice buckets: Kromex aluminium, Georges Briard and Culver gold-decorated, Irvinware and Kraftware vinyl/woodgrain/plaid (1960s–70s), Ice Tub insulated, Tiffany & Co. and Baccarat crystal (acid-etched mark on the base), Dansk Quistgaard teak ($100–300).

Cocktail shakers: Napier (Meriden CT) figural penguin ($300–1,000+), bell, and "Hour-Glass" shakers; West Bend penguin; Chase Brass & Copper and Revere Copper & Brass Art Deco chrome (marked with a centaur or the Revere logo); Kromex and Atomic-star aluminium;

MCM glass sets: 22k gold-decorated highballs and rocks glasses. Signatures in gold on the side: "Culver" (Culver Ltd.), "Georges Briard" (script), "Fred Press", "Cera" (Cera Glass), "Dorothy Thorpe" is unsigned but known by the sterling or silver band and sand

baseball-card-wax-boxes.title: Sealed baseball-card wax boxes
baseball-card-wax-boxes.full: Sealed baseball-card wax boxes (1980s–90s "junk wax") (Topps, Donruss, Fleer, Score, Upper Deck)
baseball-card-wax-boxes.fakes: Resealed boxes and searched/repacked packs are the main risk for valuable years (1986 Fleer basketball, 1989 UD, 1980s Topps). Only buy high-end boxes with BBCE wrap (general knowledge, verify).
baseball-card-wax-boxes.buy: 1986–87 Donruss/Topps ≤ $30/box, 1989 Upper Deck ≤ $100; pass 1988–92 over $20 and anything priced off an AI quote.

battery-lanterns.title: Battery lanterns
battery-lanterns.full: Battery lanterns (Delta Electric "Powerlite/Buddy", Justrite, Star Headlight & Lantern, Conger, Bright Star, Eveready, Winchester, Burgess, Dietz electric, Railroad conductor lanterns)
battery-lanterns.money: early 1910s–30s Winchester, Delta "Buddy" with tin litho, Burgess, Justrite carbide/electric $50–200.
battery-lanterns.fakes: Fake railroad stampings added to common lanterns occur — look for crisp, period-appropriate stamping fonts. Not widely reproduced otherwise. Modern LED "railroad lanterns" (Barebones Living, Rail-Tek) are sold alongside
battery-lanterns.buy: Pass on unmarked 6-volt lanterns; buy railroad-marked electric lanterns (RR initials stamped on base/handle) and Winchester-marked lanterns at ≤ $20 each.

beaded-fruit-decor.title: Beaded fruit décor
beaded-fruit-decor.full: Beaded fruit décor (1960s–70s pinned/sequin "beaded fruit", wired glass-bead fruit, modern sugared/beaded faux fruit)
beaded-fruit-decor.money: 1960s pinned-bead/sequin fruit $5–15/pc, bowls $30–80 (Terapeak median $22 for lots)
beaded-fruit-decor.fakes: Modern sugared fruit is often listed as "vintage". New Chinese glass-bead grapes exist (lighter, uniform plastic-coated wire).
beaded-fruit-decor.buy: Only pinned-bead/sequin or wired glass-bead vintage fruit in large lots under ~$15 qualify; modern sugared microbead fruit is always a pass.
tells: 1960s–70s pinned/sequin fruit: Styrofoam forms covered with sequins and seed beads held by straight pins — home craft kits and Hong Kong/Japan imports. Visible pin heads in rows; sequin sheen. Popular c. 1940s to mid-1970s; hexagonal beads pinned with steel pi
Wired glass-bead fruit/grapes (Czech, Italian, Japanese, 1920s–60s): grapes and berries of blown or pressed glass beads on wire stems; heavier; true collector item.

Modern sugared / microbead fruit (1990s–now, Pottery Barn, Hobby Lobby, Kirkland's): foam fruit rolled in tiny glass or plastic microbeads giving a frosted, granular "sugared" look; no pins, uniform granular coating, plastic stems.

beaded-jewelry.title: Beaded jewelry
beaded-jewelry.full: Beaded jewelry (Miriam Haskell, Native American beadwork, Czech/Venetian glass, African trade beads, Baar & Beards / Glentex collars, natural-stone strands)
beaded-jewelry.money: signed Miriam Haskell, early Native beadwork, rare trade beads $150–1,500+.
beaded-jewelry.fakes: - Fake Haskell plaques soldered onto unsigned pieces; Haskell's own modern reissues are signed but lower value. - Imported "Native American" beadwork sold as Native-made — a federal crime under the Indian Arts and Crafts
beaded-jewelry.buy: Pass on anything that looks modern and uniform; buy only clear old-material or signed pieces (Haskell plaque, old Venetian/African trade beads, real amber/coral, pre-1960 Native beadwork on hide) where the sold median clears profit ≥ max($50, price).
tells: Miriam Haskell / Haskell-style: clusters of tiny seed pearls and glass beads hand-wired onto a gilt filigree base, "Russian gold" warm finish, ornate box or hook clasp with an oval "MIRIAM HASKELL" plaque.

Native American beadwork: loomed or peyote/brick-stitch seed beads, often on hide or with leather ties; older pieces use smaller, slightly irregular beads, sinew or cotton thread, period colors (greasy yellow, white heart red, Cheyenne pink).

Old Venetian / African trade beads: chunky millefiori (mosaic flower canes), chevron beads (layered star pattern visible at the ends), "white heart" red beads (red over white core), worn uneven beads strung on raffia or cord.

beanie-babies.title: Beanie Babies
beanie-babies.full: Beanie Babies (Ty Inc.: Beanie Babies, Teenie Beanies, Beanie Buddies, Beanie Boos, NFL/MLB/NBA team bears)
beanie-babies.money: specific early tag-generation errors and true rarities (1st/2nd-gen tags on early styles, Royal Blue Peanut, Brown Teddy old-face, Nana, Spot without spot, Employee Bear, Billionaire bears) $50–2,000+
beanie-babies.fakes: Counterfeit Beanies flooded the late 1990s (especially Princess, Peace, Garcia, Erin, Britannia, Royal Blue Peanut, Brown Teddy) – thin tags with wrong fonts, poor stitching, wrong pellet feel. High-value examples need p
beanie-babies.buy: Pass every Beanie Baby lot and every Princess/Diana bear; only consider items with a visible 1st- or 2nd-generation hang tag (single-page tag, no poem) on an early style, or Ty employee/Billionaire bears, at ≤ $10 – and these need verification.
tells: 1st gen (1993): single heart, no poem, "ty" in thin letters, narrow.
2nd gen (1993–94): fat "ty", single page, no poem.
3rd gen (1995): bubble letters "ty", single page.

beer-neon-signs.title: Beer / soda neon signs and neon clocks
beer-neon-signs.full: Beer / soda neon signs and neon clocks (Coors, Budweiser, Miller, Stroh's, Hamm's, Lone Star; Cheerwine/Coke clocks)
beer-neon-signs.fakes: Licensed reproduction neon clocks (Cheerwine, Coke) are the common case. LED "neon" passed off as neon. Modern reproductions of vintage brewery neons exist (general knowledge, verify). Also: Terapeak results for vintage
beer-neon-signs.buy: Only pre-1970s or scarce-regional neon < $40 that is local; pass common 1990s neons > $40 and anything that must ship.

beer-steins.title: Beer steins
beer-steins.full: Beer steins (Mettlach, regimental, Westerwald, character, Budweiser/Anheuser-Busch, tourist)
beer-steins.fakes: Post-1960s regimental reproductions (thin, glossy, no lithophane, "West Germany") $30–80. Reproduction Mettlach-style etched steins and fake castle marks exist (general knowledge, verify): check the form number, date cod
beer-steins.buy: Mettlach castle mark or lithophane regimental visible and < $60; character < $40; pass West Germany relief > $10 each and unverified lots > $50.
tells: Mettlach (Villeroy & Boch): castle/tower mark incised on base with a 4-digit form number (1xxx–3xxx) and a date code; etched or "chromolith" designs with crisp inlaid colour, or PUG (print under glaze) transfer. Etched Mettlach ½ L commonly $150–500 sold; rare

Regimental (Reservist's steins, 1890–1914): porcelain or pottery, tall, pewter lid with a soldier/eagle/cannon finial, named soldier and regiment, often a lithophane in the base. Real ones $300–900 sold; post-1960s reproductions (thin, glossy, no lithophane, "
Westerwald salt-glaze (grey-blue, cobalt and manganese): 18th–19th c. $100–400; 20th c. tourist Westerwald (Gerz, Merkelbach, Marzi & Remy) $15–60.

belt-buckles.title: Belt buckles
belt-buckles.full: Belt buckles (Western sterling: Edward H. Bohlin, Vogt, Clint Orms, Comstock, Montana Silversmiths; Native American Navajo/Zuni/Hopi silver; trophy and rodeo buckles; Hesston NFR; Award Design Medals, Tiffany/Bergamot, Lewis Buckle, Siskiyou, Spec-Cast pewter advertising; military and fraternal)
belt-buckles.money: Bohlin, Clint Orms, gold-overlay trophy and old Navajo cast-silver $500–5,000+.
belt-buckles.fakes: Fake Civil War buckles (dug-look repros), fake Navajo (Asian-made "Native style" stamped sterling and stabilized/block turquoise), "sterling" stamps on nickel silver, Bohlin marks on unrelated buckles. High-value Native
belt-buckles.buy: Buy only sterling-marked (".925", "Sterling", maker hallmark) Western or Native buckles, early Hesston NFR (1974–76) or named trophy buckles at ≤ 1/3 sold median; pass pewter advertising/event buckles over $10.
tells: Trophy buckles: oval, engraved event/year/name, silver overlay or sterling with gold figures, made by Montana Silversmiths (low), Gist, Comstock, Clint Orms, Vogt (high).
Navajo/Zuni: hand-stamped sterling, cast silver ("ketoh"-style), inlay or petit point turquoise; artist hallmarks on the back.
Back stamps: maker, copyright year, metal ("Solid brass", "Pewter", "Sterling", ".925", "Silver overlay", "German silver/nickel silver" – NOT silver), issue numbers ("12 of 500").

bench-vises.title: Bench vises
bench-vises.full: Bench vises (Wilton bullet, Columbian, Prentiss, Reed, Charles Parker)
bench-vises.fakes: China-made Wilton-branded vises (later production) – check casting text. Listing/photo mismatches occur (a "Wilton" title with a Sears vise in the photo, as seen in sweep).
bench-vises.buy: Real Wilton bullet/Parker/Prentiss/Versa-Vise ≤ $90, 5"+ bullet ≤ $150; pass Sears/import castings and anything ≥ 50% of sold.

big-box-pc-games.title: Big-box PC / computer games
big-box-pc-games.full: Big-box PC / computer games (1980s–90s Sierra, LucasArts, Infocom, Origin)
big-box-pc-games.money: sealed early Sierra/Infocom, Akalabeth, Ultima I $500–5,000+.
big-box-pc-games.fakes: Resealed boxes (fake shrink) and reproduction feelies/manuals exist; also later re-releases and anthology packs (general knowledge, verify). Graded sealed games carry their own authentication risk.
big-box-pc-games.buy: 1980s Sierra/Infocom/Origin complete ≤ $40, lots of 5+ boxed games ≤ $50; pass single titles priced ≥ $100 and CD re-releases.

big-eye-art-prints.title: Big-eye art prints
big-eye-art-prints.full: Big-eye art prints (Margaret/Walter Keane, Lee, Gig, Eden, Maio, Ozz Franca, Igor Pantuhoff, Medeiros, Dallas Simpson and unsigned "big eyes" kitsch)
big-eye-art-prints.money: original oil paintings by the named big-eye painters $200–5,000+ (Margaret Keane originals far more).
big-eye-art-prints.fakes: - Keane prints are reprinted constantly; modern posters and giclées sold as "vintage" are common. - Forged "KEANE" signatures on generic big-eye paintings are a known problem; any Keane "original" or signed edition needs
big-eye-art-prints.buy: Pass on all printed big-eye art (median ~$25); buy only a probable ORIGINAL oil/acrylic on canvas or board (raised paint, canvas weave, stretcher bars) by a named big-eye painter at ≤ $150 and ≤ 30% of estimated value, and only if it fits the passenger seat.
tells: Pencil-signed limited editions: signature in graphite and an edition number (e.g., 87/295) in the margin; Keane later editions come with Keane Eyes Gallery certificates.

1950s–70s "big eyes" kitsch: children (waifs in rags, clowns, ballerinas, harlequins), women, cats, dogs and owls with enormous, often tear-filled eyes. Huge mail-order and department-store decorator category 1960–1975; revived by the 2014 film *Big Eyes*.

The overwhelming majority are offset lithographs: smooth, uniform surface, rosette dot pattern under a loupe, printed signature in the lower corner. Many were glued to textured "canvas-look" board with fake brush ridges, then put in walnut/oak or gold-lip fram

bit-braces-and-auger-bits.title: Bit braces and auger bits
bit-braces-and-auger-bits.full: Bit braces and auger bits (Stanley, Millers Falls, Fray, Spofford, Peck Stow & Wilcox, Barber, North Bros. Yankee, Irwin, Russell Jennings, Ridgely, Greenlee)
bit-braces-and-auger-bits.fakes: Essentially none on the low end. Some modern reproductions of Sheffield framed braces exist; newer imported braces (India/Pakistan) with bright plating are common.
bit-braces-and-auger-bits.buy: Buy only boxed complete auger sets ≤ $15 or patent-dated/pre-1900 braces ≤ $25 each; common 20th-century braces and loose bits are below Dylan's $50 profit floor.
tells: Older braces (pre-1900) have rosewood/ebony heads with ivory or brass rings, plain (non-ratchet) chucks, patent dates on the chuck shell, and nickel plating worn to iron.
20th-century braces have a stamped steel frame, ratchet ring, painted or varnished beech handles, sweep size stamped (8", 10", 12", 14").
Bit sets: Russell Jennings pattern (double twist), Irwin (solid center), Stanley/Ridgely, often in a canvas roll or wooden/metal index box numbered 4–16 (sixteenths of an inch).

black-americana.title: Black Americana collectibles
black-americana.full: Black Americana collectibles (Aunt Jemima / Quaker Oats, Mosaic Tile Co., Pearl China, National Silver, F&F Mold & Die, Weller, handmade cloth dolls)
black-americana.money: pre-1900 folk dolls, early advertising, documented historical items $500–5,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
black-americana.fakes: This category is saturated with reproductions — probably the single biggest risk. Cast-iron banks, F&F plastic, Mosaic Tile jars, "antique" signs, and Leo Moss dolls are all reproduced, many from the 1980s–2000s and sold
black-americana.buy: Pass on 1970s–90s craft dolls and anything that might be a reproduction; only buy marked period pieces (Mosaic Tile, Pearl China, F&F with mold marks) priced well under the ladder.

blenko-glass.title: Blenko glass
blenko-glass.full: Blenko glass (Blenko Glass Co., Milton WV, 1893/1921–present; designers Winslow Anderson, Wayne Husted, Joel Philip Myers, John Nickerson, Don Shepherd, Hank Adams, Richard Blenko)
blenko-glass.money: rare designer forms (Husted/Anderson large decanters, Myers sculptures, rare colours) $250–1,500.
blenko-glass.fakes: - Blenko reissues classic designs (e.g., 384 bottle, Husted decanters in new colours). Dated signatures (e.g., "Blenko 2000") identify modern pieces (lower value).
blenko-glass.buy: Buy 1950s–70s large designer decanters, tall floor vases (18"+) and rare colours at ≤ $50; pass on 384 water bottles and small modern pieces.
tells: Hand-blown, mouth-shaped art glass in saturated colours (tangerine, sea green, jonquil, olive, cobalt, amethyst, ruby). Bubbles (seeds), pontil scars (rough or ground), slight asymmetry.
Most pieces are unmarked; 1959–61 pieces have acid-etched "Blenko" script; foil/paper labels (often lost); recent pieces signed with year.
Signature forms: tall floor vases (bottle shapes), decanters with oversized flame/teardrop stoppers, the #384 double-spout water bottle (since 1960s, still made), pinched and bent-neck decanters.

block-and-tackle-pulleys.title: Block and tackle pulleys
block-and-tackle-pulleys.full: Block and tackle pulleys (wooden ship blocks, barn and hay-trolley pulleys, cast-iron pulleys; Boston & Lockport, Merriman, Myers, Louden, Stanley, unmarked)
block-and-tackle-pulleys.money: hay trolleys and figural pieces $50–200 (general knowledge, verify).
block-and-tackle-pulleys.fakes: Decorative reproduction "nautical" blocks (India-made, brass/dark stained) are common. They look too uniform and have modern bolts. - Repros are often sold in sets with matched sizes and identical wood colour. They have
block-and-tackle-pulleys.buy: Buy only large (8"+) wooden double/triple blocks or marked hay trolleys at ≤ 30% of sold; pass on small single pulleys.
tells: Single wood blocks (one sheave), double/triple blocks (more value).
Cast-iron pulleys with a single eye — common, cheaper.
Hay trolleys (Louden, Myers, Starline) — cast iron, run along barn rails.

blue-mountain-pottery.title: Blue Mountain Pottery
blue-mountain-pottery.full: Blue Mountain Pottery (Collingwood, Ontario, Canada, 1953–2004; "BMP"; later "Blue Mountain Collection")
blue-mountain-pottery.money: a complete Noah's Ark set (ark plus 13 figures) reportedly sold for $7,000.
blue-mountain-pottery.fakes: Not faked. Other Canadian potteries (Canuck, Evangeline, Royal Canadian Art Pottery) and Japanese imports have similar drip glazes. Japanese pieces usually have a white or buff body and a foil "Japan" sticker. Unmarked d
blue-mountain-pottery.buy: Pass on small dinnerware pieces; buy large animal figures, tall vases or rare-glaze pieces under ~$25.
tells: Common shapes: stylised animals, swans, fish, tall bottle vases, jugs, and cream and sugar sets.

Marks: impressed or moulded "BMP Canada" (a "BMP" logo) on the underside, or a paper label/hang tag (later "The Blue Mountain Collection, Collingwood, Ontario"). Many pieces lost their labels and are unmarked, so identification is then by glaze, form and red-c
In a photo: tall elongated swans with S-necks, leaping dolphins on waves, long-neck cats, ewers and bottle vases, all with a vertical streaked glossy glaze, green over black being the classic.

blue-willow-china.title: Blue Willow china
blue-willow-china.full: Blue Willow china (Spode, Wedgwood, Royal Doulton/Booths, Buffalo Pottery, Johnson Bros, Churchill, Sadler, Homer Laughlin, Royal China, Japanese export)
blue-willow-china.money: early pearlware/large platters/rare forms $200–1,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
blue-willow-china.fakes: Modern Chinese "Willow" with fake old marks; Churchill and Johnson Bros still produce Willow. "Spode" Blue Willow is still made, and modern backstamps say Spode with a date.
blue-willow-china.buy: Only buy 19th-century pieces (pearlware, unmarked early Staffordshire, big well-drainers/platters), Gaudy Willow, or rare forms; pass on teapots and dinnerware from 1950 on.

bobbleheads.title: Bobbleheads
bobbleheads.full: Bobbleheads (1960s Japanese papier-mâché nodders; Sports Specialties; Lego-era Alexander Global; Toy Site / BD&A Rudolph & holiday; Funko Wacky Wobblers; MLB stadium giveaways; Royal Bobbles)
bobbleheads.money: 1960s Japanese papier-mâché sports nodders (MLB/NFL "Sports Specialties") $75–400, rare teams/players and Beatles/character 1960s $300–2,000.
bobbleheads.fakes: 1960s nodder repros (2000s Japan-style) exist; repro decals. Retro-style modern reissues are usually resin and heavier, with printed (not hand-painted) detail and a copyright/licence line under the base (general knowledg
bobbleheads.buy: Buy 1960s Japanese papier-mâché/composition nodders (gold/colored base, "Japan" sticker) at ≤ 1/3 resale; pass on 2000s licensed holiday/SGA bobbleheads unless a complete set or a hot player.

bohemian-glass.title: Bohemian glass
bohemian-glass.full: Bohemian glass (Moser, Egermann, Harrach, Loetz, "Bohemia Crystal" / Crystalex, Czech ruby flash and cut-to-clear)
bohemian-glass.money: signed Moser, 19th-c. enamelled Harrach, Loetz/Kralik art glass $150–2,000+.
bohemian-glass.fakes: - Chinese "Loetz-style" iridescent glass (2000s) with fake "Loetz Austria" signatures — scratchy engraving signature, too-even iridescence. - Fake "Moser" acid stamps added to unsigned glass. - Ruby flash deer-and-castle
bohemian-glass.buy: Buy only acid-signed Moser, Loetz-type iridescent art glass, or 19th-c. enamelled/gilt Bohemian at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on foil-label cut crystal and souvenir ruby flash unless ≤ $15.
tells: Art glass (1870s–1930s): Moser (Karlovy Vary) heavily enamelled and gilt pieces, faceted amethyst/Alexandrite "Royal" glass; Loetz/Lötz Witwe (Klostermühle) iridescent Art Nouveau; Harrach (Nový Svět) enamelled and gilt; Kralik, Pallme-König, Rindskopf iridesc

Post-war export crystal (1950s–present): cut or pressed lead crystal (24% PbO) bowls, vases, ashtrays, card-suit dishes, sold with a gold or silver foil label "Bohemia Crystal / Hand Cut / Lead Crystal 24% PbO / Czech Republic (or Czechoslovakia)". Diamond-and

Flash / stain and engraving (1850s–1980s): clear glass coated with a thin ruby (red), amber, blue or green layer, then wheel-engraved through to clear — deer in forest, castles, spa towns, flowers and vines. Bedside "tumble-ups" (carafe with an upturned tumble

book-photo-and-paper-ephemera-marks.title: Book, photograph and paper-ephemera marks — reading guide
book-photo-and-paper-ephemera-marks.full: Book, photograph and paper-ephemera marks — reading guide (first-edition statements and number lines by publisher: Scribner, Random House, Knopf, Harper, Doubleday, Little Brown, Viking; book-club tells; dust-jacket points; inscriptions and ex-library marks; CDV tax stamps, card mounts, daguerreotype plate hallmarks; postcard backs and RPPC stamp boxes; map plate and fold marks; revenue stamps, stock certificates and poster printer imprints)
book-photo-and-paper-ephemera-marks.money: A copyright-page line or a back-of-card stamp is usually the whole value: the same title runs $5–20 as a book-club or later printing and $100–180,000 as a first-state first in a first-issue jacket
book-photo-and-paper-ephemera-marks.fakes: - **Facsimile dust jackets** (Gatsby, Hobbit, Catcher, Hemingway) put on firsts or BCEs — usually marked "facsimile" on the flap but sometimes trimmed off (general knowledge, verify). - **Married jackets** — a first-issu
book-photo-and-paper-ephemera-marks.buy: Never buy a "first edition" without a copyright-page photo and a jacket-flap photo; check the BCE tells first (no flap price, blind dot, gutter code); for photos and postcards read the back before the front; pay only for marks you can read in the photos.
tells: Books: copyright page (verso of the title page) — edition statement, number line, printing codes; title page — date; last page or gutter — Doubleday gutter codes, Harper number lines (1962–75); back board — BCE blind dot or square, lower right corner; jacket f
Card photographs: back of the mount — tax stamp, photographer imprint; front — mount colour, border lines, corners, imprint under the image.
Cased images: the plate hallmark is on the image side at a corner, hidden under the brass mat and preserver — visible only if the packet is opened (do not ask a casual seller to open it).

bookends.title: Bookends , K&O, Borghese, Dodge, Marion Bronze, Galvano; stone/onyx/petrified wood; Art Deco spelter)
bookends.full: Bookends (Frankart, Roycroft, Bradley & Hubbard, Judd, Armor Bronze, Pompeian Bronze, Jennings Bros (JB), K&O, Borghese, Dodge, Marion Bronze, Galvano; stone/onyx/petrified wood; Art Deco spelter)
bookends.fakes: - Frankart reproductions (1980s on) are cast resin or lighter metal with crude detail; real Frankart mark is stamped into the metal, not cast in raised letters on resin. - Cast-iron repros (Scotties, ships, Indian heads)
bookends.buy: Only pairs with a maker mark (Frankart, Roycroft orb-and-cross, B&H, Tiffany Studios, Gorham) or obvious solid bronze; buy at ≤ 1/3 of conservative resale; pass on stone, onyx, resin, Borghese chalkware and singles.
tells: Solid bronze: heavy, uniform patina, crisp chasing, maker stamp (Tiffany Studios NEW YORK + number, Gorham Co Founders, Roman Bronze Works). Rare on Craigslist.

Cast iron (1900s–1930s): painted or plated (Judd, Bradley & Hubbard, Hubley, Connecticut Foundry). Ships, Scottie dogs, Lincoln, Indian chiefs, galleons, owls, parrots. Rough sand-cast back, often hollow back with an open cavity.

Bronze-clad / "bronzed" (1910s–30s): Armor Bronze, Pompeian Bronze, Marion Bronze, Galvano: thin bronze electroplated over a plaster or cast-iron core, usually felted base with a paper/foil label or stamp. Rubbed edges show white plaster or dark iron.

bookshelf-speakers.title: Bookshelf speakers
bookshelf-speakers.full: Bookshelf speakers (vintage hi-fi: AR, KLH, Advent, Bose 901/301, JBL, Klipsch, Boston Acoustics, Polk, Infinity, ADS, Rogers/Harbeth LS3/5A, KEF, B&W, Technics, Pioneer, Sony, Realistic Minimus)
bookshelf-speakers.fakes: Unauthorized LS3/5A clones and kit versions; otherwise low. - LS3/5A has also been reissued by modern makers (e.g. Falcon Acoustics, Stirling, Rogers reissues); these are new speakers and should be sold as such (Falcon r
bookshelf-speakers.buy: Pass rack-system/home-theater sets; buy only AR, KLH, Advent, JBL, KEF, B&W, Rogers/LS3/5A small monitors tested on video ≤ 1/3 comps.
tells: LS3/5A: a very small (about shoebox-size) sealed box with a recessed front baffle, felt strips around the drivers and a grille; the back label names the licensee and carries the BBC LS3/5A designation (Stereophile).

Where the marks are: a paper or metal label on the back (maker, model, impedance, serial); badges on the grille; AR has an AR emblem on the grille and, on 1970s models, arrows on the back marking level-control settings (AR-2ax page).
Realistic Minimus-7: a die-cast aluminium cabinet with a removable metal grille, about 180 × 113 × 110 mm and 2.03 kg each, made in Japan for Tandy/Radio Shack from c. 1977 (zstereo).

boomboxes.title: Boomboxes
boomboxes.full: Boomboxes (JVC, Sharp, Panasonic, Sony, Conion/Clairtone, Lasonic, Crown, Hitachi, Aiwa, Sanyo, Marantz, GE, Realistic)
boomboxes.money: "big" 80s collector models (JVC RC-M90, Sharp GF-777, Conion C-100F, Lasonic TRC-931, Panasonic RX-7700, Sanyo M-X920) $300–2,000+ working.
boomboxes.fakes: Modern retro-styled reissues (e.g., Lasonic i931, 2010s) and retro-look Chinese units — check model numbers, country of manufacture and USB/Bluetooth inputs.
boomboxes.buy: Only 1980s full-size collector models with seller video playing tape and radio, at ≤ $150; pass on 1990s CD units and anything untested.

boss-compact-pedals.title: Boss compact pedals
boss-compact-pedals.full: Boss compact pedals (and other common used stompboxes)
boss-compact-pedals.fakes: Boss Waza Craft reissues (e.g. DM-2W, SD-1W, CE-2W) are modern and distinct from originals (general knowledge, verify). Fake Japan labels and housing swaps (Japan shell with later board) exist – check the board and label
boss-compact-pedals.buy: MIJ CE-2/OD-1/DM-2/silver-screw SD-1 ≤ $70, VB-2/DC-2 ≤ $150, boutique ≤ 40% of Reverb used; pass Taiwan-era and shells.

bossons-chalkware-heads.title: Bossons chalkware heads
bossons-chalkware-heads.full: Bossons chalkware heads (W.H. Bossons Ltd, Congleton, England; Fraser Art; Legend Products; "Bossons-style" imitators)
bossons-chalkware-heads.money: rare early/limited heads and Fraser Art pieces $60–200+
bossons-chalkware-heads.fakes: No modern fakes of note, but "Bossons-style" heads are sold as Bossons ($20–22 sales of "Bossons-style/like" in comps). Always check the back stamp.
bossons-chalkware-heads.buy: Buy clean Bossons lots at ≤ $3 per head (seller-supplied back-stamp photo); sell singly or in themed pairs. Pass on single common heads.

bottle-cappers-and-corkers.title: Bottle cappers and corkers
bottle-cappers-and-corkers.full: Bottle cappers and corkers (Crown-cap levers, Kork-N-Seal, Italian floor corkers, cast-iron home-brew cappers, Prohibition-era tools, bar-mounted re-corkers)
bottle-cappers-and-corkers.money: best 19th-c. corking machines to ~$350 (£360 at Bonhams in 2003 against a £100–200 estimate) (general knowledge, verify)
bottle-cappers-and-corkers.fakes: Not faked; modern working tools are mislabeled "vintage". Modern cast-iron décor corkers (e.g. Pottery Barn/East Elm "Vintners", seen at $250 on Terapeak) are not antiques.
bottle-cappers-and-corkers.buy: Pass on generic cappers; buy only ornate or marked early bench corkers ≤ $20 with resale ≥ $100.
tells: Bench lever crown cappers (1910s–1930s) — cast-iron upright on a flat base with mounting holes, a long arm working a toothed rack or sprocket-and-cam, and a bell (crowning die) at the bottom of the plunger. Example: Ramsey Bros. Mfg. Co., Toledo, Ohio, about 1
Hand (two-handled) cappers — butterfly-style cast cappers whose arms open to ~15"; e.g. "COMSTOCK BOLTON ~ KANSAS CITY, MO. ~ PATENT PENDING", patent December 21, 1920.
Flat-base hinged cappers — e.g. "Trade Mark Climax, Patented, Made in U.S.A." (Detroit Historical Society): capping head on a sliding hinge lowered by a horizontal lever.

bottle-jar-and-pressed-glass-marks.title: Bottle, jar and pressed-glass marks — reading guide
bottle-jar-and-pressed-glass-marks.full: Bottle, jar and pressed-glass marks — reading guide (pontils, mould seams, applied lips, Owens-Illinois date codes, Hazel-Atlas H-over-A, Anchor Hocking anchor, "Federal Law Forbids", Duraglas, Ball logo eras, Mason's Patent 1858, sun-coloured amethyst, uranium/vaseline UV, Fenton/Northwood/Imperial/Westmoreland/L.E. Smith/Heisey marks, Depression-glass repro tells, Fire-King and McKee, Baccarat/Clichy/St Louis/Perthshire canes, insulator embossing and CD numbers)
bottle-jar-and-pressed-glass-marks.money: The base and the seam decide whether a bottle or jar is a $3–20 machine-made common or a $50–600+ hand-finished pre-1900 piece (Terapeak sold: cobalt figural poison asks ~$100, threadless insulators $85 median against $21.50 for cobalt Hemingray). Logos split reissues from originals in pressed and c
bottle-jar-and-pressed-glass-marks.fakes: - Repro **bitters, flasks and figural bottles** (Clevenger, Wheaton 1970s commemoratives, Taiwanese): too-crisp embossing, machine glass and fake pontils (general knowledge, verify). - **Irradiated SCA**: deep, even purp
bottle-jar-and-pressed-glass-marks.buy: Read the base, the seam and the logo before the title. Buy pre-1900 hand-finished bottles, true off-colour jars, logo-confirmed old carnival or Heisey, genuine Fire-King or McKee Jadeite, and signed or dated canes at ≤ 30% of the tier's sold median. Pass on se

bowl-back-mandolins.title: Bowl-back mandolins
bowl-back-mandolins.full: Bowl-back ("tater bug") mandolins (Lyon & Healy/Washburn, Martin, Vega, Bacon, Vinaccia, Calace, Embergher)
bowl-back-mandolins.fakes: No significant fakes. Labels can be missing or replaced; Martin is confirmed by the headstock stamp, not a label (general knowledge, verify).
bowl-back-mandolins.buy: Labeled L&H/Washburn/Vega/Bacon < $60 with straight neck; any Martin stamp < $200; pass unlabeled, $100+, or separated ribs.

bowling-collectibles.title: Bowling collectibles
bowling-collectibles.full: Bowling collectibles (Brunswick, AMF, Ebonite, Columbia 300, Hammer, Dexter, Linds, Etonic; vintage bowling shoes, shirts, pins, bags, balls, trophies)
bowling-collectibles.money: chain-stitch 1950s gabardine/rayon shirts (King Louie, Hilton, Nat Nast, Swing-ster) $40–250
bowling-collectibles.fakes: Modern retro bowling shirts (Charlie Sheen, Steady, Hawaiian-cut "retro" from 1990s–2000s) – screen print instead of chain stitch, polyester, modern care labels. "Vintage-style" bowling shoes from fashion brands (Gola, P
bowling-collectibles.buy: Pass ordinary used bowling shoes and modern shirts; buy only 1950s–60s chain-stitched rayon/gabardine shirts with embroidered business names, NOS boxed vintage shoes in common sizes, or unusual advertising/mid-century bags at ≤ 30% of the ladder.
tells: Shirts: 1950s camp-collar, gabardine/rayon, chain-stitch embroidered names, union labels; makers King Louie, Hilton, Nat Nast, Swing-ster, Wolverine, Classic.

Shoes: lace-to-toe derby/blucher style, smooth leather, one slide sole (felt/microfibre leather) and one braking heel; rental shoes have size numbers on heel and two-/three-colour panels. Vintage (1950s–80s) have leather uppers and soles, Goodyear welt or stit
Bags: 1950s–60s round "bowler" vinyl bags with Brunswick/AMF logos, two-tone; 1970s leather.

boy-band-memorabilia.title: Boy band memorabilia
boy-band-memorabilia.full: Boy band memorabilia ('N Sync, Backstreet Boys, New Kids on the Block, 98 Degrees, Hanson, Jonas Brothers, One Direction)
boy-band-memorabilia.money: signed or tour-exclusive items $100–500 (general knowledge, verify)
boy-band-memorabilia.fakes: Unauthorized dolls and bootleg tees; signatures widely faked.
boy-band-memorabilia.buy: Buy only boxed complete sets or bulk lots priced ≤ 1/4 of summed sold value; loose single items never pay.

brass-band-instruments.title: Brass band instruments
brass-band-instruments.full: Brass band instruments (Olds, Conn, King, Holton, Bach, Martin, Getzen, Reynolds, Selmer/Bundy, Yamaha)
brass-band-instruments.money: rare (Olds Mendez, Martin Committee pre-1960, Conn 38B/Coprion, sterling bells) $800–3,000 (general knowledge, verify)
brass-band-instruments.fakes: Not much faking; the issue is mis-labelled model names (sellers call an Ambassador "Olds Super") and Asian "stencil" horns engraved to look like Bach. Chinese horns engraved "Bach Stradivarius" exist — tell is wrong seri
brass-band-instruments.buy: Buy only pro-line US horns (Olds Super/Recording/Special, Bach Strad, Martin Committee, King Silver Flair/Liberty, Conn Constellation/Connstellation) with free valves/slides at ≤ 25% of sold; student horns only if ≤ $25 and playable.

brass-decor.title: Brass decor
brass-decor.full: Brass decor (Indian/Korean/Taiwanese import brass, Dolbi Cashier, Virginia Metalcrafters, Sarreid, Chapman, Frederick Cooper, English pressed-brass plaques)
brass-decor.fakes: - Brass is a reproduction-heavy category generally: "antique" bells, ship instruments, sextants, telescopes and spyglasses with fake maker names are made in India today. - Fake Dolbi Cashier attributions are common in ti
brass-decor.buy: Pass on generic brass at any price above ~$5 a piece; only buy signed Dolbi Cashier/Sarreid/Maitland-Smith/Chapman-class pieces or large stylised MCM sculpture where sold median clears profit ≥ max($50, price).
tells: Decorative brass made 1950s–1990s for gift shops and department stores: animal figurines (elephants with trunk up, unicorns, horses, ducks, swans, cats), bells, candlesticks, planters/baskets, goblets, trays, key racks, wall pieces and repoussé (hammered/embos
Most is hollow or thin sand-cast brass from India, Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong, polished and lacquered. Solid cast pieces are heavy for their size; stamped sheet brass is light and rings.
English pressed-brass wall plates and plaques (tavern scenes after Teniers, galleons, coaching scenes) were mass-produced 1950s–70s as souvenirs.

breast-drills.title: Breast drills and hand drills
breast-drills.full: Breast drills and hand drills (Millers Falls, Goodell-Pratt, Stanley, Yankee)
breast-drills.fakes: None known. Later reissues/budget versions of the same model numbers exist (general knowledge, verify).

breweriana.title: Breweriana
breweriana.full: Breweriana (beer advertising: signs, trays, coasters, tap knobs, lighted signs, steins, cans; Schlitz, Hamm's, Olympia, Blatz, Pabst, Budweiser, Miller, Falstaff, regional brewers)
breweriana.money: rare regional and pre-Pro items $500–5,000+ (general knowledge, verify).
breweriana.fakes: Reproduction tin signs ("Ande Rooney" and many others) are common and often sold as vintage. Reproduction trays exist. Breweries reissue retro designs. - Fake signs show deliberate edge-only chips, orange-red rust, new-l
breweriana.buy: Buy pre-1960 regional brewery tin, tin-over-cardboard (TOC), reverse-glass or motion signs and ball tap knobs at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on national-brand 1970s+ promos, coaster sets and anything electrical untested.
tells: Coaster sets / bar-ware: 1970s plastic giveaways, like a bottle-shaped holder of six cork coasters (the example, Schlitz).
Signs: tin, TOC, reverse-painted glass, lighted (plastic bubble, "motion" signs with rotating scenes like Hamm's bear).
Trays: lithographed tin, pre-Prohibition (before 1920) trays are prized.

british-and-irish-hallmarks.title: British and Irish hallmarks
british-and-irish-hallmarks.full: British and Irish hallmarks (London, Birmingham, Sheffield, Chester, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Dublin assay offices; Hester Bateman, Paul Storr, Omar Ramsden, Liberty & Co Cymric / Archibald Knox, Charles Horner, Murrle Bennett, Arts & Crafts guilds)
british-and-irish-hallmarks.fakes: - **Pseudo-hallmarks** on plate (above) are the commonest false positive. - **Forged hallmarks** (cast copies, transposed marks) exist on Georgian silver and are a specialist problem; at our price levels the bigger risk
british-and-irish-hallmarks.buy: The edge is unrecognised marks: buy any piece showing a lion passant, a crown with 9/15/18/22 or 375/625/750/916, or a town mark plus date letter at or below melt; pay a maker premium only from a sharp photo of the sponsor's mark; EPNS, EP, EPBM, A1, "Sheffiel
tells: Lion passant (walking lion, facing left, one paw raised) = sterling 925. In England since 1544 (general knowledge, verify). The lion was in a shaped shield; from 1999 it is optional when a millesimal "925" is struck (general knowledge, verify). On pre-1844 Eng

Britannia (seated figure of Britannia) = 958 silver. Compulsory 1697–1720, optional afterward (925-1000.com). Struck with a lion's head erased (a lion's head in profile, ragged neck) in place of the London leopard (general knowledge, verify). Britannia standar

Scotland: Edinburgh used a thistle as the standard mark (from 1759, general knowledge, verify) and a lion rampant from 1975 (925-1000.com). Glasgow used a lion rampant (from 1819, general knowledge, verify).

buck-knives.title: Buck knives – 110 Folding Hunter, 112 Ranger and fixed blades
buck-knives.full: Buck knives – 110 Folding Hunter, 112 Ranger and fixed blades (Buck Knives Inc., San Diego/El Cajon CA 1945–2005, Post Falls ID 2005–)
buck-knives.money: early 1960s, boxed, or rare variants (Buck 110 "Ranger" prototypes, custom shop, Hoyt Buck fixed blades) $200–1,000+.
buck-knives.fakes: Buck reissues: "110 50th anniversary", limited editions with early-style marks; Chinese counterfeits of 110 with poor stamping, aluminium-look bolsters. Check stamp crispness.
buck-knives.buy: Buy 110/112 only if the tang stamp shows pre-1986 multi-line "BUCK/U.S.A." marks, or for boxed early knives, at ≤ 40% of tier price; date-coded modern Bucks are pass above ~$15.

buffalo-pottery.title: Buffalo Pottery
buffalo-pottery.full: Buffalo Pottery (Buffalo Pottery Co., Buffalo NY; Deldare, Emerald Deldare, Abino, Blue Willow, commemorative/"Multi-color" jugs)
buffalo-pottery.fakes: Deldare has some decorator/fake pieces (an old blank decorated later); the 1923–25 Deldare revival is real but valued slightly lower. Few outright reproductions of the jugs exist. Watch for "Buffalo" Christmas plates bei
buffalo-pottery.buy: Buy only perfect (no cracks) Deldare/Emerald Deldare/Abino or rare named jugs at ≤ 1/3 of resale; cracked or common pieces = pass.

byers-carolers.title: Byers' Choice Carolers and look-alike caroler figures/ornaments
byers-carolers.full: Byers' Choice Carolers and look-alike caroler figures/ornaments (Byers' Choice Ltd., Chalfont PA, 1978–; also Annalee, Possible Dreams Clothtique, Department 56, flat painted tin ornaments)
byers-carolers.money: rare retired/limited pieces and early "Cries of London" $80–250 (general knowledge, verify
byers-carolers.fakes: No real forgery market; many inexpensive look-alikes. Byers' continues to make similar figures each year, so date the base.
byers-carolers.buy: Buy only true Byers' (signed bottom tag, sculpted clay faces — the first run said papier-mâché — wire armature) in lots at ≤ $8 each, or early/retired Cries of London under ~$30 (Terapeak median $28.73 makes even that marginal; prefer Halloween/seasonal pieces
tells: Byers' Choice carolers (10–13" tall) have hand-painted sculpted heads with characteristic round "O" singing mouths, wire armature bodies with fabric costumes, a wooden or felt base with Byers' signature/date on the bottom, and a hang tag.

Construction per the maker: the body is tissue paper wrapped around a bent wire skeleton; heads are cast by filling moulds with clay, then nostrils and lips are added and the face hand-painted; fabric is cut to Joyce Byers' patterns (Wikipedia). Joyce sculpts
Base: since 1986 figures reportedly have a green felt ring and a dated gold seal on the bottom, and each is signed by a member of the Byers family (blog source; verify against a photographed base).

california-art-pottery.title: California art pottery
california-art-pottery.full: California art pottery (Metlox Romanelli, Bauer, Catalina, Brayton Laguna, Hedi Schoop, Kay Finch)
california-art-pottery.fakes: Bauer lookalikes (Pacific, Garden City) and later Bauer reissues (the brand revived in the late 1990s) exist (general knowledge, verify). Catalina Pottery (GMB, post-1937) sold as Catalina Island. Unmarked nude vases fro
california-art-pottery.buy: Marked Romanelli/Catalina Island/Bauer large forms ≤ 35% of sold; unmarked "nude lady vase" ≤ $40 (check base); pass named-and-priced ≥ 60% of sold.

california-pottery-ringware.title: California pottery ringware
california-pottery-ringware.full: California pottery ringware (Bauer, Pacific, Garden City)
california-pottery-ringware.money: black/burgundy, full nesting sets and early inside-ring bowls $150–400.
california-pottery-ringware.fakes: Bauer Pottery Company of Los Angeles reissued ringware shapes in the 2000s (newer, often marked differently and with crisper, lighter bodies) (general knowledge, verify). Modern "Fiesta" and generic ringed bowls get mis-
california-pottery-ringware.buy: Buy a #9/#12 ringware bowl in a good colour under $25 or two+ bowls under $40 – but sold data (median $38) means only scarce colours or multi-bowl lots really clear the profit rule; pass chipped or anything already titled "Bauer" at $50+.

camera-speedlights.title: Camera speedlights / flashes
camera-speedlights.fakes: Counterfeit Canon/Nikon-branded flashes exist in small numbers, and third-party look-alikes are sometimes mis-titled (general knowledge, verify). Check fonts, serial label and the menu system.
camera-speedlights.buy: Buy pro Nikon/Canon flashes (SB-700/800/910, 580EX II, 600EX-RT) at ≤ $40 or SB-5000/600EX II at ≤ $90; pass anything priced ≥ 50% of eBay sold.

camera-tripods.title: Camera tripods & gimbals
camera-tripods.fakes: Counterfeit "Gitzo" and "Manfrotto" carbon tripods and clone heads are sold on AliExpress/eBay (general knowledge, verify). Check fonts, serials and casting quality.
camera-tripods.buy: Buy Gitzo/RRS/Sachtler under $100 or Manfrotto carbon + head under $80; pass aluminium Manfrotto at $40+ and anything priced at market.

camping-gear.title: Vintage camping gear
camping-gear.full: Vintage camping gear (Coleman, Primus, Svea/Optimus, Sigg, Kelty, Gerry, Eddie Bauer, Woods, Holubar, Sierra Designs, Frostline, Boy Scout/BSA, Greatland, Ozark Trail, Wenzel)
camping-gear.money: rare Coleman (pre-1930 lanterns, 1940s military, colour variants) $150–600.
camping-gear.fakes: Coleman reissued "vintage" anniversary lanterns (e.g. 2000s 100th anniversary). Reproduction decals. Chinese Svea 123 copies exist. Not a big fake problem otherwise.
camping-gear.buy: Pass all modern big-box camping gear (Greatland/Ozark Trail/Coleman synthetic bags) and bulky tents; buy only dated Coleman lanterns/stoves (pre-1975, complete), brass Svea/Optimus/Primus stoves, and 1960s–70s down gear from heritage makers at ≤ 30% of the lad
tells: Coleman lanterns/stoves: green (stoves) or red/green/silver lanterns; Coleman stamps a month/year date code on the base (e.g. "5 72" = May 1972) from 1920s on. Single-mantle 200A (red, 1950s–), 228, 220E/F, 242C. Pre-war nickel or brass founts.

Modern big-box: Greatland (Walmart/Target private label, 2010s, "Born to Roam" tagline with stylised "G" mountain triangle), Ozark Trail (Walmart), Coleman synthetic rectangular bags, Wenzel – polyester fill, printed labels, Chinese manufacture. pid 7971219129
Backpacking stoves: Svea 123 (Sweden, brass, 1955–), Optimus 8R/111, Primus (brass, pumped kerosene). Brass with tins.

candle-holders.title: Candle holders and candlesticks
candle-holders.full: Candle holders and candlesticks (Jarvie, Roycroft, Stickley, Georg Jensen, Dansk/Jens Quistgaard, Baldwin, Virginia Metalcrafters, Fostoria/Heisey/Cambridge, Kosta Boda, Holmegaard, Partylite, import decor)
candle-holders.money: Arts & Crafts hand-hammered (Jarvie, Roycroft, Stickley) and Georg Jensen silver $300–5,000+.
candle-holders.fakes: - Roycroft and Stickley marks are faked on modern hammered copper; check that the mark is crisp-stamped (not cast-in) and the forms match catalogue shapes. - 18th-century English brass candlesticks heavily reproduced in
candle-holders.buy: Buy only signed/marked Arts & Crafts copper or brass, Scandinavian-modern designer pieces, or sterling-free designer pairs at ≤ 1/3 of sold median; pass driftwood, garden stands, souvenir/bazaar copper and weighted sterling.
tells: Hand-hammered surfaces with visible planishing marks, rivets, and a stamped maker mark under the base = Arts & Crafts (1900–1930).
Spike (pricket) on a stamped tin plate = modern pillar-candle decor (1970s–present); example 7950325606 is a driftwood log with a stamped steel pricket plate.

Push-up rod in the shaft of a brass candlestick = 18th–19th-century English/American; seam down the shaft (cast in two halves and brazed) = pre-1800s; solid-cast one-piece with a threaded tenon base = 19th–20th century.

candle-lanterns.title: Candle lanterns , carriage lanterns, and modern decor box lanterns)
candle-lanterns.full: Candle lanterns (antique tin/punched-tin "Paul Revere" lanterns, railroad/ship candle lanterns, folding candle lanterns (Stonebridge, UCO), carriage lanterns, and modern decor box lanterns)
candle-lanterns.money: early 18th–19th-century horn-pane, sheet-iron and documented railroad/ship candle lanterns $200–1,000+.
candle-lanterns.fakes: Indian/Chinese reproductions of punched-tin and ship lanterns are everywhere (aged finishes, "Paul Revere" pierced pattern with machine-regular holes). Treat any "antique ship lantern" in brass with a maritime brand name
candle-lanterns.buy: Pass modern decor lanterns and generic galvanised boxes; buy only soldered-tin 19th-century lanterns (punched tin, wood frame, horn or wavy glass, stamped makers) or Stonebridge/early UCO folding lanterns at ≤ 25% of the ladder.
tells: Antique (pre-1900): hand-cut tin plate with soldered seams (lumpy solder lines), wire-reinforced rolled edges, hand-blown wavy glass with bubbles or horn panes, ring handle, conical punched-tin top with vent holes, crimped candle socket, often a cone "chimney"
Folding candle lanterns (Stonebridge 1908–, UCO, Coleman Candle Lantern, military): brass/aluminium frame with mica windows, fold flat.

Modern decor (1990s+): machine-folded galvanised steel or zinc finish (uniform grey "antiqued" paint/wax), flat float glass with perfectly straight edges, crisp spot welds, glued glass, big pillar-candle platform, often LED or with plastic hooks. The example m

capodimonte-porcelain.title: Capodimonte porcelain
capodimonte-porcelain.full: Capodimonte porcelain (Naples crowned-N style: lamps, flowers, figurines; Guido Cacciapuoti, Giuseppe Cappé, Giuseppe Armani/Florence, Luigi Fabris, Ronzan, Ginori-Doccia; Stellacraft and other importers)
capodimonte-porcelain.fakes: The crowned N has been used or imitated by hundreds of makers since the 19th century – it proves nothing. Asian copies carry "Capodimonte" stickers. "Antique" claims on 1950s–70s lamps are standard and wrong. Coalport/En
capodimonte-porcelain.buy: Almost everything sold as "Capodimonte" is 1950s–90s Italian or Asian decorative ware; buy only signed figurines (Cacciapuoti/Cappé/Armani 12 in+) with all flowers and fingers intact at ≤ $60, and pass every lamp and flower basket.
tells: Lamps (1950s–70s): urn-shaped porcelain bodies with relief putti scenes, sometimes reticulated (pierced) panels, gilt scroll handles, floral cartouches, mounted on brass/bronze-tone pedestal bases with filigree, 28–36 in tall, often with a period silk bell sha

Flowers: porcelain bouquet in a woven-porcelain basket or vase, pastel enamels (example 7969521555). Italian (marked crowned N "Capodimonte Made in Italy") or English bone-china (Coalport, Royal Doulton, Crown Staffordshire – Lens matched Coalport) or Japanese
Figurines: clowns, fishermen, hobos, drunks, Napoleonic soldiers, ladies; signed Italian artists sell; unsigned 1970s–80s gift pieces don't.

carbide-miners-lamps.title: Carbide miner's lamps and mining lights
carbide-miners-lamps.full: Carbide miner's lamps and mining lights (Justrite, Auto-Lite, Guy's Dropper, Dewar, Baldwin)
carbide-miners-lamps.money: pre-1915 Baldwin, rare makers, coal-company marked $200–600.
carbide-miners-lamps.fakes: Reproduction and decorative "miner's lamp" brass pieces exist; some modern carbide lamps for caving are still made (general knowledge, verify). Unusual "rare maker" stamps should be checked against collector references.
carbide-miners-lamps.buy: Buy Baldwin/Guy's Dropper/Dewar ≤ $30 or brass box lots ≤ $10/lamp; pass a single Justrite over $25.

carnival-glass.title: Carnival glass
carnival-glass.full: Carnival glass (Fenton, Northwood, Imperial, Millersburg, Dugan/Diamond, Indiana Glass, Westmoreland, Jeannette)
carnival-glass.fakes: Many reproductions of Northwood patterns with fake N marks; Chinese "carnival" in old patterns. When unsure, assume new.
carnival-glass.buy: Old (pre-1930) carnival in purple, amethyst, ice/pastel or rare patterns at ≤ 1/3 of sold; late Indiana/Fenton reissue sets are pass above ~$25.
tells: Old carnival (c. 1907–1930): Fenton, Northwood (underlined N in circle mark), Imperial, Millersburg, Dugan/Diamond; marigold, purple/amethyst, cobalt blue, green, ice blue, white, peach opal. Thick, richly detailed molds, ground or collar bases.

New/contemporary (1960s–present): Imperial reissues (IG mark), Fenton (marked), Indiana Glass (Harvest Grape, Heirloom — very common, blue/marigold/purple 1970s–80s), Westmoreland, L.G. Wright, Boyd, St. Clair, Summit, Mosser; plus Taiwanese/Chinese reproducti

carpet-sweepers.title: Carpet sweepers
carpet-sweepers.full: Carpet sweepers (Bissell, Grand Rapids Carpet Sweeper Co., Goshen, National, Ewbank, Sweeper-Vac; toy sweepers)
carpet-sweepers.money: salesman samples and toy/child sweepers with original paint $40–150.
carpet-sweepers.fakes: Little faking. Some modern "vintage style" sweepers (Bissell still makes manual sweepers). Decorative repro decals on refinished cases.
carpet-sweepers.buy: Buy only toy/child-size sweepers and 1880s–1910s veneered or decaled sweepers with intact brushes at ≤ $20; full-size common sweepers fail on shipping.
tells: Early (1880s–1910s): wooden case, often veneered (walnut, maple, burl, oak), brass or nickel corner trim, decals or gilt stencils with the model name ("Grand Rapids", "Cyco Bearing", "Gold Medal", "Parlor Queen"), cast-iron wheel housings.
Mid (1920s–50s): painted wood or steel cases, decals, rubber bumpers, Bissell "Grand Rapids" decal.
Late (1950s–80s): plastic and steel, pastel colors.

carved-santos.title: Carved santos
carved-santos.full: Carved santos (polychrome wood religious figures – Spanish, Mexican, Spanish-colonial, Philippine, Portuguese/Brazilian)
carved-santos.money: 17th–18th-c. figures with original polychrome and glass eyes $1,000–3,000+.
carved-santos.fakes: Large market of resin and newly carved "antique" santos from Mexico, the Philippines and Indonesia, artificially distressed. Tells: even crackle, paint loss in "logical" places only, no gesso layer, modern fasteners, sta
carved-santos.buy: Buy an 18"+ carved, gessoed figure with gilt and honest paint loss under $200; pass under 12", glossy/even paint, resin, "Made in" stamps, or pieces already titled "antique santos polychrome" at $300+.

carved-wood-sculptures.title: Carved wood sculptures souvenir figures, Black Forest, Anri , Oberammergau, Philippine and African tourist carvings, American folk/whittled figures)
carved-wood-sculptures.full: Carved wood sculptures (Balinese Mas/Ubud carvings, Chinese boxwood and hardwood figures, Japanese netsuke-scale and okimono, Indian sandalwood/rosewood, Andean (Peru/Ecuador) souvenir figures, Black Forest, Anri (Italy), Oberammergau, Philippine and African tourist carvings, American folk/whittled figures)
carved-wood-sculptures.money: important Japanese/Chinese carvings and documented folk art $1,000–20,000.
carved-wood-sculptures.fakes: Modern Chinese "antique" boxwood with artificial patina and fake seals sold as Qing; Balinese tourist busts copying master styles; resin "Black Forest" bears; Anri composite resin pieces.
carved-wood-sculptures.buy: Pass on tourist carvings; look for genuinely old Chinese boxwood (fine detail, honey patina, shrinkage cracks, worn high points), Black Forest bears, and signed Balinese master pieces in ebony/sawo; buy at ≤ 1/3 resale with base photos.
tells: Chinese: boxwood (huangyang, pale yellow to honey), rosewood/hongmu (dark), rootwood; Daoist immortals, Luohans, Zhongkui, Budai; 19th–early 20th-c. pieces show crisp undercut detail, softened worn high points and natural age cracks; modern ones are dark-stain

Balinese (Mas, Ubud, 1930s–today): elongated stylised figures and busts in suar, crocodile wood, hibiscus, ebony, sawo (sapodilla); dancers, fishermen, Dewi Sri, busts with udeng headcloth and flower behind ear. 1950s–70s pieces from master workshops are elong
Indian: sandalwood (fragrant, pale) and rosewood/sheesham (dark), elephants, deities, warriors; tourist-grade mostly.

cash-registers.title: Cash registers
cash-registers.fakes: Reproduction brass registers (1970s Taiwan, "Model 313" copies) exist: thin castings, no serial plate. Also decorative toy/bank copies.
cash-registers.buy: Buy only a brass candy-store NCR with serial plate under $150 (local/regional pickup); pass every painted/chrome post-1935 model.

cassette-decks.title: Cassette decks , Technics, Pioneer, Yamaha, Aiwa, Denon, Harman Kardon, JVC, Kenwood, Onkyo, Marantz, Sanyo, Fisher, Realistic)
cassette-decks.full: Cassette decks (Nakamichi, Tandberg, Revox, TEAC/Tascam, Akai, Sony (ES), Technics, Pioneer, Yamaha, Aiwa, Denon, Harman Kardon, JVC, Kenwood, Onkyo, Marantz, Sanyo, Fisher, Realistic)
cassette-decks.money: Nakamichi (Dragon, CR-7, 1000ZXL, ZX-7), Tandberg, Revox B215, Aiwa XK-S9000 $300–3,000.
cassette-decks.fakes: Not applicable (no fakes). Watch for "serviced" claims without proof.
cassette-decks.buy: Pass anything untested or belt-dead (most decks need belts/idlers); buy only seller-demonstrated working 3-head decks or Nakamichi/Tandberg/Revox/Aiwa XK-S, with playback shown, at ≤ 25% of the ladder.
tells: "3 HEAD", "Dolby S", "dbx", "Dual capstan", "Direct drive", "Closed loop", bias/level calibration knobs, "ES" (Sony), "Dragon"/"NAAC" (Nakamichi), "Auto Azimuth".
Single decks are usually better than dual "dubbing" decks; dual decks with "Playback only" Deck A are budget models.
Brushed aluminium faceplates, VU meters (1970s top-loaders) are attractive; black plastic 1990s = budget.

cast-iron-cookware.title: Cast iron cookware
cast-iron-cookware.full: Cast iron cookware (Griswold, Wagner, Birmingham Stove & Range, Favorite Piqua, Wapak, Lodge)
cast-iron-cookware.fakes: Chinese reproductions of Griswold/Erie pieces with grainy, rough castings and blurry logos; "Wagner 1891" modern reissues; Taiwan-made unmarked sets. Fake rare items (e.g. Griswold-marked novelty pans) appear on eBay (ge
cast-iron-cookware.buy: Griswold block/slant logo under $50; unmarked only under $15
tells: The bottom photo is everything: logo, its position (centre vs 12 o'clock), the words under it ("ERIE", "ERIE, PA., U.S.A.", "SIDNEY -O-"), the size number at 12 o'clock, a pattern/catalogue number with a letter (e.g. "704 R", "1056 E"), and whether there is a
Size numbers refer to wood-stove eye sizes, not inches; a #8 skillet is roughly 10½" across the top rim (general knowledge, verify).

Look-alikes: modern Lodge (pebbly surface, "LODGE USA" with "Made in USA" and often a logo like a skillet outline), Asian imports (rough, heavy, "Taiwan"/"China" or 3-legged "8 IN" marks), and enamelled cast iron (Le Creuset, Descoware — separate category).

cast-iron-doorstops.title: Cast iron doorstops & figures
cast-iron-doorstops.full: Cast iron doorstops & figures (Hubley, Bradley & Hubbard, Albany Foundry, National Foundry, Judd, Spencer)
cast-iron-doorstops.fakes: Large 1970s–today repro market, often from original doorstops used as patterns (slightly smaller than original because of mould shrinkage – general knowledge, verify). Tells: grainy rough casting, loose fit, Phillips scr
cast-iron-doorstops.buy: Buy original-paint figural dog/cat/ship/cottage ≤ $40–50, flower basket 8"+ with good paint ≤ $30, B&H-marked ≤ $100; pass repaints, Phillips screws and repro tells.

cast-iron-figural-decor.title: Cast iron figural decor
cast-iron-figural-decor.full: Cast iron figural decor (Hubley, Judd, Wilton, Bradley & Hubbard, Japanese/Chinese export, modern Taiwan/China repros)
cast-iron-figural-decor.money: signed US pre-1940 figurals (Hubley, B&H, Judd) $60–300+ (general knowledge, verify)
cast-iron-figural-decor.fakes: The whole doorstop/bank/figural field is saturated with reproductions; assume unmarked rusty pieces are post-1970 unless proven otherwise. Reproduction finish rust is uniform and orange; real age shows black patina and w
cast-iron-figural-decor.buy: Pass on rusty unmarked figurals; buy only signed/numbered American pre-1940 pieces with original paint at ≤ $40.

cast-iron-pitcher-pumps.title: Cast iron pitcher pumps
cast-iron-pitcher-pumps.full: Cast iron pitcher pumps (F.E. Myers, Fairbanks Morse, Red Jacket, Goulds, Deming, Baker/Monitor, Dempster, Woodford; modern Hitzer/Heller-Aller and imports)
cast-iron-pitcher-pumps.fakes: Modern imports are routinely sold as "antique". The tell is the absence of maker castings and fresh, even paint. Also watch for: new US-made pumps (Hitzer/Heller-Aller) offered as old; "decor only" import pumps that can'
cast-iron-pitcher-pumps.buy: Buy only complete (body, cap, handle, plunger) US-maker marked pumps ≤ $20; skip parts and imports.

cast-iron-toys.title: Cast iron toys
cast-iron-toys.full: Cast iron toys (Arcade, Hubley, Kenton, A.C. Williams, Dent, Grey Iron, Kilgore, Champion; plus Taiwan/China reproductions)
cast-iron-toys.money: large Arcade buses, Kenton horse-drawn, Hubley motorcycles $500–5,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
cast-iron-toys.fakes: Saturated: probably the majority of "antique cast iron cars" on Craigslist are reproductions. Look for maker names cast inside; repros copy them too, so rely on casting quality. - Banks: Book of Knowledge and other repro
cast-iron-toys.buy: Buy only toys with crisp castings, nickel or original rubber/ cast spoked wheels with peened (not screwed) axles and original worn paint, at ≤ $40; assume shiny red rough castings are repros.
tells: Other families in the same market: mechanical and still banks (A.C. Williams, J. & E. Stevens, Grey Iron), cap guns (Kilgore, Hubley), horse-drawn rigs and fire pumpers (Kenton, Hubley, Dent), airships and planes (Dent ZEP, Hubley "Air Ford"), farm toys (Arcad
Seller words: "antique cast iron", "Arcade", "Hubley", "Kenton", "Model T", "fire pumper", "Yellow Cab", "Greyhound bus".

Construction: most vehicles are two cast halves joined by a rivet or peened pin (or one-piece on small A.C. Williams cars); wheels on steel axles with the ends peened (mushroomed) over; separate nickel-plated drivers, grilles or wheels on better pieces.

cast-iron-tractor-seats.title: Implement and tractor seats – cast iron and pressed steel
cast-iron-tractor-seats.full: Implement and tractor seats – cast iron and pressed steel (McCormick, Deering, Champion, Buckeye, Walter A. Wood, Osborne, Milwaukee, John Deere, unmarked pressed steel)
cast-iron-tractor-seats.money: rare-maker or ornate cast seats $200–1,000+ (cast reproductions are everywhere).
cast-iron-tractor-seats.fakes: Cast iron reproductions of popular seats (Champion, Deering, Buckeye, "Plano") have been cast for decades (Taiwan/India decor foundries): sharper but softer detail, uniform thickness, rough unfinished casting gates, fake
cast-iron-tractor-seats.buy: Buy only original cast-iron seats with raised maker names/towns and old wear under ~$60; pressed steel pan seats are pass above ~$15.
tells: Cast iron (1870s–1910s): thick (~1/4"), heavy (6–12 lb), often ornate with raised lettering (maker name and town), patterned holes (stars, hearts, scrolls), a single slot or bolt holes in centre. Edges are rounded, surfaces show casting texture.

Pressed (stamped) steel (1900s–1950s): thin sheet (~1/8"), rim rolled/flanged, rows of round punched holes, square or round centre hole, light (3–5 lb); usually unmarked or with embossed name only on late John Deere/IH seats. These are the common type and are

ceramic-and-glass-marks-that-multiply-va.title: Ceramic and glass marks that multiply value
ceramic-and-glass-marks-that-multiply-va.full: Ceramic and glass marks that multiply value (cross-culture index: Meissen, KPM, Sèvres, Vienna, Nymphenburg, Herend, Royal Copenhagen, Bing & Grøndahl, Royal Worcester, Royal Doulton, Wedgwood, Minton, Rookwood, Chinese reign marks, Kutani, Satsuma, Makuzu Kozan, Noritake/Nippon, Grueby, Teco, Newcomb, Van Briggle, Ohr, Marblehead, Fulper, Overbeck, Roseville, Pewabic, S.E.G., Weller, Natzler, Beatrice Wood, Leach, Rie, Coper, Gustavsberg, Arabia, Rörstrand, Lalique, Steuben, Tiffany, Loetz, Daum, Gallé, Orrefors, Kosta, Venini, Seguso, Barovier, Quezal, Durand, Fenton)
ceramic-and-glass-marks-that-multiply-va.money: The same-looking vase or bowl is worth $10–60 with a look-alike or decorator mark, $100–1,000 with a genuine factory mark on production ware, and $1,000–150,000 with a period or artist mark (Ohr $5,700
ceramic-and-glass-marks-that-multiply-va.fakes: - **Added signatures on genuine glass:** Tiffany marks on Quezal and Loetz (Heritage comp); R. Lalique marks on later Lalique or VDA bottles (rlalique.com). - **Fake marks on new ware:** Chinese reign marks, Nippon decal
ceramic-and-glass-marks-that-multiply-va.buy: Never pay for a mark you have not seen in a clear, square-on base photo. Buy when the mark, the body, the foot and the decoration all agree and the price is ≤ 25% of the sold comp for that mark's tier. Pass on "Dresden", "Royal Vienna", "Sèvres-style", "Laliqu
tells: Impressed (stamped into the wet clay). The edges are crisp and the glaze pools in the recess. Examples: G.E. OHR / BILOXI, Grueby lotus, Teco, Marblehead ship, Overbeck OBK, Wedgwood, Minton cyphers, Nymphenburg shield, KPM plaques, Rie/Coper/Leach seals. Impr
Incised (scratched freehand into the clay). Examples: artist cyphers on Rookwood, Newcomb, Grueby and Van Briggle, and the Natzler, Beato and Ohr script signatures.

Underglaze blue (painted or printed before the glaze). The mark sits *under* the glass of the glaze: the colour is soft at the edges and slightly blurred, and the glaze surface over it is smooth. Real examples include Meissen swords, Vienna shield, KPM sceptre

ceramic-christmas-trees.title: Ceramic Christmas trees
ceramic-christmas-trees.full: Ceramic Christmas trees (Atlantic Mold, Holland Mold, Duncan, Arnel's, Nowell's, Byron, Doc Holliday, Dogwood, hobby-cast)
ceramic-christmas-trees.money: large 18–24" or white/gold/pink, with birds or music box $150–350+ (general knowledge, verify). Terapeak: Atlantic Mold median $90
ceramic-christmas-trees.fakes: - Mr. Christmas and many retailers sell new "nostalgic ceramic trees" — glossy, lighter, often with music; worth $25–60. - New trees poured from original Atlantic molds carry the 1958 mark: a "1958" mark alone does not p
ceramic-christmas-trees.buy: buy only when ≤ $40 for a 16"+ tree in uncommon colour (white, pink, gold, flocked) or with birds/music box, intact with base; shipping a fragile 10 lb tree costs $35+.
tells: Mold maker mark is inside the bottom rim of the tree: "Atlantic Mold" (most common), "Holland Mold", "Duncan", "Arnel's", "Nowell's", "Byron", "Doc Holliday", with year. The hobbyist often signed and dated the bottom too (craft trees are often crudely incised

The year in the mark is the mold's copyright, not the tree's age. Atlantic Mold copyrighted its tree design in 1958 and made the molds until 1999, then sold them, so "1958" trees are still poured today (Mining Journal; Denver7).
Title words: "vintage ceramic tree", "Atlantic Mold", "light up", "birds", "music box", "24 inch", "white", "flocked".

character-mugs.title: Character mugs
character-mugs.full: Character mugs (figural/head mugs and licensed mugs: King Features Popeye, Disney, Peanuts/Snoopy, Holt Howard, Fitz & Floyd, Applause, Arabia Moomin, Royal Doulton character jugs, Potpourri Press, Pfaltzgraff, Hallmark)
character-mugs.money: Arabia Moomin limited and older Royal Doulton large character jugs $60–250+.
character-mugs.fakes: Popeye mugs were reissued in the 1990s–2000s (e.g. Vandor); Moomin mug counterfeits from China exist (check Arabia backstamp and year).
character-mugs.buy: Pass on single licensed mugs; only Arabia Moomin seasonal/discontinued mugs or rare Royal Doulton character jugs at ≤ $20 clear Dylan's profit floor.
tells: Arabia Moomin (Finland, 1990–): straight white porcelain mug with Moomin character illustration; seasonal and discontinued editions command $60–200.
Royal Doulton character jugs: English ceramic heads (Old Charley, Sairey Gamp etc.), not drinking mugs but often called "mugs".

Figural head mugs: whole mug moulded as a face (Popeye with pipe, Santa, Garfield, Star Wars by California Originals 1977, Batman by Applause). Popeye 1980 King Features mug: flesh-coloured head, white sailor hat rim, brown pipe, "© 1980 King Features Syndicat

character-watches.title: Character and novelty wristwatches
character-watches.full: Character and novelty wristwatches (Ingersoll, U.S. Time/Timex, New Haven, Bradley, Ingraham, Sheffield, Dirty Time Co., Lafayette; cowboy, Disney, comic and political watches)
character-watches.money: boxed 1930s–50s (Ingersoll Mickey 1933, Hopalong with saddle box, Roy Rogers, Dan Dare) $200–1,500.
character-watches.fakes: - Reproduction dials (Mickey, Hoppy, Roy Rogers) installed in old cases. - Official reissues: Timex/Disney 1990s "re-creations" of 1933 Mickey; Fossil limited editions; Hopalong reissue watches 1980s–2000s with modern qu
character-watches.buy: Buy only 1930s–50s US/UK character watches that run, with a clean original dial, at ≤ $30 (≤ $100 if with original box); pass on 1970s+ novelty watches over $10.
tells: 1933–40s: Ingersoll Mickey Mouse (1933, Mickey's hands are the watch hands), Big Bad Wolf, Popeye, Dick Tracy, Superman (New Haven 1939), Buck Rogers; small chrome cases, leather straps sometimes with a metal figural strap ornament.

1949–55 cowboy boom: Hopalong Cassidy (U.S. Time, 1950; Hoppy bust on dial; famous saddle display box), Roy Rogers (Ingraham/Bradley), Dale Evans, Gene Autry (Wilane), Lone Ranger (New Haven), Davy Crockett (U.S. Time).
1970s: Bradley and Timex Mickey, Snoopy, Big Bird; political novelty: Spiro Agnew (Dirty Time Co., 1970), Nixon, Republican elephant / Democratic donkey dial watches with patriotic straps.

check-writers.title: Check writers
check-writers.full: Check writers (F&E / Hedman "Checkwriter", Todd Protectograph, Paymaster, Safeguard, Hall-Welter Protectograph, Williams, Peerless, Sengbusch)
check-writers.money: Victorian perforators (Williams, Lightning, Sengbusch) and coin-op/ornate early models $80–250.
check-writers.buy: Pass on mid-century office units; buy ornate pre-1920 brass/nickel perforating protectors in working order at ≤ $25.
tells: Three generations, visible in photos:

chess-sets.title: Vintage chess sets
chess-sets.full: Vintage chess sets (Jaques, Drueke, Soviet/Russian painted, Staunton, Renaissance, Anri, Mexican onyx, Chinese ivory/bone)
chess-sets.fakes: Modern Indian factories make "Jaques-style" and "Soviet replica" weighted sets; modern Russian souvenir painted sets (post-1991) are common and worth less than Soviet-era ones. Fake Jaques stamps exist.
chess-sets.buy: Buy only complete Soviet-era themed/weighted sets ≤ $40 or anything Jaques-stamped; Indian/Chinese tourist sets, onyx and painted-resin themed sets are pass.
tells: Staunton pattern (standard tournament design 1849): Jaques of London (stamped "Jaques London" under the king; red-stamped boxes), 1930s–60s Drueke (Grand Rapids, MI), Lardy (France), Soviet "Baku"/"Tal"/"Latvian" tournament sets (weighted, often with felt base

Soviet/Russian painted folk sets: matryoshka-style turned pieces painted as warriors, e.g. Russian knights vs Tatar/Mongol ("Golden Horde") with crescent rooks, from Khokhloma/Semenov workshops or Uzbekistan; 1970s–90s.
Carved figural sets: Indian sandalwood/rosewood, Chinese bone/"ivory" (illegal to sell ivory interstate in many cases), Anri/Italian, Mexican onyx/marble, Philippine wood.

childrens-china.title: Children's china
