childrens-china.full: Children's china (nursery mugs, plates, bowls and feeding dishes: Royal Doulton Bunnykins, Wedgwood Peter Rabbit, Roseville Juvenile, Buffalo Pottery Campbell Kids, Homer Laughlin, Knowles Taylor Knowles, Shenango, Hazel Atlas/Hocking glass, Staffordshire ABC plates, Japan/Occupied Japan, Royal Bayreuth, Shelley Mabel Lucie Attwell, Beatrix Potter by Royal Albert)
childrens-china.fakes: Reproduction ABC plates (1970s–present); Royal Bayreuth fake marks; Bunnykins reissues (dates in backstamp).
childrens-china.buy: Pass on generic decal mugs; look for Roseville Juvenile, Buffalo Pottery, Shelley/Attwell, Royal Bayreuth or ABC plates at ≤ $20.
tells: ABC plates (1820–1900, Staffordshire): alphabet moulded or transfer-printed around the rim, central transfer scene.
American semi-vitreous (1900–1940): Homer Laughlin, Knowles Taylor Knowles, Smith-Phillips, Salem — decal of children, gold trim, cream/ivory body.
Roseville Juvenile (1916–1930s): creamware with stencilled chicks, rabbits, Sunbonnet babies, "Rv" ink stamp.

childrens-tea-sets.title: Children's tea sets
childrens-tea-sets.full: Children's tea sets (Japan lusterware, Akro Agate, German porcelain, Wolverine/Ohio Art tin, Disney 1930s)
childrens-tea-sets.money: complete Akro Agate boxed sets $60–200 (Play-Time sets to ~$250 at auction)
childrens-tea-sets.fakes: Modern Chinese lusterware-look sets; reproduction Akro boxes. Akro-like glass toy dishes by other makers in similar colours (BDN warns shades were also made by other companies); check for the crow-in-A and pattern match.
childrens-tea-sets.buy: buy only boxed Akro Agate, German porcelain with transfer scenes or Disney lusterware at ≤ $30; plain floral Japan lusterware is a pass.
tells: Akro Agate: marbled or opaque pressed glass in bright colours; boxed sets "Little American Maid" and "Play-Time Glass Dish Set". Pressed patterns with broad panels or bands; mark is a crow flying through a capital A (not always present).

Japan lusterware: iridescent tan/peach/blue glaze, hand-painted flowers, "Made in Japan" or "Hand Painted Japan" (1921–41) or "Made in Occupied Japan" (1945–52). Many pieces in a set are unmarked; often only the sugar or teapot is marked.
German: thin porcelain with transfer prints, gold trim, often unmarked.

china-dinnerware-sets.title: China dinnerware sets
china-dinnerware-sets.full: China dinnerware sets (Noritake, Lenox, Royal Doulton, Wedgwood, Royal Albert, Haviland Limoges, Bavaria, Mikasa, Spode, Herend, Royal Copenhagen; import "Sorelle"/"Royal" tea sets)
china-dinnerware-sets.money: high-end patterns (Herend, Royal Copenhagen Flora Danica, Meissen, Royal Crown Derby Imari, Wedgwood Florentine) $30–300 per piece.
china-dinnerware-sets.fakes: Fake Meissen crossed swords and Herend lookalikes from China; "Dresden"-style generic marks. Royal Crown Derby imitations "Imari style".
china-dinnerware-sets.buy: Pass on full services and decorative import tea sets (heavy, slow, cheap); only buy small lots of high-value patterns (Herend, Royal Copenhagen, Meissen, Royal Crown Derby, Flora Danica) when piece value ≥ $30 and the lot is ≤ $40.
tells: Royal Copenhagen: blue fluted (fluted half-lace), Flora Danica botanical with serrated rims.
Royal Crown Derby: Imari cobalt/rust/gold (2451, 1128).
Herend (Hungary): hand-painted fishscale (Rothschild Bird, Chinese Bouquet "Apponyi" green/rust/blue fishscale).

chinese-brass-and-bronze.title: Chinese brass and bronze
chinese-brass-and-bronze.full: Chinese brass and bronze (incense burners/censers, hand warmers, bowls, vases, Buddhas, scholar's objects, wall plaques; Qing, Republic, post-1950 export; Taiwan/Hong Kong/Korea decorative brass)
chinese-brass-and-bronze.fakes: This is one of the most faked categories in antiques: "Xuande" censers, "Zhang Mingqi" hand warmers, archaic-style ritual vessels with fake burial patina, gilt Buddhas. Any claim older than 19th century needs expert auth
chinese-brass-and-bronze.buy: Buy only heavy, finely cast or pierced pieces with old wear (hand warmers, censers) at ≤ $40 and only as "20th century" resale; pass decorative wall plaques and engraved souvenir bowls; never pay for dynasty claims.
tells: Hand warmers (shou lu): oval or round lidded pots with pierced lids (often with flower/lattice/shou patterns), swing handle(s), 4–7" wide; Qing examples have hand-pierced lids, thick walls, a cast or engraved maker seal on the base, worn patina; 20th-c. and mo
Decorative wall plaques (dragons, phoenixes): thin sand-cast or stamped brass, flat back with hangers, polished bright, 1960s–90s Taiwan/Korea/Hong Kong (example 7952631186).

Engraved bowls and trays: thin spun brass with chased dragon/phoenix and key-fret borders, 20th-c. export (example 7934115711) – sometimes sold as "singing bowls"; Tibetan/Nepalese bowls are thicker hammered bell bronze.

chinese-cloisonne.title: Chinese cloisonné enamel , 1950s–2000s export; plus Japanese cloisonné for comparison)
chinese-cloisonne.full: Chinese cloisonné enamel (Qing/Republic cloisonné, Lao Tian Li, Jingfa (Beijing Enamel Factory), 1950s–2000s export; plus Japanese cloisonné for comparison)
chinese-cloisonne.money: Qing dynasty and fine Japanese Meiji cloisonné $500–20,000+.
chinese-cloisonne.fakes: Fake reign marks (Jingtai, Qianlong) on modern pieces; artificially aged modern pieces with wax/dirt; Chinese copies of Japanese Meiji work. High-value claims need specialist authentication. Also: a mark that only looks
chinese-cloisonne.buy: Pass on modern black/blue-ground export vases; buy only Republic/Qing-indicative pieces (darker pitted enamel, gilt-copper wire, "China" mark or Lao Tian Li mark, Japanese silver wire/Meiji) at ≤ 25% of conservative resale — with auction-specialist risk in min

chinese-export-porcelain.title: Chinese export porcelain
chinese-export-porcelain.full: Chinese export porcelain (Canton/Rose Medallion, Rose Canton, Mandarin, Famille Rose, Fitzhugh, Nanking, Blue & White, Millefleur; Republic period, Hong Kong and Macau export; and Japanese look-alikes)
chinese-export-porcelain.fakes: The single biggest problem in this type. Since the 1980s China has produced massive volumes of "Rose Medallion", "Famille Rose" and "Qianlong-mark" porcelain sold as antique; many are artificially aged (stained crackle,
chinese-export-porcelain.buy: Buy only pieces showing 19th-century tells (unglazed gritty foot with orange firing blush, thick glassy glaze with "orange-peel", hand-painted gilding, no mark or "China" only) at ≤ $40; pass anything with red Qianlong seal, "Macau/Hong Kong" or decal-like reg
tells: Rose Medallion: panels alternating figures (people) and birds/butterflies/flowers around a central medallion, pink/green/gold. Rose Canton = no people. Mandarin = figure scenes in landscapes. 19th c. versions have soft, fine brushwork and clear separation of p

Millefleur ("thousand flowers"): entire surface covered in overlapping painted flowers on a gold/red ground. 18th–19th c. examples are rare; 1950s–1980s Hong Kong/Macau demitasse and cup-and-saucer sets are common, with a red four- or six-character "Qianlong"
Blue and white Canton/Nanking: landscape with bridge, boats, rain-and-cloud border (Canton) or spear-head and gilt (Nanking).

chinese-export-silver.title: Chinese export silver
chinese-export-silver.full: Chinese export silver (Wang Hing, Luen Wo, Tuck Chang, Zee Sung, Wing Nam, Hung Chong, Woshing, Khecheong, Cutshing and other Canton/Shanghai/Hong Kong retailers)
chinese-export-silver.money: tea services, large dragon bowls, early Canton pseudo-hallmarked pieces and enamel/filigree work $600–3,000+ (Chiswick results £188–2,375
chinese-export-silver.fakes: Modern Chinese cast "export silver" with fake WH and character marks, often silver-plated base metal or low-grade silver; recent "dragon" cups sold as antique. Weight, patina, tooling sharpness and a magnet/acid test sep
chinese-export-silver.buy: Weigh and read the marks: buy small marked pieces at ≤ melt, and figural/dragon/bamboo pieces with a retailer plus a Chinese-character mark at ≤ 40% of a cited sold comp; pass on unmarked "Chinese silver" and on paktong/plated souvenir ware.
tells: Early (c.1785–1850s): Western-shaped (Georgian/Regency) tea wares and flatware, plain or bright-cut, struck with pseudo-hallmarks that imitate English marks (lion, head, letter) plus initials of the Canton retailer — easily mistaken for English silver.

Later (c.1860s–1940s): overtly Chinese decoration — dragons chasing a flaming pearl, bamboo, prunus, chrysanthemum, village scenes, pagodas, rickshaws, junks — deeply embossed or applied, on cups, bowls, boxes, napkin rings, spoons with figural finials, cigare

chinese-famille-rose-porcelain.title: Chinese famille rose porcelain
chinese-famille-rose-porcelain.full: Chinese famille rose porcelain (Jingdezhen; Qing imperial and export; Republic period; PRC 1950s–present)
chinese-famille-rose-porcelain.money: genuine Qing mark-and-period pieces $2,000–1M+ (general knowledge, verify)
chinese-famille-rose-porcelain.fakes: The single most faked area in Asian ceramics. Assume any "imperial" piece in a Craigslist listing is modern unless proven. - Apocryphal reign marks have been used on later pieces since the Qing itself, so a mark alone da
chinese-famille-rose-porcelain.buy: Pass on PRC-era pieces above ~$15; only buy Republic or 19th c. pieces when foot ring, enamel, and mark all line up — but anything priced as imperial needs specialist authentication (out of scope).
tells: Seller title words: "Chinese vase", "famille rose", "Qianlong mark", "Qing", "Republic", "antique Chinese", "Rose Medallion", "Canton", "mille fleur", "hand painted Chinese".

Where the mark is: on the base, inside the foot ring. It may be a four- or six-character reign mark in underglaze blue or overglaze iron red, a seal-script square, a red "Jingdezhen zhi" stamp, a "China"/"Made in China" mark, or a paper label. The base, mark a
Main groups seen in listings:

chinese-lacquer-and-mother-of-pearl.title: Chinese black lacquer and mother-of-pearl panels and plaques
chinese-lacquer-and-mother-of-pearl.full: Chinese black lacquer and mother-of-pearl panels and plaques (unbranded Chinese export, Hong Kong/Taiwan/PRC 1970s–1990s)
chinese-lacquer-and-mother-of-pearl.money: genuinely old (pre-1930) lacquer with fine thin-shell inlay or hardstone $200–1,500+.
chinese-lacquer-and-mother-of-pearl.fakes: The whole decor category is mass production, so "fake" mainly means a 1990s–2020s piece being sold as "antique" or "Qing". Anything round with birds/peony on glossy black is 20th-century export unless proven otherwise. N
chinese-lacquer-and-mother-of-pearl.buy: Buy only matched sets of small panels or signed/old fine-inlay pieces under ~$40; single 1980s decor plaques are pass at any price above ~$25.

chinese-opium-and-scholar-objects.title: Chinese opium and scholar objects
chinese-opium-and-scholar-objects.full: Chinese opium and scholar objects (opium lamps, pipes and saddles; brush pots, ink stones, seals, wrist rests, brush washers)
chinese-opium-and-scholar-objects.money: top-tier bamboo/hardwood brush pots and imperial-period scholar objects $2,000–100,000+ (auction, expert-only) (general knowledge, verify)
chinese-opium-and-scholar-objects.fakes: Extremely common: Chinese factories have produced "antique" opium pipes, lamps, scales and scholar objects for export since the 1980s, and they are aged with acid, soot and shoe polish. Assume reproduction unless clear e
chinese-opium-and-scholar-objects.buy: Pass by default – the category is dominated by modern reproductions and high-end pieces need professional authentication; only cheap (≤ $30) obvious old opium-lamp bases or Republic-period porcelain brush pots with clear age wear.

chinese-paktong-boxes.title: Chinese paktong / white-copper boxes
chinese-paktong-boxes.full: Chinese paktong / white-copper boxes (ink boxes, snuff and tobacco boxes; "Shanghai Best", crossed-flag Republic-era types)
chinese-paktong-boxes.money: finely engraved signed (Yao Meibo / Chen Yinting style) scholar ink boxes $150–1,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
chinese-paktong-boxes.fakes: Crossed-flag/"Shanghai Best"/"Shanghai Fan" boxes are among the most common Chinese "antique" reproductions sold at flea markets and on eBay/AliExpress. Misspelled English (SANHGAI) is a reproduction red flag. Fake Liuli
chinese-paktong-boxes.buy: Pass on crossed-flag "Shanghai Best" boxes unless finely hand-engraved with poetry/scenes and a maker's seal, at ≤ $40.

chinese-silk-embroidery.title: Chinese silk embroidery
chinese-silk-embroidery.full: Chinese silk embroidery (late Qing and Republic sleeve bands, purse faces, panels, rank badges, robe fragments; kesi; Suzhou souvenir and machine-made embroidery)
chinese-silk-embroidery.money: genuine Qing rank badges, kesi and dragon-robe fragments $200–2,000+.
chinese-silk-embroidery.fakes: Copies of rank badges and sleeve bands made 1930s–1980s for the tourist and export trade, sometimes artificially aged; machine-made "antique" panels; Suzhou institute pieces sold as "Qing". Japanese embroidery (kimono fr
chinese-silk-embroidery.buy: Buy hand-worked pre-1930 panels on silk satin (Peking knots, couched gold, fine flat satin stitch) at ≤ $40 each, matched pairs ≤ $70; pass on machine embroidery, polyester, and souvenir Suzhou pictures; large framed pieces must fit a passenger seat.

chinese-soapstone-and-hardstone-carvings.title: Chinese soapstone and hardstone carvings
chinese-soapstone-and-hardstone-carvings.full: Chinese soapstone and hardstone carvings (Qingtian and Shoushan soapstone, foo dogs, seals; agate, rose quartz, amethyst, jade and look-alikes)
chinese-soapstone-and-hardstone-carvings.money: genuine Qing jade and top Shoushan $500–20,000+ (expert/auction) (general knowledge, verify)
chinese-soapstone-and-hardstone-carvings.fakes: Heavily faked across the board: new soapstone artificially stained to look old, resin cast "soapstone", dyed/treated "jade" (B/C-jade = bleached/polymer-filled or dyed jadeite), glass "jade". Assume new unless age eviden
chinese-soapstone-and-hardstone-carvings.buy: Buy only well-carved, larger early-20th c. soapstone groups or hardstone carvings with fitted wood stands at ≤ $30–40; any "jade" pricing needs testing/authentication – pass.

chinese-wooden-tubs.title: Chinese wooden tubs, buckets and rice measures , water buckets, food baskets; Japanese oke/hibachi look-alikes; Korean rice chests)
chinese-wooden-tubs.full: Chinese wooden tubs, buckets and rice measures (fir/cedar coopered baby baths and foot tubs, wedding buckets, rice measures (dou/sheng), water buckets, food baskets; Japanese oke/hibachi look-alikes; Korean rice chests)
chinese-wooden-tubs.fakes: New-made "antique" buckets and measures with artificial distressing are sold widely by import dealers; some carry new painted characters. Assume decor unless age tells are clear.
chinese-wooden-tubs.buy: Pass unless a red-lacquered wedding bucket with original brass, or a nested set of measures, at ≤ $40; shipping (bulky, $30–50 each way) kills single plain tubs.
tells: Rice/grain measures (dou, sheng): tapered square boxes, often with a centre divider/handle bar, iron or brass straps at corners, painted characters (shop name, "double happiness", "abundance") on sides. Standard sizes nest.
Baby bath / foot tubs: oval coopered fir/cedar staves with a thick rolled rim, brass or iron hoops; often with red lacquer inside.
Wedding / dowry buckets: lidded, red lacquer, brass mounts and handles, sometimes gilt and carved; part of a bride's dowry set.

chocolate-molds.title: Chocolate and candy molds
chocolate-molds.full: Chocolate and candy molds (Anton Reiche Dresden, T.C. Weygandt NY, Eppelsheimer & Co. NY, Letang Fils Paris, Vormenfabriek Tilburg, Dehaeck, H. Walter Berlin; pewter ice-cream molds by E&Co./Schall/Krauss)
chocolate-molds.fakes: Decor reproductions are lighter, thinner tin with soft detail and usually no maker name or number. Some recast copies of famous Reiche Santas exist; compare weight and crispness, and look for genuine stamped (not cast-in
chocolate-molds.buy: Buy hinged figural molds with a stamped maker/number (Reiche, Eppelsheimer, Weygandt, Letang) ≤ $30 (≤ $100 for 15"+ display molds); pass flat bar trays, plastic, and unmarked light tin.
tells: Marks: stamped into the metal along the flange/edge: maker name and city ("ANTON REICHE DRESDEN", "T.C. WEYGANDT CO. NEW YORK", "E & CO. N.Y." or "EPPELSHEIMER & CO N.Y.", "LETANG FILS PARIS", "VORMENFABRIEK TILBURG HOLLAND"), a 4–6 digit model number, and oft

Hinged/clamp (two-part) figural molds: two mirror-image halves of tinned steel (or nickel-plated) joined by a hinge or held by separate clips, making a hollow 3-D figure. Heavy, grey-silver tin finish with a dull patina.
Flat or tray molds: a single sheet with several shallow figures or bars in a row; often a frame. 3-section bar trays and egg trays are low value.

christmas-dinnerware.title: Christmas dinnerware
christmas-dinnerware.full: Christmas dinnerware (Spode Christmas Tree, Waechtersbach, Lenox Holiday, Johnson Bros)
christmas-dinnerware.fakes: No significant fakes; the issue is later, cheaper production of the same patterns (Spode non-England backstamps) and look-alike patterns from other makers (general knowledge, verify).
christmas-dinnerware.buy: Buy Spode/Waechtersbach/Lenox sets ≤ $25 locally or serving pieces ≤ $15 each; pass anything that means shipping a full plate set.

circus-posters.title: Circus posters
circus-posters.full: Circus posters (Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey; Clyde Beatty; Cole Bros.; Strobridge, Erie, Courier printers)
circus-posters.fakes: Reprints far outnumber originals. Common traps: 1970s Ringling "nostalgia" reprints of 1930s–40s designs (offset, sometimes with a small modern credit line), bookstore/museum prints, and "aged" decor prints. Check imprin
circus-posters.buy: Buy only posters with clear original-printing tells (printer imprint, litho texture, period fold lines, correct size) ≤ $60 for 1930s–50s; never buy "framed decor" reprints.

clarinets.title: Clarinets
clarinets.full: Clarinets (Selmer Paris, Selmer USA/Bundy, Buffet Crampon, Leblanc, Yamaha)
clarinets.money: Centered Tone, 1960s R13, matched pairs, bass clarinets $1,500–4,000.
clarinets.fakes: Chinese "stencil" clarinets with invented brand names; occasional counterfeit Buffet stamps on Asian-made bodies (general knowledge, verify). Mismatched joints from different instruments ("married" horns) reduce value.
clarinets.buy: Buy only with a visible Selmer Paris or Buffet R13 stamp under $400 and no cracks; pass plastic student horns over $40.
tells: Selmer Paris (stamp "Henri Selmer Paris" with the crossed-S logo): Centered Tone (1950s), Series 9 / 9*, 10G, Recital, Signature – professional, $800–2,500 used.
Buffet Crampon R13 / Festival / Prestige: pro, $900–2,500 used; Buffet E11/E12 wood intermediate $250–500; B12 plastic $80–150.

Selmer USA (Elkhart; stamp "Selmer USA" or "Selmer Signet / Bundy"): Signet Soloist/Special (wood intermediate, $200–500 restored), Bundy/CL300/CL301 (plastic student, $60–150). Modern black "SELMER" plastic cases with a blue logo badge = student line.

class-rings.title: Class rings
class-rings.full: Class rings (Jostens, Balfour, Herff Jones, ArtCarved, Dieges & Clust, Josten's/Balfour military-academy rings)
class-rings.money: military-academy and early (pre-1940) college rings can sell above melt (melt figures at $4,194/oz gold, 2026-10-10).
class-rings.fakes: Fakes as such are rare; the risk is **misdescription**: alloy rings sold as "gold", plated "10K GE" rings, and stamps that read "10K" but are followed by "GF/GE". Counterfeit academy rings are uncommon but replacement ri
class-rings.buy: Buy any class ring stamped 10K/14K/18K with a maker name at ≤ 50% of melt (weight × $56/g for 10K, × $79/g for 14K at Oct-2026 spot, minus ~1 g for the stone); kill every base-alloy stamp and anything without a karat stamp.

clothing-textile-and-rug-labels.title: Clothing, textile and rug labels — dating and value guide , Navajo trading-post tags, Hudson's Bay points, Beacon blankets, quilt fabrics, Aubusson bolducs, Persian/Turkish woven dates and knot counts)
clothing-textile-and-rug-labels.full: Clothing, textile and rug labels — dating and value guide (ILGWU and ACWA union labels, RN and WPL numbers, care labels, "Made in USA", Talon/Conmar/Crown/Lightning zippers, Sanforized, Levi's Big E and button numbers, Lee and Wrangler Blue Bell, Pendleton, L.L.Bean, Filson, Eddie Bauer, Patagonia, The North Face, Screen Stars/Hanes/Giant tees, Hermès and Chanel (avoid), Navajo trading-post tags, Hudson's Bay points, Beacon blankets, quilt fabrics, Aubusson bolducs, Persian/Turkish woven dates and knot counts)
clothing-textile-and-rug-labels.money: Labels decide which decade a garment or textile comes from, and the decade sets the price. Care-tag 1980s–90s clothing sells for $15–60. The same item from before 1971 (no care tag, union label, metal Talon zip, Big E, single stitch, early Pendleton label) sells for $80–500, and grails sell for $500
clothing-textile-and-rug-labels.fakes: - **Levi's Vintage Clothing (LVC) and Japanese repro brands** copy Big E tabs, selvedge, arcuates and button numbers. **A 555 Valencia button with a Big E tab is a 1990s–2000s reissue**, and **a Big E with a care tag** i
clothing-textile-and-rug-labels.buy: Read the labels and hardware before the title. Pay ≤ ~1/3 of the decade-tier sold median, only with label, zipper and hem photos. Pass on anything where a care tag, a modern RN or a reissue label contradicts the "vintage" claim. Never buy Hermès, Chanel or oth

cocoa-and-confection-tins.title: Cocoa and confection tins
cocoa-and-confection-tins.full: Cocoa and confection tins (Walter Baker & Co., Droste, Huyler's, Van Houten, Bensdorp, Runkel, Lowney's, Hershey's)
cocoa-and-confection-tins.money: sample/trial-size and clean pre-1920 paper-label or lithographed rarities $40–150+ (general knowledge, verify)
cocoa-and-confection-tins.fakes: Common: 1980s–90s Baker's nostalgia tins, Droste current production, and Chinese tin-litho "vintage style" tins sold at craft stores. Tells: barcodes, perfect litho, lightweight thin metal, "replica" stamped in small pri
cocoa-and-confection-tins.buy: Buy only ≤ $15 and only for sample-size or pre-1920 lithographed tins in clean condition; most cocoa tins can't reach $50 profit.

coin-mint-marks-and-key-dates.title: Coin mint marks and key dates — reading guide
coin-mint-marks-and-key-dates.full: Coin mint marks and key dates — reading guide (US mint-mark locations CC/O/S/D/P/W by series, key dates and varieties, 90%/40%/35% silver cutoffs, photo-visible errors; world silver and gold bullion including sovereigns, Mexican 50 pesos and French 20-franc Roosters; Civil War tokens and so-called dollars; proof sets, slabs and Chinese fakes)
coin-mint-marks-and-key-dates.money: gold at $4,200: sovereign ≈ $989 · 20-franc Rooster ≈ $784 · Mexican 50 pesos ≈ $5,064. The edge is the tiny letter or date: a 1909-S VDB cent is $700–2,500+, a 1916-D dime ~$1,000+ in Good, a 1955 doubled die $1,200–3,800 circulated-to-MS63, and a gold sovereign hiding in a "foreign coin lot" is ~$
coin-mint-marks-and-key-dates.fakes: - **Chinese copies of Trade dollars and Morgans** (also Seated, Bust, Flowing Hair, Draped Bust, gold, Silver Eagles and Pandas): sold by the bag on marketplaces and from "found in grandpa's attic" listings. Tells (NGC f
coin-mint-marks-and-key-dates.buy: Sort first by metal (date + country) and price lots at ≤ ~70% of melt for silver and ≤ ~85% of melt for gold only when resold at melt (otherwise ≤ 40–45% per Dylan's rule); pay over melt only for a key date or variety you can see in a sharp photo of the date a

coleman-lanterns.title: Coleman gas lanterns
coleman-lanterns.fakes: Reproduction decals and globes exist; modern Coleman retro reissues (e.g. anniversary editions) are dated recent (general knowledge, verify). Married parts (wrong globe or ventilator for the model) are common. - Repainte
coleman-lanterns.buy: Buy pre-1952 dates, black band, model 200, 202, nickel-fount 242/243 or any 1920s–30s at ≤ $50; pass 220/228 or red 200A after 1955 over $25.
tells: Date-stamp formats (Old Town Coleman): from 1951 on, month left / year right ("4 82" = April 1982); c.1947–1953 an alphanumeric code where the number is the year and the letter (commonly read as A = Jan–Jun, B = Jul–Dec) the half-year ("A 51"); c.1924–1947 yea

Company-name stamp when no date: Coleman Lamp Company 1913–1925; Coleman Lamp & Stove Company 1925–1934; Coleman Lamp and Stove Company 1934–1945; The Coleman Company Inc. 1945–present (Old Town Coleman).

200 vs 200A vs 242: the 200 (Wichita, 1950–51) has an inverted-U brass tube burner (not the 242C's cast burner) and a single-leg burner frame; 242s have a two-leg frame; the 200 fount filler is about 1/2" ID vs about 3/8" on a 242 (terry-marsh; TNTTT). 200/200

collectible-figurines.title: Collectible figurines & tiles
collectible-figurines.full: Collectible figurines & tiles (Josef Originals, Sid Dickens, Cherished Teddies, Precious Moments, Hummel)
collectible-figurines.money: complete rare Josef series, large early Hummels $250–800.
collectible-figurines.fakes: Japanese and other knock-offs of Josef-style big-eyed girls (Lefton, Napco and unmarked) are common – not fakes but lower value. Hummel look-alikes (Napco, "Erich Stauffer"/Arnart). Precious Moments re-issues of popular
collectible-figurines.buy: Buy Josef California-era lots under $15/figure or retired Sid Dickens under $30; pass Cherished Teddies/Precious Moments at any price.
tells: Josef Originals (1946–85): big-eyed girl figurines, black eyes with lashes, foil label "Josef Originals" + "Japan"/"California"; series Birthday Girls, Days of the Week, Months, Musicale, "Little Internationals". Common ones $10–25; 1950s California-period ("H

Photo tells per family: Josef = matte-ish pastel dresses, tiny black pupil-less eyes with painted lashes, gold accents, oval foil/paper label; Hummel = rustic children in muted earth colours on a round or square base, incised "M.I. Hummel" signature on the bas
Sid Dickens Memory Blocks: 6×8" plaster tiles, embossed, signed on back; retired tiles $80–200, common $40–80.

collectible-porcelain-dolls.title: Collectible porcelain dolls
collectible-porcelain-dolls.full: Collectible porcelain dolls (modern collector dolls: Seymour Mann, Gorham, Effanbee, Ashton-Drake, Knickerbocker/Melissa Jane "Victorian Collection", Dan-Dee/Ashley Belle, Heritage Mint, Geppeddo, Linda Rick "The Doll Maker", Bonnie Chyle; antique bisque: Armand Marseille, Kestner, Simon & Halbig, Jumeau)
collectible-porcelain-dolls.fakes: - Reproduction "antique" bisque heads poured by hobbyists from 1970s–90s kits (Seeley's moulds) carry copied incised marks plus the hobbyist's name and year near the neck, sometimes scratched in. They are too smooth and
collectible-porcelain-dolls.buy: Never buy modern porcelain collector dolls for resale; only antique bisque (marked "Germany"/mould number, glass eyes, composition body) or named-artist limited babies at ≤ 20% of sold median.

collector-barbies.title: Collector Barbies
collector-barbies.full: Collector Barbies (Holiday, Hollywood Legends, I Love Lucy, Marilyn, Bob Mackie, Silkstone, vintage)
collector-barbies.fakes: Mattel's own reproductions of vintage dolls (e.g. 35th-anniversary #1 ponytail reissues, 1990s–2000s) are often mistaken for originals (general knowledge, verify). Fake/clone dolls and outfits from Asia; re-boxed dolls i
collector-barbies.buy: Buy Silkstone ≤ $50, Bob Mackie ≤ $40, 1988 Holiday NRFB ≤ $60, any 1959–66 vintage ≤ $100; pass 1990s Holiday, Hollywood Legends over $25 and played-with 1990s lots.
tells: The year on a boxed collector doll is printed on the box front or side with the stock number. The year moulded on the doll's back/buttocks is the copyright year of the body or head mould, not the year the doll was made (e.g. many 1990s dolls are marked 1966 or
Vintage dolls (1959–66) have a ponytail or bubblecut hairstyle, side-glancing eyes, heavy eyeliner on the earliest, and a solid (1959–60) or hollow (1961+) body.

collector-plates.title: Collector plates
collector-plates.full: Collector plates (Bradford Exchange, Royal Copenhagen, Bing & Grøndahl, Hamilton Collection, Knowles, Franklin Mint, Royal Worcester, Wedgwood, Danbury Mint, Lenox, Goebel/Hummel, Gorham/Rockwell, Lladró, Rosenthal; Audubon and decorative bird plates)
collector-plates.money: early Royal Copenhagen/B&G Christmas plates (1895–1910), Rosenthal/Wiinblad, Lalique 1965 $80–400
collector-plates.fakes: Not commonly faked because values are low. "Limited edition" by firing days means huge runs (tens of thousands). Some sellers present decal "Audubon" plates as Audubon originals.
collector-plates.buy: Pass on virtually everything; the only targets are pre-1915 Royal Copenhagen/B&G Christmas plates (check the year), Lalique 1965 "Deux Oiseaux" crystal plate, Bjørn Wiinblad Rosenthal, and hand-painted (not transfer) service plates by Minton/Royal Doulton/Pick
tells: Royal Copenhagen and Bing & Grøndahl Christmas plates: blue-and-white underglaze, year in the design; issued every year since 1895 (B&G) and 1908 (RC).
Royal Worcester "Fabulous Birds" (1970s), Wedgwood jasper Christmas plates, Lenox Boehm birds, Goebel Hummel annual plates (since 1971), Gorham Rockwell plates.
Bradford Exchange / Hamilton / Knowles / Franklin Mint / Danbury: 8–9" plates, gold rims, series numbers, mail-order; box and COA.

composition-dolls.title: Composition dolls
composition-dolls.full: Composition dolls (Effanbee, Madame Alexander, Ideal, Horsman, Arranbee, American Character, Vogue, Cameo; unmarked "mama" and baby dolls)
composition-dolls.fakes: - Reproduction Shirley Temple dolls (vinyl 1957/1972/1982, porcelain Danbury Mint) are often sold as "vintage Shirley Temple"; composition is the original 1934–40. - Unmarked look-alike "Shirley Temple type" dolls from s
composition-dolls.buy: Pass on crazed, unmarked babies; buy only when the seller shows a maker mark (back of neck/shoulders) for a premium line (Shirley Temple, Madame Alexander, Effanbee Patsy/Anne Shirley, Dionne, Buddy Lee) in clean all-original condition and the sold median clea
tells: Matte to satin painted skin with fine crackle lines ("crazing"), flaking at fingertips, toes, nose and chin, often darkened/yellowed varnish.
Mama dolls / babies: composition shoulder head + arms + lower legs on a stuffed cloth body; legs often stitched straight across at the hip; crier box in the torso.

All-composition toddlers/girls (Patsy, Shirley Temple, Anne Shirley): jointed at neck, shoulders, hips; molded or mohair/human-hair wig; sleep eyes with real lashes; open mouth with tiny teeth (Shirley Temple has 6 teeth and dimples).

compound-bows.title: Compound bows
compound-bows.full: Compound bows (used, 1995–2015 era – Hoyt, Mathews, Bowtech, PSE, Bear, Elite, Prime)
compound-bows.fakes: Not a fake-prone category; the risks are mis-stated models and bows with replacement limbs of the wrong weight (general knowledge, verify).
compound-bows.buy: Buy named Hoyt/Mathews/Bowtech/Elite under $60 with sight and rest, or under $100 with spare limbs/case; pass no-name, 1980s wheel bows, cracked limbs/cams, and > $120 unless < 5 yrs old.

concert-posters.title: Concert posters
concert-posters.full: Concert posters (1960s–1990s originals – Fillmore/Family Dog, telephone-pole, Hatch Show Print)
concert-posters.money: 1960s psychedelic 1st prints and punk originals $1,000+ (1950s boxing-style rock'n'roll originals: dealers advertise buying at $2,000–5,000+).
concert-posters.fakes: Fillmore/Family Dog posters had many later printings and outright counterfeits; Nirvana and other 1990s posters are heavily reproduced (general knowledge, verify). Check paper, size and printing method against reference
concert-posters.buy: Buy an original 1980s-or-earlier poster for a name act under $25; pass reprints and heavily damaged posters.
tells: San Francisco psychedelic (1966–71): hand-lettered, hard-to-read swirling type, vivid clashing colours, often split-fountain colour fades. Bill Graham posters carry a BG number (e.g. "BG-62" / "#9") and Family Dog/Avalon posters an FD number (e.g. "No 33"). Ty

Boxing style (1950s–80s): big bold wood and metal type, block colours (often a fluorescent or split-fountain background band), photo of the act, venue, date, ticket price and outlets. Printed on heavy cardboard; sizes of 14" x 22", 17" x 22" and 22" x 28" are
Telephone-pole silkscreens (1970s–90s): flat matte ink, few colours, card stock, staple/pin holes.

condenser-microphones.title: Large-diaphragm condenser microphones
condenser-microphones.full: Large-diaphragm condenser microphones (Rode, AKG, Neumann, Audio-Technica, Shure)
condenser-microphones.fakes: Counterfeit Neumann U87 and AKG C414 bodies and Chinese clones with copied branding exist; Shure SM7B fakes too (general knowledge, verify). Check serials with the maker and inspect engraving and internal boards.
condenser-microphones.buy: Buy C414 under $200, AT4050/KSM44 under $150, Neumann TLM under $300, Rode NTK/K2 with PSU under $120; pass decent-tier mics over $60 and USB mics.
tells: Rode NT2 (original, 1997–2003): satin nickel body, three slide switches on the front (pattern/pad/HPF), "NT2" under the Rode logo, serial engraved on the lower barrel. Replaced by NT2-A (2004+, silver with "NT2-A", switches in a row). NT1 original (satin) vs N

conga-drums.title: Conga drums
conga-drums.full: Conga drums (Gon Bops, Valje, LP/Latin Percussion, Junior/Matador, Meinl, Toca, Mexican/Tijuana and Cuban workshop drums)
conga-drums.money: vintage Gon Bops and Valje (California 1950s–80s) $400–1,500+ per drum (general knowledge, verify)
conga-drums.fakes: Fake Gon Bops decals on Mexican drums exist; modern Gon Bops reissues (DW 2001–2010, then SABIAN from 2010) are separate. (Corrected: the earlier entry dated DW reissues to the 2010s; DW owned the brand from 2001 and SAB
conga-drums.buy: Single congas rarely pay after freight; only buy confirmed Gon Bops/Valje/early LP at ≤ $150 with heads intact.
tells: Badge or decal: Gon Bops, Valje (or "Valje of San Francisco"), LP brass badge (Garfield NJ = older), Matador, Meinl, Toca; no badge = check construction.
Gon Bops (Mariano Bobadilla, Los Angeles, 1954–1980s): "Gon Bops" decal, distinctive rounded side plates and center band, heads tacked or tuned; classic red/brown finishes.

Valje (Tom Flores, Los Angeles, late 1950s–70s; later San Francisco and LP): thick red-oak staves; early drums have scored (grooved) interior staves; about 31" tall (LA) or about 30" (SF); "Valje of San Francisco" decal on SF drums; extremely collectible. (Cor

construction-and-tool-marks-for-dating.title: Construction and tool marks for dating small antiques : dovetails, Knapp joints, saw marks, cut vs wire nails, screws, plywood, staples, shrinkage and patina, labels, clock-movement stamps , lamp marks , mid-century labels
construction-and-tool-marks-for-dating.full: Construction and tool marks for dating small antiques (boxes, frames, small furniture, clocks, tools, lamps): dovetails, Knapp joints, saw marks, cut vs wire nails, screws, plywood, staples, shrinkage and patina, labels, clock-movement stamps (Seth Thomas, Ansonia, Junghans, Kienzle, Lenzkirch), lamp marks (Handel, Pairpoint, Bradley & Hubbard, Miller, Tiffany Studios), mid-century labels (Herman Miller, Knoll, Heywood-Wakefield)
construction-and-tool-marks-for-dating.money: This is a dating guide, not an item type. Construction tells you whether a "Victorian" or "primitive" box, frame, stand or clock case is period (often 2–10× a later copy) or a 20th-century reproduction. Signed lamp bases and shades multiply value enormously: an antique slag lamp runs $150–900, a sig
construction-and-tool-marks-for-dating.fakes: - **Reproduction primitives:** artificially distressed pine boxes and benches (1970s–present). Tells: uniform distress, wire nails or Phillips screws, power-planer ripples, fresh wood under the stain. - **"Rose-head" nai
construction-and-tool-marks-for-dating.buy: Date it from at least three independent tells (joinery, saw marks, fasteners, oxidation, label) that agree. Buy period pieces at ≤ ~43% of the period sold median. Pass when any tell contradicts the claimed age (Phillips screws, wire staples, plywood or particl

contemporary-art-prints.title: Contemporary street-art prints
contemporary-art-prints.full: Contemporary street-art prints (Shepard Fairey/Obey, Banksy, KAWS, Invader)
contemporary-art-prints.money: early (1998-2008) small editions, large formats, Obama "Hope" 2008 editions and letterpress/Lotus series $500-5,000
contemporary-art-prints.fakes: Obey: bootleg offset copies of popular images (Hope, Andre) and pencil signatures added to open-edition posters; verify against obeygiant.com (edition size, size, date) and look for the blindstamp. Fairey has also re-rel
contemporary-art-prints.buy: Only Fairey ≤$200 can work, and only early/small editions; Banksy/KAWS/Invader need COA-level authentication and are outside the rules unless the seller's Pest Control/edition paperwork is in the photos.

continental-european-hallmarks.title: Continental European hallmarks
continental-european-hallmarks.full: Continental European hallmarks (Germany crescent-and-crown and 333/585/750; Austria-Hungary Diana head; Netherlands lion and sword; Belgium; Italy star-number-province; Portugal eagle and javali; Spain; Greece; Poland and Czechoslovakia; Turkey; the Convention CCM; Theodor Fahrner, Wiener Werkstätte, UnoAErre, Lalaounis/Zolotas)
continental-european-hallmarks.money: 916 ≈ $122/g at Oct 2026 prices). Signed mid-century Pforzheim or Italian designer pieces sell at melt plus 20–100%. Fahrner, Wiener Werkstätte, Jugendstil and Secession designers, Lalaounis and Zolotas reach $250–5,000+. Melt figures are calculated
continental-european-hallmarks.fakes: - **Hanau reproductions** of 17th–18th-century silver carry pseudo-marks that imitate old French, Dutch or English marks. They are usually 800 silver; value them as 800 plus decorative value (general knowledge, verify).
continental-european-hallmarks.buy: The edge is unrecognised precious metal ("800", "835", "333", "585", "750" or a small animal-head stamp on a piece listed as "silver tone", "gold tone" or "costume"). Profit must be ≥ the price paid, so pay ≤ ~40% of melt for commodity pieces. Pay a designer p
tells: "Alpacca", "Alpaka", "Neusilber", "German silver" (nickel silver).
"WMF" with "I/O" or "90" alone. 90 and 100 are grams of silver plate on German flatware, not fineness.

"Hanau" pseudo-marks: fake old-style marks on Hanau reproductions. These are often real 800 silver, so value them as 800 silver only (925-1000.com links a Hanau pseudo-marks page; general knowledge, verify).

convex-bubble-glass-frames.title: Convex "bubble glass" portrait frames
convex-bubble-glass-frames.full: Convex "bubble glass" portrait frames (American c. 1890–1925 crayon-portrait and devotional frames; oval walnut/mahogany, gesso and gilt arched frames)
convex-bubble-glass-frames.fakes: - Modern convex frames exist (import decor) but are uncommon; lighter and painted.
convex-bubble-glass-frames.buy: Pass almost always: large, fragile and heavy for low resale; only buy small (≤ 14") ornate frames with intact glass at ≤ $15.
tells: Wood (walnut, mahogany-grain painted, oak) or gesso-on-wood frames with domed (convex) glass, sold door-to-door c. 1890–1925 with enlarged "crayon" (charcoal/pastel over photo) portraits of family members, or devotional prints.
Shapes: oval (most common), arched-top, rectangular with oval opening. Gesso frames have applied floral corners and gilt or bronze paint.
Size: typically 16×20 to 20×24", so they are large items.

cookie-jars.title: Cookie jars
cookie-jars.full: Cookie jars (McCoy, Shawnee, Brush, Hull, American Bisque, Red Wing, Metlox, Twin Winton, Regal China, Abingdon, Robinson Ransbottom, Treasure Craft, California Originals, Doranne, Fitz & Floyd, Department 56, Warner Bros. Studio Store)
cookie-jars.money: top Shawnee gold-trim, Brush rarities, Hull Little Red Riding Hood variants, Regal Hubert Lion and rare figurals $300–2,000+.
cookie-jars.fakes: Mid-1990s onward: large-scale fakes of Shawnee Muggsy/Smiley/Winnie, Brush jars, Hull Little Red Riding Hood, McCoy (with fake "McCoy" marks – after Nelson McCoy's trademark lapsed someone registered "McCoy" and produced
cookie-jars.buy: Buy only correctly marked, full-size originals of known-value jars (Shawnee gold trim, Brush, Regal, Metlox, Red Wing) at ≤ 1/3 sold median after checking size and mark against reproductions; pass hobby-ceramic, modern and anything heavily reproduced without p
tells: Mark on the base: "McCoy" (in-mould, often "USA"), "Shawnee USA" or "Patented Muggsy U.S.A."/"Patented Smiley U.S.A.", "Brush" or "W" + number, "Hull Ware Little Red Riding Hood Pat. Des. No. 135889", "American Bisque" (often unmarked, "USA" plus wedges on the

Finish: underglaze paint (colours under the gloss) is factory; cold paint (painted after firing, rubs off) is hobby or factory secondary; "wood-stain" brown matte = Twin Winton or hobby copies; gold trim = factory-decorated premium versions (Shawnee).

Hobby/ceramic-class jars (1960s–80s): molds from Holland Mold, Atlantic Mold, Duncan copied Twin Winton and McCoy shapes; signed with a painter's name and date, uneven glaze, often stain-painted; worth $15–40 (example 7956647751's realistic flesh-painted Friar

copper-bed-warmers.title: Copper and brass bed warmers, warming pans and chestnut roasters
copper-bed-warmers.full: Copper and brass bed warmers, warming pans and chestnut roasters (English/American 18th–19th c.; Dutch/Continental; 20th c. reproductions)
copper-bed-warmers.money: 18th c. engraved brass lids, pierced decoration, wrought-iron handles $200–800.
copper-bed-warmers.fakes: Many 20th c. reproductions; married pieces (old pan, new handle); fake engraved dates.
copper-bed-warmers.buy: Pass on long-handled bed warmers (too long for the car seat and slow to sell); buy small 18th–19th c. engraved/pierced pieces only at ≤ 25% of resale.
tells: Bed warmer / warming pan: shallow round copper or brass pan (10–13 in) with a hinged, often pierced or engraved lid, on a long (30–45 in) wooden or iron handle. Filled with embers to warm beds.
Chestnut roaster: smaller (7–10 in) pan with a lid pierced with large round holes, short iron or wood handle (12–20 in); 19th–early 20th c.
Foot warmers: boxes or pans with pierced tops.

copper-cookware-and-molds.title: Copper cookware and molds
copper-cookware-and-molds.full: Copper cookware and molds (Mauviel, Dehillerin, Gaillard, Bourgeat, Revere, Paul Revere Ware, Waldow, Portuguese/Taiwan decorative molds, Benjamin & Medwin, Hammersmith)
copper-cookware-and-molds.fakes: Indian reproductions of "antique French" pans, thin with stainless rivets; faux dovetail seams; fake Dehillerin stamps rare but present. - Modern Mauviel still makes traditional shapes; a uniform piston-hammered surface,
copper-cookware-and-molds.buy: Buy heavy (2 mm+) French/English culinary copper with stamped marks under ~1/4 value; thin decorative wall-hanging molds are a pass.
tells: Decorative wall molds (1970s–90s): thin copper or copper-plated steel, brass hanging ring soldered on the back, often tin-lined or lacquered inside; motifs: fish, pig, rooster, lobster, heart, grapes, turban. Sold by the millions (Portugal, Taiwan, India).
Culinary molds (19th–mid 20th c.): heavier, seamed or spun, tin-lined, deep relief, stamped inventory numbers or maker marks (e.g., "Benham & Froud", "Jones Bros").
Cookware: saucepans, sauté pans, rondeaux with cast iron or bronze handles; thickness is the value driver (1.5 mm decor vs 2.5–3 mm professional).

cordey-porcelain.title: Cordey porcelain and Cybis-era lace-and-rose busts and lamps
cordey-porcelain.full: Cordey porcelain (Cordey China Co., Trenton NJ, founded 1942; lamp production as Schiller Cordey from 1969) and Cybis-era lace-and-rose busts and lamps
cordey-porcelain.money: pairs/large figures and pristine lace pieces $150–400
cordey-porcelain.fakes: No direct fakes; many generic "Cordey-style" pieces get labelled Cordey. Look for model numbers and signature. - Remember many real pieces are unmarked; an unmarked piece is priced as "attributed" and should not be sold
cordey-porcelain.buy: Buy marked Cordey busts/pairs with intact lace and flowers at ≤ $35; lamps only if seller confirms they work; unmarked "style" busts are pass.
tells: History (corrected): founded 1942 by Boleslaw Cybis, a Polish painter who came to the New York World's Fair (1939–40; one source says 1938) to paint murals for the Polish pavilion (Potteries of Trenton Society, citing Lehner 1980). Early wares were plaster; Cy
Forms: Victorian-style busts of men and women (best known), animal figurines, Victorian figures made into lamps, coffee sets, covered dishes, vases and boxes (HHJ; Trenton society).

Lamps: many Cordey lamps carry "Cordey" on the porcelain beside the socket (EBTH example, 26" white leaf-form lamp on a wood base); Schiller Cordey lamps from 1969 on are a later lamp-company product.

cordless-power-tools.title: Cordless & corded power tools
cordless-power-tools.full: Cordless & corded power tools (Milwaukee, DeWalt, Makita, Hilti, Festool, Ryobi, Craftsman)
cordless-power-tools.money: Festool Domino/track saws, Hilti TE, Mafell, Lamello $500–1,500.
cordless-power-tools.fakes: Counterfeit Milwaukee/DeWalt/Makita batteries are widespread on eBay/Amazon/marketplaces; fake Festool/Milwaukee tools less common but exist (general knowledge, verify). Only buy batteries with hologram/date-code photos.
cordless-power-tools.buy: Buy Festool/Hilti under 40% of sold, Milwaukee/DeWalt estate lots ≤ $5/tool, genuine HD12.0/XC8.0 batteries under $40 with hologram photo; pass Ryobi/Craftsman/B&D, single pro tools within $40 of sold, anything over 40 lb.
tells: Hilti / Festool: Festool Domino DF500 $600–800, TS-55 track saw $350–450, CT dust extractors $250–400; Hilti SID/SF 22V $100–200 tool-only, Hilti TE hammer drills $200–500. Festool "Toolie" multi-tool $120–160 (seller aware).

Batteries: Milwaukee M18 XC8.0/HD12.0 $70–100 / $120–150 genuine used; M18 5.0 $35–50; DeWalt 20V 5Ah $35–50, FlexVolt 9Ah $90–120; Makita 18V 5Ah $35–50; Ryobi 40V 6Ah $60–80; Hilti B22 Nuron 12Ah $120–160. Fakes are everywhere – only buy with photos of the M

Milwaukee tool-only: M18 Fuel hammer drill/impact combos $120–180, M12 Fuel 3/8 ratchet $80–110, M18 Fuel Sawzall $100–140, deep-cut band saw M18 $200–250 (corded 6232 $120–180), cable stapler M12 $150–200 new/$100–140 used, corded Super Sawzall $50–90, 7/9" s

corkscrews-and-wine-openers.title: Corkscrews and wine openers , Chief, Champion, Estate/Brunswick repros, Rabbit, Screwpull, Laguiole)
corkscrews-and-wine-openers.full: Corkscrews and wine openers (antique T-handle, mechanical, bar-mount pullers; Williamson, Clough, Walker, Thomason, Lund, Heeley, Armstrong, Rapid, Yankee (Arcade), Chief, Champion, Estate/Brunswick repros, Rabbit, Screwpull, Laguiole)
corkscrews-and-wine-openers.fakes: High: decorative bar mounts sold as antiques, Chinese mechanical repros of English King's screws. Also later production by period-licensed firms (Thomason II made by Heeley, Dowler etc. after 1816) – genuine but not "Tho
corkscrews-and-wine-openers.buy: Pass reproduction bar mounts and modern openers; buy only marked original pre-1930 US bar mounts (Yankee/Arcade, Chief, Quick & Easy, Swift, Champion) or English mechanicals at ≤ 1/4 comps.
tells: Bar-mount types (Wikipedia): wall, clamp or top mount (some converted to floor stands); manual "crank and pump"/"coffee grinder" types (crank the worm in, lever the cork out, crank back to release); automatic types that drive the worm in and out with one lever

Model names were chosen for function (Extractee, Pullmee, Yankee), size (Midget, Little Giant, Jumbo), strength (Champion, Hero, Invincible, Titan), speed (Quick & Easy, Simple, Express, Safety, Perfect, Presto, Swift), class (Ritz, Luxury), or celebration (Ne

Hand corkscrews: T-handles (wood, bone, antler), wire "Clough" types twisted from one piece of steel, folding "finger"/bow types (Williamson), Walker "bell" types, and English mechanical barrel types (Thomason, King's screw).

costume-jewelry-lots.title: Costume jewelry and jewelry lots
costume-jewelry-lots.full: Costume jewelry and jewelry lots (signed: Trifari, Monet, Napier, Coro, Weiss, Sarah Coventry, Garne, Marvella, Vendome, Miriam Haskell, Schreiner, Juliana/DeLizza & Elster; unsigned and modern fashion jewelry)
costume-jewelry-lots.money: top designers (Haskell, Schreiner, Juliana, Eisenberg, Hobé) and sterling/gold content $80–400+.
costume-jewelry-lots.fakes: - Fake signatures (added "Haskell", "Eisenberg", "Juliana" tags) and Chinese copies of Trifari Jelly Bellies and Eisenberg figurals. - "DeLizza & Elster/Juliana" attributions on unsigned pieces are often wishful. - Moder
costume-jewelry-lots.buy: Pay for marks, metal content and sets, not for the word "vintage": buy lots only when photos show signed pieces, sterling/gold-filled stamps, or top-designer construction, at ≤ 30% of what the identifiable pieces sell for.
tells: Mid-century costume (1940s–60s): prong-set (not glued) rhinestones, rhodium or gold plating, japanned (black) backs, foil-backed glass, aurora borealis (AB, iridescent coated) stones from 1955+, hook-and-eye or box clasps, screw-back or clip earrings.
1970s–80s: goldtone chains, Monet/Napier/Trifari signed chains, Sarah Coventry home-party sets, chokers, wood and heishi beads, snake/herringbone chains.

Modern fashion (1990s–now): cast zinc alloy, glued stones, lobster clasps, lightweight stamped findings, "statement" bib necklaces with faux pearls and spikes, gunmetal "vintage-look" cocktail rings, Disney Couture.

country-of-origin-patent-and-registratio.title: Country-of-origin, patent and registration marks — dating guide
country-of-origin-patent-and-registratio.full: Country-of-origin, patent and registration marks — dating guide (Nippon, Occupied Japan, England vs Made in England, Bavaria, US Zone / West / Western / East Germany, Czechoslovakia, Austria, Bohemia, Saxony, Hong Kong, Taiwan/R.O.C., PRC, USSR/CCCP, Hecho en Mexico; British diamond and Rd No; US patent and design numbers; Pat. Pend.; DRGM/DRP; Breveté SGDG/Déposé; Swiss cross; ®/™; ZIP codes, state abbreviations, phone formats)
country-of-origin-patent-and-registratio.money: US Zone 1945–49) or exposes the "antique" as post-1963, post-1970s or modern. Price effect: a period-confirming country mark is typically worth ~1.5–3× over the same form with a later mark (Nippon coralene median $161.50 vs post-1921 Japan floral $10–30)
country-of-origin-patent-and-registratio.fakes: - **Fake "Nippon" marks** on Chinese reproductions from the 1970s on: pale green M-in-wreath with the wrong letters, an "hourglass" mark, a rising sun, maple leaf and "RC" copies, and the green "M" and blue wreath marks
country-of-origin-patent-and-registratio.buy: Use the mark to put a ceiling ("not before") and, where the law changed, a floor on the date; pay period prices only when the country wording, the patent or Rd number and the construction all agree, and remember that a patent date or an Rd number dates the des

craftsman-hand-tools.title: Craftsman hand tools – wrenches, sockets, ratchets
craftsman-hand-tools.full: Craftsman hand tools – wrenches, sockets, ratchets (Sears Craftsman; makers Moore Drop Forging, New Britain/NBT, Danaher/Western Forge, Apex/Easco)
craftsman-hand-tools.money: collector rarities (Craftsman "Industrial", Herbrand-made, Moore "V" with forge marks, boxed sets) $100–300+.
craftsman-hand-tools.fakes: No faking at these prices. Note that modern Chinese "Craftsman" shares the name; check "USA" marking.
craftsman-hand-tools.buy: Pass on generic USA-made metric/SAE combination sets unless ≤ $15; buy pre-1950 "=V=" / Herbrand / Moore early-mark wrenches in lots ≤ $30 when marks are visible.

crosscut-logging-saws.title: Crosscut logging saws
crosscut-logging-saws.full: Crosscut logging saws (two-man felling and bucking saws, one-man crosscut saws; Simonds, Disston, Atkins, Great American/Warren, Peerless, Diamond, Pennsylvania Saw)
crosscut-logging-saws.money: premium user saws (Simonds No. 325/Disston Great American, Atkins Perfection, Champion tooth vintage in excellent temper) $200–500.
crosscut-logging-saws.fakes: - None significant; Crosscut saws are still made new (Lynx, Pax, Tuatahi) at $250–600 new, which supports user prices.
crosscut-logging-saws.buy: Pass: 5–7 ft saws don't fit a passenger seat; buy only one-man saws (≤ 4 ft) with legible etch at ≤ $30.
tells: Tooth patterns: plain/peg tooth (oldest), lance tooth, champion, perforated lance, great American; rakers identify later better saws.

Tooth patterns in a photo (WTA): Plain/peg — cutters only, no rakers; M tooth — paired teeth forming an "M"; Great American — three teeth per gullet; Champion — two set cutters then an unset raker; Lance — four cutters then a raker (soft green western timber);

Long (4–8 ft) thick steel blades with large teeth, often with rakers (deep-gulleted teeth) between cutter groups; wooden D or straight handles at each end (two-man) or a pistol grip plus auxiliary handle (one-man).

crystal-animal-figurines.title: Crystal animal figurines
crystal-animal-figurines.full: Crystal animal figurines (faceted cut-crystal miniatures; Swarovski Silver Crystal, Swarovski SCS, Crystal World, Crystal Temptations, Hoya, Waterford, Baccarat, Lalique, Asian generic)
crystal-animal-figurines.money: Lalique and Baccarat animals $100–500 (general knowledge, verify).
crystal-animal-figurines.fakes: Counterfeit Swarovski with fake swan logos exist, especially for popular pieces. Swarovski reissued many designs, so date by logo style. Treat "Swarovski style" titles as lookalikes.
crystal-animal-figurines.buy: Buy only items with a visible Swarovski swan or SC logo, Lalique or Baccarat signature, at ≤ 30% of sold; pass on unmarked faceted glass with painted eyes or noses.
tells: Swarovski tells: very bright, crisp facets with high lead/optical clarity; black crystal eyes (faceted jet stones), not paint; an etched logo under the base or on a facet: block "SC" (1976–88), swan (1989 on); often a silver-coloured metal tail or whisker (mic
Lookalike tells: painted eyes and red nose (as in the example), cloudier glass, rough glue joints, gold cord hangers, bubbles.

crystal-candelabra.title: Crystal and pressed-glass candelabra
crystal-candelabra.full: Crystal and pressed-glass candelabra (Heisey, Cambridge, Fostoria, Duncan & Miller, Imperial, New Martinsville, Paden City, Waterford, Baccarat, Bohemian)
crystal-candelabra.fakes: Modern Chinese/Indian candelabra with acrylic prisms sold as "vintage crystal". Fenton/Imperial reissued some Heisey moulds after 1957 (often marked IG or with Heisey Collectors' marks). Prisms are routinely replaced. -
crystal-candelabra.buy: Buy only matched pairs with all original bobeches/prisms and a known mid-century pattern at ≤ $40, or marked Waterford/Baccarat at ≤ 30% of resale; pass on singles.
tells: Vocabulary:
Candelabrum (singular) and candelabra (plural, though sellers use it for one).
"2-light" or "3-light" is the number of candle cups.

crystal-decanters.title: Crystal decanters
crystal-decanters.full: Crystal decanters (Waterford, Baccarat, Lalique, Saint-Louis, Orrefors, Kosta Boda, Stuart, Edinburgh, Webb Corbett, Moser, Val Saint Lambert, Bohemian/Czech, Cristiro Romania, Godinger/Shannon, Riedel)
crystal-decanters.money: empty Louis XIII Baccarat bottles $200–1,500 (depending on edition).
crystal-decanters.fakes: Fake Waterford acid marks on Eastern-European cut glass; Louis XIII decanter replicas without Baccarat stamp/numbering. Some period dealers describe Louis XIII decanters as "an exact replica" of a historic flask: that re
crystal-decanters.buy: Pass on unmarked glass; buy only acid-etched marked Waterford/Baccarat/Lalique/Saint-Louis/Moser decanters with stopper at ≤ $40, or an empty Rémy Martin Louis XIII Baccarat decanter with fleur-de-lis stopper at ≤ $100.
tells: Baccarat (France): heavy, very clear, "Baccarat France" circle stamp (acid-etched; the acid stamp dates a piece to after 1936; earlier Baccarat is usually unmarked or paper-labelled); Harcourt, Massena, Fleur-de-Lys/Chablis engraved, Louis XIII decanter for Ré

Rémy Martin Louis XIII: flattened round flask shape with fleur-de-lis decoration and a fleur-de-lis stopper; the base is acid-etched with the Baccarat mark and "E. Rémy Martin & Cie, Cognac, France"; about 11" tall for the standard 700/750 ml size.
Louis XIII: fleur-de-lis stopper present, Baccarat and Rémy Martin acid marks on the base, any number, and whether the original coffret (case) is included.

crystal-giftware.title: Crystal and pressed-glass giftware
crystal-giftware.full: Crystal and pressed-glass giftware (Godinger, Shannon, Waterford, Marquis, Lenox, Gorham, Mikasa, Cristal d'Arques, Princess House, Fifth Avenue; EAPG with ruby/gold stain)
crystal-giftware.money: rare EAPG, Heisey/Fostoria signed pieces, American Brilliant cut glass $80–500+.
crystal-giftware.fakes: - EAPG reproductions (L.G. Wright, Westmoreland, Mosser, Summit) in clear and colours, with crisp moulding and wrong-feeling glass. - Fake ABP: pressed "near cut" (Imperial "Nucut", Heisey) sold as cut glass; modern Asia
crystal-giftware.buy: Buy only acid-marked Waterford (pre-2000 Irish), American Brilliant Period cut glass (deep sharp cuts, heavy) or rare EAPG patterns at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on Godinger/Shannon/pressed "crystal" giftware.
tells: Early American Pattern Glass (EAPG) (1850s–1915): pressed patterns by US Glass, Duncan, Heisey, Westmoreland, McKee, often with ruby stain or gold and enamel flowers (like the tumbler in our sweep).
American Brilliant Period cut glass (1876–1917): Hawkes, Libbey, Dorflinger, Clark, Hoare; deep, sharp hand cuts, very heavy, often signed with acid stamps. Valuable.

Modern giftware crystal (1970s–2010s): Godinger (Shannon, Dublin), Mikasa, Gorham (Lady Anne, Althea), Lenox, Marquis by Waterford, Waterford, Cristal d'Arques (France, lead crystal, "Longchamp" etc.), Princess House (Highlights, Heritage), Fifth Avenue, Fifth

crystal-hurricane-lamps.title: Crystal hurricane lamps
crystal-hurricane-lamps.full: Crystal hurricane lamps (Waterford, Baccarat, Lenox, Gorham, Godinger, Fostoria, Imperial, L.E. Smith, Westmoreland; pressed-glass boudoir hurricane lamps; Gone-with-the-Wind lamps)
crystal-hurricane-lamps.fakes: Unmarked "Waterford style" imports; seller "Waterford" claims without etched mark. - Copies are made worldwide (Hunker); verify the pattern against Replacements before paying.
crystal-hurricane-lamps.buy: Only buy lead crystal with an acid-etched maker mark (Waterford word mark or later seahorse mark, Baccarat mark) at ≤ 1/3 resale; pass on pressed glass pairs above $20.
tells: Where the mark is: underside of the base (Waterford: etched word or seahorse; Baccarat: engraved/etched name or logo). Chimneys are often unmarked; marks may be faint and need raking light (Hunker).
Seller titles: "Waterford hurricane", "crystal boudoir lamp", "Lismore lamp", "pair crystal lamps", "Gone with the Wind" (usually painted-globe parlour lamps, a different type).

Two forms: the two-piece hurricane (crystal base holding a socket, with a separate crystal chimney on top, often 9–12 in tall) and the crystal table lamp with a fabric shade; both are called "hurricane" by sellers.

cuboro-marble-runs.title: Cuboro and premium wooden marble runs
cuboro-marble-runs.full: Cuboro and premium wooden marble runs (Cuboro, Quadrilla/Hape, HABA Ball Track, Gravitrax-not-wood, Naef, Grimm's)
cuboro-marble-runs.fakes: Chinese generic clones exist; they do not carry the cuboro mark burned/printed and do not fit Cuboro cubes precisely. - Clone tells: lighter or pinkish wood, fuzzy tunnel bores, cubes slightly over or under 5 cm, glossy
cuboro-marble-runs.buy: Buy only complete Cuboro Basis/Standard (54 cubes) or larger lots ≤ $75; count cubes from photos.
tells: Size and feel: every element is a 5 cm (≈2 in) cube of solid beech, natural (unpainted, unvarnished) finish. Each element takes up to ~30 machining steps (Magazin listing). Grooves are on the top face; tunnels run through the body, so a photo of a cube's side
Weight as a count check: current Standard 32 weighs 3.2 kg and Standard 50 weighs 4.6 kg (Magazin), so roughly 90–100 g per cube. A shipped weight lets you sanity-check a cube count.
Marbles: glass marbles; current sets include 5 coloured marbles made in Japan (Magazin).

cufflinks.title: Vintage cufflinks
cufflinks.full: Vintage cufflinks (Swank, Anson, Hickok, Shields, Krementz, Foster, Georg Jensen, Tiffany, Cartier, Dunhill)
cufflinks.fakes: Fake Tiffany/Cartier common; fake gold marks rare but exist. Luxury brands need authentication — Dylan avoids. Tiffany tells (Era Gem): genuine marks read "Tiffany & Co." or "T & Co." (always the ampersand); stamps are c
cufflinks.buy: Buy only 14k/18k (stamped), sterling designer, or large mixed lots at ≤ $2/pair; single Swank/Anson base-metal pairs are pass.
tells: Back types (Rau Antiques): *bullet back* (bullet-shaped cylinder that flips 90°; the classic mid-century US type), *whale back* (a solid toggle shaped like a whale's tail that flips flat), *chain link* (two faces joined by a short chain; the oldest form, decor
Where marks sit: on the flat underside of the toggle, on the post, or on the back of the face. A loupe photo is needed; most phone photos don't show them.

Period style (Rau): Victorian = highly decorative; Edwardian = simpler; Art Nouveau (c. 1900) = flowing natural forms; Art Deco = bold colour and geometry (enamel, onyx, MOP). 1950s–70s US = big novelty faces, Lucite, coins, stones, "Florentine" textured gold-

curtis-jere-metal-wall-art.title: Curtis Jere metal wall art
curtis-jere-metal-wall-art.full: Curtis Jere metal wall art (Curtis Jeré / Artisan House, C. Jere; also Higgins-style, Syroco/Homco/Burwood look-alikes, Masketeers, Raymor-era decor)
curtis-jere-metal-wall-art.fakes: Modern "Curtis Jere style" imports from India/China sold new at HomeGoods/Wayfair; some bear fake "C. Jere" signatures. Fake signatures tend to be painted or engraved rather than welded/raised, and appear on light constr
curtis-jere-metal-wall-art.buy: Buy only when a "C. Jere" or "Curtis Jere" signature (welded/stamped plaque or scratched signature, often with a year) is visible or confirmed by the seller, at ≤ 1/3 of conservative resale; pass on painted wire/tin decor regardless of what Lens says, and on a
tells: Real C. Jere tells: heavy brass, copper or bronze-finished steel; torch-cut, welded and brazed construction with visible weld beads; layered depth (pieces stand 1–4 in off the wall); finishes are patinated brass/copper, enamel accents, verdigris, gold leaf; a

Look-alikes: Homco/Home Interiors, Syroco (resin!), Burwood (plastic), and imported 1970s wire decor: thin painted wire bent into shapes, flat stamped sheet metal, faux-rust or gold spray paint, tiny hanging loops, no welding beads, no signature. Painted white

Sailboats are among the most-copied subjects. Real C. Jere sailboats use brass rods for rigging with brazed joints and copper/brass sails or a long hull with patina; the cheap ones use painted wire grids.

cut-glass.title: Cut glass
cut-glass.full: Cut glass (American Brilliant Period cut glass: Libbey, Hawkes, Dorflinger, Clark, Hoare, Pairpoint, Egginton, Straus, Sinclaire, Tuthill; later Waterford, Stuart, Webb, Edinburgh; pressed "imitation cut" by Imperial, McKee, Fostoria, Anchor Hocking, Indiana, L.E. Smith)
cut-glass.money: signed Hawkes/Libbey/Dorflinger rare patterns and lamps $500–10,000.
cut-glass.fakes: Forged acid signatures (Hawkes, Libbey) on unsigned or later glass; modern Asian/European cut pieces in ABP patterns; pressed glass described as "cut crystal" everywhere.
cut-glass.buy: Look only for heavy, sharp-edged ABP pieces with hobstars and acid signatures (Hawkes, Libbey) at ≤ $40; pass on pressed glass and ashtrays.

danish-bronzes.title: Danish bronzes & diskometal
danish-bronzes.full: Danish bronzes & diskometal (Just Andersen, Tinos, Buch & Deichmann, Ildfast, Bing & Grøndahl)
danish-bronzes.money: large bronze sculptures, signed Gauguin/Ruge, Deco pairs $800–3,000.
danish-bronzes.fakes: Unmarked Deco pewter from other makers is often attributed to Just Andersen; some recasts of popular figures exist (general knowledge, verify). Insist on a stamped mark. Dealers also sell "Tinos style" bronzes made by ot
danish-bronzes.buy: Buy a marked piece at ≤ 30% of the sold band (bust under $120, vase under $50); pass when the seller names Just Andersen and prices near market.
tells: Just Andersen (1884–1943), born in Greenland, trained as sculptor and silversmith, founded his workshop with his wife Alba in 1918 making jewellery, silver, pewter, bronze and diskometal. Diskometal (named after Disko Bay, Greenland) is a tin–lead–antimony all

Scale: many figural pieces are small. The Fanø girl bust (model 2111, Carl Emil Ruge) is about 4.25" (10.8 cm) tall in bronze; a 1940s diskometal Ruge figurine is about 4.3" (11 cm) (1stDibs). Don't expect a large bust from the name.

Tinos (Tinos Bronce, Denmark, active 1930s–1950s): solid ("massive") patinated bronze bowls, chargers, vases, candlesticks, bookends, boxes, lighters and figures; Art Deco fluting/ribbing and figural motifs (eagles, swans, centaurs, kneeling women) (1stDibs).

dansk-kobenstyle.title: Dansk Kobenstyle enamelware
dansk-kobenstyle.money: rare colours (black, olive, orange) and early France paella w/ teak, boxed sets $200–400.
dansk-kobenstyle.fakes: Dansk's own 2012+ reissues are the main confusion: marked "Dansk Kobenstyle" and made in Thailand/China, worth $15–40. No significant fakes (general knowledge, verify).
dansk-kobenstyle.buy: Buy vintage "France/Denmark"-marked, unchipped pieces ≤ $35 (casserole/paella) or ≤ $60 (complete fondue) – realistically only rare colours clear the profit rule; pass if the seller names Quistgaard or prices ≥ $100.

darkroom-equipment.title: Darkroom equipment
darkroom-equipment.full: Darkroom equipment (GraLab timers, enlargers, enlarging lenses, Zone VI, cold-light heads, Metz/Vivitar flashes)
darkroom-equipment.money: Focomat, Zone VI field cameras, Jobo CPP-3 $600–2,000.
darkroom-equipment.fakes: Not a fake category. Risks are mis-identification (Metz 45CT vs 32CT; generic "camera lens" vs Componon-S) and missing parts (general knowledge, verify).
darkroom-equipment.buy: Buy darkroom lots containing a Componon-S/Rodagon lens or Metz 45/60 under $40, Zone VI washers/cold-light heads ≤ $80, Zone VI field camera ≤ $200, stabilizer ≤ $30; pass enlarger bodies and GraLab-only lots at $50+.

dazor-lamps.title: Dazor floating-arm lamps
dazor-lamps.full: Dazor floating-arm lamps (Dazor Mfg. Corp., St. Louis)
dazor-lamps.fakes: No significant fakes; Dazor's later production and generic articulating lamps get mis-titled as vintage Dazor (general knowledge, verify).
dazor-lamps.buy: Buy saucer/UFO models under $100 or weighted-base floating fixtures under $40; pass clamp-base fluorescents over $40 – shipping eats them.

dearmond-guitars.title: DeArmond guitars
dearmond-guitars.money: Korean sparkle finishes, X-155 hollowbodies, Jet-Star Special $700–1,100.
dearmond-guitars.fakes: Not a fake target. Confusion risks: Guild-made originals vs DeArmond reissues, and Korean vs Indonesian (general knowledge, verify).
dearmond-guitars.buy: Buy Korean M-75T/M-77T/X-155 ≤ $200 or Indonesian M-75 w/ case ≤ $120; pass Indonesian over $150, missing case, or amp-padded bundles.

decipher-star-wars-ccg.title: Decipher Star Wars CCG
decipher-star-wars-ccg.full: Decipher Star Wars CCG (Star Wars Customizable Card Game, 1995–2001)
decipher-star-wars-ccg.fakes: Resealed booster boxes/packs and proxy printed rares exist (general knowledge, verify). Check shrink seams and Decipher logos on wrap.

decorative-birdcages.title: Decorative birdcages
decorative-birdcages.full: Decorative birdcages (Hendryx, Victorian wire/wood cages, Chinese bamboo cages, Bauhaus/Art Deco brass, modern décor imports: Pier 1, Hobby Lobby, Ballard Designs)
decorative-birdcages.money: 19th-c architectural wooden/wire cages (Victorian house shapes) $200–1,500 local only.
decorative-birdcages.fakes: Large volume of new "antique Chinese" cages with aged finishes; distressed "Victorian" décor cages (the Lens matches to $300+ are new retail from bol.com etc.).
decorative-birdcages.buy: Pass on décor cages; buy only small antique Chinese songbird cages with original porcelain/brass feeders and ivory-like or carved hook fittings at ≤ $40.
tells: Victorian architectural cages: hand-made wood-and-wire models of houses/churches; large; local sale only.

Chinese songbird cages (Qing to mid-20th c): round or dome-shaped, thin bamboo bars, carved hardwood base ring, hook at top (brass or carved), tiny porcelain feeding cups (often blue and white), brass fittings. Small (10–16" tall).
Hendryx (New Haven CT, 1870s–1950s): brass or painted wire cages with a stamped "Hendryx" seed guard; 1950s brass dome cages with stands.

decorative-china-vases.title: Decorative china vases
decorative-china-vases.full: Decorative china vases (Seymour Mann "China Blue", Andrea by Sadek, Madison & Max, Moorcroft, Chinese export, Nippon/Satsuma)
decorative-china-vases.fakes: - Chinese reign marks (Kangxi, Qianlong, Xuande six-character marks) are on millions of 20th–21st c. pieces. A mark alone means nothing; judge form, glaze, foot and wear (Oriental Antiques guide). - Modern "Chinese Expor
decorative-china-vases.buy: Pass on any 1980s–2010s import brand (back stamp names a US importer); buy only maker-marked European/Japanese art pottery or a real Qing piece at ≤ 30% of sold, ask for a base photo first.
tells: Hand-painted brushwork that varies stroke to stroke, slight blurring of cobalt into the glaze ("heaping and piling" on genuine Ming/Qing blue), raised enamel or moriage slip beading (Nippon), tube-lined raised outlines (Moorcroft), crackled ivory glaze with de

Marks: Moorcroft impressed "MOORCROFT MADE IN ENGLAND" + painted WM/initials; KPM blue sceptre; Royal Copenhagen three waves; Herend blue shield; Rosenthal crown "Studio-Linie"; Nippon "hand painted Nippon" wreath/M-in-wreath (1891–1921); Satsuma gold mon (cro
Decal decoration: identical flowers repeating, dot-matrix edges under magnification, no brush texture, colour sitting perfectly inside outlines.

decorative-prints.title: Decorative prints
decorative-prints.full: Decorative prints (offset lithographs, chromolithographs, hand-coloured photos and foil art: Robert Wood, Grandma Moses, Huldah, Monteague Flagg, Osthaus, Wallace Nutting, Maxfield Parrish, Dufex/foil art)
decorative-prints.money: original antique chromolithographs/advertising prints and limited-edition signed works $100–500+.
decorative-prints.fakes: - Nearly everything in this category is a reproduction by design. The fraud risk is sellers calling prints "paintings" (look for a printed signature, uniform surface, dot pattern) or calling modern reprints "antique". -
decorative-prints.buy: Never buy a "signed print" on the signature – it's printed in the plate; buy only period originals (pre-1940 chromolithographs, hand-coloured photos, advertising prints, artist-pencil-signed limited editions) that fit the car, at ≤ 30% of sold median.
tells: Offset lithograph reproductions (1940s–1990s): the bulk of "vintage prints". Under magnification they show a regular rosette dot pattern; signatures are printed. Often on textured board (fake brushstrokes) in ornate gold or gesso frames (Turner Mfg., Windsor A

Chromolithographs (c.1860–1920): printed from many stones; rich, layered colour with a grainy, non-rosette stipple; often on board; frequently advertising or calendar art (DuPont, Remington, Winchester for sporting dogs).
Hand-coloured photographs (Wallace Nutting, David Davidson, Sawyer, 1900–1940): platinum/gelatin prints coloured by hand, titled and signed in pencil on the mat.

decorative-tin-trays.title: Decorative tin trays and bowls , Worcester Ware, Ballonoff, Coca-Cola and brewery serving trays)
decorative-tin-trays.full: Decorative tin trays and bowls (Daher Decorated Ware, Elite (England), Worcester Ware, Ballonoff, Coca-Cola and brewery serving trays)
decorative-tin-trays.money: pre-1930 advertising serving trays (Coca-Cola, breweries) $75–1,000+ (general knowledge, verify).
decorative-tin-trays.fakes: **Coca-Cola and beer trays are heavily reproduced** (1970s–2000s reprints of early designs). Reprints are thinner and have bright, flat colour and often a modern copyright line. Daher-type decorative tin is not faked; it
decorative-tin-trays.buy: Pass on all 1950s–80s decorative litho tin (Daher, Elite, Worcester Ware); only buy pre-1930 advertising trays or hand-painted antique toleware at ≤ 25% of sold.
tells: Advertising serving trays: printed with a brand (Coca-Cola, beer, soda), made by American Art Works, Chas. W. Shonk, Kaufmann & Strauss. These are a different, collectible class.
Daher: marked on the underside "Daher Decorated Ware, Long Island City, NY, Made in England" plus a year (1950s–80s). Scalloped or round bowls, 8–13" across.
Elite (England), Worcester Ware, Ballonoff, Chein (USA), Ohio Art: similar decorative litho tin.

decorator-swords-and-blades.title: Decorator swords, "antique" machetes and tourist blades
decorator-swords-and-blades.full: Decorator swords, "antique" machetes and tourist blades (Indian/Pakistani decorators; real makers: Wilkinson, Ames, Emerson & Silver, Collins, Solingen, Klingenthal)
decorator-swords-and-blades.money: signed Japanese blades and presentation swords $2,000+ (outside scope).
decorator-swords-and-blades.fakes: Indian-made Civil War and Japanese "gunto" reproductions are common; fake Japanese tang signatures and fake Ames stamps exist (general knowledge, verify). Authenticating Japanese blades and Confederate swords needs an ex
decorator-swords-and-blades.buy: Buy only with a legible arsenal/maker stamp at ≤ 25 % of comps; velvet scabbard or "Made in India/Pakistan" = instant pass.

decorator-table-lamps.title: Decorator table lamps
decorator-table-lamps.full: Decorator table lamps (Stiffel, Frederick Cooper, Chapman, Rembrandt, Marbro, Aladdin, Fenton, Murano imports, Uttermost/resin imports)
decorator-table-lamps.money: designer (Frederick Cooper, Chapman, Marbro, Murano mushroom/teardrop, signed leaded) $150–600.
decorator-table-lamps.fakes: - Tiffany-style leaded lamps (1970s–today) – not Tiffany; sold $40–145. Real Tiffany/Handel/Pairpoint need professional authentication (outside Dylan's rules). - "Murano-style" mushroom lamps from Amazon/Temu are listed
decorator-table-lamps.buy: Only buy lamps whose maker is provable from a label/marks or unmistakable design (Chapman, Frederick Cooper, Stiffel, Murano, Fenton) and whose sold median clears profit after ~$25–35 shipping each way; skip resin, faux stone, fillable glass and anything needi
tells: Frederick Cooper (Chicago, 1923–2000s): high-end brass, porcelain and plaster lamps (ginger jars, tobacco-leaf, Asian, neoclassical). Look for "FC"/"F" on the base, switch or socket (1stDibs) and a heavy, finely cast or hand-painted body.
Chapman (Long Island, 1960s–1990s): cast brass Hollywood Regency, bamboo, candlestick and bouillotte lamps; usually dated and marked on the base or socket ("Chapman 1972").
Murano/Venetian glass (1960s–70s): mushroom lamps, teardrop/"root beer" bodies; many modern copies.

delft-tiles.title: Delft tiles and tile tableaux
delft-tiles.full: Delft tiles and tile tableaux (Westraven, De Porceleyne Fles / Royal Delft, Royal Makkum / Tichelaar, Ravesteijn, De Delftse Pauw, Holland souvenir makers)
delft-tiles.money: 17th–18th c. antique single tiles $20–100 each, antique tableaux $500+.
delft-tiles.fakes: Makkum and Royal Delft both make reproductions of antique designs — legitimate but modern. Taiwanese and Chinese "Delft" souvenir tiles 1970s–now. Antique "17th c." tiles are faked by artificially aging modern tiles (fak
delft-tiles.buy: Buy only framed, genuinely hand-painted multi-tile tableaux at ≤ $35 (≤ $60 if a Royal Delft/Makkum mark is shown), or 17th–18th c. tin-glazed tiles in lots; pass on transfer-printed souvenir tiles and single modern tiles.

depression-and-elegant-glass.title: Depression and elegant glass
depression-and-elegant-glass.full: Depression and elegant glass (Hocking/Anchor Hocking, Federal, Hazel-Atlas, Jeannette, Indiana, Westmoreland, Fenton, L.E. Smith, Tiffin, Heisey, Cambridge, Fostoria)
depression-and-elegant-glass.money: true rarities $500+ but almost never seen.
depression-and-elegant-glass.fakes: - **Cameo:** only the salt and pepper shakers were reproduced (faint pattern, thick bottom; salt only fills halfway). Mosser Cameo miniatures are scale models, not fakes (Just Glass). - **Reproduced depression patterns:*
depression-and-elegant-glass.buy: Only buy a specific scarce shape in a collected pattern, identified from the photo, at ≤ 35% of its sold median; skip sets of stemware, ruby flash, Moon & Stars and anything Mosser/L.E. Smith-reissued.
tells: Depression glass (c.1928–1940): machine-pressed tableware sold cheaply or given as premiums. Colours: green (often uranium – glows bright green under UV), pink, amber, yellow ("topaz"), cobalt, ruby, jadeite/opaque. Thin walls, mould seams, faint bubbles and "

Elegant glass (c.1925–1960): hand-finished glass by Heisey, Cambridge, Fostoria, Tiffin, Duncan & Miller, Imperial. Fire-polished edges, ground/polished bases, etched (acid) patterns rather than moulded ones, heavier and clearer. Heisey often carries an H-in-d

Mid-century pressed/novelty glass (1950s–1980s): Westmoreland, Fenton, L.E. Smith, Indiana, Imperial, Viking. Ruby-flashed ("ruby stain") pieces have a red coating on clear glass – look for clear glass showing where the coating stops or is scratched. Amberina

designer-accessories.title: Designer accessories — boxed small accessories and gift sets
designer-accessories.full: Designer accessories — boxed small accessories and gift sets (Yves Saint Laurent, Christian Dior, Pierre Cardin, Givenchy, Lanvin, Cartier "Must de", Dunhill, Gucci)
designer-accessories.money: true house-made fine jewelry/leather/Cartier/Dunhill lighters $150–600+ (general knowledge, verify)
designer-accessories.fakes: High fake risk for Cartier, Dunhill, Hermès, Gucci and for YSL jewelry sold on resale platforms. Licensed vintage YSL/Dior gift sets are rarely faked because values are low. Anything priced as "authentic designer" over ~
designer-accessories.buy: Only buy when the contents are visible and identifiable as a sought piece under ~1/4 of its sold median; an empty or closed box is a pass, and anything needing authentication is out of scope.

designer-handbags.title: Designer and vintage handbags
designer-handbags.full: Designer and vintage handbags (Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Chanel, Burberry, Coach, Dooney & Bourke, Calvin Klein, Mondani, Guy Laroche; non-authentication vintage: Whiting & Davis, Lucite box bags, Enid Collins, alligator, Bakelite, beaded)
designer-handbags.money: luxury labels (LV, Gucci, Chanel, Burberry, Hermès) $150–5,000+, but these need professional authentication, so they are out of scope.
