designer-handbags.fakes: - Luxury brands have a counterfeit rate high enough that buyers and platforms demand authentication. This is the reason they're out of scope. - Coach has 1990s–2000s fakes with mis-stamped creeds and wrong fonts. - Moder
designer-handbags.buy: Never buy luxury-label bags (authentication required; out of scope). Buy only non-authentication vintage with visual tells: 1950s Lucite box purses (Llewellyn/Rialto/Wilardy) ≤ $40, real alligator with a hornback ≤ $40, Enid Collins ≤ $20, at ≤ 25% of sold.
tells: 1950s Lucite box purses: hard acrylic boxes in tortoise, pearlized, confetti or clear-with-rhinestones, with brass hinges and clasps. Makers: Llewellyn (Rialto label), Wilardy, Patricia of Miami, Maxim, Gilli, Myles Originals, Florida Handbags. $80–400, with c
Whiting & Davis mesh bags (1900s–80s): metal mesh with an enamel-printed design. 1920s Art Deco painted mesh $100–400. 1970s–80s plain gold mesh $20–60.
Enid Collins of Texas (1959–1970s): painted and jewelled wooden box bags and canvas bucket bags with "ec" signature. $40–200.

designer-shoes.title: Designer shoes – vintage and luxury
designer-shoes.full: Designer shoes – vintage and luxury (Julianelli, Ferragamo, Delman, I. Miller, Herbert Levine, Roger Vivier; Christian Louboutin, Manolo Blahnik, Jimmy Choo)
designer-shoes.money: collectible vintage (Herbert Levine, Roger Vivier for Dior, 1930s–50s Ferragamo, museum-grade) $150–600
designer-shoes.fakes: - Louboutin is among the most counterfeited shoes: wrong font on the insole (the C and L shapes), red sole too orange or painted, poor box/dustbag. eBay's Authenticity Guarantee does not cover women's heels, so buyers di
designer-shoes.buy: Pass on modern luxury heels (authentication required); buy vintage designer or genuine-exotic shoes only in common sizes 7–9, unworn-looking, at ≤ $20.
tells: Vintage (1930s–60s) American luxury: gold-stamped insole script ("Julianelli", "Delman", "I. Miller", "Palter DeLiso", "Herbert Levine", "Saks Fifth Avenue", "Bergdorf Goodman"), leather sole with a fine waist, slender almond toe, small stacked or covered heel

Genuine alligator/crocodile: large irregular rectangular "tiles" that vary in size and shape across the vamp, each with soft creases between; on belly-cut skins the tiles get smaller toward the sides. Glazed shine with natural colour variation. Embossed cowhid
Lizard (teju, ring lizard, karung): small even scales in rows, often glazed burgundy, navy or black; 1970s–80s Italian ankle-strap sandals.

designer-silk-scarves.title: Designer Silk Scarves
designer-silk-scarves.full: Designer Silk Scarves (Hermès, Chanel, Gucci, Ferragamo, Vera, Echo, Coach, Liberty, Pucci)
designer-silk-scarves.fakes: Hermès, Chanel, Gucci and Louis Vuitton scarves are heavily counterfeited — needs authentication; Coach fakes exist but are low value either way. Hermès fake tells: machine/overlocked hems, contrasting hem thread, patter
designer-silk-scarves.buy: Pass on mall brands; Hermès and Chanel require authentication, so excluded; Ferragamo/Pucci/Gucci only under ~$30 with clear signature and care tag.
tells: Where the signature sits: Hermès prints "Hermès Paris", a circled ©, the design title and the artist's signature inside the design (often small and subtle) (Fellows). Pucci repeats "Emilio" through the print. Vera prints "Vera" (with or without the ladybug) in

Hermès carrés went into production a century after the house opened (1837 → 1937), created by Robert Dumas (Fellows). Every Hermès design can be traced to a year and an artist; only about 12 new designs a year (Fellows).
Measure it: 90 cm (35"), 70 cm (27–28"), 45 cm "petit carré"/gavroche, and long narrow twillies; size is part of the identification and the price.

desk-paperweights.title: Desk paperweights
desk-paperweights.full: Desk paperweights (glass: Baccarat, Clichy, St. Louis, Perthshire, Caithness, Orient & Flume, Lundberg, Murano; metal and stone figural: apples, animals, advertising)
desk-paperweights.fakes: Chinese copies of French antique weights with fake date canes are common. Signatures on Caithness can be checked against edition lists. - Some weights carry false dates or misleading signature canes; explicit signature c
desk-paperweights.buy: Pass on novelty apples and souvenir weights; look for signed studio glass (cane signatures, etched base) and 19th c. French weights mislabelled as "old glass ball".
tells: Glass: domed clear glass encasing millefiori canes, lampwork flowers, fruit, or sulphides. Antique French (c.1845–1860: Baccarat, Clichy, St. Louis) have date canes ("B1848"), concave ground bases, crisp canes, star-cut or polished bases. American (New England

Classic period 1845–1860: Baccarat, Saint-Louis and Clichy made most of them, roughly 15,000–25,000 weights in all (Wikipedia). So true French antiques are scarce relative to what is titled "antique French".

Figural metal/stone: brass/bronze/iron animals, apples, advertising weights (company names cast in), marble/onyx shapes. The example is a red-painted cast metal apple with brass stem and leaf — a 1970s–90s teacher-gift novelty.

diecast-model-cars.title: Diecast model cars 1:18 / 1:24 / 1:43
diecast-model-cars.full: Diecast model cars 1:18 / 1:24 / 1:43 (Franklin Mint, Danbury Mint, Carousel 1, Exoto, AUTOart, Kyosho, Ertl)
diecast-model-cars.money: Exoto Motorbox, rare CMC, pewter/sterling Danbury $400–1,500+.
diecast-model-cars.fakes: Little faking at the 1:18 level; Hot Wheels Redlines get restored or reproduced wheels and repaints; brands re-issue popular castings, so check the base plate and year (general knowledge, verify).
diecast-model-cars.buy: Carousel 1 / Exoto / CMC under $50; Danbury 1:12 or trucks under $40 boxed; lots ≤ $5/car with premium bases. Pass Franklin/Danbury 1:24 over $30 and all budget brands.
tells: Exoto 1:18 (Ford GT40, Ferrari, Cobra, Chaparral): $250–800+; Exoto Motorbox Signature $500+.

Franklin Mint / Danbury Mint 1:24 (1980s–2010s): opening doors/hood, mostly $30–80 sold loose; with box, papers and display case $60–150; rare editions (Danbury Mint 1:12, pewter/sterling, Duesenberg, limited "Trucks" series) $150–400. "Precision Models" era (
AUTOart / Kyosho / Minichamps / CMC 1:18: $80–300 (CMC $300–600).

disc-music-boxes.title: Disc music boxes
disc-music-boxes.full: Disc music boxes (Thorens AD30, Regina, Symphonion, Polyphon, Reuge/Porter)
disc-music-boxes.fakes: Few fakes; modern reproduction discs exist for Regina/Polyphon (lower value than originals), and married cases/movements occur (general knowledge, verify). - AD30 movements were sold into many third-party cases (Sorrento
disc-music-boxes.buy: Thorens AD30 + 15+ discs ≤ $75–100 (playing); 10"+ disc box with discs ≤ $200; pass broken teeth / no discs / "needs work".
tells: Antique tabletop: a Regina 15½" double-comb box in cherry measures about 13" H × 21" W × 19" D with the Regina logo printed under the lid (Renaissance Antiques) — far bigger than an AD30 and the photo shows a large flat disc lying over a long comb.

AD30 disc detail: the 4.5" (11.5 cm) disc is edge-driven with sawtooth projections, and the tune title is printed/embossed on the disc (MMD 1995, 2009). A swing arm holds the disc on the spindle; a lever or switch starts it.

Later AD30 cases: about 10 × 10 in boxes with a domed lid, movement on the left and upright disc slots on the right, sold through the San Francisco Music Box Company in the 1990s (MMD 1995). These are late Reuge-era production, not 1940s–70s.

doctors-bags.title: Doctor's bags and Gladstone bags
doctors-bags.full: Doctor's bags and Gladstone bags (antique leather medical/Gladstone bags; walrus, bark-grain, alligator, cowhide; makers often unmarked; Hartmann, Gladstone/English trunk makers, Feick, Murphy, Indestructo)
doctors-bags.money: real alligator/large bags with interior fittings $250–800
doctors-bags.fakes: Modern Indian goatskin "vintage doctor bags" with fake distress; embossed cowhide sold as "walrus". Ivory/walrus legality is not an issue for hide in most listings but some platforms flag it.
doctors-bags.buy: Buy only clearly genuine walrus/alligator or excellent complete leather bags ≤ $60; pass worn generic leather and anything needing restitching.

dollhouses-and-doll-furniture.title: Dollhouses and doll furniture
dollhouses-and-doll-furniture.full: Dollhouses and doll furniture (Bliss, Schoenhut, Tynietoy, Converse, Rich/Keystone, Marx tin litho, Real Good Toys, U-Bild plans, Renwal/Ideal/Plasco/Strombecker/Tootsietoy furniture, doll-size cribs and beds)
dollhouses-and-doll-furniture.money: Bliss, Schoenhut, Converse houses and Tynietoy furniture $300–30,000.
dollhouses-and-doll-furniture.fakes: - Reproduction Bliss-style lithographed houses (1970s–90s) and "antique-style" Chinese wood houses. - Reproduction Tynietoy-style hand-painted furniture and German copies (noted by the Roadshow appraiser). - Ideal Petite
dollhouses-and-doll-furniture.buy: Most dollhouses fail the passenger-seat rule and cost $50–120 to ship — pass on houses; look only at small furniture (Tynietoy stamps, Tootsietoy, Renwal/Petite Princess boxed sets, Schoenhut) and at antique dolls riding along with cribs, where sold median cle
tells: Bliss (R. Bliss Mfg., Pawtucket RI, 1890s–1914): wooden houses covered in chromolithographed paper (brick, clapboard, windows), turned porch posts, "R. BLISS" printed on the door or gable.
Schoenhut (Philadelphia, 1917–1930s): wood houses with embossed fiberboard "stone/brick," celluloid windows, decal labels.
Converse (Winchendon MA), Wolverine, Keystone of Boston, Rich Toys (1930s–50s): printed fiberboard or Masonite houses with lithographed details — moderate value.

dresden-lace-figurines.title: Dresden lace figurines
dresden-lace-figurines.full: Dresden lace figurines (Volkstedt / Unterweissbach / Sitzendorf / Ackermann & Fritze / Muller / Irish Dresden / Japanese copies)
dresden-lace-figurines.money: large/early Volkstedt-Rudolstadt groups and pre-war pieces $200–600+ (general knowledge, verify)
dresden-lace-figurines.fakes: Not faked so much as copied: Japanese copies use "Dresden" in titles; some Chinese pieces since 2000s carry fake crown/"Dresden" marks. The tell is lace quality and painting finesse; also look for factory-fresh gilt with
dresden-lace-figurines.buy: Only buy perfect-lace, marked German pieces ≥6" or multi-figure groups at ≤ $40; never singles under 5" with lace chips.

duck-decoys.title: Duck decoys
duck-decoys.full: Duck decoys (working wood decoys, factory and hand-carved; Mason, Herter's, Victor/Animal Trap, Evans, Dodge, Stevens, Peterson; modern GHG/Avian-X/Flambeau)
duck-decoys.fakes: Artificially aged "antique" decoys (faked crazing, distressed paint, new glass eyes), fake Mason/Ward stamps, and decorative carvings sold as working decoys exist; named-carver attributions need an auction house (general
duck-decoys.buy: Wood body, glass eyes, keel/weight and original crazed paint (or a belly stamp) at ≤ $40 each; pass plastic/foam lots, glossy decoratives, repaints.
tells: Modern hunting decoys (GHG/Avian-X, Flambeau, Herter's foam/plastic): hollow plastic or foam, moulded feather detail, keel with line tie. $5–15 each used. 90 % of Craigslist "duck decoys".

Wood vs plastic: a moulded seam line with a hollow moulded underside = plastic. Note the conflict between the two earlier write-ups: one lists a side seam (hollow two-piece wood body) as a working-decoy tell, the other says factory wood has "no seam line" and

eames-fiberglass-shells.title: Eames fiberglass shells
eames-fiberglass-shells.full: Eames fiberglass shells (Herman Miller, Zenith Plastics; Modernica and knockoffs)
eames-fiberglass-shells.fakes: Many unmarked fibreglass knockoffs; Herman Miller reissued fibreglass shells (2014+) and Modernica made them in the 2000s, so a mark doesn't always mean vintage (general knowledge, verify).
eames-fiberglass-shells.buy: Buy marked Herman Miller/Zenith under $100 only if it fits the car

eapg-pressed-glass.title: EAPG and near-cut pressed glass
eapg-pressed-glass.full: EAPG and near-cut pressed glass (US Glass Co., McKee "Prescut", Imperial "Nucut", Heisey, Fostoria, Cambridge "Near Cut", Tarentum, Duncan, Westmoreland, Higbee, Indiana Glass; later reissues by L.E. Smith, Anchor Hocking, Indiana)
eapg-pressed-glass.fakes: Many popular EAPG patterns were reproduced from the 1930s on (Westmoreland, Fenton, L.E. Smith, Imperial, Summit Art Glass, AA Importing): Daisy and Button, Moon and Star, Bellflower, Three Face, Lion, Westward Ho, Thous
eapg-pressed-glass.buy: Pass on clear punch bowls and near-cut bowls; buy only flint-era (heavy, ringing, pre-1870) pieces, rare colour (vaseline/amethyst/emerald with gilt) or Heisey Diamond-H at ≤ 1/3 resale.
tells: Flint era (c.1840–1870): lead glass; heavy, rings when tapped, slightly grey-clear; patterns like Ashburton, Bellflower, Horn of Plenty, Thumbprint, Comet, Lacy Sandwich. Pontil scars on early lacy pieces.

Non-flint EAPG (1870–1910): soda-lime, lighter; hundreds of patterns (Daisy and Button, Westward Ho, Lion, Three Face, Thousand Eye, Manhattan, Bull's Eye); ruby-stained and amber-stained souvenir pieces ("Mother 1904 World's Fair").

Near-cut (1905–1930): pressed imitations of cut glass with hobstars, fans and crosshatching; McKee "Prescut", Imperial "Nucut", Cambridge "Near Cut", Heisey. Crisp sawtooth rims, mould seams through the pattern. Large punch bowls on separate bases are common.

east-and-southeast-asian-gold-silver-mar.title: East and Southeast Asian gold and silver marks
east-and-southeast-asian-gold-silver-mar.full: East and Southeast Asian gold and silver marks (Chinese 足金/千足金 gold and shop chops, Hong Kong chuk kam, Japanese K18/Pt900/純銀 and Japan Mint hallmark, Mikimoto, Meiji export silver, Korean 순금/순은, Siam nielloware, Thai 96.5% gold, Burmese, Straits Chinese, Yogya/Djokja 800, Philippine 18K)
east-and-southeast-asian-gold-silver-mar.money: Meiji export silver, Burmese repoussé and Straits Chinese belts $300–10,000 at dealers and auction (Pushkin sold £3,595 and £9,995 retail).
east-and-southeast-asian-gold-silver-mar.fakes: - **Fake 足金 / 999 stamps on brass or gold-plated copper** — common in cheap Chinese marketplaces; tell by weight, colour at wear points and a tester (general knowledge, verify). - **Tungsten-filled gold bars and heavy pe
east-and-southeast-asian-gold-silver-mar.buy: Weigh it and read the stamp; buy unrecognised 足金/999/순금/K18/Pt900 gold only at ≤ 40% of melt (Dylan's rule makes melt-only items need a 2× spread); pay above that only for a named premium (Mikimoto, Meiji maker, Maung Yin Maung, signed Peranakan); never pay go
tells: 24K, 999, 9999, Au999, G999 on Chinese shop chops; Au750 / G18K = 18K; Au916 = 22K; Pt950 / Pt900 / Pt990 for platinum (Sky Jems, GB 11887).
S925 / S990 / 999 — modern Chinese silver jewelry.
Chinese export silver (WH 90, LW, TC, ZS, pseudo-hallmarks) is a separate, collector market: see `chinese-export-silver`. This entry does not repeat it.

egyptian-perfume-bottles.title: Egyptian perfume bottles
egyptian-perfume-bottles.full: Egyptian perfume bottles (Cairo/Khan el-Khalili workshop hand-blown Pyrex glass; no named makers)
egyptian-perfume-bottles.money: nothing in this type normally exceeds $50 per piece.
egyptian-perfume-bottles.fakes: The whole category is souvenir production; "antique Egyptian" claims are almost always wrong. Real ancient Egyptian glass (core-formed, opaque, small) is a completely different, museum-grade field and needs authenticatio
egyptian-perfume-bottles.buy: Never a buy for resale; pass on all Egyptian souvenir perfume bottles regardless of price unless a huge lot (20+) under $15.

electric-guitar-pickups.title: Electric guitar pickups
electric-guitar-pickups.full: Electric guitar pickups (Gibson, Seymour Duncan, DiMarzio, EMG, Fender, vintage PAF)
electric-guitar-pickups.fakes: Fake PAF stickers on later pickups, re-stickered Patent-number pickups, and boutique "PAF replicas" sold as originals exist; vintage claims need baseplate, solder and bobbin inspection by someone experienced (general kno
electric-guitar-pickups.buy: Any "old Gibson pickup" with a PAF or patent-number sticker under $300; boutique sets under $80; pass modern Gibson/Duncan at market.

elvis-memorabilia.title: Elvis Presley memorabilia
elvis-memorabilia.full: Elvis Presley memorabilia (Elvis Presley Enterprises 1956 merchandise, RCA records, concert items, McCormick decanters, life-size statues, modern licensed goods)
elvis-memorabilia.money: life-size resin/fiberglass statues $500-2500 local pickup (general knowledge, verify)
elvis-memorabilia.fakes: Forged autographs are endemic - requires PSA/JSA/Beckett, outside Dylan's rules. Reproduction concert posters and tickets common. Also: counterfeit Sun records (coloured vinyl, or fakes made with genuine leftover Sun lab
elvis-memorabilia.buy: Only 1956-57 Elvis Presley Enterprises-marked merchandise or concert ephemera ≤ $40; pass on statues (size), autographs (authentication) and post-1977 souvenirs.
tells: "© 1956/1957 Elvis Presley Enterprises" (or "EPE"): the original fan merchandise.
"Boxcar" (Boxcar Enterprises) trademark: 1974–1981 (Mountain States Collector) — 1970s concert-era souvenirs.

"Elvis Presley Enterprises, Inc." with later dates / Graceland: the EPE name reverted to Graceland in 1982 — anything with a later EPE date is post-death licensed product. Modern goods also show Authentic Brands Group (ABG) licensing.

emglo-air-compressors.title: Contractor air compressors
emglo-air-compressors.full: Contractor air compressors (Emglo, Rol-Air, Thomas, Makita MAC)
emglo-air-compressors.fakes: None known; brand rebadges (Emglo → DeWalt) only. Note the Emglo name later appeared on DeWalt-era and Jenny-era products; old US-made Emglos are the ones contractors want.
emglo-air-compressors.buy: Emglo/Rol-Air/Makita under $60 within driving distance; local resale only; pass anything that must ship.

endorsed-baseball-gloves.title: Vintage player-endorsed baseball gloves
endorsed-baseball-gloves.full: Vintage player-endorsed baseball gloves (Rawlings, Wilson, Spalding, MacGregor)
endorsed-baseball-gloves.fakes: Rawlings and Wilson have issued heritage/reissue gloves; added "autographs" on facsimile-stamped gloves are a risk (general knowledge, verify).
endorsed-baseball-gloves.buy: USA-made Mantle/Mays/Clemente/Koufax pro model ≤ $40, boxed ≤ $100; pass youth models, repaired lacing, DF1/MMF ≥ $45.

english-ironstone.title: English ironstone
english-ironstone.full: English ironstone (Mason's Patent Ironstone, Ashworth, Hicks & Meigh, Spode Stone China, Wedgwood/Meakin/Mellor white ironstone, Johnson Bros, Alfred Meakin, J&G Meakin)
english-ironstone.money: early (1813–1840) Mason's large jugs, tureens and 19th-c. white ironstone tureens/pitchers $100–600.
english-ironstone.fakes: - Ashworth reissued early Mason's patterns for 100+ years — the main source of "1800s" mis-dating. Check the mark carefully. - White ironstone has few fakes; modern "farmhouse" ironstone reproductions from China exist (l
english-ironstone.buy: Buy only pre-1850 Mason's/Ashworth large pieces (jugs, tureens, platters) or 19th-c. white ironstone tureens and pitchers at ≤ $50; pass on 20th-c. plates and coffee sets.
tells: Dense, heavy, slightly grey-white stoneware-like earthenware patented by C.J. Mason in 1813, sold as hard-wearing "china".
Mason's Imari/chinoiserie: rich iron-red, cobalt, green and gilt over a printed outline; jugs with snake handles (octagonal "Hydra" jugs), rim soups, plates with flowering rock and dragons.
Later ironstone (1890–1990s): Johnson Bros, Meakin, Mason's (under Ashworth/Wedgwood) blue-printed dinnerware.

english-saddles.title: English saddles
english-saddles.full: English saddles (Stübben, Pessoa, Prestige; also CWD, Devoucoux, Antares, Passier, Wintec, Crosby)
english-saddles.fakes: Counterfeit/badged no-name saddles with fake maker stamps exist in the low end (general knowledge, verify). Check that the serial number format and stamp style match the brand; for Stübben the serial can be traced throug
tells: Tree width is not standard across brands: some use cm between the tree points, others narrow/medium/wide; a Stübben 32 doesn't fit like a Prestige 32; roughly 27 = narrow, 30 = medium, 32 = wide (Equine Ink). Estimating from photos: fist test at the gullet, D-

Type by flap: close contact = forward-cut flap, minimal knee roll, shallow seat; all-purpose/general purpose = moderately forward flap and deeper seat; dressage = long, straight flap, deep seat, usually long billets (short girth); monoflap = single flap combin

Where size is marked: Crosby put "M" or "W" on the near-side stirrup bar; Stübben marks tree width on the far-side billet guard in cm (28–32 cm, 31 = medium) and older Stübbens used letters A–D, which can wear off (EquiSearch). Stübben, Passier and Hermès sadd

english-teapots.title: English Teapots
english-teapots.full: English Teapots (James Sadler, Arthur Wood, Price Kensington, Wade, Royal Albert, Wedgwood, Minton, Shelley)
english-teapots.money: Sadler racing car / Clarice Cliff / Shelley Art Deco $100–600+ (general knowledge, verify)
english-teapots.fakes: Clarice Cliff fakes exist (wrong backstamp, muddy painting). Sadler racing car reissued (later versions with "Sadler" printed and slightly different colors); Churchill reissued Sadler designs post-2000. Floral pots are n
english-teapots.buy: Pass on floral Sadler/Arthur Wood pots above ~$10; hunt novelty Sadler (racing car OKT42), Clarice Cliff, Shelley, chintz (Royal Winton) and Art Deco shapes priced as "grandma's teapot".

etched-glass-stemware.title: Etched and cut glass stemware and pitchers
etched-glass-stemware.full: Etched and cut glass stemware and pitchers (Fostoria, Cambridge, Heisey, Tiffin, Duncan & Miller, Seneca, Libbey Rock Sharpe, Morgantown, Central; modern Toscany, Princess House)
etched-glass-stemware.money: Cambridge Rose Point, coloured-stem and rare patterns $25–80+ per stem, sets of 8–12 $200–700.
etched-glass-stemware.fakes: Little faking of elegant patterns; Fostoria made some later reissues (Lenox era 1980s). Mixed "sets" assembled from similar patterns are common — check that the etching and stem shape match.
etched-glass-stemware.buy: Buy only identifiable elegant-era plate-etched patterns (Rose Point, Chantilly, Navarre, Orchid, June Night) in sets of 8+ at ≤ $3–5 per stem; pass on unmarked wheel-cut floral and modern pitchers.
tells: Plate (acid) etching: a lace-like design printed with wax resist and etched with acid — fine, detailed, even depth; the hallmark of 1920s–50s "Elegant Glass" (Fostoria, Cambridge, Heisey, Tiffin, Duncan, Central, Morgantown).
Wheel cutting / grey cutting: simple daisies, leaves and stems ground with a copper wheel, left matte grey ("gray cut") — 1920s–70s, many small factories, unmarked (as in both sweep examples).
Needle etching: machine-traced thin parallel lines in bands (1920s–50s).

ethnic-folk-dolls.title: Ethnic / folk / souvenir costume dolls , Kachina , Japanese Hakata/Kokeshi/Gofun, Russian matryoshka, Native American beaded dolls, Klumpe, Lenci, Paris "Poupée" souvenirs, Peggy Nisbet, Mexican, Peruvian)
ethnic-folk-dolls.full: Ethnic / folk / souvenir costume dolls (Hill-tribe carved dolls (Hmong, Yao/Dao, Akha, Karen), Kachina (Hopi), Japanese Hakata/Kokeshi/Gofun, Russian matryoshka, Native American beaded dolls, Klumpe, Lenci, Paris "Poupée" souvenirs, Peggy Nisbet, Mexican, Peruvian)
ethnic-folk-dolls.money: Lenci felt dolls, early Japanese Gofun Ichimatsu, signed Hopi Katsina (Kachina) carvings, early 20th-century Native American beaded dolls $100–2,000+.
ethnic-folk-dolls.fakes: "Kachina" dolls imported from Asia/Mexico; fake Lenci; mass-produced "hill tribe" dolls sold in Chiang Mai night markets are the norm. Native American objects: watch for Indian Arts and Crafts Act misrepresentation – nev
ethnic-folk-dolls.buy: Pass tourist costume dolls (hill-tribe, Peruvian, Mexican, flag dolls, Dolls-of-the-World); buy only signed Hopi carvings, Lenci felt, old Japanese gofun/Hakata, signed creative kokeshi at ≤ 25% of the ladder – Native American items need provenance (pass if un
tells: Japanese: Hakata clay (painted fired clay figures, signed on base), Gofun/Ichimatsu (crushed-shell gesso faces, glass eyes, 1900s–40s), Kokeshi (lathe-turned wood, traditional vs creative, signed underneath), geisha souvenir dolls in glass cases (1950s–80s, $1
Hopi Katsina (Kachina): carved cottonwood root, painted; signed carvings by known artists valuable; Navajo-made/"Kachina-style" and Asian imports cheap.
European: Lenci (Turin, felt faces, 1920s–40s, side-glancing eyes), Klumpe (Spain, felt caricature 1950s), Roldan, Peggy Nisbet (UK, 1953–90s, tags), Paris souvenir "Poupée".

eurorack-modules.title: Eurorack synthesizer modules
eurorack-modules.full: Eurorack synthesizer modules (Make Noise, Mutable Instruments, Erica Synths, Endorphin.es, Intellijel, ALM, Noise Engineering, Doepfer, Behringer)
eurorack-modules.fakes: Mutable Instruments clones (open-source; panels sometimes say "uClouds", "Rings clone") sold as originals; check for the original MI logo and PCB markings (general knowledge, verify).
eurorack-modules.buy: Only a full case or "synth parts" lot from a non-musician at < 30% of the ModularGrid sum; pass musician sellers pricing per module.

eye-wash-cups.title: Eye wash cups and eye baths
eye-wash-cups.full: Eye wash cups and eye baths (John Wyeth & Brother, Lavoptik, Optrex, John Bull, Glasco, Murine; Victorian English hand-blown, ceramic and sterling silver eye baths)
eye-wash-cups.money: hand-blown Victorian pedestal cups, ceramic transfer-printed and sterling silver eye baths $60–300 (estimates).
eye-wash-cups.fakes: Modern hand-made or Chinese decorative "apothecary" eye cups in cobalt, amber and green exist, sold as antique — very crisp, sometimes with fake embossing, no wear on the foot. Carnival-glass iridescent cups are mostly m
eye-wash-cups.buy: Single cups almost never clear the profit bar; buy only lots of 15+ old cups at ≤ $2 each, or a hallmarked sterling or Victorian ceramic eye bath ≤ $25; pass ordinary cobalt and clear cups.
tells: A small (2–3" tall) cup with an oval rim shaped to fit the eye socket, usually on a short stem and round foot. Glass (clear, cobalt, green, amber, milk, uranium), ceramic, silver, aluminium, rubber/vulcanite and later plastic.

Forms: pedestal/stemmed (classic); "potbelly" or "squat" with no stem; cups that screw or cap onto a solution bottle (Wyeth, Lavoptik "bottle and cup" sets); double-ended; tulip, panelled, ribbed or barrel shapes.

Marks: embossed on the base or bowl — "WYETH", "LAVOPTIK", "OPTREX", "JOHN BULL" with patent date (1917), "GLASCO PAT", "MURINE", numbers. Ceramic eye baths may carry a chemist's/retailer's name; silver carries hallmarks.

farm-implement-wrenches.title: Farm implement wrenches
farm-implement-wrenches.full: Farm implement wrenches (International Harvester / McCormick / Deering, John Deere, Oliver, Moline Plow, J.I. Case, Avery, Superior Drill, Emerson-Brantingham, P&O, Ford/Fordson, Osborne, Tague & Kirlin)
farm-implement-wrenches.money: cut-out letter wrenches, hub wrenches with caps and patented combination tools $100–500
farm-implement-wrenches.fakes: Some reproduction cast-iron John Deere and IH "wrenches" and cut-outs exist (souvenir castings): crisp, sandy cast texture, too-perfect letters, wrong weight. Rare cut-outs should be bought from photos only at plain-wren
farm-implement-wrenches.buy: Buy lots only when ≥ 5 wrenches show legible cast maker names/part numbers or a cut-out/multi-end/patent piece is visible, at ≤ $2 per pound; pass anonymous rusty lots, Ford/car-kit wrenches and anything over ~25 lb unless a rarity shows.
tells: Wrenches supplied with a plow, planter, mower, binder or tractor to fit its nuts. Usually cast (malleable) iron or drop-forged steel, flat, 4–14" long, with open ends, box ends, square sockets or several openings ("multi-end"). The maker's name and part number
Cut-out wrenches have the maker's name cut right through the handle (letters are holes) — top tier.
Combination tools: wrench + hammer + screwdriver + pliers + thread die, often patent-dated (Chamberlain 1912, etc.).

fashion-watch-lots.title: Fashion watch lots and ladies' dress watches
fashion-watch-lots.full: Fashion watch lots and ladies' dress watches (fashion: Skechers, Kathy Ireland, Fossil, Guess, Anne Klein, Armitron, Geneva, Timex; mid-tier: ESQ/Movado Group, Bulova, Seiko, Citizen; sleepers: Jostens and other service-award watches, solid-gold-cased ladies' mechanicals)
fashion-watch-lots.money: solid-14K ladies' mechanical cases $200–450 (gold melt driven)
fashion-watch-lots.fakes: - Fake luxury watches (Rolex, Omega, Cartier, Michael Kors copies) appear in lots constantly: never buy or list a watch as a luxury brand without authentication. - "14K" stamps on plated Asian watches exist. Test with an
fashion-watch-lots.buy: Ignore fashion brands; buy only when the dial or case-back photos show "14K"/"18K" solid (not GF/RGP/plated) or a known collectible mechanical reference, at ≤ 25% of melt or sold median.
tells: Dial text: "21 Jewels" or "17 Jewels" plus "Swiss" = mechanical (not quartz, whatever the seller says). "Quartz" on the dial = battery.

Case-back stamps: "14K", "18K", "0.585", "0.750" with no "GF", "RGP", "Gold Filled", "Plated" or "Base metal back" = solid gold. "10K RGP", "10K GF", "Gold Electroplate" and "Stainless steel back" = not solid.
Wear: brass showing through on lugs and edges = plated or filled. Solid gold doesn't brass.

fat-lava-pottery.title: West German "fat lava" pottery
fat-lava-pottery.full: West German "fat lava" pottery (Scheurich, Roth, Ruscha, Bay Keramik, Carstens, Jopeko, Otto Keramik, ES Keramik, Dümler & Breiden, Spara)
fat-lava-pottery.money: rare Otto, Ruscha "Vulcano" and best glazes $300–1,500 (ES Keramik mostly sells low: Terapeak median $20).
fat-lava-pottery.fakes: Modern Chinese "lava-style" vases; some contemporary studio work. Marks and shape numbers help. - Ruscha forms continued under Scheurich after 1996 (Modern Redux), so a Ruscha shape number alone does not prove 1950s–70s
fat-lava-pottery.buy: Buy West German pottery with bold bubbly lava glazes and numbered bases under ~$40; crackle-paint resin lamp bodies and US/Chinese decor are pass.
tells: Base mark format: shape (model) number, usually three digits, then height in cm, e.g. Scheurich 242-22 (Wikipedia; Peacock). Ruscha sometimes adds a single size digit after the form number, e.g. 311/5 (Modern Redux).
Seller words: "WGP", "West German", "fat lava", "MCM vase", "Keramik", "W. Germany pottery", "lava lamp" (often meaning a lamp base, not a liquid lava lamp).

Period: West German art pottery was made 1949–1990, mostly in the Westerwald; over 100 potteries; the heyday ran 1950s–70s (Wikipedia; Peacock). "W. Germany"/"West Germany" means made 1949–1990; unmarked or "Germany" alone may be pre-1949 or post-1990 (Peacock

felt-souvenir-pennants.title: Felt souvenir pennants
felt-souvenir-pennants.full: Felt souvenir pennants (1910s–1970s travel, college and sports pennants; Chicago Pennant Co., Trench Mfg, Crown Pennant, Keezer, Asco, souvenir makers)
felt-souvenir-pennants.money: World's Fair, early national parks, 1920s–30s college and vintage MLB/NFL team pennants $40–500 each (pre-1970 named-team, roster and championship pieces
felt-souvenir-pennants.fakes: - Modern reproductions of sports pennants (Mitchell & Ness, Wincraft throwbacks) exist; usually labelled. Some reproduction World's Fair pennants. - Modern repros use thin synthetic felt, bright digital prints and modern
felt-souvenir-pennants.buy: Buy lots of 15+ travel pennants at ≤ $2 each, or any sports/World's Fair/pre-1950 pennant at ≤ $15; pass on single 1960s–70s travel pennants above $5.
tells: Title words: "vintage felt pennant", "souvenir pennant", "1950s", "wool felt", "full size", "roster", "World Series", "World's Fair".
Triangular wool or rayon felt pennants with screen-printed scenes, flocked letters and a contrasting header strip with ties.

Age tells: 1910s–40s wool felt with sewn-on felt letters or tassels; 1930s–60s printed graphics on felt, sometimes with factory colour embellishments (AntiqueSportsShop); 1950s–60s screen-printed colourful scenes (roadside attractions, turnpikes, parks); 1970s

fenton-art-glass.title: Fenton art glass
fenton-art-glass.full: Fenton art glass (Fenton Art Glass Co., plus look-alikes: Mosser, Boyd, Imperial, Westmoreland, L.G. Wright, Northwood)
fenton-art-glass.money: rare colours and off-hand art glass (Karnak, Mosaic, Hanging Hearts) $300–2,000+.
fenton-art-glass.fakes: Fenton reissued its own carnival and hobnail shapes many times; the moulded logo with a decade number dates them. Chinese copies of Fenton fairy lamps and hobnail exist (lighter, thinner, no mark). L.G. Wright and Mosser
fenton-art-glass.buy: Buy only Fenton cranberry/Burmese/Rosalene/Connoisseur, early carnival or stretch glass, big lamps (careful shipping) and off-hand art glass at ≤ $25; pass on milk glass, amber/colonial hobnail, 1990s–2000s hand-painted gift pieces and anything priced above $4
tells: Marks: oval "Fenton" moulded in the base from 1970 (with decade digit added: "8" under the logo 1980s, "9" 1990s, "0" 2000s); script "F" in an oval for pieces made from Verlys/other moulds (1983+). Paper oval labels "Fenton Handpainted in USA" with script F (1
Hand-painted: decorator's signature on the base (e.g., "S. Kibbe", "D. Barbour") plus a Fenton family signature on some special issues (Bill, Frank, Shelley, George, Don Fenton) which adds little.
Hobnail: raised dots; opalescent (white-tipped) and cranberry hobnail are wanted; amber, colonial blue, colonial green 1960s–70s hobnail is common.

fiesta-ware.title: Fiesta ware
fiesta-ware.full: Fiesta ware (Homer Laughlin China Co.; also sister lines Harlequin, Riviera, Kitchen Kraft, Fiesta Ironstone, Post-86 Fiesta)
fiesta-ware.money: medium green, rare forms (tripod candleholders, syrup, comport, onion soups, vases) $120–1,500+.
fiesta-ware.fakes: Post-86 Fiesta reissued many shapes in new colours, including the bulb candleholder and disk pitcher – learn the colour differences. Fiesta lookalikes: Vernon Kilns "Early California", Bauer, Taylor Smith & Taylor "Luray
fiesta-ware.buy: Buy only vintage (1936–72) serving pieces in medium green, red, cobalt, or 1950s colours and rare forms at ≤ 1/3 sold median; pass single plates/bowls and anything Post-86.
tells: Concentric rings: vintage plates have rings on the rim; fruit bowls ("nappies" and 5½" fruits) have rings inside the centre (example 7949371872).

Marks: vintage = ink stamp "Fiesta HLC USA" (lowercase "fiesta" in Art Deco script) or in-mold "fiesta / HLC USA"; many vintage pieces are unmarked (chop plates, candleholders, cups, some bowls). Post-86 = in-mold "FIESTA ® HLC USA" with a capital F and ® plus
Feet: vintage foot rings are typically glazed, with three small sagger-pin dots or a dry (unglazed) narrow ring; Post-86 have a wider dry foot.

figural-planters.title: Figural planters
figural-planters.full: Figural planters (Shawnee, McCoy, Hull, Royal Copley, Napco/Inarco lady head vases, Relpo, Lefton, Napcoware, Japanese export, Holland Mold hobby ceramics)
figural-planters.money: 1950s–60s Japanese lady head vases (Napco, Inarco, Relpo, Lefton) $40–250, large with jewellery and lashes $150–400.
figural-planters.fakes: Reproduction head vases from China since 2000s (heavier, poorer facial paint, no wear). McCoy marks faked on Chinese planters.
figural-planters.buy: Pass on hobby/ceramics-class figures; buy lady head vases with eyelashes/pearl earrings at ≤ $25 and marked Shawnee/McCoy figurals at ≤ $10.
tells: Lady head vases: glossy porcelain woman's head/bust, painted face, applied pearl necklace/earrings, real-looking hair-curl moulding, often stiff black lashes, gloved hand at the cheek. Paper label or stamped "Napco", "Inarco E-xxxx", "Relpo", "Lefton", "Japan"
American art pottery figurals: McCoy, Shawnee, Hull, Royal Copley — even airbrushed glazes, unglazed dry foot with moulded mark (McCoy "USA", Shawnee "USA 7xx").
Hobby/ceramics-class: thick, chalky bisque with matte acrylic or "stain" paint, sometimes scratched initials and date underneath — 1970s–80s home ceramics (Holland Mold, Atlantic Mold). Low value.

figural-table-lamps.title: Figural table lamps
figural-table-lamps.full: Figural table lamps (Frankart, Nuart, Moss, Kron/Texans, Royal Haeger, Lane, Shawnee, Claes, Gilbert, Japanese moriage/Satsuma-style, porcelain courting-couple, 1990s–2000s resin fantasy)
figural-table-lamps.money: Frankart/Nuart Art Deco nude lamps and Moss lucite figurals $250–2,000+.
figural-table-lamps.fakes: - Frankart and Art Deco nude lamps are heavily reproduced (resin and brass, 1980s–present, "Art Deco style" imports). - Moss-style lucite lamps reproduced by small makers (2000s). - Blackamoor ceramic heads reproduced/im
figural-table-lamps.buy: The money is in Art Deco metal nudes with glass globes (Frankart/Nuart) and Moss lucite figurals – buy at ≤ $80 if complete and marked; pass resin fantasy, pottery boudoir and porcelain courting-couple lamps unless ≤ $15, and never buy for eBay anything eBay's
tells: Art Deco metal (1925–40): Frankart (Brooklyn), Nuart, Dodge, JB Hirsch, Ronson – spelter/white metal with green-bronze or gold "art finish", stylised nude women holding or dancing around a crackle or frosted glass globe/cylinder; base stamped "Frankart Inc. Pa

Moss Manufacturing (San Francisco, 1937–68): Lucite/plexiglass panels with ceramic figurines (often Dorothy Kindell or Hedi Schoop figures), revolving turntables, built-in planters – unmistakable clear plastic sheet frames.

MCM pottery TV lamps (1945–65): Kron (Texans Inc.) and Royal Haeger black/green panthers, gazelles, stallions; Claes ceramic; Lane (Van Nuys) figurals; Shawnee and Royal Haeger "Blackamoor/Nubian" head lamps with turbans; sizes 8–15 in, often with built-in pla

figurines-lladro-hummel-precious-moments.title: Porcelain figurines: Lladró, Hummel, Precious Moments, Cherished Teddies, collector plates
figurines-lladro-hummel-precious-moments.full: Porcelain figurines: Lladró, Hummel, Precious Moments, Cherished Teddies, collector plates (also Nao, Boyds, Willow Tree, Royal Copenhagen / Bing & Grøndahl)
figurines-lladro-hummel-precious-moments.fakes: Hummel reissues of old models with later marks; Chinese Lladró look-alikes and fakes with painted logos; Hummel-style figurines by other makers (general knowledge, verify). - A Lladró made after 1960 with no mark is like
figurines-lladro-hummel-precious-moments.buy: Pass by default. Buy only Hummel full-bee/crown mark under $40 or Lladró limited edition under 25% of comps.
tells: Lladró: glossy pastel blue/grey, blue backstamp with tulip logo + number. Most $40–120 sold; large groups/limited editions $300–1,500 (e.g. "Old Man with Violin" 5x= depends on number; nuns ~$60–100). [Note: the "5x=" fragment is garbled in the original text;

Hummel (Goebel): brown-eyed children, bee/V mark on base. TMK-1/2 (1935–59 "crown"/"full bee") $80–300; TMK-5+ $15–40. Large (7"+) and early = only ones worth it. The base also carries the incised mould number ("Hum" number) and the "M.I. Hummel" signature inc

Precious Moments: teardrop-eye children; $5–25 except first-year (1978–79, no mark/triangle) rare pieces $50–200. [Note: the triangle annual mark dates from 1981; 1978–80 pieces have no annual mark ("original 21" are the 1978 issues) – general knowledge, verif

film-cameras.title: Film cameras
film-cameras.full: Film cameras (35 mm SLR / rangefinder / compact / cine; Nikon, Canon, Olympus, Pentax, Minolta, Contax, Leica, Bell & Howell, Bolex)
film-cameras.money: Leica, Contax T2/T3, F3HP, Hasselblad, Mamiya 7 $500–3,000.
film-cameras.fakes: Fake Leicas (Soviet Zorki/FED bodies re-engraved as Leica) are common; check serial numbers and engraving (general knowledge, verify). Specific tells of a Zorki/FED conversion (Mike Eckman): - The exposure counter and sh
film-cameras.buy: Collectible body+lens < 40% of sold median with "works"; any Leica/Contax/Hasselblad/mju-II under $100; pass decent tier at $40+ and Polaroid/Disc.
tells: Look-alikes: Soviet Zorki/FED and Kiev bodies look like Leica and Contax rangefinders (see Fakes). Store brands were made by the big Japanese makers: Sears/Tower (Mamiya, Ricoh, Fujica), Revue, Vivitar, and Argus Cosina. They resell for $20–80, not as the make

Where the identifiers sit: the model name is on the prism front or top plate. The serial number is on the top plate (Leica, Nikon F-series), the back of the body, or the base plate. The lens name, focal length, f-number and serial are on the front name ring.
Seller title words: "old camera", "vintage camera with case", "box of cameras", "estate camera lot", "Leica style", "untested", "as is".

film-slr-cameras.title: 35 mm film SLRs, rangefinders & lenses
film-slr-cameras.full: 35 mm film SLRs, rangefinders & lenses (Minolta, Canon, Nikon, Pentax, Olympus, Leica, Contax, Exakta, Yashica)
film-slr-cameras.money: Leica M, Contax T2/T3/G2, Hasselblad, Rolleiflex, FM3A, GR1, Hexar $500–4,000+.
film-slr-cameras.fakes: Fake Leicas (Soviet FED/Zorki bodies re-engraved) are common – authenticate serials (general knowledge, verify). Otherwise little faking.
film-slr-cameras.buy: The lens is the money. Buy kits/lots ≤ $60 showing a fast prime or collectible body (seller ships), tested common body + prime ≤ $40, cult compacts < $100, medium format < $200; pass single common bodies at $70+, untested electronic bodies, fungus, pickup-only
tells: Yashica FX-3 Super 2000: plastic-top Contax/Yashica-mount body – valued for the mount, not itself.
Pentax Spotmatic (SP/SPII/SPF, "Asahi Pentax" on prism, M42 screw lens, 1964–76); Pentax K1000 (K-mount, 1976–97; the student camera, plain chrome, holds value).
Olympus OM-1/OM-2/OM-4: small, shutter-speed ring around the lens mount.

filmstrip-projectors.title: Filmstrip projectors
filmstrip-projectors.full: Filmstrip projectors (DuKane, SVE Picturol, Standard Projector & Equipment Co., Viewlex, Bell & Howell, GAF/Graflex, Spencer Delineascope)
filmstrip-projectors.money: Art Deco 1930s SVE/Spencer models $60-150 (general knowledge, verify)
filmstrip-projectors.buy: Pass unless ≤ $20, tested with lamp lit, and cased or Deco-styled.
tells: 1920s–1930s "Picturol" era — small cylindrical or upright black-enamel or nickel projectors, often in a fitted wooden case; SVE (Society for Visual Education, Chicago) coined "Picturol" for its filmstrip rolls and projectors. Models in the Eastman Museum inclu

1930s–1950s lantern/filmstrip combos — Spencer Lens Co. (Buffalo NY) Delineascope (models D, M, MK3, SA) and Filmascope; black sheet-metal or crackle-finish bodies with chrome trim; some take glass lantern slides too.
1950s–1970s classroom units — wrinkle-finish cast aluminium in tan, grey or brown; Viewlex, Standard (500 series), SVE, Bell & Howell, Graflex/GAF, DuKane.

filson-clothing.title: Filson waxed and wool clothing
filson-clothing.full: Filson waxed and wool clothing (C.C. Filson Co., Seattle – Tin Cloth, Shelter Cloth, Cover Cloth, Mackinaw wool)
filson-clothing.fakes: - Some knockoff waxed jackets with Filson-like labels exist (general knowledge, verify). - Filson's own reissues and current production use older patterns; dating relies on label and tags, not cut. - Sellers sometimes ca
tells: Mackinaw: dense virgin wool in plaid or solid. Label: "C.C. Filson Co. Seattle WA" inside the collar or on the waistband; older labels are said to say "Since 1897" and "Made in USA" (general knowledge, verify).
Heavy outdoor workwear from C.C. Filson (Seattle, founded 1897 by Clinton C. Filson; HistoryLink).

Tin Cloth: stiff, oil-finish waxed cotton duck, the heaviest Filson canvas, in tan/"dark tan"/otter green, often with a darker mottled waxed look; smells waxy when warm. Shelter Cloth: medium-weight cotton duck, oil or dry finish, more tightly woven. Cover Clo

fish-spearing-decoys.title: Fish spearing decoys & duck decoys
fish-spearing-decoys.full: Fish spearing decoys (ice-fishing decoys) & duck decoys (Oscar Peterson, Hans Janner, Bud Stewart, Lake Chautauqua; Mason, Herter's, Victor/Animal Trap)
fish-spearing-decoys.money: top Mt. Clemens carvers (Hans Janner) have reached $69,000–168,000 at Guyette & Deeter.
fish-spearing-decoys.fakes: Artificially aged "antique" fish decoys and carvings in the style of Peterson are common; real wear vs faux distressing is the key judgment (general knowledge, verify). Peterson is documented as "widely copied and counte
fish-spearing-decoys.buy: Visibly old fish decoy (crazed paint, tin fins, lead belly) ≤ $30, or anything a seller attributes to Peterson/Stewart/Mason ≤ $100; pass new decor carvings.
tells: Old ones (1900–50s) have worn paint, hand-cut tin or copper fins, folk-art character; named carvers (Oscar Peterson, Hans Janner, Bud Stewart, Lake Chautauqua) bring big money. New ones by living carvers are decor ($15–40).

History that dates pieces: Michigan outlawed ice spearing c.1910 (except some Native use); when the ban ended around the start of the Depression, spearing boomed and factories (e.g. South Bend) made mass-produced decoys, now also collected (fishdecoy.com histo

Species seen: trout, perch, sucker, pike, bass, shad, bluegill/sunfish, walleye, muskie, plus frogs, polliwogs and minnows. Odd species (frog, polliwog, sucker, shad) and large sizes are worth more than a plain generic "fish".

fishing-tackle-lots.title: Fishing tackle lots
fishing-tackle-lots.full: Fishing tackle lots (vintage lures, reels, rods: Heddon, Creek Chub, Pflueger, Shakespeare, South Bend, Paw Paw, Bomber, Penn, ABU)
fishing-tackle-lots.money: boxed early lures, Pflueger Supreme / early ABU Ambassadeur reels $50–400 (general knowledge, verify)
fishing-tackle-lots.fakes: Heddon/Creek Chub reissues in wood (1990s–2000s "Collector" series) and repainted "folk art" lures sold as old. Modern lures copying old shapes (Pikie, Plunker, Game Fisher-style plugs are still made) are not fakes but a
fishing-tackle-lots.buy: Buy only lots showing wooden glass-eye lures, lure boxes, or named vintage reels (ABU red, Pflueger Supreme, early Shakespeare) at ≤ $40; pass on spoons/jigs/saltwater bucktails.
tells: Reels: maker's name and model engraved on the side plate or foot; ABU Ambassadeurs carry a serial and a name plate.

Wood vs plastic from a photo: wood shows paint crazing ("age lines"), chipped paint revealing grain at the nose and hook hangers, and slightly irregular shapes; plastic has crisp mould seams, a glossy uniform finish and moulded or painted eyes.

Side-hook minnows (three or five trebles along the sides, some with six) and see-through hook mounts are early (c. 1900–1920s); the Shakespeare Wooden Minnow used clip/plate side hooks for about ten years from 1906 (MDC).

fluorescent-desk-lamps.title: Fluorescent desk lamps
fluorescent-desk-lamps.full: Fluorescent desk lamps (Art Specialty Co "Lite Master", Eagle, Faries, Dazor, Luxo, Industrial Lamp Corp, generic 1940s–60s office)
fluorescent-desk-lamps.money: Dazor/Luxo/Lite Master with chrome or two-tone and working original ballast $100–250 (general knowledge, verify)
fluorescent-desk-lamps.fakes: Little faking. Modern "industrial" reproductions (Restoration Hardware-style, Pottery Barn) use LED or incandescent bulbs, not fluorescent tubes, and have new hardware — easy to tell. Repainted lamps are the main "misrep
fluorescent-desk-lamps.buy: Only buy the streamline "flying wing" or chrome/two-tone Art Deco versions under ~$40, complete with original diffuser/shade and reportedly working; pass on plain crinkle-finish office pedestals.
tells: Flying wing / streamline: hood with swept, tapering wing-like ends, often a curved "tail" pedestal; Art Deco or Streamline Moderne styling. This is the desirable look (Art Specialty Co "Lite Master", some Eagle and Faries models).
Articulated drafting/task: Dazor floating-arm, Luxo L-1 with circline tube and magnifier — a different collector market (task-lighting users, industrial décor).
Pedestal "tombstone": rectangular slab hood on a stepped, flared square base with ribbed neck (the pid 7929762122 type). Common, plain.

fly-reels.title: Fly reels
fly-reels.full: Fly reels (Hardy, Scientific Anglers System 2, Pflueger Medalist; also Orvis, Ross, Abel)
fly-reels.money: Hardy Perfect/Marquis $150–400 (Terapeak 365d: Perfect median $325, Marquis median $162.50)
fly-reels.fakes: Hardy has re-issued Perfect models; check vintage details (general knowledge, verify). Current Hardy-made replicas include the **1921 Wide Spool Perfect** (sold new by Pure Fishing/Hardy and fly shops) and **brass-faced

folk-art-painted-wares.title: Folk-art painted wares
folk-art-painted-wares.full: Folk-art painted wares (Pennsylvania Dutch/German painted woodenware and tinware, tole, Peter Hunt, Bauernmalerei, Rosemaling, painted buckets, firkins, boxes, trays)
folk-art-painted-wares.money: 19th c. original-paint firkins, boxes and tinware $150–1,500
folk-art-painted-wares.fakes: Old buckets/boxes repainted in "PA Dutch" style to pass as original; reproduction distelfink pieces from Lancaster County gift shops; fake aged paint. Also: new tin "country" boxes artificially rusted; reproduction Penns
folk-art-painted-wares.buy: Buy 19th c. original-paint wood/tin pieces (square nails, hand-forged bails, wear on paint) or signed known decorators (Peter Hunt) at ≤ 25% of resale; pass on unsigned mid-century decor pieces above ~$20.
tells: Firkin / sugar bucket: lidded stave bucket with a wooden bail handle and bentwood (finger-lapped) bands held by small tacks. Original 19th c. paint is usually a single colour (blue, red, mustard, green); decorated firkins are rarer.
Wastebasket / bucket: mid-century open stave or slab bucket, often black or red ground with stencilled or freehand PA Dutch motifs — the commonest form on Craigslist.
Document box / deed box: tin box with domed lid and wire bail; the classic 19th c. "country tin" form.

foot-warmers.title: Foot warmers and metal hot-water bottles
foot-warmers.full: Foot warmers and metal hot-water bottles (galvanized zinc "pigs", copper/brass bed warmers, stoneware pigs, soapstone, carriage foot stoves)
foot-warmers.fakes: Decorative warming pans widely reproduced 1920s–70s; foot stoves reproduced as "primitives" with modern punched tin and nails. Zinc bottles not usually faked (too cheap).
foot-warmers.buy: Pass on zinc ovals; buy only 19th-c. pierced-tin wood-frame foot stoves or marked stoneware pigs at ≤ $40.

framed-needlepoint.title: Framed needlepoint and petit point
framed-needlepoint.full: Framed needlepoint and petit point (still lifes, florals, pastoral scenes; Austrian/Viennese petit point, mid-century American kits, Bucilla, Paragon, Columbia-Minerva)
framed-needlepoint.money: 19th-century Berlin woolwork pictures in period frames $100–400 (general knowledge, verify).
framed-needlepoint.fakes: Machine-made "tapestry" pictures (woven jacquard) are often sold as needlepoint — woven pieces have a flat, uniform surface and no diagonal stitches.
framed-needlepoint.buy: Buy only fine petit point (Austrian, signed or labelled) or 19th-c. Berlin woolwork at ≤ 25% of sold and only if it fits a passenger seat; pass on kit gros point.
tells: Berlin woolwork (c.1830–1880): bright aniline wools, sometimes with glass beads or silk highlights, in rosewood or gilt Victorian frames.

Gros point / kit needlepoint (1950s–80s): large visible stitches, stepped "pixel" edges (like the example), wool yarns, printed-canvas kit designs (fruit baskets, florals, pastoral copies). Decorator gilt frames with velvet liners are typical of the 1960s–80s.
Petit point: tiny stitches (often 18–40 per inch) that read like a painting from a distance, usually Austrian ("Made in Austria" label), often with a small figurative scene.

franklin-mint-collectibles.title: Franklin Mint collectibles
franklin-mint-collectibles.full: Franklin Mint collectibles (House of Fabergé eggs and carousel figures, die-cast cars, pewter, porcelain dolls, sterling medals/ingots)
franklin-mint-collectibles.money: sterling silver medal sets and ingots = melt value ($50–1,500+ by weight
franklin-mint-collectibles.fakes: Not faked; but "Fabergé" naming misleads sellers into Russian-Fabergé prices. Post-2003 revived "Franklin Mint" products exist under the old name.
franklin-mint-collectibles.buy: Ignore figurines/plates; buy only Franklin Mint STERLING (marked .925/sterling) below melt, or boxed 1:24 die-cast with paperwork at ≤ $40.
tells: Correction on origin: the company was founded in 1964 by Joseph M. Segel as General Numismatics Corporation in Yeadon, PA, renamed Franklin Mint (listed 1967), and later based at Franklin Center, PA (CoinWeek). "Wawa" is imprecise. It stopped producing medals,

Business history that matters for value: high issue prices and almost no secondary market, so most pieces sell for a fraction of issue price (publicised by a 1978 *60 Minutes* report); silver pieces are protected by their metal value.
Marks: "Franklin Mint" or "FM" on bases and packaging; "F/M" mintmark on some early medals; ".925" or "STERLING" on silver; artist marks such as Gilroy Roberts' "GR".

frankoma-pottery.title: Frankoma pottery
frankoma-pottery.full: Frankoma pottery (Frank Pottery / Frankoma, Norman then Sapulpa, Oklahoma)
frankoma-pottery.money: rare sculptures (Joseph Taylor), Pot & Puma mark, early Norman pieces $150–1,000+.
frankoma-pottery.fakes: Frankoma reissued earlier moulds in red clay (check clay colour). Few outright fakes.
frankoma-pottery.buy: Pass on red-clay (Sapulpa) Frankoma; buy Ada-clay (cream/tan body) figurines and "Frank Potteries/Pot & Puma" marked pieces at ≤ $20.

fraternal-memorabilia.title: Fraternal memorabilia
fraternal-memorabilia.full: Fraternal memorabilia (Shriners/AAONMS, Masonic, Knights Templar, Odd Fellows, Elks, Knights of Pythias)
fraternal-memorabilia.money: early folk-art regalia, painted aprons, rare 1890s convention pieces $300–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
fraternal-memorabilia.fakes: Few. Some modern "Masonic" reproduction swords and aprons exist.
fraternal-memorabilia.buy: Pass on common Shrine/KT convention mugs above ~$15 unless it's a rare year/city or figural form; buy early painted Masonic aprons and folk-art pieces at ≤ 1/3 of resale.

french-gilt-bronze-andirons.title: French gilt-bronze andirons
french-gilt-bronze-andirons.full: French gilt-bronze andirons (chenets) (Louis XV, Louis XVI, Napoleon III; Bouhon, Barbedienne; repros by Virginia Metalcrafters and Italian/Spanish makers)
french-gilt-bronze-andirons.fakes: Large 20th-c. repro output in the same styles; mid-century Italian/Spanish copies and Virginia Metalcrafters pieces are the usual look-alikes. Tell by back casting, chasing and weight.
french-gilt-bronze-andirons.buy: Chased rococo/Louis XVI pair with log bars and verdigris under $200; pass bright smooth repros, singles, and sellers who already say "chenets/ormolu" at $500+.

french-hallmarks.title: French hallmarks
french-hallmarks.full: French hallmarks (eagle's head 18k gold, owl, rhinoceros, Minerva silver, crab and boar's head small silver, dog's head platinum, maker's lozenge, doublé; Puiforcat, Christofle, Odiot, Boucheron, Cartier Paris, René Lalique)
french-hallmarks.fakes: - Fake eagle's-head stamps on cheap gold-plated jewelry exist but are uncommon; true marks are crisp, in a shaped cartouche, and sit next to a lozenge (general knowledge, verify). - Modern Lalique glass pendants and "Lal
french-hallmarks.buy: An eagle's head, owl, dog's head or Minerva is a guarantee of metal: buy at ≤ 80% of melt from a sharp photo of the mark; a lozenge alone proves nothing about metal; "doublé", "plaqué" and "métal argenté" are not gold or silver; pay maker premiums only for a r
tells: Eagle's head (tête d'aigle) = 18k gold, 750, French manufacture, from 1838 to present; the most frequent gold mark on new and vintage French pieces (Artcurial; Spectra; Vintagesieraden). Paris and departmental versions differ in the shape of the cartouche and

Horse's head (tête de cheval): 18k gold from the departments (outside Paris) until 1919 (Vintagesieraden; Antique Jewel gives 1838–1919 for a gold mark shown). Sources disagree on the horse's head details (Skyjems wrongly calls it a platinum mark, contradicted
Before 1919, large gold works also bore a medical-man head (tête de médecin) with a titre number 1, 2 or 3 (920 / 840 / 750) (general knowledge, verify).

furbys.title: Furbys
furbys.full: Furbys (1998–2001 Tiger Electronics originals; Furby Babies; Hasbro 2005/2012 reissues)
furbys.fakes: Hasbro 2005/2012 reissues and knock-off "Furby-like" toys get listed as "original"; check the Tiger logo, model number 70-8xx and the box design.
furbys.buy: NIB first-gen 70-800 ≤ $20 each, special-edition NIB ≤ $60; pass loose, Hasbro 2005+/2012, NIB common over $35.

fused-glass-art.title: Fused glass art
fused-glass-art.full: Fused glass art (Peggy Karr, Higgins Glass, Bullseye studio, Fiesta-era kilnformed, Annieglass, Mexican/Indian import)
fused-glass-art.money: Higgins (Michael & Frances Higgins) 1950s–60s signed pieces $100–800+ (general knowledge, verify)
fused-glass-art.fakes: Higgins knockoffs unsigned; Peggy Karr not widely faked. Higgins Glass Studio continues to make Rondelays and other designs — newer studio pieces are not Dearborn-era; check the signature style.
fused-glass-art.buy: Higgins is the target (signature "higgins" in gold on face); Peggy Karr only large platters ≤ $15 and only if local.
tells: Riverside studio (later): "Frances Stewart Higgins" on Frances's work; "Michael Higgins" with date and title on his sculptures.

Correction on Higgins marks: the gold screened "higgins" signature on the face is itself the Dearborn Glass (Bedford Park, IL) mark, 1957–1964 (Higgins Glass Studio FAQ); there is no separate "Dearborn" stamp — unsigned Dearborn pieces carried paper labels. Ro
Chicago studio, c. 1948–57: lowercase "higgins" signature; a stylised dancing-man figure sometimes cast in. Most important to museums and serious collectors.

galvanized-watering-cans.title: Galvanized watering cans
galvanized-watering-cans.full: Galvanized watering cans (Haws, Dennis, Wheeling, Dover, Behrens, Rowell, Thureau and other French "arrosoirs", unmarked American)
galvanized-watering-cans.money: marked 19th-c. French zinc/copper to $1,000+ retail (general knowledge, verify)
galvanized-watering-cans.fakes: Modern decorative galvanized cans (Target, Hobby Lobby), often thin with faux aging. "Haws pattern" cans by competitors since the late 1880s. Current-production Haws (1886 medallion) sold as antique. Replacement Haws med
galvanized-watering-cans.buy: Buy only French zinc, Haws (medallion), or copper/brass cans under ~$30; common American galvanized cans are a pass.

gas-cans.title: Vintage gas and safety cans
gas-cans.full: Vintage gas and safety cans (Justrite, Eagle, Protectoseal, George W. Diener, Gilbert & Barker, oil company branded cans, Blitz/Wedco jerry cans)
gas-cans.money: small early graphic cans $100-500 (general knowledge, verify)
gas-cans.fakes: Reproduction branded oil cans and fake "Texaco" decals are common. - Modern decorative "jerry cans" (often Chinese) imitate WWII cans but lack embossed maker/date markings. - Restored cans with new decals are sold as "or
gas-cans.buy: Only buy branded/graphic (oil company logo) cans ≤ $30, or embossed, maker-and-date-stamped WWII German cans ≤ $60; pass on plain red safety cans.

german-pocket-knives.title: German pocket and folding knives
german-pocket-knives.full: German pocket and folding knives (Puma, Boker, Henckels, Hen & Rooster, Wüsthof, Hubertus, Linder, Herder, Otter, Victorinox-type Solingen)
german-pocket-knives.money: Puma White Hunter, Game Warden, Bowie fixed blades and NOS with box/papers $150–500 (Terapeak + general knowledge, verify)
german-pocket-knives.fakes: Counterfeit Puma White Hunter and Puma folder copies from Pakistan/China exist (wrong logo font, no model number, "Puma" without Germany). Puma IP is legitimate but cheap; sellers routinely omit "IP" from titles. Married
german-pocket-knives.buy: Ask for the blade tang stamp; buy only Puma/Boker made in Germany (not "Puma IP") at ≤ $40 loose or ≤ $70 with original box/papers.

gilt-wall-brackets.title: Gilt wall brackets and wall shelves
gilt-wall-brackets.full: Gilt wall brackets and wall shelves (Italian Florentine giltwood, French Louis XV/Rococo carved giltwood, Syroco, Homco/Home Interiors, Burwood, Dart, Universal Statuary, chalkware, resin)
gilt-wall-brackets.money: 19th-century carved giltwood/gesso French or Italian brackets $200–1,200 a pair
gilt-wall-brackets.fakes: Modern resin "Florentine" brackets (Chinese, 1990s–now) mimic aged gilding but have mold uniformity and resin backs. Period-style reproductions are common at HomeGoods.
gilt-wall-brackets.buy: Buy carved wood (not resin) Florentine or 19th-century giltwood brackets ≤ $40 each / $80 a pair; pass on Syroco, Homco, Burwood and chalkware unless under $10.
tells: Carved wood (Florentine/Italian, 1940s–70s): carved linden or poplar with gesso, water gilding or gold leaf mixed with polychrome (silver-gray, red, cream), often distressed. Chips reveal white gesso over wood grain; back is unfinished wood, often with "Made i
Antique (pre-1900): deeper hand-carving, hand-cut nails, aged gesso with craquelure, oxidized gilding, sometimes oil gilding on gesso.

Molded resin / Syroco (wood fiber composite), Homco/Home Interiors (plastic), Burwood, Dart: crisp identical molded details, hollow backs with molded maker marks and copyright dates (1960s–80s), uniform gold paint, lightweight.

glass-and-porcelain-insulators.title: Glass and porcelain insulators
glass-and-porcelain-insulators.full: Glass and porcelain insulators (telegraph, telephone and power-line insulators; Hemingray, Brookfield, Whitall Tatum, Armstrong, McLaughlin, Locke, Pyrex, Ohio Brass, Knowles)
glass-and-porcelain-insulators.money: rare CDs, threadless, unusual colours $150–5,000+ (general knowledge, verify).
glass-and-porcelain-insulators.fakes: **Altered colours**: clear glass irradiated or heat-treated to purple/amber; fake "rare" colours. Reproductions of rare CDs exist. Use the NIA guides.
glass-and-porcelain-insulators.buy: Buy only coloured glass (cobalt, deep purple, amber, olive, yellow), threadless or rare-CD pieces at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on aqua, clear and brown porcelain.
tells: Glass: embossed with maker and style (HEMINGRAY-42, BROOKFIELD, W.T.CO., ARMSTRONG). Colour is the main value driver. Aqua and clear are very common; sun-coloured (SCA) purple is mid; true cobalt, deep amber, yellow-green, and "milk" are better.
Porcelain: glazed brown, white or blue-grey. Small spool and "saddle-top" types (Locke 8881 – the example) are common.

glove-stretchers.title: Glove Stretchers
glove-stretchers.full: Glove Stretchers (wooden, bone, celluloid, ivory, sterling; Whiting, Gorham, Unger Bros.; Victorian vanity tools)
glove-stretchers.fakes: Little reproduction activity; some resin "ivory". Modern silver-plate reproductions of vanity tools exist (general knowledge) — look for "STERLING" plus a maker mark, not "silver plate" or nothing.
glove-stretchers.buy: Pass plain wooden ones; buy sterling (hallmark visible, especially Whiting/Gorham) under ~$25; avoid ivory.

golf-clubs.title: Golf clubs
golf-clubs.full: Golf clubs (modern used, classic 1980s–2000s, persimmon, hickory; Scotty Cameron, Ping, Mizuno, Titleist, Hogan, TaylorMade, Callaway, MacGregor)
golf-clubs.money: Tour/Circle T, Anser 1A, Eye-O-Matic, rare hickory $600–5,000+.
golf-clubs.fakes: Counterfeit Scotty Cameron putters and fake current-gen drivers are common online; Tour/Circle T claims need authentication; hickory reproductions exist (general knowledge, verify).
golf-clubs.buy: Scotty Cameron < $100, Ping Anser Scottsdale/Phoenix < $60, Mizuno MP/Titleist MB set < $80, current-gen driver < $80; pass budget sets, 2000s drivers, common hickory singles.
tells: Putters: Scotty Cameron (Newport, Newport 2, Studio Stainless, Circa 62, Pro Platinum) $200–600 used, Tour-only/rare $1,000+; Ping Anser 1960s–70s "Scottsdale"/"Phoenix" address $150–800, 1980s Karsten Anser $40–80; Odyssey White Hot/Tri-Hot $40–90; Bettinardi

Irons: Ping Eye 2 (1982–90) sets $80–200 (BeCu copper-colour $200–350, "square groove" 1985–90 more); Mizuno MP forged (MP-33, MP-32, MP-14) $150–300; Titleist 690/714/718 MB/CB $200–400; Hogan Apex forged (1970s–90s) $80–200; Hogan "Bounce Sole" 1960s $100–25

Woods/drivers: current-gen (TaylorMade Qi10/Stealth 2, Callaway Paradym/Ai Smoke, Titleist TSR, Ping G430) $150–350; 2–4 gens old $50–120; 2000s titanium (Ping Rapture, Titleist 975D/983K, R7) $20–50; persimmon woods (MacGregor Tommy Armour 693/945, Toney Penn

golf-putters.title: Golf putters
golf-putters.full: Golf putters (Scotty Cameron, Ping, Bettinardi, Sacks Parente, Odyssey, hickory antiques)
golf-putters.fakes: Counterfeit Scotty Cameron putters and fake Circle T/tour stamps are widespread; Ping has reissued vintage-style Ansers (general knowledge, verify).
golf-putters.buy: Scotty Cameron ≤ $100, Ping Scottsdale ≤ $80, Sacks Parente ≤ $60, hickory Nicoll/Stewart ≤ $25; pass sellers who name the model and ask within 30% of market.

graniteware-and-enamelware.title: Graniteware and enamelware , Olkusz , Romanian, Riess ; Dansk Kobenstyle, Copco, Catherineholm, Cathrineholm Lotus, Le Creuset )
graniteware-and-enamelware.full: Graniteware and enamelware (US graniteware: Lisk, Columbian/Vollrath, Lalance & Grosjean "Agate", St. Louis Stamping "Granite Iron Ware", Matthai-Ingram; European enamel: Emo Celje (Yugoslavia), Olkusz (Poland), Romanian, Riess (Austria); Dansk Kobenstyle, Copco, Catherineholm, Cathrineholm Lotus, Le Creuset (enamelled cast iron))
graniteware-and-enamelware.money: Cathrineholm Lotus bowls/kettles and rare swirl or end-of-day pieces $80–400+.
graniteware-and-enamelware.fakes: New speckled camp enamelware (Crow Canyon, GSI) and Asian swirl reproductions; Cathrineholm-style knockoffs.
graniteware-and-enamelware.buy: Pass on grey graniteware and plain European enamel pots; only Cathrineholm (lotus leaf pattern), Dansk Kobenstyle, Copco Michael Lax pots, and coloured swirl graniteware at ≤ $25.
tells: Mid-century Scandinavian: Cathrineholm (Norway) lotus-leaf pattern in orange/red/blue/green; Dansk Kobenstyle (Jens Quistgaard) with X-shaped handles on lids.
Grey graniteware (1870s–1930s): mottled grey with black rim; pans, platters, coffee pots. Common.
Swirl graniteware: cobalt/white, green/white "relish", red/white swirls — valuable.

grinding-wheels.title: Grinding wheels and grindstones
grinding-wheels.full: Grinding wheels and grindstones (treadle sandstone grindstones, hand-crank wheels, Luther, Keen Kutter, Craftsman bench grinders, Tormek-type wet grinders)
grinding-wheels.fakes: Little faking. Cast-iron "Keen Kutter" decor reproductions exist in small items. Watch for fake-aged finishes (Farm Collector).
grinding-wheels.buy: Pass on full-size treadle/floor grindstones (too big, freight). Consider only hand-crank bench grinders with clear maker castings ≤ $25.

guatemalan-and-maya-textiles.title: Guatemalan and Maya textiles
guatemalan-and-maya-textiles.full: Guatemalan and Maya textiles (huipiles, cortes, tzutes, perrajes; Mexican rebozos)
guatemalan-and-maya-textiles.fakes: No faking at the low end – the issue is modern tourist production (acrylic, machine-made, chain-stitch embroidery) sold as "vintage Mayan". Printed "Guatemalan pattern" fabric from China. Old-looking pieces artificially
guatemalan-and-maya-textiles.buy: Buy only hand-woven backstrap huipiles or rebozos at ≤ $40–60 with photos of the back side and weave; machine/tourist pieces and printed "Aztec" fabric are passes.
tells: Huipiles are untailored rectangles, usually woven by the wearer on a backstrap loom, in one, two or three panels, generally sleeveless; most are worn tucked into the skirt, so the lower part is often plain or unfinished — not damage. Long, wide ceremonial huip
Decoration: brocade, soumak, ikat, embroidery and appliqué, especially at the neck.

Village tells: Patzún — diamond-shaped neck motifs; San Juan Sacatepéquez — bold purple and yellow stripes with mythical beasts ("winged serpents"); Chichicastenango area — traditional motifs mixed with cross-stitch-derived flowers, birds and cupids; San Anton

guitar-cases.title: Vintage guitar cases
guitar-cases.full: Vintage guitar cases (Lifton, Geib, Stone, Victoria, Gibson brown/pink "shell", Fender tweed/brown, Harmony/Kay chipboard, Ampeg; modern SKB/Gator)
guitar-cases.money: Fender tweed/brown and Gibson brown-with-pink-lining 1950s cases $400–2,500 (general knowledge, verify)
guitar-cases.fakes: Reissue Fender/Gibson cases (2000s+) look like vintage but have modern labels, hardware.
guitar-cases.buy: Only buy branded vintage hardshells (Lifton, Geib, Fender tweed, Gibson brown/pink) that fit the passenger seat at ≤ 1/3 sold; chipboard cases are freight losers.
tells: Gibson 1950s–60s: brown with pink lining (Lifton/Stone), "Gibson" logo; Fender tweed with red plush or brown with orange plush.

Chipboard (cardboard composite): textured faux-leather or tweed paper over pressed board; stitched edging, simple latches, thin; Harmony, Kay, Stella, Silvertone. The example is a gray textured chipboard parlor-shape case.
Geib/Lifton (1930s–60s): plywood shell, leather/pebbled covering, plush lining (green, purple, pink, brown), "Geib" or "Lifton" label in the storage lid.

guitar-effects-pedals.title: Guitar effects pedals
guitar-effects-pedals.full: Guitar effects pedals (Boss, Ibanez, MXR/EVH, Electro-Harmonix, Dunlop, Wampler, Keeley, Strymon, Klon, Damnation, OBNE, Digitech, boutique)
guitar-effects-pedals.money: CE-1, TS-808, Ram's Head Muff, Klon, Space Echo, Mu-Tron $500–6,000.
guitar-effects-pedals.fakes: Reissues are the main trap: TS9 reissue vs 1982 Japan original; Boss Waza Craft vs MIJ originals (CE-2 vs CE-2W, DM-2 vs DM-2W); MXR script reissues; Klon clones ($50–300) and fake Centaurs (general knowledge on fakes, v
guitar-effects-pedals.buy: Only vintage-era tells (MIJ black-label Boss, script MXR, Japan TS-808/TS9, big-box RAT) or boutique/top-tier at ≤ 40% of Reverb sold, or lots ≤ 50% of the sum of medians; pass single modern pedals near Reverb used price and untested electronics.
tells: Electro-Harmonix Big Muff: 1970s big-box Ram's Head/Triangle vs Russian Sovtek vs modern nano.
Ibanez Tube Screamer: green; TS-808 narrow box (1979–81); TS9 original (1982–84, Japan, "R" logo, JRC4558D chip inside).

Boss: rectangular compact, one colour per model, model code printed under the footswitch (DD-3, PS-3, CS-2, DS-1, MT-2, OD-1, CE-2, SD-1). Vintage = "Made in Japan" on the back + black label + silver thumbscrew (1977–~1988 per one write-up; "pre-1990 = Japan,

guitar-straps-and-accessories.title: Vintage guitar straps and accessories
guitar-straps-and-accessories.full: Vintage guitar straps and accessories (Fender, Ace, Levy's, Gibson, Gretsch, Mosrite, Dunlop, D'Andrea; straps, cases, pick tins, strings, cords, tremolo arms)
guitar-straps-and-accessories.money: original Fender/Gibson/Gretsch cases and dealer "case candy" (pick tins, NOS string packets, hang tags, manuals) $75–1,500+ (general knowledge, verify)
guitar-straps-and-accessories.fakes: Fender Monogrammed strap reissued constantly; D'Andrea Ace reissue; Chinese "vintage style" hippie straps; reproduction pick tins and decals. Fake "case candy" made to complete vintage guitars exists at high end (hang ta
guitar-straps-and-accessories.buy: Buy vintage-era Fender/Ace/Gibson straps and NOS case-candy at ≤ 25% of sold when the photo shows period construction tells; pass on reissues, generic straps and anything in a big case unless it is a documented original Fender/Gibson case.

hall-china-teapots.title: Hall China teapots & tea sets
hall-china-teapots.full: Hall China teapots & tea sets (Hall China Co., East Liverpool OH; Jewel Tea Autumn Leaf; Hallcraft / Eva Zeisel)
hall-china-teapots.money: Automobile, Football, Basketball, Basket in rare colours $400–1,500.
hall-china-teapots.fakes: Chinese-made lookalike donut teapots sell $8–15. Hall itself reissued some shapes and colours later (general knowledge, verify) – check base marks. - Hall reintroduced several old dinnerware and teapot lines in 1985 (Mus
hall-china-teapots.buy: Novelty shape ≤ $60 with no chips; pass Boston/New York/Philadelphia over $15.
tells: Novelty series, 1938: Automobile (car body, spout as the hood), Donut (ring with a hole through the body), Basket (6-cup), Birdcage (embossed birds in a cage), Airflow (8-cup 1938, 6-cup added 1939; teardrop streamline). Nautilus (1939, shell spiral). Football

Late commemoratives: Ronald Reagan caricature (1982), Anne Hathaway Cottage / Ye Olde McCormick Tea House (1984 and 1985, year above the door), 1993 Autumn Leaf Automobile (60th anniversary of the 1933 decal).

Boston (1916 onward; knob-lid in 7 sizes, sunken-lid in 4): plain round body, short spout. Still made into the 2000s, so a Boston can be any age. The 7-cup green and brown Bostons were the first Hall teapots Jewel Tea carried (1924).

halloween-decorations.title: Halloween decorations
halloween-decorations.full: Halloween decorations (Beistle, Dennison, German paper/papier-mache, Union Products & Empire blow molds, Don Featherstone, Paper Magic Group, Bethany Lowe, Gemmy, Department 56)
halloween-decorations.money: German pre-WWII papier-mâché/composition JOL lanterns, candy containers and figures $150–2,000+.
halloween-decorations.fakes: Big repro market: modern papier-mâché "vintage-style" JOLs (Bethany Lowe, Ragon House, TJ Maxx), new pulp from Asia, reproduction German figures and Beistle reissues (Beistle reissued many 1930s die-cuts in the 1990s–200
halloween-decorations.buy: Hunt pre-1960 paper and papier-mâché (German or US), stamped "Germany" items, and Beistle die-cuts; pass on foam/plastic newer than the 1970s unless it's a known rare blow mold under $20.
tells: German papier-mâché/composition (1910–1939): jack-o'-lanterns with paper insert faces (thin tissue eyes/mouth), cats, devils, veggie-people; candy containers; stamped or labelled "Germany". Hand-painted, often worn, very light.
US pulp (1940s–50s): molded pressed-paper JOLs, cats and witches, thicker and grayer pulp inside, cut-out faces with paper inserts; bail handles of wire.
Beistle and Dennison paper: embossed die-cut cardboard (cats, witches, owls, skeletons) with "Beistle Co." mark, honeycomb tissue, table centerpieces; Dennison "Bogie Book" items.

ham-and-scanner-radios.title: Ham and scanner radios
ham-and-scanner-radios.full: Ham and scanner radios (Collins, Drake, Hallicrafters, Heathkit, Kenwood/Trio, Yaesu, Icom, Swan, Lafayette, Hammarlund, National; scanners: Electra Bearcat, Regency, Uniden, Radio Shack Realistic/Pro)
ham-and-scanner-radios.money: Collins S-line, KWM-2 and rare National/Hammarlund $300–2,000+.
ham-and-scanner-radios.fakes: None; watch for parts radios sold as working. - Married stations (S-line pieces from different emblem eras or a non-matching supply) are common; check emblem and serial consistency. - Reproduction knobs, dial glass and d
ham-and-scanner-radios.buy: Pass by default under Dylan's no-untested-electronics rule; buy only small, demonstrably working 1980s–2000s Kenwood/Yaesu/Icom handhelds or mobiles at ≤ 30% of comps with video proof of transmit/receive; never buy boatanchors or untested gear.
tells: Tube transmitter/transceiver tell: separate "PLATE" (tune) and "LOAD" knobs, a "GRID" or "DRIVE" control, and a meter switch for "Ip/Ig/PO". Receivers alone (Hallicrafters S-38/SX, Hammarlund HQ) have no plate/load controls and usually a slide-rule or round di

Scanners: 1970s–80s crystal and early programmable scanners (Electra Bearcat BC101 1974–76, the first synthesised programmable scanner; Bearcat 210/220/250; Regency Touch; Realistic Pro-2004/2006 — the Pro-2004/2006 are the valued ones). Analog scanners are mo

Crystal scanners (Regency, early Bearcat III/IV, Realistic Pro-series of the early 70s) have a row of channel lamps and plug-in frequency crystals behind a door or under the lid; each channel needs its own crystal. Photo tell: a numbered strip of 4–16 small la

hand-painted-porcelain.title: Hand-painted porcelain – American china painting on European blanks
hand-painted-porcelain.full: Hand-painted porcelain – American china painting on European blanks (Pickard, Stouffer, Donath, Rosenthal, T&V Limoges, Bavaria, Austria, R.S. Prussia/Germany, Nippon)
hand-painted-porcelain.money: exceptional Pickard/Nippon moriage/RS Prussia portrait pieces $400–2,000+.
hand-painted-porcelain.fakes: - R.S. Prussia: the red wreath and star mark is faked as a decal since the 1960s on Asian-made pieces; fake marks are often too bright, slightly crooked, glazed over, and the molds are cruder. - Nippon: fake "Nippon" bac
hand-painted-porcelain.buy: Buy only professional-studio marks (Pickard, Stouffer, Donath) or genuine R.S. Prussia/Nippon moriage at ≤ $40; pass amateur-painted plates, relish dishes and transfer-printed chocolate pots.
tells: Raised gold paste, heavy gold rims and etched gold borders = professional studio (Pickard, Stouffer).
Moriage (raised slip dots and beading) and heavy enamel jewelling = Nippon (1891–1921).

Soft airbrushed or washed backgrounds (purple/lavender, green, yellow) blending into fruit or flowers – blackberries, cherries, grapes, violets, roses, poppies (example 7981033239). Typical amateur work.

hand-planes.title: Hand planes
hand-planes.full: Hand planes (Stanley Bailey & Bedrock, Lie-Nielsen, Veritas, Record, Sargent, Millers Falls)
hand-planes.fakes: Few outright fakes. Risks are married parts (Bedrock frog in a Bailey body or vice versa), replacement irons, and modern reissues (Stanley Sweetheart reissue line 2010s, Woodriver Bedrock-pattern copies) being sold as ol

hand-tool-lots.title: Hand tool lots
hand-tool-lots.full: Hand tool lots (Stanley, Millers Falls, Yankee/North Bros, Goodell-Pratt, Disston, Lufkin, Craftsman, Klein, Trimo, Stillson, mixed garage lots)
hand-tool-lots.money: good pre-1950 woodworking lots of 10–20 named tools $120–300 when parted out
hand-tool-lots.fakes: Little faking. The main traps: modern Indian or Chinese "antique style" brass gauges and decorative braces sold at home décor shops; reissued Stanley Sweetheart planes (2000s); later types sold as "antique". Composite to
hand-tool-lots.buy: Buy only pre-1960 woodworking lots of named tools at ≤ $3 per tool and ≤ 20% of the parted-out total; never modern Harbor Freight/plastic-case lots or rusty plumbing wrenches.

hard-hats-and-pith-helmets.title: Vintage hard hats and pith helmets , Willson, Jackson; Hawley, Vero, colonial cork pith helmets)
hard-hats-and-pith-helmets.full: Vintage hard hats and pith helmets (E.D. Bullard Hard Boiled, MSA Skullgard/Comfo-Cap, McDonald T (B.F. McDonald), Willson, Jackson; Hawley, Vero, colonial cork pith helmets)
hard-hats-and-pith-helmets.money: decal-rich company/union/oilfield hats, Bullard 502 early, and miner's carbide-light caps $120–400
hard-hats-and-pith-helmets.fakes: Decals applied later to plain hats to fake oilfield provenance; reproduction WWII pith helmets (Indian-made); modern Hawley-style "safari" helmets sold as vintage. Union/company decals are reproduced as stickers.
