hard-hats-and-pith-helmets.buy: Buy metal (aluminum) or early fiberglass Bullard/MSA/McDonald hard hats with original decals or company stencils at ≤ $25; pith helmets only if pre-WWII British/colonial with makers' label at ≤ $40; pass on plastic hard hats and modern Hawley "safari" souvenir

harry-potter-merchandise.title: Harry Potter merchandise
harry-potter-merchandise.full: Harry Potter merchandise (Noble Collection, Hallmark Keepsake, Funko, LEGO, Mattel 2001, Wizarding World park exclusives, Silver Buffalo, Bioworld, Loungefly)
harry-potter-merchandise.money: rare Funko exclusives, retired sealed LEGO (Hogwarts Castle 71043, Diagon Alley 75978), Noble limited editions $80–500+.
harry-potter-merchandise.fakes: Massive volume of Chinese knockoffs: Time-Turners, Snitches, Deathly Hallows necklaces, wands, Funko fakes (wrong font, poor paint), LEGO knock-offs (Lepin/"Bela"). Noble re-releases many items.
harry-potter-merchandise.buy: Buy only sealed retired LEGO, Noble Collection boxed limited items, or rare Funko exclusives at ≤ 30% of sold; pass on mixed mug/keychain lots unless ≤ $20 for 20+ pieces and light.
tells: LEGO: 2001–2011 sets (Hogwarts Castle 4709, 5378), 2018+ sets; sealed retired sets have collector value.
Funko Pop (2011–present): box condition matters; exclusives (Convention, Hot Topic, Barnes & Noble) and chase/flocked versions.

Noble Collection (1990s–present): heavy, quality die-cast and resin replicas — wands in boxes with Noble labels, Time-Turner (gold-plated with turning hourglass), Golden Snitch, Horcrux replicas. Look for "Noble Collection" stamp and a numbered card on limited

herman-miller-chairs.title: Herman Miller Setu / Aeron
herman-miller-chairs.full: Herman Miller Setu / Aeron (and other Herman Miller office seating)
herman-miller-chairs.fakes: Copy chairs styled like Aeron exist widely online; no label and wrong frame details. Refurbished-dealer chairs (remanufactured with replacement parts) are a large market and set the ceiling. (general knowledge, verify)
herman-miller-chairs.buy: Setu under $90 only if relisted within a week

hessian-soldier-andirons.title: Hessian soldier andirons
hessian-soldier-andirons.full: Hessian soldier (figural) andirons (unmarked foundries, Virginia Metalcrafters, Rostand)
hessian-soldier-andirons.fakes: Reproductions are the norm: Virginia Metalcrafters, Rostand and unmarked mid-century castings; modern imports are also cast from originals (soft detail can fool – check fasteners and paint layers). Repainted 20th-c. pair
hessian-soldier-andirons.buy: full-size (16"+) pair under $60; pass small 9–12" repro pairs over $40

heywood-wakefield-furniture.title: Heywood-Wakefield furniture
heywood-wakefield-furniture.full: Heywood-Wakefield furniture (wicker, Old Colony maple, Streamline/Modern birch)
heywood-wakefield-furniture.fakes: Heywood-Wakefield name was revived (1990s–2000s, Heywood-Wakefield Co. in Gardner reproduced classic designs) – reissues look new and carry newer labels (general knowledge, verify). - **Correction (2026-10-13)**: the rev
heywood-wakefield-furniture.buy: Modern-line blonde birch piece ≤ $100 that fits a passenger seat; most pieces are bigger and excluded
tells: Atomic Ranch: a black eagle logo stamp was used from 1949, usually in the left-hand drawer or on the underside. Earlier Streamline pieces had paper tags that are usually lost, so unmarked does not rule out pre-1949 H-W.
Company history (Wikipedia):
Heywood Brothers (1826) and the Wakefield Rattan Co. (1855) merged in 1897 as Heywood Brothers & Wakefield, and became the Heywood-Wakefield Company in 1921.

hickory-golf-clubs.title: Hickory-shaft golf clubs, pre-1935
hickory-golf-clubs.full: Hickory-shaft golf clubs, pre-1935 (Tom Stewart, Gibson, George Nicoll, Spalding, MacGregor, Forgan, Auchterlonie)
hickory-golf-clubs.fakes: Modern reproduction hickories (St Andrews Golf Co and others) for the hickory-play market; fake cleekmarks on generic heads; married heads on later shafts. Repros look too perfect. (general knowledge, verify)

hohner-chromatic-harmonicas.title: Hohner chromatic harmonicas and holders
hohner-chromatic-harmonicas.full: Hohner chromatic harmonicas (Chromonica 270/280, CX-12) and holders
hohner-chromatic-harmonicas.fakes: No meaningful fakes; Chinese generic chromatics with Hohner-like styling exist (no Hohner stamp). Reissued boxes/cases are sometimes mixed with older instruments. (general knowledge, verify)
hohner-chromatic-harmonicas.buy: 280C ≤ $40, 270 ≤ $25, or lots of Hohner chromatics ≤ $10 each

hohner-harmonicas.title: Harmonicas
hohner-harmonicas.full: Harmonicas (Hohner Marine Band, Chromonica, pre-war; Suzuki, Seydel)
hohner-harmonicas.fakes: No significant fakes. Hohner reissues vintage-style packaging on current models, and the 1896 name is used on the current Marine Band – don't confuse "1896" on a modern harmonica with the date. (general knowledge, verify
hohner-harmonicas.buy: chromatic or boxed limited edition under $25; pass anything over $35

home-interiors-decor.title: Home Interiors & Gifts decor
home-interiors-decor.full: Home Interiors & Gifts decor (Home Interiors & Gifts Inc., Dallas TX, 1957–2008; Homco figurines incl. Masterpiece Porcelain and Denim Days; Burwood Products)
home-interiors-decor.fakes: Not applicable. No faking of this low-value line is known. The confusion is attribution: department-store Syroco and Burwood decor, and post-2008 Celebrating Home pieces, get listed as "Home Interiors". Only an HI&G stic
home-interiors-decor.buy: Pass; only bulk Homco figurine lots ≤ $1/piece with resale sets ≥ $100.
tells: Framed prints: offset-litho prints in ornate gilt resin/composition or wood-look frames, often with oval or arched double mats. Subjects: lighthouses and coastal scenes, cottage gardens, florals, Victorian children (often in oval frames), Madonna and Child / C
Mirrors, brass-tone sconces, candle holders, shelves, plaques (many of the plaques and frames are moulded resin by Burwood Products).

Homco figurines: porcelain and bisque children, animals, birds, horses, Native American figures, religious and Victorian figures; the premium porcelain line is Masterpiece Porcelain; the 1985 Denim Days line is small figurines of children (Danny and Debbie) in

hot-wheels-redlines.title: Hot Wheels Redlines
hot-wheels-redlines.money: rare (Rear-Loader Beach Bomb, pink/rare colours, Mighty Maverick variants, sealed blisters) $200–5,000+.
hot-wheels-redlines.fakes: Hot Wheels Classics/Vintage reissues and "Real Riders" with redline tyres (2000s) — bases dated 2000s, Malaysia/China. Reproduction wheels and drilled/riveted bases indicate restoration.
hot-wheels-redlines.buy: Buy redline groups at ≤ $10 per car (≤ $15 if spectraflame paint is bright and wheels clean); never pay "collector" prices for worn cars.

hull-pottery.title: Hull Pottery
hull-pottery.full: Hull Pottery (A.E. Hull Pottery Co., Crooksville, Ohio, 1905–1986)
hull-pottery.money: Little Red Riding Hood cookie jars/pieces $100–800 (heavily reproduced)
hull-pottery.fakes: Little Red Riding Hood reproductions are rampant (smaller, crude paint, wrong marks). Matte florals rarely reproduced; Chinese copies occasionally. - Repro tells: undersized vs catalogue height, heavier, white/grey body,
hull-pottery.buy: Buy pre-1950 matte lines in large sizes or Bow-Knot/Red Riding Hood ≤ 1/3 sold; average 8" matte vases are pass above $20.
tells: Mark sequence (Hull Pottery Association): c. 1910 wreath with gallon number (stoneware); "H" in a circle or diamond (kitchen/stoneware/artware, early decades); 1930s–1950 "Hull Art USA" or "Hull USA" with a letter-number code; "Hull Ware" logo on 1940s kitchen

Company timeline: founded 1905 by Addis Emmet Hull; flood and fire destroyed the factory and most molds in June 1950; reopened 1 Jan 1952 as The Hull Pottery Company; closed March 1986 (Lion and Unicorn). The 1950 fire is the dividing line: pre-fire matte art

Reading a code: letter = line, first number = mold/shape, last = height. "Hull Art W-3 5½" = Wildflower shape 3, 5½" (Lion and Unicorn). Bow-Knot uses "B-", Water Lily "L-", Wildflower "W-", Magnolia gloss "H-"; some pieces carry only mold and size numbers.

hummel-figurines.title: M.I. Hummel figurines
hummel-figurines.full: M.I. Hummel figurines (Goebel, Rödental, Germany; later Manufaktur Rödental)
hummel-figurines.fakes: Asian knock-offs and resin copies; Goebel itself reissued older models in later TMKs. Dubler pieces are not Goebel (some collect them). "Hummel" name on non-Goebel items.
hummel-figurines.buy: Buy lots at ≤ $5/figure (resale ~$15–25/figure) or any crown/full-bee (TMK-1/2) at ≤ $20; single later Hummels are pass.

ice-cream-makers.title: Vintage hand-crank ice cream makers / freezers
ice-cream-makers.full: Vintage hand-crank ice cream makers / freezers (White Mountain, Alaska, Shepard's Lightning, Peerless Iceland, Gem, Kwik Freeze, Auto Vacuum, Richmond Cedar Works, Sears; electric Rival, Salton, Waring)
ice-cream-makers.money: miniature 1-pint and salesman-size, cast-iron Gem/Peerless table models, and rare painted examples $150–400.
ice-cream-makers.fakes: White Mountain still makes the same design (modern ones have stickers, galvanised hoops, electric options). "Primitive-style" decor reproductions.
ice-cream-makers.buy: Pass – they are bulky (bucket, ice and crank), heavy and ship poorly; consider only 1-pint/1-quart miniature freezers or cast-iron table-top models that fit in a box ≤ 16" at ≤ $20.
tells: Maker name and patent dates are cast into the iron gear frame ("White Mountain Freezer Co. Nashua NH", "Alaska Freezer Co. Winchendon Mass", "Shepard's Lightning", "Peerless Iceland", "Gem", "Kwik Freeze").
Triple-motion (canister and dasher turn opposite ways) White Mountain = best quality.
Original paint (blue/green/red), stencilled lettering on the tub, wooden crank handle.

ice-tools.title: Ice tools
ice-tools.full: Ice tools (ice tongs, ice picks, ice chippers/shavers, ice saws; Gifford-Wood, Woodruff, Gilchrist, North Bros, Enterprise, advertising ice picks)
ice-tools.money: ice plows, early ice-harvesting tools and rare advertising pieces $80–300 (often too big).
ice-tools.fakes: Cast-iron décor tongs and hooks (2000s–present, India/China), painted black or "rust" finished, often sold as "antique" — rough cast texture, no wear on the pivot, perfect symmetry. Reproduction Coca-Cola ice picks with
ice-tools.buy: Buy only advertising ice picks with crisp company names or marked Gifford-Wood/early harvest tools at ≤ $10; pass on generic tongs and chippers, which ship heavy for $15–30.
tells: Tongs: scissor-like, pointed hooked jaws, wrought or forged steel, from 10" household to 30" harvest/2-man.

Picks: single steel spike in a wooden handle with a steel ferrule and often a cap; advertising picks have the company stamped or printed on the handle ("Coolerator", "Coca-Cola", "XYZ Ice & Fuel Co.").
Chippers: 4–6 prongs on a cast head (like our sweep's example) for breaking blocks; shavers: a hand-held box with a blade for shaved ice (Gilchrist, Enterprise).

indian-textile-boxes.title: Indian textile boxes
indian-textile-boxes.full: Indian textile boxes (zari/zardozi embroidered, sequin and brocade covered boxes; Kashmiri papier-mâché; Sadeli; export gift-shop production)
indian-textile-boxes.money: antique (pre-1940) metal-thread embroidered boxes, Kashmiri papier-mâché and Sadeli micro-mosaic $60–300 (a late-18th-c. sadeli sandalwood workbox realised about £504 at Lyon & Turnbull, 2025). Note: Terapeak "Kashmiri papier mache box" median is only $14 — modern pieces dominate.
indian-textile-boxes.fakes: Mostly modern production sold as "vintage". Persian khatam and modern Indian "mosaic" boxes (often with plastic and bone) are sold as antique sadeli. New Kashmiri tourist papier-mâché is artificially "aged".
indian-textile-boxes.buy: Pass on fabric-covered cardboard boxes; only antique Kashmiri papier-mâché, Sadeli or silver-mounted pieces at ≤ 1/3 resale.

industrial-pressure-gauges.title: Industrial pressure and steam gauges
industrial-pressure-gauges.full: Industrial pressure and steam gauges (Ashton Valve Co., Crosby Steam Gage & Valve, Ashcroft, American Steam Gauge, Star Brass, U.S. Gauge, Marsh, Jas. Morrison, Utica)
industrial-pressure-gauges.fakes: Decor reproductions with cast "steam gauge" dials and faux brass, sold as "steampunk" — light weight, printed fake makers, plastic lenses. Married parts (later bezel or glass) are common but minor. Modern Ashcroft gauges
industrial-pressure-gauges.buy: Buy brass-cased 8"+ gauges with intact glass and a clean dial ≤ $40, or any user-company dial (Case, Frick, Westinghouse, railroad) ≤ $50; pass small iron-case gauges, painted modern dials, clock conversions and anything over ~15 lb.
tells: A round Bourdon-tube gauge: dial (face) with a scale in psi, a needle, glass held by a bezel ring, a case, and a threaded stem (bottom or back connection). Sizes 2½"–14" dial.

Old: brass or nickel-plated bezel and case, silvered or engraved brass dial with wax-filled black numerals (19th c.–c.1905), later enamelled/painted dials; maker name and city on the dial ("THE ASHTON VALVE CO. BOSTON", "CROSBY STEAM GAGE & VALVE CO. BOSTON",
Test gauges: larger (8½"–12"), high accuracy, often a mirror band around the scale (to avoid parallax), a knife-edge pointer, fine graduations; Ashton dials read "Standard Test Gage".

islamic-metalwork.title: Islamic metalwork
islamic-metalwork.full: Islamic metalwork (Persian Safavid/Qajar bronze and tinned copper, Ottoman/Turkish tombak and copper, Mamluk Revival "Cairoware", Moroccan and Indian brass, Arabian dallah coffee pots)
islamic-metalwork.money: good Safavid-type bronze bowls, Mamluk-Revival silver-inlaid pieces and early "magic" bowls $250–1,500+ (auction).
islamic-metalwork.fakes: - Afghan, Iranian and Indian workshops make "Seljuk" and "Safavid" bowls and ewers today, artificially aged with acids and burial — very common on eBay with "11th–13th century" titles. Tells: sharp crisp edges under the
islamic-metalwork.buy: Buy only heavy cast-bronze or tinned-copper bowls with crisp hand-cut calligraphy and real wear at ≤ $60 when resale ≥ $175; pass on tourist brass, thin spun trays and modern dallahs.
tells: Metal vessels made in Iran, Turkey, the Levant, Egypt, North Africa, Central Asia and Arabia: bowls (tas), basins, ewers, trays, coffee pots (dallah), incense burners, candlesticks.

Collectable pieces carry engraved bands of Arabic/Persian script (thuluth, nasta'liq or angular Kufic-style lettering), cartouches, cross-hatched or ring-punched grounds, and twisted-rope border bands.

Persian bronze bowls (Safavid type, 16th–18th c., and Qajar 19th c.): straight flaring sides, flat narrow foot, thick cast high-tin bronze with a dark brown/olive patina; one wide inscription band between rope or chevron borders. Look for a rim that is a sligh

italian-ceramics.title: Italian decorative ceramics
italian-ceramics.full: Italian (and Portuguese) decorative ceramics (Deruta, Vietri, Bitossi/Raymor, Fratelli Fanciullacci, Capodimonte-type, Faenza/Gubbio maiolica, Caltagirone, Nove; Portuguese Coimbra faience; modern import trays)
italian-ceramics.money: signed designer MCM (Gambone, Fantoni, Londi Rimini Blu large) and antique maiolica $250–3,000.
italian-ceramics.fakes: - Bitossi still produces Rimini Blu; reissues are lighter and cleaner; Raymor label suggests period. - Fake Gambone signatures exist. - Bitossi look-alikes from other Italian makers are widespread; "Bitossi" in a title i
italian-ceramics.buy: Hunt for 1950s–70s Italian MCM pottery with Raymor/"Italy" numbered bases and designer signatures at ≤ $60; pass on modern Deruta/Vietri tableware and printed decor trays.
tells: MCM Italian art pottery (1950s–70s): Bitossi Rimini Blu (stamped geometric patterns, bright cobalt/turquoise), Fratelli Fanciullacci and Fantoni (thick lava glazes, abstract figures), Raymor imports with paper labels and incised numbers ("Italy 453").
Rimini Blu in a photo: deep cobalt-to-turquoise glaze pooled in impressed geometric or figural (fish, birds, faces) panels on a matte-to-satin ground; bottles, ewers, pitchers, lamp bases.

Maiolica (tin-glazed earthenware): opaque white tin glaze with hand-painted cobalt, yellow, green, ochre; Deruta Ricco and Raffaellesco patterns (dragons, grotesques); signed with town + painter initials on base.

japanese-bronze-vases.title: Japanese bronze vases
japanese-bronze-vases.full: Japanese bronze vases (Meiji / Taisho / Showa archaistic & mixed-metal; Seiya, Nogawa, Kanaya, Miyao)
japanese-bronze-vases.fakes: Modern Chinese castings of Meiji designs with fake signature cartouches are common; tells are coarse sand interior, crude seams, light weight, uniform gold/brown chemical patina (per appraisily repro tells). Postwar "Mad
japanese-bronze-vases.buy: crisp 12"+ bird/elephant-handle vase ≤ $60, or any visible kanji signature ≤ $150

japanese-cloisonne.title: Japanese cloisonne and champleve
japanese-cloisonne.full: Japanese cloisonne and champleve (Namikawa Yasuyuki, Ando Jubei, Hayashi Kodenji, Ota Tamesaburo; mass export workshops)
japanese-cloisonne.money: marked masters (Ando, Hayashi, Namikawa, Ota) and pairs $600–5,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
japanese-cloisonne.fakes: - Chinese and Taiwanese cloisonne sold as "Meiji Japanese" is routine on eBay. - Fake Namikawa/Ando marks exist on modern Chinese pieces; a famous mark on mediocre work is a red flag. - Modern champleve brass (India, Chi
japanese-cloisonne.buy: Pay ≤ $25 for brass champleve export pieces; only go higher for fine-wire, tight-pattern, fully enamelled cloisonne with a maker mark or silver wires/rims.
tells: Cloisonne (shippo): thin metal wires (cloisons) soldered to a copper or silver body form cells filled with enamel. Whole body is enamel, polished smooth and glassy. Meiji (1868–1912) high-end work has hair-fine wires, very small cells, deep colors (midnight bl

Champleve on cast brass/bronze: enamel only in recessed bands on a cast brass body, with the rest of the surface stamped in a dense diaper/hexagon/turtle-shell pattern, often with archaic Chinese taotie "mask" bands, ring handles and elephant/lion mask lugs. T

japanese-dolls.title: Japanese dolls
japanese-dolls.full: Japanese dolls (musha ningyo / gogatsu ningyo, hina ningyo, kimekomi, gofun-faced ichimatsu, hakata, kokeshi, geisha souvenir dolls; makers Yoshitoku, Kyugetsu, Mataro, Ningyo no Kyugetsu)
japanese-dolls.money: Edo/Meiji gofun dolls (gosho, ichimatsu, early musha) $300–3,000+
japanese-dolls.fakes: Modern Chinese-made "Japanese" dolls; souvenir dolls sold as "antique". Real antique dolls show hand-painted features, tissue paper stamped tags, and natural aging.
japanese-dolls.buy: Buy pre-war (Meiji–Showa early) gofun dolls with original silk and tags, or signed maker dolls, at ≤ 30% of median; pass on souvenir dolls in glass cases unless ≤ $15 and shipped without the case.
tells: Gosho: chubby white babies (Edo–Meiji), high value.

Musha ningyo (gogatsu ningyo): warrior dolls displayed for Boys' Day (May 5): armor of silk brocade with lacquered "scales", kabuto helmet with kuwagata horns, bows/arrows/swords, often on a horse; cheeks plump with gofun (crushed shell) gesso faces and glass
Hina ningyo: Girls' Day (March 3) Emperor/Empress dolls and court sets on tiered stands.

japanese-export-china.title: Japanese export china
japanese-export-china.full: Japanese export china (Thames, Lefton, Napco, Norcrest, Enesco, Holt Howard, Occupied Japan, Noritake, Moriage, Nippon)
japanese-export-china.money: Noritake Art Deco and early Satsuma $100–1,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
japanese-export-china.fakes: Fake Nippon marks (common reproductions from 1980s); compare mark guides (maple leaf, M-in-wreath). More: fake Nippon pieces are usually decal-decorated with bright, unworn gold, and the mark is a crisp decal (often in o
japanese-export-china.buy: pass on 1950s–70s giftware unless it is Holt Howard/Lefton Christmas or figural kitsch lots; buy only Nippon-marked moriage/hand-painted vases or Noritake Deco ≤ $40.

japanese-porcelain-figurines.title: Japanese porcelain figurines , Inarco, Norcrest, Ucagco, Relco, Kreiss, Holt Howard, Josef-style)
japanese-porcelain-figurines.full: Japanese porcelain figurines (Made in Japan / Occupied Japan export; Lefton, Napco, Enesco, Erich Stauffer (Arnart), Inarco, Norcrest, Ucagco, Relco, Kreiss, Holt Howard, Josef-style)
japanese-porcelain-figurines.money: Holt Howard, Kreiss Psycho-Ceramics, Napco planter heads $40–300+.
japanese-porcelain-figurines.fakes: Fake "Occupied Japan" stamps on newer Chinese porcelain; head vase reproductions (lighter, poorly painted lashes). Hummel-alikes are not fakes of Goebel, just imitations.
japanese-porcelain-figurines.buy: Only buy lady head vases/planters (Napco, Inarco, Relpo) with lashes and pearls, Kreiss Psycho-Ceramics and Holt Howard pixies at ≤ 30% of median; pass ordinary figurines.

japanese-tetsubin.title: Japanese tetsubin iron kettles
japanese-tetsubin.full: Japanese tetsubin iron kettles (Ryubundo, Kamebundo, Kinjudo and other Kyoto foundries; Nambu/Morioka makers incl. Iwachu; modern Chinese copies)
japanese-tetsubin.fakes: Large volume of Chinese "Japanese tetsubin" teapots, many with fake 龍文堂 or other cast/stamped marks; sharp-looking marks on a dull surface may be later additions (Nio Teas). Ryubundo-style lids were made by many workshop
japanese-tetsubin.buy: Buy only raw-interior (not enamelled) kettles with bronze/copper lids at ≤ $60 unsigned, or ≤ 25% of comp value when a cast foundry seal is visible on the BODY; a lid signature alone is not an attribution; pass on enamel-lined teapots and sets.

japanese-woodblock-prints.title: Japanese woodblock prints
japanese-woodblock-prints.full: Japanese woodblock prints (ukiyo-e, shin-hanga, reprints; Hiroshige, Hokusai, Kunisada, Hasui, Yoshida)
japanese-woodblock-prints.fakes: Re-cut blocks and later editions of Hiroshige/Hokusai; Meiji-era and 20th-c. reprints sold as Edo; photomechanical reproductions; posthumous/later Hasui editions with later Watanabe seals (worth less than lifetime editio
japanese-woodblock-prints.buy: visible Watanabe/period publisher seal under $100; pass bamboo-framed bright "antique" pairs

japanese-yatate.title: Japanese yatate
japanese-yatate.full: Japanese yatate (Edo–Meiji brass, copper, shakudo, iron and wood portable brush-and-ink cases)
japanese-yatate.money: signed fine metalwork or rare forms (sword-shaped, figural) $200–800 (Goto-school signed shakudo est. $400–800 at Leland Little 2019).
japanese-yatate.fakes: Chinese-made modern copies, often with crude castings and artificial patina. Also modern Japanese tourist/craft yatate (still made for calligraphers) which are clean, crisp and unworn. Tells of a copy: soft cast detail,
japanese-yatate.buy: Buy only decorated/inlaid/signed yatate at ≤ $30, or plain ones at ≤ $10; most plain brass ones resell for $25–55, so asking prices above $25 are a pass.

jewelry-bench-tools.title: Jewelry bench tools
jewelry-bench-tools.full: Jewelry bench tools (rolling mills, disc cutters, arbor presses, flex shafts; Durston, Pepe, Cavallin, Foredom)
jewelry-bench-tools.fakes: No true fakes, but import mills are painted green to resemble Durston; check for the cast/plated Durston name on the side plate. (general knowledge, verify)
jewelry-bench-tools.buy: Durston/Pepe/Cavallin visible and ≤ 35% of retail; pass unbranded imports

kamaka-ukuleles.title: Kamaka ukuleles
kamaka-ukuleles.fakes: Non-Kamaka ukuleles with a Kamaka decal (junk tier). Kamaka reissued the Pineapple. Labels can be swapped – check construction matches the era. (general knowledge, verify)

kenner-12-inch-star-wars-figures.title: Kenner 12-inch Star Wars figures
kenner-12-inch-star-wars-figures.full: Kenner 12-inch Star Wars figures (1978–80 "Large Size Action Figures"; vs 1996–99 Hasbro/Kenner Collector Series)
kenner-12-inch-star-wars-figures.fakes: Reproduction accessories (sabers, blasters, Leia's comb/brush) and repro outfits are sold to complete figures – originals have correct plastic and stamps; repro boxes exist for MIB. 1996+ Collector Series lumped in as "v
kenner-12-inch-star-wars-figures.buy: 1978 figure with its main accessory ≤ $70 per figure; pass 1996+ Collector Series over $15

kerosene-lanterns.title: Kerosene lanterns , Handlan, Dressel, Armspear, CT Ham, Perkins, Feuerhand, Hurricane/Paull's, Defiance, Barn lanterns; railroad lanterns)
kerosene-lanterns.full: Kerosene lanterns (Dietz, Embury, Adams & Westlake (Adlake), Handlan, Dressel, Armspear, CT Ham, Perkins, Feuerhand, Hurricane/Paull's, Defiance, Barn lanterns; railroad lanterns)
kerosene-lanterns.money: colored-globe or embossed RR conductor's lanterns $400–2,000+.
kerosene-lanterns.fakes: Reproduction railroad globes and lanterns with fake RR markings are common (especially "Santa Fe", "Union Pacific" casts). New Dietz from China. Fake brass-plating. RR names stamped crisply on a clean top on an otherwise
kerosene-lanterns.buy: Only buy lanterns with a railroad name stamped in the frame/top or embossed/etched on the globe, or brass/scarce models, at ≤ 1/3 resale; pass on ordinary barn lanterns over $15 each and anything electrified.

kerosene-oil-lamps.title: Kerosene and oil lamps
kerosene-oil-lamps.full: Kerosene and oil lamps (EAPG stand lamps, Aladdin/Mantle Lamp Co., Rayo, Miller, Bradley & Hubbard, P&A/Eagle and Scovill "Queen Anne" burners, Lamplight Farms reproductions, Sail Boat brand Hong Kong, electrified hurricane lamps)
kerosene-oil-lamps.money: Gone-with-the-Wind, banquet, Bradley & Hubbard/Miller brass and rare colours $150–1,000.
kerosene-oil-lamps.fakes: - Lamplight Farms and Asian copies of EAPG patterns. - Reproduction Gone-with-the-Wind lamps (1950s–1990s) with decal flowers instead of hand-painted ones, and electric-only construction. - Married lamps: an antique base
kerosene-oil-lamps.buy: Buy only coloured-glass or named-pattern EAPG (1870–1910), Aladdin models with B-burners, or signed brass lamps at ≤ 25% of sold median and ≤ $40; pass on clear generic lamps, Hong Kong imports and electrified hurricanes.
tells: Antique EAPG (1860s–1910): thick pressed glass with a named pattern (e.g., Peanut, Banner, Bull's Eye, Prince Edward, Lincoln Drape), a collar of brass or plaster-set, a slight ripple or bubble in the glass, wear on the base rim.

Modern (1960s–2020s): Lamplight Farms (USA), Chinese and Hong Kong imports. Mould-perfect, thin glass, often with a stamped "Lamplight" or "Made in China/Hong Kong" burner, and plastic or aluminum collars; bright coloured lamp oil (red, blue) inside clear font

Burners: "P&A Mfg Co Eagle" burners (1890s–1950s) are common and not proof of age. "Queen Anne" burners (Scovill Mfg., Waterbury CT) are 1890s–1920s. "Aladdin" and "Model B/NU-Type" = Mantle Lamp Co. (1908–), B-series 1932–1955.

kettler-kettcars.title: Kettler Kettcar pedal go-karts
kettler-kettcars.full: Kettler Kettcar pedal go-karts (and other German pedal cars; Berg, Puky)
kettler-kettcars.fakes: No fakes; the risk is current Chinese-made Kettler models sold as "original German". (general knowledge, verify)
kettler-kettcars.buy: bigger than a passenger seat – excluded by the size rule

key-cutting-machines.title: Vintage key cutting machines
key-cutting-machines.full: Vintage key cutting machines (Curtis Clipper, Ilco, HPC, Cole National, Framon)
key-cutting-machines.fakes: None meaningful. Watch for married lots (cams from different machines) – check they fit the model. (general knowledge, verify)

kitchen-canister-sets.title: Kitchen canister sets
kitchen-canister-sets.full: Kitchen canister sets (Jeannette/McKee/Fire-King jadeite & Delphite, Hazel-Atlas, Hall China, Kromex, Mirro/West Bend aluminum, Lincoln Beautyware, Holt-Howard, Ransburg, Pfaltzgraff, R.B. Bernarda)
kitchen-canister-sets.money: jadeite/Delphite/green-glass square lettered canisters $75–300 each, full sets $400–1,500.
kitchen-canister-sets.fakes: - Jadeite: large volume of 1990s–2020s Chinese reproductions and Martha Stewart/Pottery Barn "jadeite" (2000s) – brighter colour, crisp, sometimes marked "Martha by Mail". Fire-King jadeite is also reproduced (no Fire-Ki

Painted tin (1940s–70s): Ransburg (Indianapolis, hand-painted fruit/flowers on red, black, yellow), Lincoln Beautyware, Decoware, Chein (litho), Kreamer.

lane-furniture.title: Lane furniture
lane-furniture.full: Lane furniture (Acclaim, Rhythm, Perception, cedar chests; Lane Company, Altavista VA)

laser-tag-toys.full: 1980s laser-tag toys (Entertech/LJN Photon, Worlds of Wonder Lazer Tag)
laser-tag-toys.fakes: No fakes; later Tiger/Hasbro reissues may be listed as "vintage". (general knowledge, verify) Check the copyright line.

Moulded copyright line: "© 1986 Worlds of Wonder" or Entertech/LJN on the 1980s units; later units carry Shoot the Moon, Tiger Electronics, Hasbro or Nerf marks.

latin-american-and-caribbean-hallmarks.full: Latin American and Caribbean hallmarks (Peru: Camusso, colonial Lima and Cuzco; Bolivia: Potosí; Chile: Mapuche silver; Argentina and Uruguay: platería criolla, mates, bombillas, facones, Pallarols, Patarca; Colombia and Ecuador 18K, pre-Columbian replica gold; Brazil: 750 gold, H. latin-american-and-caribbean-hallmarks.buy: Weigh it and read the mark: 900/925/800 or "PLATA" with "PERU/BOLIVIA/ARGENTINA" pays at ≤ 80% of melt; "ALPACA", "PLATEADO", "BAÑO DE PLATA" and "metal" without a fineness are not silver; pay over melt only for Camusso, signed criollo smiths, 18K applique you

latin-american-folk-art.title: Latin American folk art
latin-american-folk-art.full: Latin American folk art (Tonalá burnished and petatillo pottery, Tlaquepaque, Mata Ortiz, Oaxacan alebrijes and barro negro, Olinalá lacquer and Michoacán bateas, Metepec trees of life, Guatemalan/Mexican clay banks, Peruvian retablos, Ocumicho devils)
latin-american-folk-art.money: master works (Juan Quezada, large Soteno trees, early Wilmot) $500–5,000+.

latin-american-folk-art.buy: Pass on unsigned tourist pieces; look for signatures (Mata Ortiz potter names, Ken Edwards "KE"/"Tonalá Mexico", Wilmot), fine-line burnished petatillo and thin-walled Mata Ortiz pots; buy at ≤ 1/3 of a signed resale.
tells: Jorge Wilmot (Tonalá): high-fired stoneware with refined birds/flowers, signed; $150–800.

Tonalá burnished (barro bruñido/ "bruñido"): low-fired matte clay, hand-burnished to a soft satin, painted in grey, blue-grey, rust, cream and black with birds, flowers, rabbits, deer; jugs (pitchers), vases, plates, animals. 1930s–60s pieces are finer, thinne
Petatillo (Tonalá): very fine cross-hatched background ("little mat") behind animals; the finest Tonalá work.

lawn-games.title: Vintage lawn games
lawn-games.full: Vintage lawn games (croquet sets: Jaques, Forster, Sportcraft, South Bend, Spalding, Brookline; lawn bowls: Thomas Taylor, Jaques; horseshoes, badminton)
lawn-games.money: boxed early sets and Jaques London sets $150-500 (a complete c.1860–80 Jaques Prize Medal set carried a £1,000–1,500 estimate but went unsold, Bellmans 2025)
lawn-games.fakes: Distressed "antique" decor mallets. Jaques still makes croquet sets; modern Jaques sets carry current branding and are not antiques.
lawn-games.buy: Pass on full croquet sets (too long/heavy for shipping); consider only early boxed sets or Jaques at ≤ $50, or small lawn bowls/ring sets.
tells: English "association" croquet sets (Jaques and rivals), 1860s–1950s — four (or eight) heavy mallets with square-ended or cylindrical boxwood or lignum heads, often brass-bound at the ends, ash shafts about 36–37" long; solid composition or wood balls in blue,
Victorian garden/parlour sets, 1860s–1890s — eight mallets and balls, ten hoops, start and finish posts, scoring abacus, gilt-brass clips (Bellmans lot 696).

American backyard sets, 1880s–1990s — painted maple mallets with coloured rings, banded shafts, wire wickets, two striped stakes, on a wooden stand or wire cart; mid-century sets by Forster, Sportcraft, South Bend, Spalding.

leather-briefcases.title: Vintage leather briefcases and satchels

Top-zip or messenger: Coach, Ghurka, Filson; leather or twill with leather trim.
Ghurka: chestnut leather or khaki/army twill with leather trim, brass hardware, a numbered model name (Express No. 2, Examiner No. 5) and a registration number.

leather-motorcycle-jackets.title: Leather motorcycle jackets
leather-motorcycle-jackets.full: Leather motorcycle jackets (Schott Perfecto, Langlitz, Vanson, Buco, Harley-Davidson, Brooks, Lewis Leathers, Belstaff, Wilsons, Excelled, Bermans)

Police / "Highway Patrolman": Schott 118/618 with belt and "D" pocket.

madame-alexander-dolls.full: Madame Alexander and Vogue Ginny-type 8" dolls (Alexander Doll Co. "Wendy/Alexander-kins", Cissy, Cissette, Lissy, Elise; Vogue Ginny; Nancy Ann Storybook; Effanbee; McDonald's Happy Meal Madame Alexander minis)

Portuguese: Bordallo Pinheiro (cabbage ware, 1884–present), Secla; marked.

mantel-clocks.full: American mantel & shelf clocks (Seth Thomas, Gilbert, Waterbury, Ansonia, Ingraham, Sessions, New Haven, Chelsea)

mauchline-and-tartan-ware.title: Mauchline ware and tartan ware
mauchline-and-tartan-ware.full: Mauchline ware and tartan ware (W. & A. Smith of Mauchline, Archibald Brown, Davidson, Wilson & Amphlet)
mauchline-and-tartan-ware.fakes: Modern reproductions are rare but tartan "style" boxes from the 1950s–80s (Japan, Hong Kong, UK souvenir) and decoupage DIY pieces exist. Tell: no clan name, fabric rather than paper, plastic film surface, screw hinges.
mauchline-and-tartan-ware.buy: Buy real tartan ware (paper tartan on sycamore, clan name printed on it) under $40 for small cases or under ~1/3 of sold median; most priced over $60 are pass.
tells: Tartan ware: covered with tartan pattern — first hand-painted (pre-1840s, rare), then machine-printed paper tartan glued on and heavily varnished (1840s–1900). Usually a clan tartan name is printed in small gold/black letters on a seam or band ("McBeth", "Stua
Transfer ware: plain varnished sycamore with a black transfer print of a tourist view (seaside towns, churches) — the most common.
Fern ware (fern-leaf stencil), photographic ware, Black lacquer with views, Tunbridge-like pieces.

mccoy-pottery.title: McCoy pottery
mccoy-pottery.full: McCoy pottery (Nelson McCoy Pottery Co., Roseville OH, 1910–1990; J.W. McCoy; Brush-McCoy)
mccoy-pottery.money: rare cookie jars (Hillbilly bear, Pontiac Indian), large Arts-and-Crafts jardinieres, rare colours $100–600.
mccoy-pottery.fakes: - McCoy cookie jars (Mammy, Aunt Jemima, Hillbilly) have widespread repros, including fake "McCoy" marks (the trademark lapsed; reproductions in the 1990s marked "McCoy" by Mt. Clemens/Ohio). Smaller size and soft detail
mccoy-pottery.buy: Buy only rare cookie jars, large jardiniere/pedestal sets or rare-colour 1940s floor vases at ≤ $40; pass on planters, Floraline and common vases.
tells: 1926 stoneware line (Nelson McCoy Sanitary & Stoneware): embossed pitchers like Buccaneer, Grape, Pine Cone, Indian; green or brown glaze; often marked shield/clover or unmarked.
Mass-produced American art and kitchen pottery. Glossy solid glazes (aqua, pink, yellow, green, white) on 1940s–50s pieces; matte green and brown Onyx on 1920s–30s stoneware.
Marks: "McCoy" in block or script, "NM USA" (1930s–40s), "McCoy USA" with LCC (Lancaster Colony 1974+). Many unmarked.

mechanical-stopwatches.title: Mechanical stopwatches
mechanical-stopwatches.full: Mechanical stopwatches (Minerva, Heuer/Heuer-Leonidas, Hanhart, Gallet, Meylan, Longines, Excelsior Park, Lemania, Breitling, Elgin/Waltham, Camero, Junghans, Smiths)
mechanical-stopwatches.money: split-seconds (rattrapante) by Heuer, Minerva, Longines, Excelsior Park and silver-cased antique chronograph stopwatches $300–1,500+ (general knowledge, verify
mechanical-stopwatches.fakes: Low at the common level. Heuer redials and franken parts exist on higher-value timers; some Heuer "military" timers are civilian timers with engraved backs. Split-second Heuers at $1,000+ are authentication-sensitive.
mechanical-stopwatches.buy: Pass on plain sports timers (they cannot clear the $50 floor); buy split-seconds, Heuer, Longines, military-marked and silver-cased timers at ≤ 30% of estimate with a start/stop/reset video.

melody-in-motion-figurines.title: Melody in Motion musical figurines
melody-in-motion-figurines.full: Melody in Motion musical figurines (Willitts Designs; sculptor Seiji Nakane)
melody-in-motion-figurines.money: Santas, carousels, multi-figure/large or limited pieces $60–150
melody-in-motion-figurines.fakes: No meaningful fakes – value is too low. Risk is confusing generic resin musical figures (Enesco, San Francisco Music Box Co., unbranded) for Melody in Motion. Check the label.
melody-in-motion-figurines.buy: Only buy working, unchipped pieces with the original box ≤ $25, or Santa/carousel/large multi-figure pieces ≤ $40; pass non-working movements.

mens-formal-accessories.title: Men's formal accessories
mens-formal-accessories.full: Men's formal accessories (cummerbunds, bow ties, pocket squares, stud and cufflink sets; After Six, Lord West, Selix, Ike Behar, Pierre Cardin, Swank, Anson, Hickok, Krementz, Larter, Brioni, Charvet, Turnbull & Asser)
mens-formal-accessories.money: 14k gold or enamel jeweled stud sets (Cartier, Tiffany, Krementz 14k) $150–1,500+.
mens-formal-accessories.fakes: Fake hallmarks on luxury studs; high-end pieces need authentication (excluded). "14K GE" or "14K HGE" means gold electroplate, not solid gold. A "14K" stamp on a piece that shows brass at the wear points is suspect; ask
mens-formal-accessories.buy: Pass on fabric cummerbund/bow-tie sets; only stud/cufflink sets marked 14K/18K or sterling, or designer jeweled sets, at ≤ 1/3 resale (gold = melt floor).
tells: Stud backs show the age: one-piece collar-button style and spring "Bodkin clutch" backs are early (Krementz had a Bodkin-clutch stud c.1916). Bullet/toggle cufflink backs are mid-century, and fixed-swivel "whale backs" are mid-century onward. Patent numbers on
Title words: "dress set", "tuxedo studs", "Krementz", "14K", "rolled gold", "Swank", "MOP".
Fabric sets: pleated cummerbund (pleats face up), pre-tied bow tie and pocket square. Mostly polyester from rental houses (Selix, After Hours, Gingiss).

metal-lunch-boxes.title: Metal lunch boxes , 1950–1985
metal-lunch-boxes.full: Metal lunch boxes (Aladdin, Thermos/King-Seeley, Universal, ADCO, Ohio Art, Okay Industries), 1950–1985
metal-lunch-boxes.fakes: Licensed reproductions and retro tins exist (e.g. later reissues of Beatles, Star Wars and other popular titles; small "tin tote" versions) — usually thinner metal, modern copyright date, no wear consistent with age (gen
metal-lunch-boxes.buy: Buy 1950s–60s boxes with intact graphics under $75, dome-tops under $50, or key titles under 25% of sold range; pass 1975+ flat boxes over $15 and rusted boxes.

metronomes.title: Metronomes
metronomes.full: Metronomes (Wittner, Maelzel, Seth Thomas, Franz, Taktell, Paquet, Swiss Bürgi; pyramid wind-up and electric)
metronomes.money: 19th-century "Metronome de Maelzel / Paquet" French examples, rare woods, and early Seth Thomas with bell $100–300 (general knowledge, verify)
metronomes.fakes: Wittner continuously produces classic designs; antique-style Chinese copies with "Maelzel" labels; key tells are plastic parts and modern screws. - The "Métronome de Maelzel" label alone proves nothing about age or maker
metronomes.buy: Buy only 19th-century French "Maelzel/Paquet" or early Seth Thomas with bell, working, at ≤ $30; pass on modern Wittner/Taktell and electric metronomes.
tells: Label wording: many American and European metronomes carry a paper or plate label "Métronome de Maelzel" with a list of countries ("Paris, Amérique, Belgique, France, Hollande, Angleterre…") — this is the generic design label, not a maker's name; Seth Thomas e

Model numbers: Seth Thomas used numbers (e.g. "No. 7", mid-1960s, honey maple, per a Reverb listing title); Wittner "Maelzel" 800/810 series uses 80x for no-bell and 81x for bell models (e.g. 801M no bell, 816M with bell) (Reverb).
Bell: a bell model has a lever or knob to select beats per bar and a small bell visible inside; titles say "with bell".

mexican-silver.title: Mexican silver
mexican-silver.full: Mexican silver (Taxco and Mexico City: Spratling, Hector Aguilar, Los Castillo, Antonio Pineda, Margot de Taxco, Matl / Matilde Poulat, Sanborns, Tane, Maciel; modern TS/TM-coded and ATI production)
mexican-silver.fakes: - Fake Taxco and designer marks on Alpaca and on modern import silver (sterling-silver-jewelry entry). - Spratling and Aguilar designs are reproduced; post-1967 Spratling ranch production is legitimate but a lower tier.
mexican-silver.buy: Weigh first and pay ≤ 80% of melt for unsigned/modern pieces; pay up only for a readable eagle-plus-maker or named-designer mark whose sold median clears profit ≥ max($50, price); "Matl-style", "Spratling-style", bare "925" and "Alpaca" are not premium.

micro-machines.title: Micro Machines and small toy car lots
micro-machines.full: Micro Machines and small toy car lots (Galoob Micro Machines, Hot Wheels, Matchbox, Tonka, fast-food premiums)
micro-machines.fakes: Jazwares reissues; knock-off "mini cars" from China without Galoob marks; 2015–16 Hasbro Star Wars sets mistaken for 1990s Galoob.
micro-machines.buy: buy only real Galoob Micro Machines (≈1.5", "GALOOB" + year on chassis) or playsets at ≤ $40 when the lot is 50+ pieces or includes playsets/sealed packs.

middle-eastern-daggers.title: Middle Eastern and Asian daggers
middle-eastern-daggers.full: Middle Eastern and Asian daggers (Ottoman/Kurdish khanjar and jambiya, Omani khanjar, Yemeni jambiya, Persian kard and pesh-kabz, Caucasian kindjal/kama, Nepalese kukri/khukuri, Indian katar/chilanum, Moroccan koummya; Gurkha issue kukris by Ex-ACP/BSI, Indian army)
middle-eastern-daggers.money: jewelled or rhino-hilt pieces $1,000–10,000+ (rhino horn cannot legally be sold).
middle-eastern-daggers.fakes: Large export industry in India, Pakistan, Yemen, Oman, Morocco and Nepal making "antique" daggers with artificial aging (acid, sand, shoe polish). Fake tugra and assay marks. Rhino horn hilts are illegal to sell in US in
middle-eastern-daggers.buy: Pass on kukris and souvenirs over $25; buy only 19th c. silver-mounted Ottoman/Caucasian pieces with clear age wear ≤ $80.
tells: Kukri (Nepal): forward-angled recurved blade with a notch (cho) near the hilt, wood/horn/brass hilt with flared pommel and bolster, black leather scabbard with two small companion knives (karda and chakmak). pid 7930644440 is this, NOT a khanjar: heavy forward
Khanjar/jambiya: J-shaped curved double-edged blade with a central rib, hilt of horn/wood/silver with a T or mushroom pommel, scabbard sharply curved (Omani) or upturned (Yemeni).
Kindjal/kama (Caucasus): straight double-edged blade with offset fullers, silver-niello mounts.

military-field-gear.title: Military field gear
military-field-gear.full: Military field gear (US canteens, covers, mess kits, musette/haversacks, belts, compasses; makers Vollrath, Aluminum Goods Mfg., Landers Frary & Clark, Rex, Mills; compasses Superior Magneto, Waltham, Lensatic, Cammenga, Soviet Andrianov; European surplus bags)
military-field-gear.money: WWI/early items, German WWII originals, rare USMC/airborne items $150–1,000+ (authentication issues).
military-field-gear.fakes: Reproduction WWII US gear (dated stamps applied to new canvas) is common – too-bright khaki, synthetic thread. German WWII gear is the most faked area in militaria and requires expert authentication – outside Dylan's rul
military-field-gear.buy: Buy only dated, maker-marked US WWII compasses, M1936 musettes, USMC-marked gear, or complete WWI sets at ≤ 1/3 median; pass canteens, Soviet compasses, generic European bags; never buy German WWII without authentication.
tells: Compasses: WWII US lensatic (Superior Magneto, Waltham, Jewell, Union Instrument; "Corps of Engineers U.S. Army") $50–150; Vietnam-era Lensatic (Stocker & Yale, Cammenga); Soviet "Andrianov" wrist compasses (black dial with luminous markings, 0–360° bezel, str

Canteens: US M1910 shape (kidney-shaped, nested cup); aluminium (1910–42, 1944–), stainless steel (1942–45; example 7953218341 – stainless with black plastic cap), enamelled steel (1942–43), plastic (1960s+). Maker and date stamped on the shoulder ("Vollrath 1
Covers: M1910 khaki/OD canvas with "lift-the-dot" snaps and wool felt lining; maker/date stamped inside the flap ("J.Q.M.D. 1942").

military-insignia-and-maker-marks.title: Military insignia and maker marks — reading guide
military-insignia-and-maker-marks.full: Military insignia and maker marks — reading guide (US wings and insignia hallmarks: Amico, Luxenberg, N.S. Meyer, Vanguard, Josten, Balfour, Robbins, Gemsco; knife and bayonet contract marks: Ka-Bar, Camillus, PAL, RH-PAL, Case; M1 helmet seams and bails; dog-tag formats; US and British medal naming; Vietnam theater-made patches; Japanese WWII items; Soviet orders; holster and accessory stamps)
military-insignia-and-maker-marks.money: named casualty groups, rare wings (WASP, glider, liaison), theater-made SOG/recon patches and early Soviet orders $500–5,000+ — every high tier is fake-heavy.
military-insignia-and-maker-marks.fakes: - Insignia: post-war and modern casts of WWII wings with "STERLING" struck on base metal; wrong backs; modern Pakistani bullion-embroidered badges. - Knives: modern Ka-Bar 1217s aged to look WWII; fake blade markings; V-
military-insignia-and-maker-marks.buy: Value only from the back and the stamps: ask for photos of the maker mark, the "STERLING", the date, the heat stamp, the rim naming or the serial number; buy marked WWII pieces at ≤ 25–30% of a sold comp; pass on anything unmarked priced as WWII, on high-end i

military-insignia.title: Military insignia , Amcraft, N.S. Meyer, Blackinton, Balfour, Luxenberg, Robbins, Coro)
military-insignia.full: Military insignia (US Navy/USMC/Coast Guard cap devices, wings, collar and rank insignia, distinctive unit insignia, shoulder patches; makers Vanguard, Hilborn-Hamburger (H&H), Amcraft, N.S. Meyer, Blackinton, Balfour, Luxenberg, Robbins, Coro)
military-insignia.money: WWI and pre-WWI devices and rare wings $200–1,000+ (general knowledge, verify
military-insignia.fakes: Cast copies of WWII wings and devices with fake "STERLING" marks are common; reproduction theater-made and WWI pieces exist. Many modern Chinese replicas of US and foreign insignia are sold as "vintage". German WWII (Naz
military-insignia.buy: Never value from a front-only photo: ask for the back (STERLING + maker, attachment type); buy marked WWII sterling pieces and mixed lots at ≤ $8–10 per marked piece; pass on unmarked, post-war, and anything with Nazi or other hate symbols (policy kill).

miniature-cannons.title: Miniature cannons carbide cannons, cast-iron toy cannons , Italian/Spanish souvenir models)
miniature-cannons.full: Miniature cannons (signal/desk/toy cannons: cast brass/bronze decor models, Victorian bronze signal cannons, Big-Bang (Conestoga) carbide cannons, cast-iron toy cannons (Grey Iron, Kenton), Italian/Spanish souvenir models)
miniature-cannons.money: genuine 19th-century bronze signal/yacht cannons with bore and touch-hole $300–2,000+.
miniature-cannons.fakes: Indian-made "antique bronze signal cannons" are common; many marked "Napoleon" or with fake proof marks. Conestoga still makes Big-Bang cannons (date by casting details and paint).
miniature-cannons.buy: Pass souvenir desk cannons with crests and screw-assembled carriages; buy only Big-Bang carbide cannons (marked "Big-Bang", "Conestoga"), pre-1940 cast-iron toy cannons, and true bored signal cannons on wooden carriages at ≤ 25% of the ladder.
tells: Souvenir/decor models (1950s–present, Spain, Italy, Taiwan, India): solid or shallow-bored barrel, decorative crests ("coat of arms", "Toledo"), cast metal carriages with spoked wheels, slotted/Phillips screws, uniform dark patina with brass high spots. The ex

Signal / yacht cannons (1850–1920): heavy bronze barrel with a real bore (1/2"–1"), touch-hole, wooden naval truck carriage or iron carriage, often with maker marks or proof marks; can be functional black-powder pieces (antique-firearm rules apply to pre-1899)

Big-Bang carbide cannons (Conestoga Co., 1912–present): cast-iron/grey-painted barrels with "Big-Bang" cast in, plunger-igniter, calcium carbide ("Bangsite") fuel; models 6F, 10F, 15F, 25F, 60mm M60 tank, "Big Bang" field cannons.

miter-boxes.title: Miter boxes
miter-boxes.full: Miter boxes (Stanley 150/358/360, Millers Falls Langdon Acme 68–75, Goodell-Pratt, Disston, Sargent, Nobex)
miter-boxes.money: Stanley No. 358/360 or Langdon Acme 75 with original saw and full parts $100–250
miter-boxes.fakes: None. Married saws (a different maker's saw in the box) are common; state it.
miter-boxes.buy: Pass — 30 in long, 20–40 lb, $40–70 to ship; only small Stanley No. 150 or Goodell-Pratt boxes at ≤ $15 can make money.
tells: Millers Falls Langdon Acme: corrugated fence and swivel, "Langdon" casting; model number = box size + saw length.
Stanley: "Stanley" cast on frame, No. 346/358/360; flat fences. The 358 quadrant is numbered by polygon sides: 0 at 90°, then 24, 12, 8, 6 (30°), 5, 4 (45°) (Scodan).
Small clamp-type / wooden-base boxes (e.g. Stanley No. 150): small, light, a few pounds; the only shippable type.

model-kits-vintage.title: Vintage plastic model kits
model-kits-vintage.full: Vintage plastic model kits (Aurora, Monogram, Revell, Hasegawa, Airfix, Tamiya, Italeri)
model-kits-vintage.money: Aurora monsters, 1950s Revell ships, rare Japanese sci-fi $200–1,000.
model-kits-vintage.fakes: Reissues are the main issue: Aurora moulds were reissued by Monogram, Polar Lights and Moebius; Revell and Monogram repeatedly reissued 1960s kits with new box art (general knowledge, verify). Reissues are worth a fracti
model-kits-vintage.buy: Buy lots where Aurora / 1960s Monogram / early Tamiya are visible at ≤ $5 per kit average; pass 1980s+ 1/72 bins at ≥ $8 per kit.

modern-dinnerware.title: Modern dinnerware and serveware
modern-dinnerware.full: Modern dinnerware and serveware (Pottery Barn, Williams-Sonoma, Crate & Barrel, Rae Dunn, Gibson, Oneida, Tabletops Unlimited/Gallery, Certified International, Pfaltzgraff, Mikasa, Fiesta, Le Creuset/Emile Henry stoneware, Vietri, Juliska, Mackenzie-Childs, Arabia/Heath)
modern-dinnerware.money: Mackenzie-Childs Courtly Check, discontinued Heath/Arabia/Fiesta rare colours, Vietri large pieces $80–400.
modern-dinnerware.fakes: Not faked at the low end. Mackenzie-Childs and Le Creuset have knock-offs (Chinese check-pattern enamelware; enamel cast iron look-alikes). Fiesta reissued since 1986 (Homer Laughlin "HLC" mark with lower-case "fiesta" s
modern-dinnerware.buy: Pass on mass-market brands; buy only Mackenzie-Childs, Vietri, Juliska, Heath, Arabia, early Fiesta rare colours or Le Creuset at ≤ 1/3 of sold median; check backstamps.
tells: Premium: Vietri (Italian hand-painted, "Vietri Italy" + hand signature), Juliska (Berry & Thread), Mackenzie-Childs (Courtly Check black-and-white, gold and signed), Heath Ceramics (Sausalito, impressed mark), Arabia (Finland), Le Creuset and Emile Henry stone

Mass-market (China/Philippines/Indonesia): Gibson Designs, Tabletops Unlimited/Tabletops Gallery, Certified International, Oneida "Kitchen" lines, 222 Fifth, Better Homes; hand-painted-looking floral earthenware with thick glaze (Tuscan sunflowers, rooster, "S

Retailer brands: Pottery Barn (white "tea"/"coffee" typewriter-font pieces from the Coffee House line, Sausalito, Emma), Crate & Barrel, Williams-Sonoma, Rae Dunn (Magenta; tall black serif words); value limited.

modern-electric-guitars.title: Modern electric guitars — 2000s–present, import and budget US
modern-electric-guitars.full: Modern electric guitars (Kramer, Fender/Squier, Gibson/Epiphone, Ibanez, ESP/LTD, Jackson, Yamaha, Cort, Samick) — 2000s–present, import and budget US
modern-electric-guitars.fakes: Chinese counterfeit Gibson/Fender/PRS are common on marketplaces — tells: wrong headstock shape/logo, serial format, bolt-on neck on a "Les Paul", cheap hardware, price too good (general knowledge, verify). "Partscasters
modern-electric-guitars.buy: Buy Japanese- or US-made guitars priced as imports (≤ $200) or anything at ≤ 25% of Reverb used; pass current imports at ≥ 40% of used value.

modern-light-fixtures.title: Modern light fixtures
modern-light-fixtures.full: Modern light fixtures (mid-century and designer: Louis Poulsen, Nelson/Howard Miller bubble, Lightolier, Gerald Thurston, Stilnovo, Artemide, Flos, Kovacs, Raak, Nessen, Lightcraft of California; vs big-box builder-grade)
modern-light-fixtures.money: Nelson Bubble, Poulsen PH5/Artichoke, Stilnovo, Kovacs $200–2,000+.
modern-light-fixtures.fakes: Licensed reissues (Modernica Nelson Bubble, Louis Poulsen current production) and Chinese replicas of PH5/Artichoke/Sputnik/Bubble are everywhere — check labels, weight and wear.
modern-light-fixtures.buy: Pass on alabaster-swirl and big-box fixtures; buy marked mid-century designer pieces (label inside canopy) at ≤ $60 that ship in a carry-on box.
tells: Mid-century originals (high): spun aluminium in bright enamel colours, layered shades (PH), bubble-plastic over wire frame (Nelson), brass-and-walnut Lightolier/Thurston, Italian Stilnovo with coloured perspex, Danish Raak/Fog & Mørup glass. Labels inside cano

Builder-grade (low): white "alabaster swirl" acid-etched glass bowls, faux-bronze chain and canopy, "Tuscan" scroll arms, brushed-nickel 3-light bars. Made in China for Home Depot/Lowe's brands (Hampton Bay, Portfolio, Progress, Sea Gull).

modern-ukuleles.title: Modern ukuleles
modern-ukuleles.full: Modern ukuleles (Kala/Makala, Lanikai, Cordoba, Martin, Kamaka, KoAloha, Kanile'a, Ohana, Enya, Donner)
modern-ukuleles.money: Hawaiian-made (Kamaka, KoAloha, Kanile'a, Ko'olau) and Martin $400–1,500+ (general knowledge, verify)
modern-ukuleles.fakes: - Counterfeit Kala/Martin labels exist on Chinese no-name ukes but are uncommon; fake Kamaka is rare. - "Hawaiian" souvenir ukes (painted plastic, 1950s–70s Mainland makers like Maccaferri Islander plastic) are their own
modern-ukuleles.buy: Skip beginner laminates; buy only solid-wood or Hawaiian/Martin ukes where profit ≥ max($50, price) — the money is in Hawaiian koa.

modernist-costume-jewelry.title: Modernist / designer costume jewelry
modernist-costume-jewelry.full: Modernist / designer costume jewelry (Rafael of Canada, Aarikka, Trifari, Miriam Haskell, Eisenberg, Boucher, Schiaparelli, Juliana, Taxco, Lapponia, David-Andersen; Lia Sophia tier)
modernist-costume-jewelry.money: Haskell, Schiaparelli, Eisenberg Original, Boucher, Lapponia/David-Andersen $300–1,500.
modernist-costume-jewelry.fakes: Faked signatures exist for Haskell, Eisenberg, Schiaparelli and Chanel-style pieces; Juliana attributions are often wishful (general knowledge, verify). Some makers reissued designs (e.g. later Eisenberg Ice, modern Trif
modernist-costume-jewelry.buy: Buy signed Rafael/Haskell/Eisenberg/Schiaparelli/Juliana at ≤ 35% of sold, or lots showing hammered-brass-and-glass pieces at ≤ $25; pass sellers who name the designer and ask ≥ 50% of sold.

moroccan-decor.title: Moroccan Decor
moroccan-decor.full: Moroccan Decor (camel bone and nickel-silver candlesticks, boxes, mirrors; pierced brass lanterns; Berber silver; thuya wood)
moroccan-decor.money: antique Berber silver jewelry/daggers and Tuareg items $100–1,000+ (general knowledge, verify
moroccan-decor.fakes: Market dominated by new production made in the same way; "antique" claims rarely true. Imitation coral (plastic/glass) is long-standing even in genuine old pieces (Met). Tourist Tuareg crosses are made in quantity. Camel
moroccan-decor.buy: Pass on tourist-grade camel bone/metal pieces above ~$15; only buy antique Berber/Tuareg silver with hallmarks or documentable age at deep discount (and avoid ivory).

motion-clocks.title: Motion clocks
motion-clocks.full: Motion clocks (Mastercrafters, United, Spartus, Haddon, Rite-Time, Lux/Keebler, Sessions)
motion-clocks.money: Lux/Keebler wind-up pendulettes (Bobbing Bird, Shmoo, Woody Woodpecker) $100–600 (general knowledge, verify)
motion-clocks.fakes: Few reproductions. Some modern Chinese "waterfall" novelty clocks exist (clearly modern).
motion-clocks.buy: Untested electric motion clocks = pass; buy only tested-working rare models (Lux/Keebler pendulettes, rare Mastercrafters/United) at ≤ 1/3 of resale.

motion-lamps.title: Motion lamps
motion-lamps.full: Motion lamps (Scene in Action, Econolite/Roto-Vue, L.A. Goodman, Gritz-Ritter, Visual Effects, Rabbit Tanaka, Kohl's/Spencer's aquarium lamps)
motion-lamps.money: scarce Econolite titles (1962 Seattle, 1963 Venice, Hopalong Cassidy, Stutz Bearcat, pot-belly stove) are asked at $300–2,000.
motion-lamps.fakes: Econolite designs reissued in the 1990s–2000s (lighter plastic, UL labels with dates); a "1990 reproduction" was listed at $65. Replacement spinners (new) are common; married spinners from other titles also occur (check
motion-lamps.buy: Buy only 1950s Econolite/Scene in Action/Gritz-Ritter/L.A. Goodman with intact, round sleeves under ~$40; modern plastic fish lamps are a pass.
tells: 1950s Econolite (Los Angeles): cylinder or oval lithographed shade on a metal base (brass-finish, often on three ball feet), metal cap on top. The shade is printed with "ECONOLITE CORP. LITHO U.S.A. © [year] [number]". Typical shade 6 in diameter × 9.5 in tall

1920s–30s Scene in Action (Chicago): cast-metal (zinc) bodies, slag-glass panels, scene shown through a window in a figural or architectural housing; stamped copyright date on the back (e.g. "Copyright 1931 by Scene in Action Corp.").
1950s L.A. Goodman (Chicago): plastic and metal, often fireplaces, waterfalls and campfires.

motorcycle-helmets.title: Vintage motorcycle helmets
motorcycle-helmets.full: Vintage motorcycle helmets (Bell, Buco, Shoei, Arai, Simpson, McHal, Everoak, Cromwell, AGV, Nava, Honda/Harley-Davidson/Yamaha branded OEM helmets)
motorcycle-helmets.money: documented racer-used, Bell Star 1st-gen, rare colourways $500–2,500+.
motorcycle-helmets.fakes: Bell reissued the "Bell Star Classic" and "500-TX" (modern labels, DOT stickers, Chinese manufacture); repro Bell decals; modern "novelty" German/WWII-style helmets. Collector-grade Bell Stars need careful label checking
motorcycle-helmets.buy: Pass 1980s+ full-face helmets (OEM or not) above ~$20; buy only pre-1975 Bell 500/500-TX/Star, Buco, McHal and similar with intact original liners and visible labels at ≤ 30% of the ladder.
tells: 1966–1980: Bell 500-TX open face (big Bell "BELL" decal), Bell Star (1966, first full-face), Bell R-T, Shoei open faces, Arai; metalflake paint finishes highly desirable.
1950s–60s: leather "pudding basin", Everoak, Cromwell (UK), Buco "Guardian" (Buco Products, Toledo OH), early Bell 500 (1954–) – fibreglass shell, sparse snaps, chin strap with D-rings, leather trim.
1980s touring: full-face with intercom cords for Gold Wing/Aspencade (Honda "GL" wing badge), Harley-Davidson "Tour Pak" branded; smoked visors, ear speakers.

motorcycle-parts.title: Vintage motorcycle parts
motorcycle-parts.full: Vintage motorcycle parts (Harley-Davidson, Indian, Triumph/BSA, Honda, Bates/Buco accessories)
motorcycle-parts.fakes: Massive reproduction market (V-Twin, Paughco, Cycle Spectrum). OEM status must be shown by part number and features; "OEM" in listings is often wrong.
motorcycle-parts.buy: Only small, identifiable OEM pieces (emblems, NOS boxed parts, tank badges, speedometers ≤ shoebox) under $40; fenders/tanks are bulky and fitment-ID heavy - pass unless numbered and cheap.

mountaineering-ice-axes.title: Mountaineering ice axes, vintage wooden-shaft
mountaineering-ice-axes.full: Mountaineering ice axes, vintage wooden-shaft (Stubai, Charlet/Charlet-Moser, Simond, Grivel, Bhend, Hupfauf, Aschenbrenner, Chouinard)
mountaineering-ice-axes.money: historic expedition/named-maker pre-1940 axes $300–1,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
mountaineering-ice-axes.fakes: Modern decorative "vintage-style" axes exist; Indian-made reproductions exist.
mountaineering-ice-axes.buy: Buy marked Charlet/Simond/Bhend/Chouinard/early Aschenbrenner wood axes at ≤ 1/3 of resale; pass on souvenir/badged tourist axes above ~$30. Long axes (90 cm+) still fit a passenger seat diagonally.

movie-posters.title: Movie posters
movie-posters.full: Movie posters (US one-sheets, window cards, lobby cards, publicity stills; NSS-era originals vs reprints)
movie-posters.fakes: Reprints are the dominant problem: 24×36" commercial reprints and 27×39/27×40 reproductions of popular titles (Terminator, Star Wars, Jaws, Scarface) sold as "original". Faked NSS numbers on reproductions exist (general
movie-posters.buy: Buy confirmed NSS-numbered 1970s–80s cult/horror/sci-fi one-sheets at ≤ $60; pass framed posters without a back photo, 24×36/27×39 sizes and post-1995 titles.

multitool-kits.title: Multitool kits
multitool-kits.full: Multitool kits (Leatherman, Gerber, SOG, Victorinox, Buck; promo/Ozark Trail/generic gift sets)
multitool-kits.money: Leatherman/Victorinox $30–150 (Terapeak "Leatherman multitool kit" median $75, wide spread)
multitool-kits.fakes: Fake Leatherman/Victorinox exist and have hit eBay in waves (Multitool.org). Tells from a side-by-side real vs fake Tread: real screws are black only on the head and neck with bare threads, fake screws are black all the
multitool-kits.buy: Buy only Leatherman/Victorinox name tools under ~$15 in bulk (or a single retired/limited Leatherman under ~$25); generic sets are a pass.

murano-glass.title: Murano glass
murano-glass.full: Murano glass (Venini, Seguso, Barovier & Toso, Cenedese, AVEM, Salviati, Fratelli Toso, V. Nason; Murano-style imports)
murano-glass.fakes: - Chinese/Taiwanese "Murano" with fake Murano labels or "Murano" written on the base. - Fake Venini acid stamps and fake Archimede Seguso signatures (appraisily). - Modern Murano reproductions of Fazzoletto and sommerso
murano-glass.buy: Pass on animals, clowns, "lovers" sculptures and swirl vases; buy only heavy sommerso or labelled/signed mid-century pieces at ≤ $40, or a signed Venini/AVEM/Barovier piece at ≤ $100 after a base photo.
tells: Sommerso (submerged): thick, heavy pieces with two or more colours layered inside clear glass with crisp boundaries (Seguso/Flavio Poli 1950s–60s, Cenedese, Mandruzzato, later V. Nason). Teardrop bowls, faceted vases, birds and ducks.
Bullicante / controlled bubbles, pulegoso (frothy bubbles), aventurine (copper sparkles), zanfirico/filigrana (twisted white canes), murrine/millefiori (flower canes), lattimo, calcedonio (marbled).
Souvenir figurines (1960s–today): clowns, elephants, horses, fish, birds; often amber, with white or gold fused details; paper labels "Murano Glass", "ICET Arte Murano", "Made in Italy".

mustache-mugs.title: Mustache mugs and cups
mustache-mugs.full: Mustache mugs and cups (Victorian moustache cups; German, Austrian, English and American makers; RS Prussia, Limoges, ironstone, majolica)
mustache-mugs.money: majolica, RS Prussia, Limoges, sterling and left-handed cups $75–300+.
mustache-mugs.fakes: 1960s–80s Japanese and Chinese reproductions are the majority on the market; often thick, sharp edges, and modern backstamps.
mustache-mugs.buy: Buy only left-handed cups, majolica, sterling/silverplate quadruple-plate, or RS Prussia-marked cups with saucer at ≤ 25% of resale; pass on plain or souvenir porcelain.

nancy-ann-storybook-dolls.title: Nancy Ann Storybook dolls
nancy-ann-storybook-dolls.full: Nancy Ann Storybook dolls (Nancy Ann Storybook Doll Co., San Francisco, 1936–1971: bisque Storybook, hard plastic Storybook, Muffie, Debbie, Style Show, Miss Nancy Ann)
nancy-ann-storybook-dolls.money: Judy Ann, Topsy, Style Show 17–18" and mint rare series $150–600 (estimates).
nancy-ann-storybook-dolls.fakes: Few outright fakes. Risks are married outfits on the wrong doll, Japanese "occupied" lookalikes, and later hard-plastic dolls described as bisque. Boxes and wrist tags get swapped between dolls — match the box number/nam
nancy-ann-storybook-dolls.buy: Buy lots at ≤ $5 per doll when photos show boxes, gold wrist tags, jointed-leg bisque, Topsy/Judy Ann or 8" Muffie walkers; pass on lots of loose frozen-leg dolls in faded clothes above ~$8 each.
tells: Muffie (1953–56): 8" hard plastic, sleep eyes with painted upper lashes, straight-leg or bent-knee walker; competitor to Vogue Ginny. Debbie 10" (1955–57). Lori Ann 7½" vinyl (1957–58). Style Show 17–18" hard plastic, saran wig, elaborate gowns (1950s). Miss N

Hard-plastic era (1947/48–c.1955): same size and costumes but in lighter, warmer, slightly shiny hard plastic; painted eyes first, then sleep eyes; marked "STORYBOOK DOLLS USA" or "NANCY ANN STORYBOOK DOLLS". Tap test: bisque clinks like china, plastic clicks.

Small (5–6½") dolls with painted faces and mohair wigs in elaborate costume, sold by series (Mother Goose, Operetta, Days of the Week, Months, Seasons, Flower Girls, Around the World, Sports, Family, Big & Little Sister, Masquerade, Bridal).

native-american-turquoise-jewelry.title: Native American turquoise jewelry
native-american-turquoise-jewelry.full: Native American turquoise jewelry (Navajo/Diné, Zuni, Hopi, Santo Domingo/Kewa; Fred Harvey era; makers' hallmarks; also Southwestern-style imports, Bell Trading, Maisels, and modern Asian copies)
native-american-turquoise-jewelry.money: squash blossoms and top artists (Charles Loloma, Lee Yazzie, Kenneth Begay) $500–20,000+.
native-american-turquoise-jewelry.fakes: Huge problem: Indian Arts and Crafts Act makes selling non-Native work as "Native American" illegal. Fake hallmarks and fake "old pawn" tags. Dyed howlite/magnesite. Artist-signed high-end pieces need authentication (out
native-american-turquoise-jewelry.buy: Buy hallmarked or obviously handmade heavy sterling pieces at ≤ 1/3 of comps after weighing silver; pass on light link bracelets over $50 and anything with dyed/block stones.

navajo-squash-blossom-necklaces.title: Squash blossom necklaces
navajo-squash-blossom-necklaces.full: Squash blossom necklaces (Navajo / Southwest silver; Zuni and Pueblo; modern and import look-alikes)
navajo-squash-blossom-necklaces.fakes: Large market in imported "Native-style" jewelry sold as Navajo (illegal under the Indian Arts and Crafts Act if misrepresented, general knowledge, verify); fake turquoise (dyed howlite/magnesite, plastic); silver-plated
navajo-squash-blossom-necklaces.buy: Buy unmarked all-silver Navajo-style pieces under ~$1 per gram when the naja looks cast and the beads hand-formed; pass stamped imports and silver-plate.

needlepoint-rugs.title: Needlepoint rugs
needlepoint-rugs.full: Needlepoint rugs (Aubusson-style, Portuguese Arraiolos, Chinese hand-stitched needlepoint, English Victorian Berlin work, Stark/Patterson Flynn; vs machine-woven tapestry/jacquard "Aubusson")
needlepoint-rugs.fakes: Machine jacquard rugs and pillows constantly titled "needlepoint/Aubusson". Antique claims on 1990s Chinese production.
needlepoint-rugs.buy: Only hand-stitched (tent stitch visible on the back, wool) rugs ≤ 3×5 that fold into a carry-on box, at ≤ $40; pass on jacquard tapestry mats.

nemadji-pottery.title: Nemadji and swirl/marbleized pottery
nemadji-pottery.full: Nemadji and swirl/marbleized pottery (Nemadji Pottery, Garden of the Gods / "Indian" pottery, Ozark Roadside swirl, Niloak Mission Swirl)
nemadji-pottery.money: Niloak Mission/Swirl (Benton, AR, 1910–1940s) $75–600+ by size (general knowledge, verify)
nemadji-pottery.fakes: Nemadji continued until 2002 and current makers produce similar ware; age matters little. - The risk is a Nemadji-type painted piece listed as "Niloak swirl". The through-the-wall test settles it.
nemadji-pottery.buy: Pass on Nemadji (painted-dip surface, glazed interior); look instead for Niloak Mission Swirl — swirled clay body throughout, unglazed outside, NILOAK impressed mark — at ≤ $50.
tells: Niloak Mission (swirl) ware: differently coloured Arkansas clays were blended and thrown on the wheel, so the swirl is in the clay itself; the outside is left soft and unglazed and the inside is glazed to hold water (Just Art Pottery). Inside the rim and on th
Title words: Nemadji, Indian pottery, Native Clay, Badlands clay, Black Hills pottery, swirl, marbleized, Mission swirl, Niloak, Ozark pottery, Arkansas pottery.

Shapes: Nemadji used simple Southwest-style forms (bulbous vases, bowls, wedding vases with two spouts, small bottles). Niloak Mission pieces are mostly wheel-thrown vases, bowls, candlesticks and humidors with crisp, thin walls.

nikon-f-series-film-slrs.title: Nikon F / F2 / F3 professional film SLRs
nikon-f-series-film-slrs.full: Nikon F / F2 / F3 professional film SLRs (Nikon; also FM/FE/Nikkormat and consumer bodies for contrast)
nikon-f-series-film-slrs.money: F2 Titan, F2AS black, F3P, 250-exposure-back bodies $600–2,000.
nikon-f-series-film-slrs.fakes: Low fake risk. Watch for repainted chrome bodies sold as factory black and fake "Titan" or commemorative bodies (general knowledge, verify). Married finders (wrong head on body) are normal and fine, but price by the actu
nikon-f-series-film-slrs.buy: Buy when an F/F2/F3 body is in a lot under $120 or a black F2 body alone under $100; pass missing-Photomic F2s and sellers who name "F2" and ask $250+.

nippon-porcelain.title: Nippon porcelain
nippon-porcelain.full: Nippon porcelain (Japanese export porcelain 1891–1921: Noritake/Morimura Bros "M in wreath", Maple Leaf, Royal Kinran, RC; pre-Nippon; Moriage; Made in Japan successors)
nippon-porcelain.money: large moriage vases, coralene, figural/scenic humidors and tapestry ware $250–2,000.
nippon-porcelain.fakes: - Major problem since the 1970s–80s: fake Nippon marks (hourglass mark, "M in wreath" variants with wrong letters, "Nippon" with a crown-and-wreath combination, maple leaf fakes) on Chinese reproductions with crude decal
nippon-porcelain.buy: Buy only large (10"+) moriage or tapestry/coralene vases, humidors and scenic plaques at ≤ $50; pass on small floral dishes.
tells: Thin white porcelain hand-painted with roses, scenes, Art Nouveau borders, heavy gold, raised slip "moriage" beading and drips, cobalt bands.
Marks (base, green/blue/magenta): "Hand Painted NIPPON" with M-in-wreath (Morimura/Noritake), maple leaf (earliest, 1891+), Royal Kinran crown, RC Noritake. After 1921 US customs required "Japan".
Unmarked "pre-Nippon" pieces exist (pre-1891) and were also faked.

non-sports-trading-cards.title: Non-sports trading cards
non-sports-trading-cards.full: Non-sports trading cards (Topps, Fleer, SkyBox, Impel, Marvel/Comic Images, Pro Set, Upper Deck, Donruss, Bowman, Gum Inc., Wacky Packages, Garbage Pail Kids, Star Wars, Pokemon-adjacent)
non-sports-trading-cards.fakes: Reprints of Mars Attacks, Star Wars 1977, GPK; counterfeit unopened boxes (resealed). 1990s commons not commonly faked. Check card stock and print dot patterns for 1960s–70s.
non-sports-trading-cards.buy: Pass on loose 1990s commons and binders; only buy 1960s–80s Topps/Gum Inc. cards, unopened boxes/packs from before 1985, or graded keys, at ≤ 1/3 of verified sold prices.

norman-rockwell-collectibles.title: Norman Rockwell collectibles
norman-rockwell-collectibles.full: Norman Rockwell collectibles (Gorham, Dave Grossman Designs, Rockwell Museum, Bradford Exchange/Knowles, Franklin Mint, Danbury Mint, Lynell, Saturday Evening Post covers, Brown & Bigelow and Boy Scout calendars, signed lithographs)
norman-rockwell-collectibles.fakes: Fake pencil signatures on offset lithographs; printed "signatures" mistaken for hand signing; reproduction Post covers (1970s) on heavy paper.
norman-rockwell-collectibles.buy: Pass on all porcelain Rockwell collectibles; only hand-signed pencil lithographs (Circle Fine Art, Eleanor Ettinger), complete 1920s–40s Boy Scout calendars or uncut Post magazines are targets, and signed lithographs need authentication (pass unless documented
tells: Gorham bells: ~6" porcelain, turned wood handle, gold trim, title and year inside or on rim ("Chilling Chore" 1977, "Sweet Song So Young", "Gay Blades").
Saturday Evening Post covers (1916–1963): magazine covers, original or trimmed.
Calendars: Boy Scouts of America (Brown & Bigelow, 1925–76), Brown & Bigelow "Four Seasons".

novelty-pocket-watches.title: Novelty pocket watches
novelty-pocket-watches.full: Novelty pocket watches (Geneva, Infinity, Charles-Hubert, Gotham, Waltham-branded quartz, Japan-movement souvenir watches, Ingersoll character watches, Molnija)
novelty-pocket-watches.money: 1933–39 Ingersoll Mickey Mouse $150–600 loose, $400–1,500 boxed (guide figures).
novelty-pocket-watches.fakes: Generic novelty watches: not applicable; these are mass-market goods. Ingersoll Mickey: reprinted dials in original cases (the common deception), dials too crisp or colours too vivid, oval eyes on a "1933" dial, flat pri
novelty-pocket-watches.buy: Pass on mass-produced quartz/novelty pocket watches; they never clear the $50 profit bar. Exceptions: sterling-cased commemoratives below melt, and pre-war Ingersoll character watches.

olympus-om-lenses.title: Olympus OM Zuiko lenses
olympus-om-lenses.full: Olympus OM Zuiko lenses (Olympus; also Minolta MC/MD Rokkor & Celtic, Yashica ML, Pentax K/Takumar, Canon FD, store brands)
olympus-om-lenses.fakes: None significant. Risk is misidentification (e.g. 21/3.5 vs 21/2, Celtic vs Rokkor) and store-brand lenses titled as the camera brand.
olympus-om-lenses.buy: Buy collectible-tier lenses with clean glass under 40% of sold; pass fungus and sellers who already name the lens at near-market.

onewheel-boards.title: Onewheel self-balancing boards
onewheel-boards.full: Onewheel self-balancing boards (Future Motion: V1, Onewheel+, +XR, Pint, Pint X, GT, GT S-Series)
onewheel-boards.fakes: No real counterfeits; the risk is scams — stock or pawn-style photos at too-good prices — and stolen boards (ask for receipt/serial) (general knowledge, verify).
onewheel-boards.buy: Buy working, tested-in-person Onewheel+ ≤ $150 with charger, XR ≤ $300, GT ≤ $500; pass no-charger/untested/"won't balance" boards, V1s, and too-good pawn-style listings.

original-paintings.title: Original paintings – vintage decorator and amateur
original-paintings.full: Original paintings – vintage decorator and amateur (oil, acrylic, watercolour; commercial "studio" art, regional and amateur artists)
original-paintings.money: artists with real auction records $500+ (rare, need research).
original-paintings.fakes: - Prints on canvas sold as "original paintings" (check the surface and the signature – printed signatures are flat). - Hand-embellished prints (a few brushstrokes over a print) – look at the edges and shadows. - Forged s
original-paintings.buy: Buy only when the signature traces to an artist with documented auction sales (askART/LiveAuctioneers) or the piece is clearly pre-1940 with quality, and the sold median clears profit after shipping; never buy on "original oil" alone.
tells: Commercial "studio" oils (1960s–90s): painted quickly in workshops (Hong Kong, Taiwan, Mexico, Italy, later China) for furniture and department stores: palette-knife winter streams, birch forests, European street scenes, seascapes, florals. Generic signatures
Amateur paintings: hobby work, estate studio clear-outs (alcohol ink, acrylic pours, impasto), workshop exercises. Little resale demand.
Regional/listed artists: trained artists with gallery histories; signature, label, exhibition stickers or gallery stamps on the back; quality brushwork and drawing.

ouija-boards.title: Ouija and talking boards
ouija-boards.full: Ouija and talking boards (William Fuld, Parker Brothers; scarce makers: Kennard, Ouija Novelty Co., Isaac Fuld "Oriole", American Novelty "Ouija Queen", Haskelite, Mystic Hand, Swami, Volo, Espirito)
ouija-boards.money: pre-1920 Fuld/Ouija Novelty/Isaac Fuld Oriole/Kennard boards $300-1,500+
ouija-boards.fakes: Hasbro licensed "Classic Ouija" boards in wood (2016+, Winning Moves) and countless "antique style" Etsy/Amazon/Spirit Halloween boards; fakes of early Fuld boards exist (printed on new pine and distressed). Tells: moder
ouija-boards.buy: Buy a wood board with a Baltimore Fuld address or a non-Fuld/non-Parker maker name at ≤ $60; pass on any Parker Brothers (Salem/Bay Shore) board above $15.

pachinko-machines.title: Pachinko machines
pachinko-machines.full: Pachinko machines (vintage Japanese, 1960s–80s: Nishijin, Sankyo, Sanyo, Daiichi, Heiwa, Ginza)
pachinko-machines.fakes: No meaningful fakes. Risk is mixed/married parts and repainted playfields sold as original (general knowledge, verify).
pachinko-machines.buy: Buy only working 1960s single-shot or EM models at ≤ $100, local; pass "for parts or repair" and common 1970s machines over $50 that must ship.

paintball-markers.title: Paintball markers
paintball-markers.full: Paintball markers (Tippmann, Brass Eagle, Spyder/Kingman, Planet Eclipse, Dye, Smart Parts, WGP, AGD, vintage pump and stock-class guns: Nelson/Nel-Spot, Sheridan, PMI, Splatmaster)
paintball-markers.money: high-end electro (Planet Eclipse Ego/Geo, Dye DM) $200–700
paintball-markers.fakes: Clones of Autococker/Spyder bodies; no significant fake market. Note: brands reissued "retro" editions (e.g. Autococker, Shocker revivals), which sell as new guns, not vintage.
paintball-markers.buy: buy only high-end electro or vintage pump/stock-class guns ≤ $80, tested to hold air; never ship CO2/HPA tanks (hazmat) — sell tanks locally.
tells: High-end electro (2000s–now): Planet Eclipse Ego/Geo/LV/CS, Dye DM/DSR/M2, Smart Parts Shocker/Ion, Bob Long Intimidator, Angel; short barrels, electronic trigger frames with a battery, HPA tank, and an electronic hopper on top.

Vintage pumps and pistols (1980s): Nel-Spot 007 (Nelson Paint Co., Iron Mountain MI; the marker used in the first paintball game, chronicled by Sports Illustrated in 1981), Splatmaster (spring-powered .50 cal plastic pistol by JT; NSG Splatmaster pump), Sherid

Classic semi-autos and pumps (late 1980s–90s): Tippmann SMG-60 / SMG-68 (full-auto capable, stripper-clip fed), Line SI Bushmaster, AGD Automag, WGP Autococker (a rod and pneumatic ram along the top), Sheridan / Kingman, Bob Long, Shocker (Smart Parts), Angel

paper-cutters.title: Vintage paper cutters / guillotine trimmers , Premier, Kodak, Dahle, Boston/Hunt, Martin Yale, X-Acto, Rotatrim)
paper-cutters.full: Vintage paper cutters / guillotine trimmers (Milton Bradley, Ingento (Ingersoll), Premier, Kodak, Dahle, Boston/Hunt, Martin Yale, X-Acto, Rotatrim)
paper-cutters.money: ornate 19th-century cast-iron and patent paper cutters, Victorian brass desk cutters $80–300.
paper-cutters.fakes: Not a reproduction category. Modern "farmhouse" decor versions rare.
paper-cutters.buy: Pass – common school cutters are heavy/awkward to ship and resell $20–50; only 19th-century ornate cast-iron desk cutters or rare patent pieces at ≤ $20 are worth a look.
tells: Victorian: ornate cast-iron frames, gilded/painted, small desk models (photo/card trimmers).

1900s–60s: hardwood board, painted grid (green or white), brass or wood ruler, cast-iron hinge and handle, maker stamped on ruler or blade ("Milton Bradley Co. Springfield Mass", "Ingento No. 2 Ingersoll Chicago", "Premier Photo Materials", "Studio" model).
1970s+: aluminium/steel bases, plastic handles, safety guards, Dahle/Martin Yale/X-Acto/Swingline.
