paper-ephemera.title: Paper ephemera – travel brochures, park maps, theme-park guides
paper-ephemera.full: Paper ephemera – travel brochures, park maps, theme-park guides (SeaWorld, Disney, Busch Gardens, World's Fairs, roadside attractions, airline/railroad timetables)
paper-ephemera.fakes: Disney items and early tickets are reproduced; theme-park rack brochures are not worth faking. - Disney itself has issued commemorative reproductions of early tickets and maps (general knowledge, verify); check paper and
paper-ephemera.buy: Pass on single brochures; buy only pre-1970 Disney/World's Fair material or bulk ephemera lots ≤ $1/item that contain early theme-park guides.
tells: Disneyland ticket books date themselves by coupon letters: "Value Books" with A–C coupons began within three months of the July 1955 opening; D coupons were added in 1956 and E coupons in June 1959; coupons ended at Disneyland by June 1982. Walt Disney World's
Coupon face values (Wikipedia): A 10¢, B 15¢, C 25¢, D 50¢, E 85¢ — printed prices on the book also help date it.

World's Fair official guides are mass-market paperbacks with a 25¢ cover price (1933 Century of Progress, 1939 New York "World of Tomorrow"); the 1939 guide went through several editions, and the edition is stated in the book (EBTH lot listed a first and a thi

parking-meters.title: Vintage parking meters , Rockwell, M.H. Rhodes Mark-Time, Dual, Karpark, Mi-Co)
parking-meters.full: Vintage parking meters (Duncan / Duncan-Miller, Park-O-Meter (POM), Rockwell, M.H. Rhodes Mark-Time, Dual, Karpark, Mi-Co)
parking-meters.money: first-generation 1935–40 POM and rare makers $400–800. Lamp conversions sell as lamps $75–175.
parking-meters.fakes: Decorative reproduction meters and meter-shaped banks exist (general knowledge, verify). Replacement domes and new-old-stock parts (e.g. Duncan Miller "police will not turn handle" tags) are sold separately and can be us
parking-meters.buy: Buy 1930s–50s POM/Duncan-Miller/Rhodes heads, working with key, at ≤ $60; pass lamp conversions over $40 and 1970s+ Duncans over $50.

parlor-guitars.title: Vintage parlor guitars
parlor-guitars.full: Vintage parlor guitars (Harmony, Supertone/Sears, Regal, Kay, Stella/Oscar Schmidt, Washburn, Lyon & Healy, Martin, Gibson)
parlor-guitars.fakes: Modern reissue stencil guitars (Recording King, Gretsch, Loar) and Chinese "vintage-look" parlors. Tell by truss-rod covers, modern tuners, laser-cut stencils.
parlor-guitars.buy: Buy only crack-free, playable 1930s stencil or Stella guitars ≤ $50, or anything with a Stella/Lyon & Healy/Washburn/Martin label far below value; most priced $100+ are pass after big-box shipping.

parlor-lamps.title: Parlor, banquet and "Gone with the Wind" lamps
parlor-lamps.full: Parlor, banquet and "Gone with the Wind" lamps (Bradley & Hubbard, Pittsburgh Lamp Brass & Glass, Miller, Consolidated Lamp & Glass, Fostoria Glass Specialty, Fenton/Fenton-made reproductions, 1960s–80s electric GWTW lamps)
parlor-lamps.money: signed B&H/Pittsburgh/Consolidated lamps, figural and cased-glass lamps $300–1,500+.
parlor-lamps.fakes: - Massive volume of 1960s–80s electric repros; most Craigslist "antique banquet lamps" are these. Painted roses in yellow/burgundy with cream ground are the classic repro look. - Married pieces (old base, new shade) comm
parlor-lamps.buy: Buy only Victorian lamps with original matching shade and burner, period cast metal or art-glass fonts, at ≤ $60 and only if Dylan can ship the globe safely; pass on electric repros.
tells: Named designs sought by collectors include Pittsburgh "Mermaid and Seagulls", "Sheiks and Camels", "Joan of Arc", "Lady and the Swans" and "American Indian" scenic lamps (Monroe Times).
GWTW / parlor lamp: a glass base/font (often painted to match) with a ball or tulip globe shade, kerosene burner with chimney; 1880–1910 peak.
Banquet lamp: tall (24–36") slender stand, usually cast spelter or brass with an oil font and ball shade.

paul-flato-compacts.title: Paul Flato compacts
paul-flato-compacts.full: Paul Flato compacts (Paul Flato, 1948–1950s; vs unsigned Majestic, Elgin American, Volupté)
paul-flato-compacts.money: figural boxed sets $250–600 and precious-metal Flato jewelry in the $1,000s. Terapeak: 16 sold, median $108, p75 $140.
paul-flato-compacts.fakes: No known widespread fakes (general knowledge, verify). The risk is attribution: unsigned jeweled compacts listed as "Flato style" or "attributed to Flato". Only buy signed or boxed.
paul-flato-compacts.buy: Buy signed Flato (or box visible) with lipstick for ≤ $60, compact alone ≤ $35; pass unsigned, heavy stone loss, or price > $100.

pendleton-blankets.title: Pendleton & trade blankets
pendleton-blankets.full: Pendleton & trade blankets (Pendleton Woolen Mills, Hudson's Bay Company, Oregon City Woolen Mills, Cabin Craft)
pendleton-blankets.money: Oregon City, Pendleton "Round Up" and pre-1920 labels $600–2,000.
pendleton-blankets.fakes: Pendleton continually reissues heritage patterns (Chief Joseph, Harding, Glacier Park) — modern labels distinguish them (general knowledge, verify). Imported "Aztec"/"Southwest" acrylic blankets are listed as "Pendleton
pendleton-blankets.buy: Buy jacquard Pendleton/HBC with a vintage label at ≤ $80 and no moth holes; pass solid satin-bound blankets over $25 and anything needing sewing.

pez-dispensers.title: Pez dispensers , PEZ Candy Inc. ; made in Austria, Yugoslavia, Hungary, Hong Kong, China, Slovenia)
pez-dispensers.full: Pez dispensers (PEZ Haas (Austria), PEZ Candy Inc. (Orange CT); made in Austria, Yugoslavia, Hungary, Hong Kong, China, Slovenia)
pez-dispensers.money: "Regulars" (1950s, no head) and rarities (Make-a-Face, Bride, Elvis, Political) $300–10,000+.
pez-dispensers.fakes: Re-releases of classic characters in footed versions; counterfeit rarities (Make-a-Face, Political, Elvis) with re-moulded heads; married stems. Rarities need collector authentication.
pez-dispensers.buy: Buy only no-feet dispensers (thin stem without bottom feet) with an uncommon character at ≤ $5–10 each, or lots containing 1960s–70s no-feet heads at ≤ $3 per piece; pass on footed and carded post-1987 Pez.
tells: Regulars: 1950s dispensers with no character head (lighter-shaped) are the original product.
Feet: stems with small "feet" at the bottom were introduced c.1987. No feet = older (pre-1987) — the single biggest value tell.

photography-studio-gear.title: Photography Studio Gear
photography-studio-gear.full: Photography Studio Gear (Westcott, Lastolite/Manfrotto, Profoto, Neewer, Emart, Impact, Savage)
photography-studio-gear.money: pro strobes (Profoto, Elinchrom, Broncolor) $200–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
photography-studio-gear.fakes: Godox rebrands; counterfeits not significant. - Look-alikes: budget C-stands copy the Matthews shape; read the casting. Many budget strobes are rebadged Godox units.
photography-studio-gear.buy: Skip budget kits; only pro-brand strobes/modifiers that are tested and shippable, and most strobes are untested electronics — so in practice pass.
tells: Where the model is: monolights carry the model name on the rear panel or side label (Profoto D1/D2/B1/B10, Elinchrom BRX/ELC, Einstein E640, AlienBees B800/B1600); pack-and-head systems have the name on the pack face.

C-stand anatomy: chrome or black steel column on a three-leg "turtle" (removable) or sliding-leg base, plus a grip head ("knuckle") and a 40 in grip arm. Matthews, Avenger (Manfrotto group) and Kupo are the main pro brands; the brand is cast or stamped on the

Vintage film lights: Mole-Richardson ("Mole") fresnel spotlights, e.g. Type 407 Baby Solarspot and Type 414 Solarspot, with cast housings and a type/serial plate. Decorators buy them; the floor-stand versions are usually bigger than the passenger-seat rule.

pioneer-cdj-decks.title: Pioneer CDJ / DJ media players
pioneer-cdj-decks.full: Pioneer CDJ / DJ media players (Pioneer DJ / AlphaTheta: CDJ-200 to CDJ-3000, XDJ)
pioneer-cdj-decks.fakes: No fakes. Stolen club gear is a risk with too-cheap listings; check serials are intact (general knowledge, verify).
pioneer-cdj-decks.buy: Buy tested CDJ-1000MK3/900 ≤ $120, CDJ-2000 ≤ $250, NXS2 ≤ $600; pass untested or disc-reading problems and CDJ-200/400/800 over $50.

pitcher-and-bowl-sets.title: Pitcher and bowl sets
pitcher-and-bowl-sets.full: Pitcher and bowl (wash) sets (English ironstone and semi-porcelain: Johnson Bros., Meakin, Wood & Son, Doulton Burslem, Grindley, Colonial Pottery, Ford & Sons; flow blue; Victorian blush ware; American Homer Laughlin, KT&K, Carrollton)
pitcher-and-bowl-sets.money: flow blue sets, complete toilet sets with chamber pot/soap dish, signed Doulton/Wedgwood $200–700+.
pitcher-and-bowl-sets.fakes: Décor reproductions (above). Mix-and-match: pitcher and bowl from different patterns or makers sold as a set — check backstamps match.
pitcher-and-bowl-sets.buy: Wash sets almost never clear shipping (12–15 lb, $40–70 each way, high breakage); buy only for local resale or if a flow blue/Doulton set is ≤ $40; otherwise pass.
tells: Blush ware (1890s–1910s): ivory/peach ground with floral transfers and gilt scrolls (Royal Worcester blush ivory and many imitators — Wood & Son, Carlton, Wiltshaw & Robinson, Doulton Burslem) — like the $40 set in our sweep.

English Staffordshire (most common): ironstone or semi-porcelain with transfer-printed patterns in blue, teal, green, brown or multicolour; gilded edges; printed backstamp with pattern name and maker.
Flow blue: deliberately blurred cobalt transfers (1840s–1910s) — the premium category.

platinum-and-palladium-marks.title: Platinum and palladium marks
platinum-and-palladium-marks.full: Platinum and palladium marks (PLAT, PLATINUM, IRIDPLAT, 10% IRID, PT/Pt950/Pt900/Pt850, 950 PLAT, PD/PALL; French dog's head, UK orb, Japanese Pt; Edwardian and Art Deco platinum-and-diamond jewelry)
platinum-and-palladium-marks.money: with a 0.5–1 ct old European cut $1,500–6,000+
platinum-and-palladium-marks.fakes: - **Deco-style repros** in sterling, 14K white gold or base metal, sometimes stamped "PLAT" or "PT950" fraudulently (general knowledge, verify). Weight is the best check: a fake "platinum" ring is too light. - **"Platinu
platinum-and-palladium-marks.buy: A "silver" or "white metal" Deco/Edwardian piece with a PLAT/IRIDPLAT/Pt mark or a dog's head is worth melt (~$49/g) plus its diamonds — pay ≤ 40% of melt-plus-conservative-stone value, and never pay platinum prices for 18K white gold, silver or palladium.

plush-toys.title: Plush toys
plush-toys.full: Plush toys (Steiff, Gund, Ty, Merrythought, Charlie Bears, Melissa & Doug giant plush, Jellycat, FAO Schwarz)
plush-toys.money: early Steiff with button/tag $100–2,000+, pre-1950 Steiff bears $500–10,000+ (Appraisily range
plush-toys.fakes: - **Fake Steiff buttons** are added to other makers' bears and to new bears; check the button type matches the bear's era (eyes, fur, shape) — a brass button on a bear with shoe-button eyes is wrong. - **Steiff replicas*
plush-toys.buy: Buy only small Steiff (button in ear) or other pre-1960 mohair jointed bears/animals, or retired Jellycat, under ~$20; giant plush never fits rules.
tells: Fur: mohair 1902–1950s (silky, with patina and bald spots at high points); alpaca 1910s–30s; silk plush 1920s; cotton plush 1930s–50s;
Eyes: boot/shoe buttons c. 1900–1920s; glass (amber or black, painted backs) 1920s–1950s; plastic safety eyes from the 1950s, standard by the 1960s.
Stuffing: excelsior/wood wool 1900s–1930s (firm, crunchy, rustles); kapok 1920s–50s; cotton 1940s–60s; polyester/foam from the 1960s.

po-box-doors-and-postal-collectibles.title: PO box doors and postal collectibles
po-box-doors-and-postal-collectibles.full: PO box doors and postal collectibles (Yale & Towne, Keyless Lock Co., Corbin, Salsbury, Eagle Lock; Triner, Pelouze, Hanson postal scales; letter boxes, mail slots, post office signage)
po-box-doors-and-postal-collectibles.money: large ornate early doors with beveled glass, sets of matching doors, and Triner/early postal scales with weights $60–250 (general knowledge, verify)
po-box-doors-and-postal-collectibles.fakes: New-made "PO box door" bank kits are everywhere (craft stores, eBay, ~$20–30 new). Reproduction porcelain US Mail signs are common. Fake "post office" scales in brass from India.
po-box-doors-and-postal-collectibles.buy: Doors are cheap commodities; buy only ornate early brass doors (eagle/Victorian pattern, combination dials that work) at ≤ $15 each or matched lots ≤ 1/4 of sold; Triner "Official Postal Scale" only if complete and ≤ $30.

pocket-knife-lots.title: Pocket-knife lots
pocket-knife-lots.full: Pocket-knife lots (Case XX, Buck, Boker, Schrade, Camillus, Remington, Randall, Marttiini, Imperial, Colonial)
pocket-knife-lots.money: pre-1940 Case XX stag/bone, Remington bullets, Randalls $300–2,000+.
pocket-knife-lots.fakes: Case and Remington have counterfeit and "reproduction" bullet knives; Remington reissued bullet knives in the 1980s–90s as collector issues (general knowledge, verify). Chinese fakes of Buck 110 and Case exist. Re-handle
pocket-knife-lots.buy: Buy lots at ≤ $8/knife with visible Case XX bone or Buck 110 pieces, or 1960s–70s Case XX singles ≤ $25; pass sellers pricing named knives at $25+/knife and auto knives.

pocket-transits.title: Pocket transits
pocket-transits.full: Pocket transits (Brunton / Wm. Ainsworth & Sons, Brunton Co., Keuffel & Esser "Natural Sine")
pocket-transits.money: early Ainsworth with box/papers or military-marked $300–500.
pocket-transits.fakes: Decorative brass "Brunton-style" compasses from India are sold as antique (general knowledge, verify) — tells: poor engraving, no maker/serial, cheap mirror. Modern Brunton reissues are marked as current production. Veri
pocket-transits.buy: Buy genuine (aluminium) Ainsworth under $70 and K&E/later aluminium under $35; pass K&E at $60 (sold ~$100, profit < $50); pass brass "Bruntons" (replicas).

point-and-shoot-film-cameras.title: Point-and-shoot film cameras
point-and-shoot-film-cameras.full: Point-and-shoot film cameras (Olympus Stylus/mju, Contax T2/T3, Yashica T4/T5, Ricoh GR1, Nikon 35Ti, Konica Big Mini, Minolta TC-1, Leica Mini, Canon Sure Shot, Yashica Auto Focus)
point-and-shoot-film-cameras.money: cult primes (Olympus mju II ~$250, Nikon L35AF ~$200, Konica Big Mini ~$200, Yashica T4/T5 ~$550) $150-550
point-and-shoot-film-cameras.fakes: Not faked, but listings misidentify models (T4 vs T4 Super, mju vs mju II). Kyocera Slim T / T Proof are legitimate twins of the T4 / T4 Super, not fakes.
point-and-shoot-film-cameras.buy: Buy fixed-prime cult compacts ≤ $50 only with seller test (flash fires, lens extends); pass on untested generic zooms.

pokemon-card-lots.title: Pokémon card lots & binders
pokemon-card-lots.full: Pokémon card lots & binders (Wizards of the Coast 1999–2003, Nintendo/The Pokémon Company International 2003+; Japanese cards)
pokemon-card-lots.money: 1st Ed Charizard, Gold Stars, Crystal, Shiny Charizard GX, alt-art Umbreon $800–20,000+.
pokemon-card-lots.fakes: Fake cards are very common (Chinese counterfeits): wrong font, washed-out or overly glossy colours, wrong back blue, no dark inner layer (rip/light test), misspellings, wrong energy symbols (general knowledge, verify). F
pokemon-card-lots.buy: Buy lots ≤ $100 that show ≥ $250 of identifiable singles in close-ups; pass lots with no close-ups of rares, 2010s+ binders at $100+, and "mystery lots".
tells: Value lives in: holo/reverse-holo rares, full-art, secret rares (card number higher than the set size, e.g., 110/108), "Rainbow", Gold, alt-art, and any Charizard. Commons/uncommons in bulk: $0.02–0.10 each.

Card back: all eras share the blue Pokéball back; 1999–2000 Base/Jungle/Fossil have no set symbol (Base) or a Jungle/Fossil symbol, thick black border bottom text "©1995, 96, 98 Nintendo". Shadowless / 1st Edition stamps (left of the art box) on Base Set = the

Era by bottom-left/right symbols: e-Reader bar (2002–03), EX era (2003–07) with "ex" cards, Diamond & Pearl (2007–10), HGSS/Black & White (2010–13), XY (2014–16) – "XY" set symbols, full-art EX and "Break" cards, Sun & Moon (2017–19) GX, Sword & Shield (2020–2

polaroid-instant-cameras.title: Polaroid instant cameras
polaroid-instant-cameras.full: Polaroid instant cameras (Polaroid 600 OneStep/Sun 660, SX-70, Spectra, Land cameras, Impossible/Polaroid Originals)
polaroid-instant-cameras.money: pack-film Land 100–400 series $25–100, Model 180/195 $200–500 (general knowledge, verify)
polaroid-instant-cameras.fakes: Refurbished "Retro Polaroid" resellers; modern Polaroid Now. No fakes per se.
polaroid-instant-cameras.buy: buy only folding SX-70/SLR 680/690 or Land 180/195 at ≤ $60, tested with a film shot; 600 box cameras are a pass.

polaroid-sx-70-cameras.title: Polaroid SX-70 folding cameras
polaroid-sx-70-cameras.full: Polaroid SX-70 folding cameras (Polaroid: original SX-70, Alpha 1, Model 2, Model 3, Sonar OneStep, Alpha 1 SE; MiNT SLR 670; vs box cameras)
polaroid-sx-70-cameras.money: Alpha 1 SE, refurbs with warranty, MiNT SLR 670, 180/195 pack cameras $300–900.
polaroid-sx-70-cameras.fakes: No fakes. Refurbished and re-skinned cameras (Retrospekt, MiNT, Brooklyn Film Camera) are sold at dealer prices ($300–600; $350–450 refurb); modified "MiNT SLR 670" bodies are a separate higher tier (general knowledge, v
polaroid-sx-70-cameras.buy: Buy a tested SX-70 original/Alpha 1/Sonar at ≤ $90, a Sonar described as working under $60, or any folding SX-70 under $40 inside a lot; pass stand-alone untested over $70, mirror haze, or ≥ $150.

porcelain-figurines.title: Porcelain figurines
porcelain-figurines.full: Porcelain figurines (Lladró, Hummel/Goebel, Royal Doulton, Meissen, Nymphenburg, Rosenthal, Royal Copenhagen, Gerold, Fran Mar, Japan imports)
porcelain-figurines.fakes: - Meissen crossed swords is the most copied mark; overglaze or crudely painted swords, heavy bright figures = later copies. Dresden-style and "Capodimonte" sold as Meissen. - Asian Hummel copies; Nao confused with Lladró
porcelain-figurines.buy: Never buy without a base photo; pass on Japan/Taiwan bisque and post-1960 German gift figures; ask for the base when an unmarked figure shows 1900–1930s German art-porcelain modelling, and buy only if the mark checks out at ≤ 25% of sold.
tells: Crisp, lively modelling of a costume or period character (dancers, Rococo couples, Directoire dandies, Pierrots) with expressive faces, fine hand painting, pastel enamel washes and gilt base bands = German art porcelain c.1900–1935 (Rosenthal Kunstabteilung, N

Underglaze blue marks: Meissen crossed swords, Nymphenburg impressed shield (with numbers), Rosenthal green crown "Rosenthal Selb Bavaria" with "Kunstabteilung" and an artist signature on the base edge, Hutschenreuther lion with "Kunstabteilung", Royal Copenha

Japan/Taiwan/Korea bisque (1950s–80s): big-eyed children ("Moppets", Lefton, Enesco, Napco, Fran Mar), pastel colours, soft modelling, octagonal or rocky base, paper label or "Japan" stamp. Usually 4–7".

porcelain-trinket-boxes.title: Porcelain trinket boxes
porcelain-trinket-boxes.full: Porcelain trinket boxes (Limoges “Peint Main”, Halcyon Days enamels, Royal Crown Derby, Herend, Capodimonte, Heritage House, Lenox, San Francisco Music Box, Formalities/Baum Bros gift ware)
porcelain-trinket-boxes.fakes: Chinese "Limoges-style" boxes with fake "Limoges" marks (no "France", wrong hinge, poor painting) are common. - Reproductions are openly sold as decor (Hunker); a lookalike with no decorator name and a weak clasp is the
porcelain-trinket-boxes.buy: Buy only Limoges “Peint Main” (Rochard, Artoria, Chamart, Beauté) figural boxes or Herend at ≤ $10 each / lots ≤ 1/3 comps; pass gift-ware heart boxes.
tells: Mark wording seen on genuine pieces: "Rochard, Peint-Main, Limoges, France"; "Artoria Peint Main Limoges France" plus extra characters; "Limoges France PV Marque Déposée Peint Main" (1stdibs listings). "Peint main" = hand painted; "Marque déposée" = registered

Shapes collectors look for: figural novelties (houses, champagne bottles, coffee makers, ice-cream carts, animals, shoes, handbags) and themed boxes with a tiny loose accessory inside (e.g. a removable bone in a Rochard pug box).

English enamel boxes are enamel on copper, not porcelain: 18th-century Bilston/Battersea patch boxes (with a mirror), snuff boxes and animal bonbonnières, typically no more than about 2" (Homes & Antiques); modern Halcyon Days, Crummles and Bilston & Battersea

portable-music-players.title: Portable music players
portable-music-players.full: Portable music players (Sony Walkman cassette/Discman/MiniDisc/Network Walkman, Apple iPod, Aiwa, Panasonic, Toshiba, Creative Zen, Microsoft Zune, iRiver)
portable-music-players.fakes: Fake iPod Classics (Chinese clones) and refurbished/modded iPods; new retro cassette players (Jensen, We Are Rewind) are not Sony. Apple publicly warned of counterfeit iPods as early as 2006 (AppleInsider). Clone tells:
portable-music-players.buy: No untested electronics: buy only tested, known-model high-tier cassette/MiniDisc units at ≤ 1/3 of comps; pass flash players.

postmodern-halogen-lamps.title: Postmodern / Memphis-era halogen lamps
postmodern-halogen-lamps.full: Postmodern / Memphis-era halogen lamps (Sonneman, Kovacs, Koch & Lowy, Artemide)
postmodern-halogen-lamps.fakes: Modern Saturn-style knock-offs and current Sonneman Lighting production exist. Memphis/Artemide designs have been reissued and later issues are worth less than period pieces (general knowledge, verify). A missing label i
postmodern-halogen-lamps.buy: Identified Sonneman/Kovacs Saturn ≤ $80, other designer-attributed 1980s halogen ≤ $60, glass unchipped; pass over $120.
tells: Memphis-style Ettore Sottsass or Michele De Lucchi lamps (Artemide) are a tier above.
Robert Sonneman for George Kovacs "Saturn": stacked frosted-glass rings/dome on two thin black columns, round black marble or metal base, about 22–23" tall.
Sonneman "Flying Saucer" floor lamp.

power-tool-accessories.title: Power tool accessories
power-tool-accessories.full: Power tool accessories (saw blades, router bits, drill bits, flexible shafts, jigs, dado sets: Freud, Forrest, Systimatic, Amana, DeWalt, Craftsman, Delta, Rockwell, Black & Decker, Foredom)
power-tool-accessories.money: dado sets $40–200 (Forrest Dado King, Freud SD508)
power-tool-accessories.fakes: Counterfeit Freud/Diablo blades sold online; not a concern at this level. - Asian-made tenoning jigs copy the Delta design; lighter, but some owners prefer them (forum).
power-tool-accessories.buy: Pass on mixed used blades and generic attachments; only buy Forrest/Freud/Systimatic dado sets or Foredom flex-shaft machines at ≤ 1/3 of sold median.
tells: Title words: Forrest, Woodworker II, Dado King, Freud SD508, Systimatic, Foredom, flex shaft, tenoning jig, Delta 34-172, molding head, dado set.

Saw blades: steel (one-piece, small teeth, often rusty, worth scrap) vs carbide-tipped (brazed grey tips). Brand on the plate: Master Mechanic (True Value), Craftsman, DeWalt, Vermont American = cheap; Forrest Woodworker II (no branding colour, laser-etched),
Dado sets: stacked chippers and two outer blades in a case.

precious-metal-marks-reading-guide.title: Precious-metal marks — master reading guide
precious-metal-marks-reading-guide.full: Precious-metal marks — master reading guide (fineness numbers, karat marks, Russian zolotnik and kokoshnik, Soviet star, UK/French/Japanese/Chinese/Arabic marks, plated and filled marks, assay scrapes)
precious-metal-marks-reading-guide.money: Melt per gram at gold $4,200 / silver $60 / platinum $1,620: 9K $51 · 10K $56 · 14K/585/56-zolotnik $79 · 18K/750 $101 · 21K $118 · 22K $124 · 24K/足金 $134–135 · sterling $1.78 · 800 silver $1.54 · Pt950 $49. A mark the seller didn't read is the whole edge: an 8 g "gold tone" brooch stamped 56 is ≈ $
precious-metal-marks-reading-guide.fakes: - **Fake 585/750/14K stamps on base metal**, especially on Turkish, Chinese and online "Italian" chains — magnet, weight and the colour at wear points (general knowledge, verify). - **Fake 925** on base-metal chains and
precious-metal-marks-reading-guide.buy: Read every mark before reading the title; price from (grams × fineness × spot); pay ≤ ~40% of melt when scrapping and ≤ ~43% of the realistic sold price when reselling, so profit ≥ max($50, price) after fees and shipping both ways; any plated/filled mark (GF,

precision-measuring-tools.title: Precision measuring tools
precision-measuring-tools.full: Precision measuring tools (Starrett, Mitutoyo, Brown & Sharpe, Lufkin)
precision-measuring-tools.fakes: Counterfeit "Mitutoyo" digital calipers are common on marketplaces: wrong fonts, missing serial, cheap case (general knowledge, verify). Starrett and Brown & Sharpe vintage fakes are rare. Mixed-brand "sets" in one case
precision-measuring-tools.buy: Buy Starrett/Mitutoyo/B&S sets or boxes in a lot at ≤ 30% of resale; pass on single calipers and mics.
tells: Where the marks are: micrometers on the frame (front face, often with the catalog number and range, e.g. "No. 436 0–1 in."); patent dates are often on the back of the frame on older mics; calipers on the beam or dial face; indicators on the dial face and back;
Reading a mic set photo: count the instruments against the case slots and look for the setting standards (the steel rods for 1–2", 2–3" etc.) and the spanner wrench.
Look-alikes: Craftsman, Fowler, Central Tool, Harbor Freight/Pittsburgh, Insize and no-name imports. Fowler and Insize are honest mid/low brands, not fakes.

press-cameras.title: Press cameras
press-cameras.full: Press cameras (Graflex Speed Graphic, Crown Graphic, Century Graphic, Miniature Speed Graphic, Super Graphic; Busch Pressman, Burke & James, Linhof Technika, Wista, Mamiya Press, Koni-Omega)
press-cameras.fakes: None meaningful; prop/movie replicas exist but obvious. Watch for franken-combos (wrong lens board) — lower value, not fraud.
press-cameras.buy: Buy 4x5 Pacemaker Speed or Crown Graphics with a lens (Ektar, Optar, Xenar) ≤ $100 if shutter fires on all speeds in a seller video; pass on 2x3 minis and lensless bodies over $50.
tells: Pre-Anniversary (1928–1939): black hardware, no "Anniversary" plate.
Anniversary (1940–1946): black-painted metal (wartime), wooden body, no rear tilt.
Pacemaker (1947–1970): chrome hardware, body release, top rangefinder (Kalart then Graflex), lens board "Graflex" nameplate.

pressed-steel-farm-toys.title: Pressed-steel farm toys
pressed-steel-farm-toys.full: Pressed-steel farm toys (Tru-Scale, Ertl, Carter, Doepke)
pressed-steel-farm-toys.fakes: Reproduction decals and replacement tyres are sold for restorers, so restored pieces can look original (general knowledge, verify). Ertl has reissued many classic tractors as collector editions, so check for modern dates
pressed-steel-farm-toys.buy: Tru-Scale/Ertl lots ≤ $15/piece with original paint, or a complete Doepke ≤ $80; pass on repaints and per-piece pricing at $40+.
tells: Ertl: cast-aluminium tractors with "ERTL" under the seat.
Doepke Model Toys: large 1/16 construction toys (Adams road grader, Barber-Greene loader) in orange/yellow. $150–400 complete.

Tru-Scale (Carter Tru-Scale, Rockford IL): "TRU-SCALE" on the hood decal, slotted-spoke rubber tyres, red implements. Implements include the hay elevator (long angled belt), baler (square box with tines), spreader, disc, plow and wagon.

pressed-steel-toy-trucks.title: Pressed steel toy trucks
pressed-steel-toy-trucks.full: Pressed steel toy trucks (Buddy L, Keystone, Structo, Tonka, Smith-Miller, Wyandotte, Marx, Nylint; modern decorative tin replicas)
pressed-steel-toy-trucks.money: 1920s–30s Buddy L/Keystone $200–2,000+, postwar Smith-Miller in the upper range (general knowledge, verify)
pressed-steel-toy-trucks.fakes: Repro Buddy L and decor replicas. Also: reproduction decals and parts are sold for restorers, so a restored truck can look factory-new (Appraisily). Asian décor "antique" trucks (Model T pickups, fire trucks, tankers wit
pressed-steel-toy-trucks.buy: Buy 1920s–50s Buddy L/Keystone/Smith-Miller under ~$60; modern tin decor is a pass.
tells: Size: prewar Buddy L trucks are big — the 1920s tank/sprinkler truck is about 25 in long (ATCA). Postwar Tonka/Structo/Nylint are typically 10–22 in (general knowledge, verify). Décor replicas are usually 10–20 in with exaggerated spoke wheels.

Where the maker shows: Buddy L — decals and embossed names on doors/sides (e.g. "BL" seat-end decals and licence-plate decals on some 1930–32 trucks — ATCA); Tonka — oval "Tonka Toys" decal and "Mound, Minn." stampings on early pieces, embossed Tonka marks und
Construction: genuine toys are formed from heavy-gauge sheet with crimped tabs and rivets; décor replicas use thin sheet, visible modern nuts/bolts and Phillips screws, and painted-on "rust".

primitive-farm-tools.title: Primitive farm tools
primitive-farm-tools.full: Primitive farm tools (hay forks, pitchforks, shovels, scythes, grain cradles, sickles, flails, hay knives, corn knives, wooden rakes, ox yokes; makers True Temper, Ames, Union Fork & Hoe, Hussey, Kelly, Plumb, Belknap Bluegrass)
primitive-farm-tools.fakes: Modern imported "rustic" wooden hay forks and rakes for decor (Eastern Europe/China); look for real wear on tines and handle. - Tells of new decor forks: fresh pale wood under dark stain, uniform tine thickness, no rivet
primitive-farm-tools.buy: Long-handled farm tools don't fit Dylan's passenger-seat rule and are local-only items; pass all of them except small hand tools (corn knives, hay hooks, small sickles) under $10 in lots.
tells: All-wood hay forks (1800s, often New England/Pennsylvania/Europe): one piece of bent wood split into 2–5 tines, held apart by wooden dowels/cross-pieces — the decorator prize. American forks were traditionally hickory (occasionally white oak); ash also works a

How a real wooden fork is built (photo-checkable): the fork is split from one billet; the split stops at saw kerfs at the base of the tines, with an iron rivet just above the kerfs to stop the split running; tines are bent so the growth rings run along the tin
Steel-tined pitchforks (1880s–1960s): 3–5 tines with ferrule and ash handle; "True Temper", "Union", "Ames" stampings on the ferrule or tang.

primitive-kitchen-tools.title: Primitive kitchen tools , butter molds and paddles, dough bowls, rolling pins, apple peelers , cherry pitters , coffee grinders, mashers, nutmeg graters, cast-iron — see separate cast iron entry if present)
primitive-kitchen-tools.full: Primitive kitchen tools (kraut/cabbage cutters, cone sieves/chinois (Wear-Ever, Mirro), butter molds and paddles, dough bowls, rolling pins, apple peelers (Reading Hardware, Goodell White Mountain), cherry pitters (Enterprise), coffee grinders, mashers, nutmeg graters, cast-iron (Griswold, Wagner) — see separate cast iron entry if present)
primitive-kitchen-tools.money: signed/dated pieces, folk-carved butter molds, large burl bowls $200–1,500.
primitive-kitchen-tools.fakes: New "farmhouse" dough bowls (Indonesian/Mexican mango wood, distressed), reproduction butter molds, and aged kraut cutters. Look for authentic wear and tool marks.
primitive-kitchen-tools.buy: Pass on kraut cutters and Wear-Ever sieves (sold medians $16 and $25); hunt hand-carved butter stamps, burl/hewn dough bowls and patented cast-iron apple peelers at ≤ 30% of median.
tells: Kraut cutters/slaw boards: rectangular board with 1–3 diagonal steel blades and often a sliding box hopper; 1880s–1950s; common, often Pennsylvania/Midwest made, some with heart cut-outs (folk, more valuable).
Cone sieves (chinois): aluminum cone with perforations, wooden pestle, three-leg wire stand. Wear-Ever No. 8 (most common), No. 475/480/462; Mirro. 1930s–60s.
Butter molds/stamps: carved wood with designs (cows, sheep, eagles, wheat) — eagles and animals sell well.

primitive-wooden-trays.title: Primitive wooden trays
primitive-wooden-trays.full: Primitive wooden trays (19th–early 20th c American country cutlery trays, knife boxes, dough bowls and trenchers, tool totes; 1970s decor caddies; new "farmhouse" reproductions)
primitive-wooden-trays.money: signed/dated or exceptional paint and Shaker pieces $300–1,500+.
primitive-wooden-trays.fakes: Large reproduction market: distressed, painted "primitive" trays with heart handles sold by décor shops; also old boxes fitted with new handles (as in the example here). Also: old plain trays newly painted in "milk paint
primitive-wooden-trays.buy: Buy only trays with original old paint or dry untouched surface, hand-cut dovetails or square nails and an original (matching-wear) handle, ≤ 18" long, at ≤ $35; pass on refinished, replaced-handle and 1970s novelty pieces.
tells: Construction: hand-cut dovetails (few, uneven, thin pins), cut/square nails, wooden pegs = 19th c; machine dovetails/wire nails/staples = 20th c.
Surface: original dry paint (milk paint, worn through at handle and rims), grime-darkened patina, consistent oxidisation inside and out. Refinished or stained surfaces reduce value sharply.
Handle: heart, tulip or scalloped cut-outs are folk-art pluses — but the handle must show the same age and wear as the box. A pale, crisp-edged handle in a dark box is a replacement.

pro-audio-accessories.title: Pro audio accessories
pro-audio-accessories.full: Pro audio accessories (cables and connectors: Mogami, Canare, Belden, Neutrik, Switchcraft, Cannon/ITT; mic mounts: Neumann, AKG, Shure; DI boxes: Radial, Countryman, Jensen; patch bays: ADC, Switchcraft, Bittree; horn throats/adapters: Altec, JBL, Western Electric, Electro-Voice)
pro-audio-accessories.money: vintage Western Electric/Cannon connectors and rare Altec/JBL horn parts $200–1,000+.
pro-audio-accessories.fakes: Counterfeit Neutrik connectors (lighter, weak latch, no "Neutrik" logo moulded into the insert) and counterfeit Mogami cable are common on cheap Asian marketplace cables. Generic shock mounts sold as "Neumann-style".
pro-audio-accessories.buy: Buy only branded mic mounts (Neumann EA-xx, AKG H-xx), vintage patch bays/TT bays, Jensen/Radial DI boxes and identified Altec/JBL/Western Electric horn parts at ≤ 1/3 sold median; pass mixed cable lots and unidentified adapters.
tells: Horn throat adapters: cast aluminium or iron spacers with a flange at each end, bolt holes matching a driver pattern (e.g., Altec 3-bolt 1.4", JBL 2"/4-bolt) – examples 7959622827 and 7959623697 are cast, black-painted 1.4–1.5" to 2" adapters with an ear/lug f

Cables: XLR (3-pin, Neutrik with black boots and chuck-type strain relief; Switchcraft A3F/A3M nickel barrels with set-screw; Cannon XLR-3 ITT older), 1/4" TS/TRS (Switchcraft 280/297 nickel plugs), RCA, breakout/Y-cables (example 7928965992 – Switchcraft-styl
Cable brand: printed on the jacket (Mogami 2534/W2549, Canare L-4E6S, Belden 8412/1192A, Gotham GAC-3). Branded quad cable has value; generic/unprinted does not.

pro-audio-di-and-eq.title: Pro-audio rack and stage gear
pro-audio-di-and-eq.full: Pro-audio rack and stage gear (dbx EQs, Radial DIs, Shure Green Bullet, Numark, TASCAM)
pro-audio-di-and-eq.fakes: Counterfeit Shure mics exist, mostly SM58s; Green Bullet fakes are less common (general knowledge, verify). Urei 1176 has UA reissues and many DIY clones, and Neve/API modules have clones. Check the serial and internals
pro-audio-di-and-eq.buy: Only in lots at ≤ 35% of Reverb sold median; single items at > 60% of median are a pass.
tells: Radial passive DIs: ProDI $50–70, ProD2 stereo $90–130, J48/JDI $120–180.
Rapco/Whirlwind DIs: $15–30.

quimper-faience.title: Quimper faience
quimper-faience.full: Quimper faience (HB Quimper, Henriot, HB-Henriot, Porquier, Keraluc; plus "Quimper-style" peasant pottery from Italy, Japan, Desvres)
quimper-faience.money: large early chargers, figurines by named artists $200–2,000.
quimper-faience.fakes: Desvres made copies with HB-like marks; Asian copies. Henriot reissues old designs today. Many "Quimper-style" bowls from Italy and Japan show Dutch-style couples with fruit — clearly different costume (Dutch wooden shoe
quimper-faience.buy: Buy only pieces with a painted "HB Quimper", "HenRiot Quimper" or "AP/Porquier" mark showing pre-1940 style, Odetta stoneware, or named-artist figures at ≤ 25% of resale; pass on unmarked "Quimper-style" and modern souvenir pieces.

racing-memorabilia.title: Racing memorabilia
racing-memorabilia.full: Racing memorabilia (NASCAR: Action, Racing Champions, Revell, Wheels, Press Pass, Competitive Motorsports Products, Goodwrench/Winston promo; Indy 500 programs; F1)
racing-memorabilia.money: race-used parts, sheetmetal, firesuits, signed items with COA $100–1,000+
racing-memorabilia.fakes: - Forged autographs are endemic (Earnhardt especially). Fake "race-used" sheetmetal. Reprinted posters. - COAs are unregulated. Embossing, holograms and elaborate certificates prove nothing. The gold standard is photo pr
racing-memorabilia.buy: Pass on 1990s posters, calendars and common diecast; buy only pre-1985 programs/posters or race-used items with documentation at ≤ 1/3 resale; autographs need authentication (excluded).
tells: 1990s licensing produced enormous quantities. The market collapsed after the mid-2000s, and Earnhardt items spiked briefly after 2001 then fell.

Programs: about 8.5 × 11 in souvenir books. The first Daytona 500 (February 20–22, 1959) program is the landmark NASCAR paper (EBTH lot description). Indy 500 programs run back to 1911, and the speedway sells official reprints ("Program Vault"), so reprints ex
Diecast: the box end names the maker, scale and edition size. Premium Action/RCCA cars have opening hoods and detailed engines, and many are coin banks ("bank" with a slot in the rear window).

railroad-lanterns.title: Railroad lanterns
railroad-lanterns.money: tall-globe cast coloured, bell-bottom, rare roads $300–1,500.
railroad-lanterns.fakes: New Chinese "Dietz" lanterns are common. Reproduction cast railroad globes are common, especially coloured ones, so verify on any lantern over $300. Frames can have stamps added after the fact (general knowledge, verify)
railroad-lanterns.buy: Railroad-marked with cast or coloured globe ≤ $50, or tall-globe ≤ $80; pass on unmarked, repros, or named-road asks of $75+.
tells: Tall-globe (pre-~1920): globe ~5.5"+, brass-top or bell-bottom frames.
Short-globe (1920s–60s): Dietz Vesta, Adlake Kero, Handlan.
railroad initials stamped on the lid or frame (S.P. Co, UP, PRR, B&O…)

railroad-spittoons.title: Railroad spittoons and cuspidors
railroad-spittoons.full: Railroad spittoons and cuspidors (genuine low-profile railroad-marked brass/enamel/china; Handlan-Buck supplier; tall vase-shaped "Union Pacific", "Wells Fargo", "Pullman", "Chattanooga Choo Choo" reproductions; non-railroad hotel, bank and stoneware cuspidors)
railroad-spittoons.money: genuine railroad-marked low-profile spittoons $150–500+ (general knowledge, verify
railroad-spittoons.fakes: The whole tall, embossed "railroad" spittoon category is fake per railroad historians (Railroadiana) and the UP museum; they keep reappearing online with invented 1800s histories. Also reproduced: "Wells Fargo" and "Pull
railroad-spittoons.buy: Kill every tall, vase-shaped spittoon with a railroad or express-company name or a locomotive; consider only low, heavy, wide-based pieces with simple cast-in railroad initials, at ≤ $40 and with a clear base photo.
tells: Authentic railroad spittoons are low-profile and heavy (hard to tip over), with a wide mouth or funnel top, sometimes enamelled (the UP museum shows short green, silver and brass-coloured examples). Railroad marks are simple initials, cast in or incorporated i

Reproductions are tall, vase-shaped brass imports of the last few decades, embossed with company names — Union Pacific Railroad, Wells Fargo & Company Express (San Francisco Division), Pullman Silver Palace Car Company, Chattanooga Choo Choo, Hannibal & St. Jo

Companion field note (railroadiana entry, 2026-10-14): thin spun-copper bodies with a brass flare and an embossed 4-4-0 locomotive over "UNION PACIFIC RR" / "NORTHERN PACIFIC R.R." are 1970s–80s decorative souvenirs; real railroad spittoons are heavy cast/weig

railroadiana.title: Railroadiana — dining car silver, china, lanterns, locks/keys, timetables
railroadiana.full: Railroadiana — dining car silver, china, lanterns, locks/keys, timetables (Reed & Barton, International Silver, Gorham, R. Wallace, Adams Westlake, Dietz, Handlan, Syracuse, Buffalo, Shenango)
railroadiana.fakes: Fake railroad marks are common on keys, locks, lanterns (new globes etched with initials), and signs. Silver is less often faked but generic hotel silver with an added stamp exists. China reproductions of Mimbreno and B&
railroadiana.buy: Buy only top- or side-marked railroad pieces of less-common roads or scarce forms, at ≤ 1/3 of realistic sold; pass on common PRR/NYC individual teapots above ~$30.

rattan-rocking-horses.title: Rattan / bamboo rocking horses
rattan-rocking-horses.fakes: Modern Pier 1-style and import repros exist. The "Albini" attribution is the usual over-claim, not a fake per se.
rattan-rocking-horses.buy: ≤ $40, excellent, local pickup only (or a realistic $250+ Chairish sale); pass at $50+ when it has to be shipped.

record-store-crates.title: Record-store & advertising wooden crates
record-store-crates.full: Record-store & advertising wooden crates (Peaches, brewery, fruit)
record-store-crates.fakes: Repro Peaches crates and labels have been made for collectors and fans. Decorative "vintage-style" brewery crates are sold new at home stores (general knowledge, verify). Check for staples, fresh wood and too-perfect pri
record-store-crates.buy: Peaches LP crates ≤ $20 each, pre-Prohibition brewery crates ≤ $30; pass on cassette-size Peaches over $10 each and on Napa Valley crates.
tells: Peaches Records & Tapes (1970s–80s chain) crates: a pine slat crate with a lithographed "Peaches" fruit label on the end. Two sizes: the LP crate, ~13×13×12" (the one people want), and the small cassette crate, ~8×12×6".
Napa Valley Box Co. crates: 1980s–90s cassette/CD racks, common.
Brewery crates: stencilled or branded ends, dovetail or nailed corners. Pre-1920 breweries (U.S. Brewing Co. Chicago, Schlitz, Pabst) bring the most. 1950s–70s Coke/Pepsi crates are $15–30.

records-comics-cards-and-media-identifie.title: Records, comics, cards and media identifiers — reading guide
records-comics-cards-and-media-identifie.full: Records, comics, cards and media identifiers — reading guide (vinyl dead wax and labels, comic price/edition variants and CGC labels, card print/rookie/serial/error/O-Pee-Chee tells, video-game seals and box variants, Disney VHS)
records-comics-cards-and-media-identifie.money: sealed round-seal Zelda $870,000. Disney "black diamond" VHS is the reverse: $1–25.
records-comics-cards-and-media-identifie.fakes: - **Vinyl:** counterfeit Beatles (Vee-Jay), butcher covers and bootleg white labels; 2000s–2020s 180 g reissues with copied original labels but barcodes and modern matrices; reproduction obis. - **Comics:** altered price
records-comics-cards-and-media-identifie.buy: Read the label, dead wax, price box, UPC box, card back or seal before the title; pay only for a mark you can see in a sharp photo, price from the sold comp for that exact variant (never the regular copy and never an asking price), and keep to ≤ ~40% of the re
tells: VHS: the spine and top-left front corner (Disney "Classics" black diamond), the clamshell and the tape label.

LP: the label (address line, logo position, rim print, MONO/STEREO), and the dead wax / runout, the smooth band between the last groove and the label, where matrix numbers, stamper/lacquer suffixes, plant marks and mastering engineers' initials are etched (han

Comic: the cover price box (top left), the UPC box (bottom left on 1976+ Marvel/DC), the indicia (small print at the bottom of the first interior page, or the inside front cover), the centrefold (inserts), and the grading slab label.

reel-to-reel-tape-recorders.title: Reel-to-reel tape recorders
reel-to-reel-tape-recorders.full: Reel-to-reel tape recorders (Akai/Roberts, TEAC/Tascam, Sony/Superscope, Revox/Studer, Pioneer, Technics, Ampex, Tandberg, Otari, Dokorder, Wollensak/3M, Webcor, Viking)
reel-to-reel-tape-recorders.money: 10.5" decks (TEAC X-2000R, Akai GX-635D, Technics RS-1500, Pioneer RT-909, Revox A77/B77) $600–3,000+
reel-to-reel-tape-recorders.fakes: Not faked; new "Ballfinger" and Thorens decks exist at $10k+ but aren't confused. Watch for listings that call a 7" deck "10.5" because it is shown with a large reel, and for "restored" decks that only had cosmetic clean
reel-to-reel-tape-recorders.buy: Pass on almost all — heavy (30–60 lb), untested electronics; only a seller-demonstrated 10.5" deck at ≤ $200 picked up locally.
tells: Reel size: a 10.5" deck's reels overhang a standard 7" reel by a lot and sit on large NAB hub adapters; 7"-only decks have small spindles and the reels nearly fill the faceplate. A 10.5" metal reel on a deck in a listing photo is a strong sign of a 10.5" machi

Format markings on the head cover or faceplate: "2-track"/"½ track" (master-tape format, preferred by audiophiles), "4-track"/"¼ track" stereo (consumer format, plays most pre-recorded tapes), "auto-reverse", speeds (1⅞, 3¾, 7½, 15 ips — 15 ips is a premium fe
Type: deck (no power amp/speakers, connects to a stereo) vs recorder (built-in amp/speakers, usually portable case) — decks are worth more.

reel-to-reel-tapes.title: Reel-to-Reel Tapes and Reels
reel-to-reel-tapes.full: Reel-to-Reel Tapes and Reels (Ampex, Scotch/3M, Maxell, TDK, Memorex, BASF; prerecorded 4-track; 9-track computer tape)
reel-to-reel-tapes.fakes: Reproduction "studio master" claims; new-production reels by RTM/ATR/Recording The Masters (sold new $30–60) set a ceiling for used. - Chinese-made "TEAC" style reels and new-old-stock claims appear on eBay; check flange
reel-to-reel-tapes.buy: Buy 10.5" aluminum audio reels (brand on flange) under ~$5 each and prerecorded 4-track jazz/rock under ~$5 each; pass on plastic reels and computer tape.
tells: Prerecorded formats (PS Audio Copper): 2-track (half-track) stereo plays one direction across the full tape width; 4-track (quarter-track) stereo plays both directions. Major-label prerecorded tapes ran from about 1953–54 to the mid-1980s. 7.5 ips was used for

Dating clues on prerecorded tapes (PS Audio Copper): early boxes are heavier card with cloth hinges and thicker spools; later boxes and spools are thinner and the print poorer. Sealed tapes from the mid-1960s to mid-1980s have no leader, only a sticker holding
Audio vs computer at a glance: 1/4" tape with a brand box = audio; 1/2" tape, hanging canister, write-ring groove, white label strip with job numbers = computer.

religious-crucifixes.title: Religious crucifixes
religious-crucifixes.full: Religious crucifixes (pectoral/nun's crosses, Golgotha "skull and crossbones" crucifixes, wall crucifixes, sick-call boxes; French, German, Italian, Irish penal)
religious-crucifixes.money: Irish penal crosses, reliquary crosses, Georgian/early carved ivory corpus $200–1,500+ (general knowledge, verify)
religious-crucifixes.fakes: Modern Italian/Chinese reproductions of skull crucifixes sold as "antique"; tell: bright plating, glued (not riveted) corpus, plastic inlay, uniform casting.
religious-crucifixes.buy: Pass on nickel ebony-inlay crosses over $20; buy sterling-marked, reliquary (glass-fronted relic compartment) or early carved pieces at ≤ $40.

religious-jewelry.title: Religious jewelry
religious-jewelry.full: Religious jewelry (Jerusalem crosses, crucifixes, saint medals, rosaries, Stars of David, Hamsa; makers Creed, Chapel/HMH, Bliss, Catamore, Israeli 1950s–70s silversmiths, James Avery, Tiffany, Mexican Taxco)
religious-jewelry.money: gold crosses and antique reliquaries $150–1,500+ (often melt-driven).
religious-jewelry.fakes: Modern Chinese/Indian cast copies of Israeli filigree crosses sold online for $10–20, often stamped "925" falsely. James Avery and Tiffany fakes common. Test: acid/XRF needed for certainty — magnet test only rules out st
religious-jewelry.buy: Buy only stamped sterling at ≤ $15 or stamped 14K/18K below melt; pass on unmarked filigree souvenirs over $20.
tells: Jerusalem (Crusader) cross: a large cross potent with four small Greek crosses in the angles. Israeli souvenir versions (1948–1980s) in silver filigree/cannetille wirework with beaded borders and a coloured glass or synthetic stone centre (red "ruby", blue). S
Rosaries: sterling links (Creed, Chapel, HMH, Bliss), crystal or semi-precious beads; 14K gold rosaries rare.
Medals: Miraculous Medal, St. Christopher, St. Benedict; sterling (stamped) vs. base metal (common).

religious-pictures.title: Religious pictures
religious-pictures.full: Religious pictures (Sallman and Hofmann prints, lighted pictures, wood-slice plaques, icons, retablos)
religious-pictures.fakes: - Sallman and Hofmann prints are reproductions by definition; nobody fakes them because they are cheap. - Icons: modern prints glued to wood, thickly varnished and artificially aged; student copies with fake aging; risas
religious-pictures.buy: Pass on printed Jesus pictures at any price above ~$10; look only for hand-painted tin/copper retablos or hand-painted icons on wood at ≤ $60, confirmed by close-up photos.
tells: Warner Sallman (American, 1892–1968): "Head of Christ" (1940, profile, brown-gold background – over a billion copies), "Christ in Gethsemane" (1941, Jesus with clasped hands on a rock), "The Lord Is My Shepherd", "Christ at Heart's Door". Prints say "© Kriebel

Valuable outliers: hand-painted Mexican retablos (oil on tin or copper, 19th–early 20th c.), Russian/Greek icons (egg tempera and gesso on a wooden panel, often with a metal riza cover), Spanish colonial or Italian old-master oils, original Sallman sketches/pa

Heinrich Hofmann (German, 1824–1911): "Christ in Gethsemane" (1890, Riverside Church NYC – Jesus kneeling at a rock, red cloak over white, light from above), "Christ in the Temple" / "Jesus at Twelve" (1881, head and shoulders of a red-haired boy with a halo,

reloading-equipment.title: Reloading equipment
reloading-equipment.full: Reloading equipment (RCBS, Lyman, Lee Precision, Redding, Hornady/Pacific, C-H, Ideal tong tools)
reloading-equipment.fakes: No fakes. Lyman reissued 310 tools; modern 310 tools are worth less than pre-war Ideal. Collectible Ideal pieces carry "Ideal Mfg Co New Haven Conn" and patent dates.
reloading-equipment.buy: Buy RCBS/Redding/Lyman die sets in obsolete or wildcat calibers and Ideal/Lyman tong tools ≤ $25–40 each, or a complete Rock Chucker/RCBS kit ≤ $80; never buy powder, primers or loaded ammo.
tells: Dies: threaded 7/8-14 steel cylinders in sets of 2–3 (sizer, seater, expander), in a plastic box (RCBS green box, Redding blue/red box, Lyman red, Lee red/white). The caliber is printed on the box label and stamped on the die.
Presses: cast-iron "O" frame (RCBS Rock Chucker – green; Lyman Orange Crusher, Spar-T turret – orange/red), C-frame (RCBS Jr., Lee), progressive (Dillon – blue, Hornady LNL).
Scales: beam scales (RCBS 5-0-5, 10-10, Lyman/Ohaus M5).

resin-dog-statues.title: Resin and chalkware dog statues etc.)
resin-dog-statues.full: Resin and chalkware dog statues (Homco/Home Interiors, Sandicast, Castagna, Leonardo Collection, Border Fine Arts, Lenox, Royal Doulton (ceramic) etc.)
resin-dog-statues.money: Border Fine Arts and Royal Doulton/Beswick ceramic dogs $40–250
resin-dog-statues.fakes: Not a faking market; many generic imports styled like Homco/Sandicast. BFA "Studio" pieces made in China can be passed off as Scottish handmade — read the base.
resin-dog-statues.buy: Pass on Homco and generic resin; buy only Border Fine Arts, Beswick/Royal Doulton ceramic champions or rare-breed Sandicast under ~$25.
tells: Border Fine Arts (Langholm, Scotland, 1974–2016): resin (cold-cast) with very fine detail on wooden or resin bases; sculptor's name moulded on the piece; model numbers like B0668.
Beswick / Royal Doulton: glazed ceramic (not resin) with printed backstamp.

Homco is the giftware division of Home Interiors & Gifts (home-party sales). Bases typically carry a molded "© year" plus a 4-digit item number (e.g. "© 1991 8799"; pug #1287, 1997), often with a "Made in USA" sticker and sometimes felt under the base; later p

rifle-scopes.title: Rifle scopes
rifle-scopes.full: Rifle scopes (vintage: Unertl, Lyman, Redfield, Weaver, Leupold, Bushnell, Tasco, Stith, Fecker, Zeiss, Kahles, Hensoldt, Pecar, Noske, Bausch & Lomb; modern: Leupold, Nightforce, Vortex)
rifle-scopes.money: WWII/military-marked (Unertl USMC, M84, Zeiss ZF) $500–5,000+ (repro risk).
rifle-scopes.fakes: - Military sniper scopes (Unertl USMC, M73/M84, WWII Zeiss/ZF39) are widely reproduced — professional authentication needed (Dylan's rule: pass). - Advertised reproductions include a Malcolm 8x Unertl copy and an M73G4 c
rifle-scopes.buy: Pass on Tasco/Bushnell/Simmons; buy long brass/steel target scopes (Unertl, Lyman, Fecker) and marked Leupold/Redfield at ≤ $40; military-marked scopes need authentication — pass.
tells: Telescopic sights for rifles. Old target scopes are long (16–24") thin steel/brass tubes with external adjustment mounts — Unertl, Lyman, Fecker, Litschert. American hunting scopes of the 1940s–60s (Weaver K4 with El Paso marking, Lyman Alaskan, Redfield Bear
Title words: "vintage scope", "steel tube", "Weaver K4", "El Paso", "Lyman Alaskan", "Unertl", "target scope", "Bear Cub", "Balvar".

Tube diameter dates a scope: pre-war and 1940s hunting scopes are ¾" (Weaver 330) or ⅞" (Lyman Alaskan, Noske, Leupold Plainsman); post-war scopes moved to 1" as steel gave way to aluminium (Rifle magazine). Leupold's first 1" scope was the 1954 Mountaineer (R

road-flare-reflectors.title: Road flare reflectors
road-flare-reflectors.full: Road flare reflectors (truck emergency warning reflectors and kits; Bolser, Yankee, Fleet-Lite, Signal-Stat, Stratolite/Stimsonite lenses; Dietz/Toledo/Anthes smudge-pot and flare kits)
road-flare-reflectors.money: early glass-jewel or kerosene smudge pots/torches $30–100
road-flare-reflectors.fakes: Modern triangle reflectors replaced these after the 1974 FMCSA changes; no fakes. Lenses have been updated to newer reflectivity specs over the years, so a period kit with modern replacement lenses is "married". There ar
road-flare-reflectors.buy: Pass unless a complete boxed kit with original tin box is ≤ $10, or a pre-1950 glass-jewel / railroad-marked piece is ≤ 25% of sold.
tells: Double red plastic reflectors in chrome rims on a stamped steel base that folds flat (1960s–80s). The example is this type: three units, plus a steel "reflector kit" box and red flags with rods. The lenses are typically about 3 in and moulded with a maker and
Glass-jewel reflectors (1930s–50s) have faceted glass lenses and are more collectible.

Smudge pots / flare pots (Toledo Torch, Dietz, Handlan, Anthes) are kerosene pots with a separate collector market. Anthes Force Oiler Co. of Fort Madison, Iowa made "Type L" flare canisters. Dietz (Syracuse NY) made the "Traffic Gard" No. 40 red-globe road la

rookwood-pottery.title: Rookwood Pottery
rookwood-pottery.fakes: New Rookwood (2000s revival) production exists. Some pieces use old moulds, so check the date marks (general knowledge, verify). Fake marks on unmarked Ohio pottery are uncommon but possible. Artist signatures are the ar
rookwood-pottery.buy: Artist-signed under $150, or production under $30; pass on production pieces priced near $90.

roseville-pottery.title: Roseville Pottery
roseville-pottery.full: Roseville Pottery (Wisteria, Pine Cone, Futura, etc.)
roseville-pottery.money: blue Wisteria 8"+, Sunflower, Falline, Ferella and rare Futura $500–2,000+.
roseville-pottery.fakes: 1990s–2000s Chinese reproductions of Wisteria, Pine Cone, Futura and others. Tells: soft mould detail, heavy glossy glaze, wrong size for the shape number, crude raised "Roseville" letters. Fake foil stickers are possibl
roseville-pottery.buy: Blue Wisteria/Pine Cone/Futura under $120 with a clear mark photo; brown Wisteria under $60; unrecognised money-line matches under $40; pass on any repro tell.
tells: Sunflower, Blackberry, Falline, Ferella, Baneda.
Wisteria (1933): bark-textured body with purple wisteria clusters; blue ground > brown.
Futura: Art Deco geometric.

royal-bayreuth.title: Royal Bayreuth and German "Prussia-style" porcelain bowls
royal-bayreuth.full: Royal Bayreuth and German "Prussia-style" porcelain bowls (Royal Bayreuth, R.S. Prussia, R.S. Germany, R.S. Tillowitz, unmarked Germany)
royal-bayreuth.money: Royal Bayreuth Tapestry and Sunbonnet Babies, R.S. Prussia portrait/scenic/animal molds $200–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
royal-bayreuth.fakes: Fake R.S. Prussia red marks are rampant (decals applied to old or new blanks). Royal Bayreuth figurals have been reproduced. Genuine RS Prussia marks are under the glaze with clean edges; fake decal marks sit on top. The
royal-bayreuth.buy: Pass on unmarked German grape/floral bowls; buy only R.S. Prussia red-mark portrait/scenic/animal molds, Royal Bayreuth Tapestry or rare figurals at ≤ 1/3 of resale.
tells: Royal Bayreuth figurals are moulded in the shape of the subject: tomato sets, lobsters, shells (conch, oyster, crab), fruit (apple pitchers), flowers (rose, pansy, poppy, orchid), animals (dachshund, rooster, turtle, elk, bird), people (clowns, Art Nouveau lad
"1794" in the mark is the founding date, not the date of manufacture (1stDibs).
Prussia-style bowls are usually 9–11", with scalloped, heavily moulded rims, satin pastel grounds and transfer floral/fruit decoration.

royal-doulton-character-jugs.title: Royal Doulton character jugs
royal-doulton-character-jugs.fakes: Fakes of common subjects are not worth making. The risks are fake "rare colourways" (repainted common jugs) and mis-attributed non-Doulton jugs (general knowledge, verify). Doulton reissued some subjects in new sizes and
royal-doulton-character-jugs.buy: Only a rare D-number or colourway visible under $50; pass on common subjects over $8 each.

royal-doulton-china.title: Royal Doulton china and seriesware
royal-doulton-china.full: Royal Doulton china and seriesware (Royal Doulton, Doulton Burslem, Doulton Lambeth; seriesware, dinnerware, Flambé, figurines covered elsewhere)
royal-doulton-china.money: Lambeth stoneware art pottery by named artists $200–2,000+.
royal-doulton-china.fakes: Flambé has some Chinese fakes with printed red marks. Seriesware not much faked. Royal Doulton reissued some popular lines in the 1980s–2000s with modern backstamps. - Lambeth stoneware is not commonly faked, but monogra
royal-doulton-china.buy: Buy Flambé/Sung/Titanian or artist-monogrammed Lambeth stoneware at ≤ 25% of resale; pass on dinnerware and common seriesware under $40.
tells: Lambeth stoneware: salt-glazed brown/blue art pottery signed with incised artist monograms (Hannah Barlow, George Tinworth, Frank Butler, Eliza Simmance).

Dates check (Westland; thepotteries.org): John Doulton founded the pottery in 1815 at Vauxhall before it moved to Lambeth. The Burslem factory opened in 1882. The entry line above says 1877 because Doulton bought the Burslem works (Pinder, Bourne & Co.) in 187

Where to look: every piece should be photographed upside down. The printed backstamp sits in the centre of the base, with the D pattern number nearby (often handwritten or printed) and sometimes a small year number beside the lion-crown. Lambeth pieces carry i

royal-doulton-figurines.title: Royal Doulton figurines
royal-doulton-figurines.full: Royal Doulton figurines (Royal Doulton HN series, character jugs aside)
royal-doulton-figurines.money: rare colourways, prototypes, early Art Deco, Lambeth $500–5,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
royal-doulton-figurines.fakes: Some Chinese copies and fake backstamps exist, but they are uncommon. Watch for "seconds": a scratched-through backstamp (factory reject) cuts value 30–50%. (Rinker notes that claims of "prototype" or "factory second" st
royal-doulton-figurines.buy: Only buy pre-1950 HN numbers (low HN under ~1500), rare colourways, Art Deco ladies or limited editions at ≤ 1/3 of resale; pass on common mid-century to modern figures above ~$15.
tells: The HN series began in 1913 with 20 figures; HN1 was Charles Vyse's boy in a nightshirt, named "Darling" by Queen Mary (ATG). Darling is still made, so only the very early issues are valuable.
Genuine figures are hollow with a small, discreet firing hole in the base; a very large hole is not Doulton practice (Rinker).
Typical height 5–10 in. Each model has a fixed height; a different height from the catalogue is a warning sign (Rinker).

rug-beaters.title: Rug Beaters
rug-beaters.full: Rug Beaters (twisted wire, rattan/wicker, spring wire; heart, scroll and patented wire designs)
rug-beaters.money: patented/marked or unusual figural designs $60–150 (general knowledge, verify)
rug-beaters.fakes: New decorative rattan beaters (IKEA-style, Polish/German import $10–20 new) and "primitive" decor wire beaters from Asia with artificially aged finishes. Also heart-shaped wire "rug beaters" sold as farmhouse wall decor,
rug-beaters.buy: Pass on plain loop beaters over ~$10; buy only marked/patented or figural wire designs under ~$25.

russian-and-soviet-hallmarks.title: Russian and Soviet hallmarks
russian-and-soviet-hallmarks.full: Russian and Soviet hallmarks (Imperial zolotnik and kokoshnik marks, Soviet worker and star marks, factory imenniks, Russian Federation, Ukraine and Belarus; Fabergé, Khlebnikov, Ovchinnikov, Soviet jewelry factories)
russian-and-soviet-hallmarks.money: filigree, dated factory and stone-set Soviet pieces fetch melt plus 20–100%. Imperial 56 zolotnik gold carries collector premiums of 1.5–4× melt, so small crosses and rings are $300–1,500. Imperial 84/88 silver pieces are $150–2,000+. Fabergé, Khlebnikov and Ovchinnikov are $2,000–100,000+, but fake
russian-and-soviet-hallmarks.fakes: - **Fake Tsarist marks** are added to new pieces (cloisonné kovshi, beakers, cigarette cases, "Fabergé-style" eggs), to genuine lesser Russian pieces "upgraded" to Ovchinnikov, Khlebnikov or Fabergé, and to genuine Austr
russian-and-soviet-hallmarks.buy: The edge is a "gold tone" or "costume" listing that shows a star, kokoshnik or 56/583 stamp. Because profit must be ≥ the price paid, pay ≤ ~40% of gold melt (≈ $31/g for 583) for Soviet pieces and ≤ ~50% of melt for Imperial 56 pieces. Never pay a designer pr
tells: Pieces seen most: Soviet filigree "lace" rings, signet rings with synthetic rubies or alexandrite, bow and leaf brooches with stones, hoop earrings with lever backs, and Orthodox crosses. Imperial pieces include crosses, icons, cufflinks, cigarette cases, spoo
Rose-red to coppery-pink metal colour. Soviet 583 alloys run copper-heavy (see Materials), so the piece looks like "rose gold plate" to a Western seller.

The state assay mark. This is a small oval or shield-shaped stamp containing a figure plus a 2- or 3-digit number. The figure is a woman's head in a kokoshnik headdress (Imperial and Russian Federation), a worker with a hammer (1927–1958), or a five-pointed st

russian-and-soviet-porcelain.title: Russian and Soviet porcelain
russian-and-soviet-porcelain.full: Russian and Soviet porcelain (Imperial/Lomonosov LFZ–IFZ, Kuznetsov, Gardner, Dulevo, Soviet agitprop)
russian-and-soviet-porcelain.fakes: - Agitprop and Imperial: massive fake industry (new decoration on old blanks, fake marks). Do not buy. - Gardner and Kuznetsov: fake marks on recent Chinese/Eastern European porcelain. - Cobalt Net: Chinese knock-offs an
russian-and-soviet-porcelain.buy: Buy Soviet-era LFZ/Dulevo figurines or cobalt-net teapots at ≤ $40 when the underglaze mark and condition are clear; never pay up for "agitprop" or "Imperial" claims – those need expert authentication.

sad-irons.title: Sad irons and flat irons
sad-irons.full: Sad irons and flat irons (Mrs. Potts/Enterprise, Dover, Sensible, Geneva, Sargent & Co., Ober, Asbestos/Bless & Drake, Colebrookdale, unmarked foundry irons; also fluting, tailor's, charcoal and gas irons)
sad-irons.money: children's/toy, fluting machines, figural or patent irons $75–400+.
sad-irons.fakes: Reproduction "sad irons" (Taiwan/India decor) with smooth faux-black finish, sharp detail, often painted "Antique"; toy irons and trivets heavily reproduced. Many repro trivets bear old patterns.
sad-irons.buy: Pass on plain sad irons; buy only small toy/salesman irons, complete Mrs. Potts boxed sets, fluters or unusual patent irons under ~$25.

safety-razors.title: Vintage safety razors
safety-razors.full: Vintage safety razors (Gillette, Gem, Ever-Ready, Schick, Rolls, Valet, Wilkinson, Merkur)
safety-razors.money: rare/early (1904–1910 single-ring, Aristocrat #15 gold w/case, Merkur/Wilkinson Sticky boxed) $150–500+
safety-razors.fakes: Few fakes. Modern reissues (Merkur 34C, Parker, Rockwell, Edwin Jagger, Chinese "Old Type" clones such as Yaqi/Weishi) can be mistaken for vintage. Chinese 3-piece clones have no Gillette patent stamping and a crisp mode
safety-razors.buy: Buy only adjustable/gold/early Gillette or boxed rarities identified from photos at ≤ 1/3 of sold median; plain Old Type/Tech/Super Speed are pass at >$15.
tells: TTO (twist-to-open, butterfly) 1934+: one-piece; knob at the handle bottom opens "doors". Super Speed (1947–80s), Aristocrat (1940s–50s, often gold), Toggle (1960s), Fat Boy (adjustable, 1958–62), Slim adjustable (1962–70s), Black Beauty, Red Tip/Blue Tip Supe
Cases matter: Gillette sets in fitted brass/leatherette cases with original blade packets, gold "travel" kits, Aristocrat in red/blue plush cases.

3-piece Old Type (1904–1921): separate cap, guard and handle; open-comb guard (teeth like a comb); often in a small hinged metal or leatherette case with velvet lining. Handle with fine knurling and ring/ball ends. Gold-plated or nickel.

samovars.title: Samovars
samovars.full: Samovars (Russian Imperial — Batashev, Vorontsov, Shemarin, Sosenkov, Teile, Lomov; Soviet Tula "Shtamp"/Kolchugino electric; Persian/Turkish; modern)
samovars.money: Imperial Russian coal samovars with hallmarks $250–1,500+ (general knowledge, verify)
samovars.fakes: Fake medal stamps on later bodies. More: Imperial-style marks and dates on Soviet-era or modern bodies; "Batashev" is the name most often put on later samovars. Check that the construction matches the date (coal design,
samovars.buy: Buy only Imperial Russian coal (chimney-type) samovars with stamped medals under ~$75 and in passenger-seat size; electric Soviet ones are a pass unless ≤ $15.

satsuma-pottery.title: Satsuma and Satsuma-style Japanese pottery
satsuma-pottery.full: Satsuma and Satsuma-style Japanese pottery (Kinkozan, Yabu Meizan, Taizan, Hododa, Kozan; Taisho/Showa export moriage Satsuma; Nippon; postwar Satsuma-style giftware)
satsuma-pottery.fakes: - Chinese "Satsuma" (1990s–present): heavier, glossy, painted Shimazu crest and fake "Satsuma" or "Kinkozan" marks, garish colours; very common at estate sales. - Painted Shimazu cross-in-circle crest is NOT proof of age
satsuma-pottery.buy: Buy only fine-crackle ivory Meiji pieces with miniature-scale painting and a studio signature at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on heavy moriage export pieces over ~$15 and on porcelain "Satsuma style".
tells: Meiji Kyoto Satsuma (1870s–1910s): very fine, dense miniature painting (hundreds of figures, flowers, butterflies), restrained gold, a visible fine crackle, often a gold seal mark (Kinkozan, Taizan, Hododa, Yabu Meizan, Gyokuzan) and a painted cartouche.

Taisho/Showa export Satsuma (1910s–40s): heavier, thick raised gold and enamel dots ("moriage"), crowded geisha or Rakan (Buddhist saints with dragons), dark brown/black and gold grounds, scroll or shishi handles, red or blue "Satsuma" kanji mark with the Shim
Postwar "Satsuma" (1950s–80s): thin, shiny, decal-assisted, bright gold, "Made in Japan" stickers.

scandinavian-hallmarks.title: Scandinavian silver and gold hallmarks
scandinavian-hallmarks.full: Scandinavian silver and gold hallmarks (Denmark: Georg Jensen, Hans Hansen, A. Michelsen, Evald Nielsen, N.E. From; Sweden: GAB, three crowns; Norway: David-Andersen, J. Tostrup, Aksel Holmsen; Finland: Kalevala Koru, Lapponia, Björn Weckström; Iceland)
scandinavian-hallmarks.money: pre-1945 Georg Jensen, Weckström sculptural pieces and Jensen hollowware $500–5,000+ (comps below
scandinavian-hallmarks.fakes: - Georg Jensen is the most faked Scandinavian mark: cast copies of Jugendstil brooches and Koppel pieces with soft, grainy marks and wrong design numbers. Compare the mark font and the design number with the Jensen desig
scandinavian-hallmarks.buy: Read the mark cluster first: a maker name plus 826/830/925S, three towers, three crowns or crown-in-heart is real silver even when the seller says "pewter" or "silver tone"; pay ≤ 80% of melt for anonymous pieces and ≤ 40% of the maker's sold median for named

scandinavian-porcelain.title: Scandinavian porcelain
scandinavian-porcelain.full: Scandinavian porcelain (Royal Copenhagen, Bing & Grondahl, Porsgrund, Figgjo, Arabia, Gustavsberg, Rorstrand, Stavangerflint)
scandinavian-porcelain.money: Arabia/Gustavsberg/Rorstrand studio art (Kaipiainen, Lindberg, Friberg) and RC Flora Danica $100–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
scandinavian-porcelain.fakes: Few fakes; main issue is reissues and seconds. Some modern Asian copies of Blue Fluted exist.
scandinavian-porcelain.buy: Ignore plates; hunt studio art (signed Arabia, Gustavsberg Argenta, Lindberg, Friberg) and Flora Danica, which owners misread as generic.

scarab-bracelets.title: Egyptian-revival scarab bracelets
scarab-bracelets.fakes: Fake "14K" stamps on gold-plated pieces exist. Test with acid or XRF before reselling as solid gold (general knowledge, verify). Modern Egyptian tourist-market scarab bracelets are common and low value.
scarab-bracelets.buy: 14K mark visible and under $150; pass on GF or unmarked above $10.
tells: "1/20 12K GF": gold-filled, most of them
"14K": solid gold, the money ones
"925/sterling"

school-yearbooks.title: School Yearbooks
school-yearbooks.full: School Yearbooks (Walsworth, Jostens, Herff Jones, Taylor, local mimeograph/print-shop annuals)
school-yearbooks.money: books with a famous alumnus (pre-fame photo) $100–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
school-yearbooks.fakes: Reprints exist mostly for famous-alumni books (reunion reprints, "commemorative edition" stamped). Celebrity yearbooks are faked by swapping pages or claiming the wrong person — verification needs the person's name and p
school-yearbooks.buy: Buy only pre-1950 books under ~$15 each, lots of 3+ pre-1950 volumes, or a book you can tie to a famous alumnus; everything else is genealogy-slow $15–30 stock.

schramberg-smf-pottery.title: Schramberg SMF pottery
schramberg-smf-pottery.full: Schramberg SMF pottery (Schramberger Majolikafabrik, Germany 1912–1989; Eva Zeisel designs 1928–1930; earlier Uechtritz & Faist and Villeroy & Boch Schramberg majolica)
schramberg-smf-pottery.money: Eva Zeisel-designed shapes/decors (Gobelin, Mondrian etc.) $100–300+ singles, more for sets on design-market platforms
schramberg-smf-pottery.fakes: Few fakes; the risk is misattribution — sellers label any geometric SMF as "Eva Zeisel". Mondrian decor appears on non-Zeisel shapes (Porcelain Marks & More). Attribute only by documented shape/decor (Cooper Hewitt objec
schramberg-smf-pottery.buy: Buy only 1925–1935 geometric-decor SMF (Mondrian, Gobelin, Malta, Plume, Adlon, bold bands/dots) at ≤ $40 undamaged; pass on florals, landscapes, post-war pieces and anything chipped.

schwinn-bicycle-parts.title: Schwinn bicycle parts
schwinn-bicycle-parts.full: Schwinn bicycle parts (Schwinn Sting-Ray/Krate, Phantom/Black Phantom, middleweight; Mesinger, Persons, Troxel saddles; Bendix hubs)
schwinn-bicycle-parts.money: Krate parts (Solo Polo, springers, Stik shifter, chrome fenders), Phantom/Black Phantom tanks, chainguards and springer forks $100–500+ (general knowledge, verify)
schwinn-bicycle-parts.fakes: Massive reproduction market: Sting-Ray seats, Krate shifters, sissy bars, chainguards, decals, Phantom tanks. Repro tells: no date code, lighter metal, flatter stamping, "Made in Taiwan". Schwinn 2000s reissue Sting-Ray/
schwinn-bicycle-parts.buy: Buy original Schwinn-stamped Krate/Sting-Ray/Phantom parts and studded Mesinger/Persons saddles in original condition at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on generic or reproduction parts, rusted chrome and anything too big (fenders sets okay, forks okay, frames no).

scuba-gear.title: Vintage scuba gear
scuba-gear.full: Vintage scuba gear (U.S. Divers Aqua-Lung double-hose regulators, Healthways, Voit, Dacor, Sportways, Nemrod/Seamless, La Spirotechnique, steel tanks and backpacks, masks)
scuba-gear.money: brass hard-hat diving gear $1000+ (mostly reproductions) (general knowledge, verify)
scuba-gear.fakes: Brass hard-hat helmets are almost always reproductions. Regulators rarely faked. Aqua Lung itself issued a **Mistral 2005 Limited Edition** (made in France, numbered, to mark 50 years since the original Mistral); a moder
scuba-gear.buy: Buy double-hose regulators and marked 1950s-60s US Divers/Voit/Healthways gear ≤ $50; pass on tanks alone.

seashells-and-natural-specimens.title: Seashells and natural specimens
seashells-and-natural-specimens.full: Seashells and natural specimens (abalone, conch, cowries, nautilus, coral, sea urchins, minerals, fossils)
seashells-and-natural-specimens.money: rare specimen-grade shells with locality data (cones, cowries, Conus gloriamaris) $100–1,000+
seashells-and-natural-specimens.fakes: Dyed/polished shells, resin replicas, composite "abalone" sheets. For fossils and minerals: fakes and composites are common.
seashells-and-natural-specimens.buy: Pass on decorative shell lots; only buy documented specimen collections with labels (Latin names, locality, collector) at ≤ 25% of resale — and nothing CITES-listed or state-restricted.

seltzer-bottles.title: Seltzer / soda siphon bottles
seltzer-bottles.full: Seltzer / soda siphon bottles (Sparklets, BOC, Soda King, Kidde, Hoffman / Czech & Pittsburgh etched glass, Art Deco chrome)
seltzer-bottles.money: rare colors, Soda King bakelite boxed sets and NYC bottler acid-etched $100-250 (general knowledge, verify)
seltzer-bottles.fakes: Reproduction etched "seltzer" bottles exist (2000s decor), with too-crisp etching and lightweight heads. Modern Sparklets-style mesh bottles are rare.
seltzer-bottles.buy: Buy colored-glass or named-bottler etched siphons or boxed Soda King sets ≤ $30; plain clear wire-mesh Sparklets only ≤ $10.

serial-numbers-and-date-codes.title: Serial numbers and date codes — master dating guide
serial-numbers-and-date-codes.full: Serial numbers and date codes — master dating guide (Leica, Nikon, Hasselblad, Zeiss/Contax, Canon; Gibson, Fender, Martin, Gretsch, Epiphone; Elgin, Waltham, Hamilton; Selmer; Parker, Sheaffer, Montblanc; Zippo; Case, Buck, Schrade, Remington, Russell; Stanley, Disston, Craftsman; Coleman; Pyrex; Rolex)
serial-numbers-and-date-codes.money: This is a dating guide, not an item type. A serial or date code moves an object from "vintage" into a specific year or era, and some eras sell for many times the common one. Examples: a black-paint Leica M3 sold for €38,400 against about $1,500 for a chrome M3 (around 20×)
serial-numbers-and-date-codes.fakes: - **Leica:** Soviet FED/Zorki "Luftwaffe" fakes, black repaints, re-engraved serials. - **Nikon:** official S3 2000 and SP 2005 reissues (limited, labelled); fake engravings on Soviet bodies. - **Fender:** loose neck pla
serial-numbers-and-date-codes.buy: Read the number before you read the title. Decode it with the tables below, and price the item from its type entry at the decoded era. A decoded premium era gives you a buy at ≤ ~43% of the era's sold median (Dylan's rule). A number that doesn't fit the claime

shadowbox-dioramas.title: Shadowbox dioramas
shadowbox-dioramas.full: Shadowbox dioramas (1980s–2000s resin occupational shadow boxes; Pomeroy/Enesco/Home Interiors type; folk-art and Victorian shadowboxes; hair wreaths; sailor's valentines; cased taxidermy; Joseph Cornell-style assemblages)
shadowbox-dioramas.money: Victorian hair/wax/taxidermy shadowboxes and fine folk art $150–1,000+ (top attributed taxidermy cases into five figures at specialist auction).
shadowbox-dioramas.fakes: - Not relevant at the low end; "antique style" new pieces common. - Modern sailor's valentines (Barbados and elsewhere) are made by the same method with newer materials; check for modern glue, bright shells, new frames a
shadowbox-dioramas.buy: Pass on resin occupational shadowboxes; buy only handmade 19th–early 20th-c. folk-art or Victorian shadowboxes at ≤ $40.
tells: Victorian (1837–1901):
Framed box under glass with miniatures arranged as a scene.

1980s–2000s commercial (Taiwan/China): resin miniatures (doctor's coat, bag, stethoscope, microscope), printed paper ephemera, distressed wood frame with fake "wormholes"; themes: doctor, dentist, pharmacist, lawyer, sewing, golf, fishing, kitchen, nursing.

sharpening-stones.title: Sharpening stones
sharpening-stones.full: Sharpening stones (whetstones and hones; Arkansas novaculite, Carborundum, Norton/Pike/India, Belgian coticule, Thuringian, Japanese natural, razor hones)
sharpening-stones.money: Belgian coticules, yellow Thuringians ("escher") and Japanese natural razor stones $60–400+
sharpening-stones.fakes: Labels moved onto lesser stones is a known razor-hone scam; Chinese slate sold as Thuringian. Man-made stones are not faked.
sharpening-stones.buy: Pass on Carborundum/Norton man-made stones; buy only natural razor hones (coticule, Thuringian, Japanese natural, translucent Arkansas) at ≤ 25% of sold.
tells: Razor hones: Belgian coticule (yellow layer bonded to blue-grey or slate backing), Thuringian/"Escher" (blue-green or yellow-green slate with paper label), Japanese natural (tan to blue stone, often with a kanji stamp).

Man-made silicon carbide (grey/black, "Crystolon", "Carborundum") and aluminium oxide (brown/orange, "India"): uniform colour, often two-sided (coarse/fine). Boxed in printed cardboard or wooden boxes.
Natural Arkansas novaculite: white, grey, or translucent/black, waxy-looking, often with veins. "Washita" is a softer porous grade.

shawnee-pottery.title: Shawnee Pottery
shawnee-pottery.full: Shawnee Pottery (Shawnee Pottery Co., Zanesville OH, 1937–1961; Corn King/Corn Queen, Smiley Pig, Puss 'n Boots, Valencia, Kenwood, Chantilly)
shawnee-pottery.money: gold-trim/decorated Smiley and Winnie cookie jars, rare jars and Corn King large pieces $120–400+.
shawnee-pottery.fakes: - Smiley/Winnie pig, Puss 'n Boots and Corn King cookie jars were reproduced from the 1990s ("USA" mark with smaller size because of shrinkage, poor gold, sloppy paint). Repros are about 10% smaller than originals. - Pla
shawnee-pottery.buy: Buy only gold-trimmed or decal Smiley/Winnie/Puss 'n Boots/Mugsey cookie jars and gold-trim figural pieces at ≤ $40; pass on plain planters, vases and teapots unless ≤ $5.
tells: Marks: "USA" with a mold number on the base (e.g., "USA 829"), "Shawnee USA", "Kenwood USA", "Pat. Smiley USA", "Corn King Oven Ware". Many pieces carry only "USA" and a number — the edge for Dylan.
