More marks (Hunker, Kovels): "Shawnee", "Shawnee U.S.A.", "Kenwood", "Great Northern", "Pat. Smiley USA", "Shawnee Smiley 60" / "Patent Smiley 60 — Shawnee USA". Pieces were not marked "Shawnee" until the 1950s, so a 1940s piece often reads only "USA". Origina
Mid-century American semi-porcelain/earthenware: figural cookie jars, creamers, salt and pepper shakers, planters, vases and teapots for dime stores (Woolworth, Kresge, Sears).

ship-telegraphs-and-nautical-brass.title: Ship engine-order telegraphs & nautical brass
ship-telegraphs-and-nautical-brass.full: Ship engine-order telegraphs & nautical brass (Chadburn, Robinson, Bendix, Henschel, Kelvin & Hughes)
ship-telegraphs-and-nautical-brass.money: named-vessel telegraphs and complete Kelvin & Hughes binnacles $2,000–6,000.
ship-telegraphs-and-nautical-brass.fakes: Indian reproductions dominate the market, and many carry fake maker plates ("Chadburn", "Kelvin Hughes", "Ross London") on the repro bodies. A plate alone is not proof, so check weight and construction (general knowledge
ship-telegraphs-and-nautical-brass.buy: Only with a maker plate visible (Chadburn, Robinson, Henschel, Bendix) and ≤ $200; pass on 12" printed-dial "vintage ships telegraphs" and any Indian repro.
tells: sextants (real: Plath, Hughes, Tamaya $300–800; Indian repro $30–60)
Reproductions (India, 1980s–now) are often sold as "Brelco"-style decor: lightweight brass, modern screws, printed dial, ~12" tall. $80–200.
Genuine Chadburn (Liverpool), Robinson / A. Robinson, Bendix, Henschel and Siebe Gorman units are heavy (40–150 lb), with cast maker plates, a mechanical chain drive and glass dials. $800–3,000.

ships-clocks.title: Ship's clocks and marine bulkhead clocks
ships-clocks.full: Ship's clocks and marine bulkhead clocks (Chelsea, Seth Thomas, Waltham, Howard Miller, Wempe, Schatz, Hermle-movement Seth Thomas Corsair, Sestrel)
ships-clocks.money: Chelsea ship's bell, Navy-marked WWII, Wempe/Schatz $400–2,000+.
ships-clocks.fakes: Indian/Chinese brass "Chelsea" or "Navy" decor clocks with quartz movements are common and look convincing from the front: check for a battery compartment and winding holes. Re-dialled clocks with fake "U.S. Navy" text.
ships-clocks.buy: Buy only Chelsea (any, running) at ≤ $150, or USN/US Maritime Commission-marked Chelsea/Seth Thomas/Waltham at ≤ 35% of resale; pass on Seth Thomas Corsair-type German-movement clocks above ~$60 and anything not running.

shoe-shine-boxes.title: Shoe shine boxes
shoe-shine-boxes.full: Shoe shine boxes (homemade/folk wooden boxes; Griffin, Shinola, Esquire, Kiwi, Bixby, Whittemore promotional kits; cast-iron footrests by Star, Griffin, Shinola, unmarked foundries)
shoe-shine-boxes.money: 19th-century bootblack stands or exceptional folk art $250–600.
shoe-shine-boxes.fakes: New cast-iron shoe-shine footrests and "antique style" boxes are mass-produced (Pakistan/China/India) with crisp casting, bright rust or black paint, and no wear on high points. Old footrests show smoothed high points fr
shoe-shine-boxes.buy: Buy only advertising-marked, folk-art decorated or footrest boxes with strong original surface at ≤ $25; plain boxes are decor-price items that never clear $50 profit.

shortwave-receivers.title: Shortwave / communications receivers
shortwave-receivers.full: Shortwave / communications receivers (Radio Shack DX, Sony, Grundig, Hallicrafters, Drake)
shortwave-receivers.money: Drake R8B, AOR AR7030, Icom R75/R8500, Collins 51S-1 $500–1,500.
shortwave-receivers.fakes: No meaningful fakes. Rebadged clones exist: Grundig-branded radios were often Tecsun-made, and Radio Shack sets were made by others (general knowledge, verify). Grundig Satellit models were reissued with similar names, s
shortwave-receivers.buy: Fully working DX-394 under $70, ICF-2010 under $120, Satellit 800 under $150; pass on "works some", untested or missing knobs.
tells: Yaesu FRG-7/FRG-100, Kenwood R-1000/R-2000, Drake R8/R8B ($500–900).
Radio Shack DX-394/DX-394B: 1990s tabletop, black, "LSB/USB/CW" on the front. $150–250 working.

signed-costume-jewelry.title: Signed costume jewelry
signed-costume-jewelry.full: Signed costume jewelry (Boucher, Sherman, Trifari, Eisenberg, Hobé, HAR, Schiaparelli)
signed-costume-jewelry.money: HAR, Schiaparelli, Trifari Maharajah, Haskell, couture $400–2,000.
signed-costume-jewelry.fakes: Fake signatures on Eisenberg, Boucher and Haskell are reported. Modern reproductions of Trifari jelly bellies and HAR figurals exist. Trifari and others reissued vintage designs (e.g. Trifari for the Metropolitan Museum)
signed-costume-jewelry.buy: Top-maker signature visible on the back and priced ≤ 30% of tier, or Sherman parures under $50; pass on common makers, unsigned lots and front-only photos.
tells: Trifari: crown-T (Crown Trifari 1950s is the good era).
HAR: oriental and genie figurals.
Schiaparelli: script signature, lava/moulded glass.

signed-limited-prints.title: Signed and limited-edition prints
signed-limited-prints.full: Signed and limited-edition prints (original etchings, lithographs, serigraphs, woodcuts; pencil-signed and numbered decorator prints)
signed-limited-prints.money: important printmakers (Benton, Hopper, Whistler, Chagall, Miró original lithos) $300–10,000+ (authentication needed).
signed-limited-prints.fakes: - Dalí, Chagall, Miró, Picasso and Erté prints are heavily faked; "signed in the plate" vs pencil; pre-signed blank paper fraud (Dalí). Out of scope for Dylan (authentication needed). - Offset reproductions with printed
signed-limited-prints.buy: Buy only pencil-signed original intaglio prints (visible plate mark) by artists with real auction records ≥ $150 at ≤ $50; pass on decorator numbered lithos and anything needing authentication.
tells: Original print: made by the artist (or under the artist's supervision) on a plate, stone, block or screen, and printed by hand in an edition. Pencil signature at lower right, edition number (e.g. 154/250) or "A.P." / "E.A." / "H.C." / "P.P." at lower left, tit

Etching/drypoint/engraving/aquatint (intaglio): look for a plate mark, a recessed rectangle pressed into the paper around the image with slightly bevelled corners; ink lines sit slightly raised (you can feel them); drypoint lines have a soft velvety burr; aqua
Lithograph: flat, no plate mark; under a loupe an irregular, grainy or crayon-like texture (stone or plate) vs a regular grid or rosette of dots (offset reproduction = low value).

silver-certificates-and-coins.title: US silver certificates & common silver coins
silver-certificates-and-coins.full: US silver certificates & common silver coins (Morgan dollars, Mexican pesos, proof sets)
silver-certificates-and-coins.fakes: Counterfeit Morgans are rampant, especially Chinese-made fakes of CC and key dates. They have the wrong weight (26.73 g is correct), wrong ring and wrong diameter (38.1 mm) (general knowledge on specs, verify). Fake slab
silver-certificates-and-coins.buy: Silver at or below melt (lots by weight), or a slabbed key-date/CC Morgan under grey-sheet; pass on common certs over $5 and raw common Morgans over $45 (re-peg to current spot).
tells: Silver certificates: blue seal and blue serial numbers. $1 (1935, 1957 series), $5 (1934, 1953), $10 (1934, 1953). Star notes (★ in the serial) and the 1928/1934 $1 "Funnyback" are the premium ones.
Morgan dollars: 1878–1921, 0.7734 oz silver. Value = date/mint (CC mint, 1893-S, 1889-CC) + grade. Slabs graded by PCGS/NGC are trusted; ANACS and others are discounted.
Mexico 1947–48 5 pesos Cuauhtemoc: 30 g .900 = 0.868 oz ASW.

silverplate-flatware-and-servers.title: Silverplate flatware and serving pieces
silverplate-flatware-and-servers.full: Silverplate flatware and serving pieces (1847 Rogers Bros, Holmes & Edwards, Community/Oneida, Wm Rogers, Reed & Barton, Gorham plate, Christofle, Wallace, Italian/European ornate servers; 800 silver Continental pieces)
silverplate-flatware-and-servers.money: complete chest sets and Christofle/Victorian figural pieces $60–300
silverplate-flatware-and-servers.fakes: False "800"/"925" stamps on Asian silverplate; "German Silver"/"Nickel Silver"/"Alpaca" are no silver at all. Modern Italian "Made in Italy" silverplate servers sold as antique.
silverplate-flatware-and-servers.buy: Buy only pieces you can prove are sterling/800 (mark photo) under melt + $20, or Victorian figural plate under $15; pass on generic plated servers over $10.

silverplate-hollowware.title: Silverplate and pewter hollowware
silverplate-hollowware.full: Silverplate and pewter hollowware (Meriden Britannia, Reed & Barton, Homan, Simpson Hall Miller, Wm Rogers, Christofle, Bossi/Ibis, Eisenberg-Lozano, Los Castillo/Emilia Castillo, English pewter/Britannia metal)
silverplate-hollowware.money: true Georgian pewter and rare figural Victorian pieces $150–600+.
silverplate-hollowware.fakes: - Godinger, "Sheffield Silver Co." and Chinese/Indian casts copy Victorian forms. They are light, often lacquered, with soft detail and no maker mark beyond "silver plated". - "Sheffield" on 20th-century plate is often m
silverplate-hollowware.buy: Buy only signed, design-led pieces (Castillo, Bossi/Ibis, Christofle, figural Victorian) at ≤ 1/3 of sold median; never generic trays, worn-through plate or lots priced over $20.
tells: Victorian American plate (1860–1900): heavy castings, applied medallions, engraved or engine-turned bands, figural finials (birds, sphinxes, cows), "Quadruple Plate" marks with a pattern number. Aesthetic Movement (1875–1890) pieces show Japanesque fans, grids
Silverplate wear ("bleeding"): pinkish copper or yellow brass showing through on high points, rims and handles means plated. The champagne bucket in our sweep shows it everywhere.
Pewter/Britannia: dull blue-grey, soft, no plating wear, often hand-engraved ("bright-cut") decoration. It feels warm and heavy.

singer-sewing-machines.title: Singer sewing machines
singer-sewing-machines.fakes: Fake Featherweights are not common. Repainted "custom" Featherweights are a separate, decorated market. Reproduction or replacement cases and parts are common (general knowledge, verify).
singer-sewing-machines.buy: Featherweight only under ~$120; 15-91 under $40; everything else pass unless free.
tells: 221 Featherweight (1933–1964, US Elizabethport): small, about 11 lb, black (rarely white or tan 221K), scroll faceplate, fold-up bed extension, square carry case.
222K (Scotland): free-arm version of the Featherweight.
portables: a head in a carry case or a bentwood "coffin" case

slag-glass-mirrors.title: Slag/stained glass mirrors and leaded frames
slag-glass-mirrors.full: Slag/stained glass mirrors and leaded frames (1970s craft stained glass, Arts & Crafts slag-glass, Tiffany-style; makers mostly unmarked hobbyists; Handel, Bradley & Hubbard, Miller for period slag)
slag-glass-mirrors.money: period Arts & Crafts slag-glass with bronze/copper frames (Bradley & Hubbard, Handel era) $200–1,200.
slag-glass-mirrors.fakes: Modern Chinese Tiffany-style mirrors exist; craft mirrors are not fakes but often oversold as "antique". - Tiffany Studios desk pieces are faked and married (a genuine frame with replaced glass, or an added stamp). A sta
slag-glass-mirrors.buy: Pass craft 1970s mirrors (fragile, large, cheap); consider only metal-framed period slag with maker marks ≤ 1/4 comps.
tells: Title words: slag glass, caramel slag, leaded, stained glass, Tiffany style, Arts & Crafts, Mission, overlay, filigree, Grapevine, Bradley & Hubbard, Handel, Miller.

What "slag" means: in Arts & Crafts lighting, "slag" is the trade name for opaque, marbled sheets of two or more colours (opalescent sheet glass) set in metal fixtures; the name probably does not come from iron-smelting slag (Arts & Crafts Homes). Kovels uses

Two forms that sell well: small jewellery boxes and vanity boxes with leaded slag panels and a mirror lid (the Terapeak "leaded slag glass mirror" hits were mostly these), and period bronze desk and frame pieces with slag behind a pierced overlay (Tiffany Stud

snap-on-tools.title: Snap-on hand tools and tool boxes
snap-on-tools.full: Snap-on hand tools and tool boxes (Snap-on, Blue-Point)
snap-on-tools.money: large KRL roll cabs and complete 3/4"–1" sets $800–4,000.
snap-on-tools.fakes: Counterfeit Snap-on tools are sold online, mostly sets and ratchets, often new-in-box at too-good prices. Tells: logo font, stamped part numbers that don't match the catalogue, and finish (general knowledge, verify). Col
snap-on-tools.buy: 12 pc screwdriver set under $60, ratchets under $25, sockets by the tray under 30% of eBay; pass on new sets at retail and boxes that need freight unless local.
tells: Wordmark: the "Snap-on" script wordmark is stamped on the shank.
Ratchets: a flat "swivel" head and a serial code.
Screwdriver sets: hard clear acetate handles (red/black or coloured "Classic"). An 8–12 pc set retails $240–350. Soft-grip (Instinct) sets are similar.

snap-on-vintage-toolboxes.title: Snap-on vintage toolboxes and hand tools
snap-on-vintage-toolboxes.full: Snap-on vintage toolboxes and hand tools (Snap-on KRA/K-series, script-badge chests, speed ratchets)
snap-on-vintage-toolboxes.fakes: Reproduction badges are sold for restorers, so a "script badge" on a later box is possible. Check the box construction against the badge era (general knowledge, verify). Collector limited-edition tool sets (Earnhardt etc
snap-on-vintage-toolboxes.buy: Script-badge box in clean paint ≤ $100 and only with a local buyer; hand tools only in lots under $5/tool; pass on rusty/dented or anything that must ship.
tells: Chests: red steel top chests with a script "Snap-on" nameplate. 1940s–60s boxes have a raised script badge; later boxes have a rectangular logo. The model is stamped on a plate inside (KRA-53, KRA-55, K-60 etc.).
Hand tools: "Snap-on" stamped on the shank with a date code letter.

soda-crates.title: Soda crates
soda-crates.full: Soda crates (wooden and metal bottle cases and carriers: Coca-Cola, Pepsi-Cola, Dr Pepper, 7-Up, Nehi/Royal Crown, Canada Dry, Orange Crush, regional bottlers)
soda-crates.money: early Coca-Cola wooden carriers with bottler city stencil $50–200.
soda-crates.fakes: - Decor-store repro crates common. - Repro tells: butt-jointed corners, staples/Phillips screws, shiny galvanised straps, bright uniform logos, laser-burned logos, light thin wood. - Coca-Cola licensed modern "vintage st
soda-crates.buy: Pass on standard wooden crates and plastic carriers (bulky, low margin); only early six-pack wooden/metal carriers or rare regional-bottler crates at ≤ $15.
tells: Where to look for marks: the long sides carry the brand script; the end boards carry bottler name/city ("Coca-Cola Bottling Co. — [city, state]"), capacity, and often a year stamp; interior bottoms of Pepsi crates often carry a plant code plus year; route mark
Look-alikes: fruit/produce crates (no dividers), milk crates (wire/plastic, dairy names), modern decor "Coca-Cola" boxes sold in craft stores.

Wood case with dividers for 24 bottles (or 12 big bottles), metal-banded corners, stencilled brand. About 18 × 12 × 4–5 in. Plastic crates and carriers are 1970s+. Date stamps (e.g., "1968") on end boards; bottler city stencils.

soldering-irons.title: Soldering irons
soldering-irons.full: Soldering irons (vintage electric and fire-heated; American Beauty, Hexacon, Weller, Ungar, Jackson, Vulcan, Wall, Craftsman; copper "soldering coppers")
soldering-irons.fakes: None meaningful. - Reissue caution: American Beauty still makes catalog-number irons (e.g. 3158), so not every American Beauty is vintage.
soldering-irons.buy: Pass — electric tools need testing (no untested electronics). Only boxed NOS American Beauty or Hexacon at ≤ 25% of sold, tested before buying.
tells: American Beauty (Detroit, since 1894): big industrial irons, wood handles, logo stamped on the barrel, model numbers by wattage (e.g. 3138).
Hexacon (NJ): hex-section barrels, red/black handles.
Weller: pistol-grip "soldering guns" (common).

solid-state-guitar-amps.title: Guitar & bass amplifiers – solid-state practice/modelling vs tube
solid-state-guitar-amps.full: Guitar & bass amplifiers – solid-state practice/modelling vs tube (Line 6, Fender, Peavey, Roland, Vox, Marshall, Ampeg)
solid-state-guitar-amps.fakes: Fender and Vox reissue classic models (e.g. '65 Deluxe Reverb Reissue, AC30 reissues). Reissues are worth far less than originals, so check serials and construction (general knowledge, verify). Clones in old cabinets exi
solid-state-guitar-amps.buy: Vintage tube amps (Fender blackface/silverface, Vox AC, Marshall), JC-120, Music Man, B-15 under $250 and complete; pass on any solid-state practice/modelling amp and anything "needs repair".
tells: Tube amps: a back panel with glowing tubes visible and a heavier chassis. Fender (Deluxe Reverb, Princeton, Twin, Blues Jr, Hot Rod), Vox AC15/AC30, Marshall JCM/DSL, Mesa, Ampeg, Peavey Classic 30.

Vintage solid-state exceptions worth money: Roland JC-120 ($500–900), Fender Power Chorus / Princeton Chorus ($150–250), Peavey Bandit 80s "red stripe" ($120–200), Polytone Mini-Brute ($300–450), Lab Series L5 ($400–700), Music Man (hybrid, $600–1,200), Yamaha
Solid-state/modelling: Line 6 Spider (all generations), Fender Frontman/Mustang/Champion, Peavey Bandit/Rage/Vypyr, Marshall MG, Crate, Boss Katana, Orange Crush, Roland Cube, Blackstar ID.

sombreros.title: Sombreros
sombreros.full: Sombreros (Mexican palm and felt hats; charro hats)
sombreros.money: fine gold-bullion embroidered antique charro sombreros $250–1,000+ (a Tardan c. 1920 gold pitiado felt hat is asked at ~$1,270–1,345 by a dealer, asking not sold).
sombreros.fakes: Modern mariachi hats with synthetic embroidery are sold as "antique". Tell by synthetic thread, plastic sweatbands, hot-glue. Modern sugarloaf reproductions of tall early-1900s crowns exist (Fedora Lounge).
sombreros.buy: Only felt/suede charro hats with heavy metallic embroidery under $60; plain straw sombreros are pass (bulky, low value).
tells: Palm straw (palma): woven spiral of palm, cord hatband; cheapest; tourist ones have painted/sequined designs.

Felt or suede charro sombreros: stiff, heavily embroidered with silver/gold metallic thread (bordado), often in fitted boxes; makers' labels inside (e.g. Sombrerería labels from Mexico City, Guadalajara, Jalisco).
Antique 19th-c. charro hats with real silver bullion embroidery and silver toquilla bands — museum-grade, rare.

south-asian-and-middle-eastern-gold-silv.title: South Asian and Middle Eastern gold and silver marks
south-asian-and-middle-eastern-gold-silv.full: South Asian and Middle Eastern gold and silver marks (Indian 22K "916" and BIS hallmark/HUID, KDM, colonial Indian silver — Hamilton & Co, P. Orr, Oomersi Mawji Kutch; Pakistan, Bangladesh; Gulf 21K/22K with Arabic-numeral stamps; Ottoman tughra; Persian 84/90 and lion-and-sun; Egyptian cat/ibis/lotus; Israeli 925/935 and Bezalel; Yemenite and Bedouin; Turkmen Tekke, Uzbek, Afghan)
south-asian-and-middle-eastern-gold-silv.money: tughra-marked Ottoman and 84/90-marked Persian silver sells at melt-plus ($1.70–1.76/g) and big "metal trays" can carry $1,000–5,000 of silver
south-asian-and-middle-eastern-gold-silv.fakes: - **Fake BIS stamps** on underkarat gold — the HUID check in BIS CARE exposes them (IIFL). - **Underkarat Gulf/Indian "22K"** without an assay mark — test (general knowledge, verify). - **Reproduction Ottoman/Persian sil
south-asian-and-middle-eastern-gold-silv.buy: Weigh and read the digits; buy unrecognised 21–22K gold and tughra/84/90/cat silver only at ≤ 40% of melt; pay up only for named collector types (Kutch, Hamilton/Orr, Bezalel, Tekke gilt silver, Isfahan masters) with a cited comp; unmarked "Afghan/Kuchi" and s
tells: Silver: ٨٤ = 84 (Persian/Russian zolotnik standard, .875), ٩٠ = 90 (.900), ٨٠ = 80 (.800), ٦٠ = 60 (.600, Egyptian).

Tughra silver is typically .900 (Pushkin tray) and was also used in Egypt before 1916 (silvercollection.it) and in Ottoman Balkans/Levant. Large trays, bowls, hammam bowls, coffee-cup holders (zarf), rosewater sprinklers — often listed as "metal", "tray", "whi

84 — Persian silver commonly marked 84, the Russian zolotnik standard = 875/1000 (Leland Little lot cites an 84 mark for 875 fineness); 90 = .900 (general knowledge, verify; Sky Jems says Persian silver "most commonly bore 800 or 900 fineness marks").

souvenir-spoons.title: Souvenir, salt and novelty spoons
souvenir-spoons.full: Souvenir, salt and novelty spoons (sterling souvenir spoons — Gorham, Watson, Durgin, Shepard, Mechanics Sterling; enamel European spoons; figural brass/bronze mini spoons; salt spoons)
souvenir-spoons.fakes: Modern cast copies of figural sterling (often in plated base metal); fake "sterling" stamps on Asian items; 1970s reissues of Salem witch spoons.
souvenir-spoons.buy: Buy sterling spoons (marked "Sterling"/925/lion marks) by weight at ≤ melt, plus figural/enamel sterling at ≤ 30% of resale; pass on silverplate, pewter and brass "gold-toned" spoons.
tells: US souvenir spoon craze 1889–1920s: sterling teaspoons/coffee spoons with figural handles (cities, states, Indians, Salem witch, world's fairs), engraved bowls ("Niagara Falls"). Gorham's 1891 Salem witch spoon by Daniel Low started it.
European enamel spoons (Norway — David Andersen, J. Tostrup; Denmark; Netherlands; Austria) in 800/830/925 silver with guilloché or plique enamel.
Salt spoons: tiny (2–3 in) spoons for open salt cellars; sterling or plate.

spinning-and-conventional-reels.title: Vintage spinning, spincast and conventional reels
spinning-and-conventional-reels.full: Vintage spinning, spincast and conventional reels (Mitchell, Penn, ABU Garcia Cardinal/Ambassadeur, Zebco, Ryobi, Quantum)
spinning-and-conventional-reels.money: Alcedo Micron, Hardy Altex, Van Staal, Penn International 130, pre-war Pflueger/Meisselbach $150–1,500+.
spinning-and-conventional-reels.fakes: - Few outright fakes. The risk is reissues and later production: modern "retro" Mitchell and Penn models, and late Japanese-made Cardinals sold as "vintage Sweden" (general knowledge, verify). - Married parts (wrong spoo
spinning-and-conventional-reels.buy: Only lots ≤ $30–50 with a visible half-bail/boxed Mitchell, Penn 704/706, ABU Cardinal 3/4 Sweden or 1950s–60s Ambassadeur; pass Zebco/Shakespeare and every common Mitchell 300/406 over $15–20.
tells: Penn (Philadelphia, US-made before the 1990s): Senator, Squidder, Jigmaster, 220 GTO level-wind, International (gold, lever drag), Spinfisher 700-series "greenies" (704/706, 704Z/706Z), 4400SS.
Modern money: Shimano Stella, Daiwa Saltiga, Van Staal.
Low: Zebco 33/202/404, Shakespeare, Quantum budget reels, Daiwa budget reels, modern Penn Fierce. Ryobi MG3 graphite (1980s) gets minor collector interest.

spinning-reels-vintage.title: Vintage spinning and spincast reels
spinning-reels-vintage.full: Vintage spinning and spincast reels (Mitchell, Penn Spinfisher, Zebco, Shakespeare)
spinning-reels-vintage.fakes: - Few fakes. Look out for later reissues and mixed spools/handles in lots (general knowledge, verify). - Penn reissued the 704Z/706Z in 2013; these are new reels, not vintage. Later Mitchell 300 reissues (Asian productio
spinning-reels-vintage.buy: Only lots with a visible half-bail Mitchell or Penn 70x ≤ $30; pass Zebco lots
tells: Look-alikes: Mitchell 300A/300 Pro and later Asian-made Mitchells (post-1980s) share the name; Penn 4400ss, 5500ss and 6500ss are later Penn spinners in grey/gold, not "greenies".

Mitchell 300 (France): black or grey body with the maker on the side. "Garcia Mitchell" = 1960s and later, which is common. The early half-bail versions have a bail arm on one side only. Mitchell Museum data (via forum) puts the half-bail to full-bail changeov

Mitchell serial numbers: per the Mitchell Museum data quoted on fishingmagic, early reels (to 1949) carry no serial, only foot stamps; 1949–52 reels carry a letter prefix plus five digits (A = 1949/50, B = 1950/51, C = 1951/52), first stamped on the foot and l

spongeware-and-spatterware.title: Spongeware and spatterware
spongeware-and-spatterware.full: Spongeware and spatterware (Red Wing, Western Stoneware, Robinson Clay/Robinson Ransbottom, Ohio and Minnesota potteries; English spatterware for the American market)
spongeware-and-spatterware.money: English 1820–60 spatterware with figural centres $200–2,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
spongeware-and-spatterware.fakes: Lots of reproduction "antique spongeware" since the 1970s–80s country décor boom; some artificially stained. Spatterware has British/US reproductions with fake wear. Rule: if it looks perfect, it's new.
spongeware-and-spatterware.buy: Buy old (pre-1940) American spongeware bowls/pitchers at ≤ $40 when the base, weight and crazing look right; pass on even-looking new pieces; spatterware only if the figure motif is clear and price is tiny.

sporting-art-prints.title: Sporting art prints , Heywood Hardy, George Wright, Thomas Blinks; American duck stamp and wildlife prints by Maynard Reece, David Maass, Richard Bishop, Lynn Bogue Hunt; reproduction decorator prints)
sporting-art-prints.full: Sporting art prints (English fox hunting, horse racing, coaching and shooting prints: Henry Alken, John Frederick Herring Sr., Cecil Aldin, Lionel Edwards, Snaffles (Charles Johnson Payne), Heywood Hardy, George Wright, Thomas Blinks; American duck stamp and wildlife prints by Maynard Reece, David Maass, Richard Bishop, Lynn Bogue Hunt; reproduction decorator prints)
sporting-art-prints.money: signed Snaffles, Cecil Aldin, Lionel Edwards prints $200–3,000
sporting-art-prints.fakes: Most "antique hunting prints" are reproductions; restrikes of Alken plates (later 19th–20th c.); facsimile signatures on Snaffles reproductions; prints cut from books and framed as "antique".
sporting-art-prints.buy: Pass on decorator hunt-scene reproductions; buy only pencil-signed prints (Snaffles with remarque, Aldin, Edwards) or plate-marked hand-coloured aquatints ≤ $50 that fit the seat.
tells: Signed early 20th c. prints (Snaffles, Aldin, Edwards): chromolithographs/collotypes with pencil signature and sometimes a pencil "remarque" sketch in the margin.
Period aquatints/engravings (1800–1880): plate mark (rectangular indentation around image), hand-colouring, publisher line ("Pub'd by Ackermann", "Fores"), title in engraved script below.

Decorator reproductions (1960s–2000s): offset lithographs with dot screen, printed title in script below image, cream mats with gilt fillet in dark wood/gold frames; often from Royal hunt paintings by Heywood Hardy, George Wright, Thomas Blinks, John Sanderson

sports-card-lots.title: Sports card lots and singles
sports-card-lots.full: Sports card lots and singles (Topps, Bowman, Donruss, Fleer, Upper Deck, Panini Prizm)
sports-card-lots.money: 1952 Mantle, T206, 1986 Fleer Jordan PSA 8+ $5,000+ (pass unless graded).
sports-card-lots.fakes: - Reprints of the 1952 Mantle, T206 Wagner/Cobb and 1986 Fleer Jordan are everywhere. They are often glossy, the wrong size, or labelled "reprint" on the back (general knowledge, verify). - Fake PSA slabs and counterfeit
sports-card-lots.buy: Visible pre-1980 stars in a lot ≤ $40, or a graded card ≤ 40% of 130point; pass junk-wax bulk and raw modern autos.
tells: "Junk wax" era (1987–94 Topps/Donruss/Fleer/Upper Deck) = worthless in bulk ($10–30 per 5,000). Huge print runs. Shiny 1990s card stock, neon or marble borders, monster boxes.
graded cards (PSA/BGS slabs)

sports-memorabilia.title: Sports memorabilia
sports-memorabilia.full: Sports memorabilia (team merchandise, programs, tickets, magazines, stadium giveaways, autographs, game-used items)
sports-memorabilia.fakes: Forged autographs are endemic — requires professional authentication (Dylan's rule: pass). Reprinted tickets and programs from big games (e.g. Super Bowl I) exist. Counterfeit jerseys from China. - Replica, reprint and c
sports-memorabilia.buy: Pass on modern fan lots; only pre-1975 programs/pennants/ticket stubs for famous events or full tickets to milestone games, at ≤ $20. No unauthenticated autographs.
tells: Pennants: felt, triangular, sewn or printed graphics; older ones have sewn-on felt trim and tassels, cartoon art, and team name plus city. A league logo in the bottom corner marks post-1970 NFL pennants (SCD). Roster-scroll pennants (players' names listed) are

Tickets: "full" = unused, with the audit stub attached; "stub" = torn at the gate. Before 2003 Super Bowl tickets were torn at entry; barcode scanning began in 2003 and tickets stayed intact from 2004 (Collectors Weekly).
Programs and yearbooks: printed date and event on cover; World Series and Super Bowl programs were often reprinted later as commemoratives.

spring-rocking-horses.title: Spring horses and painted wood rocking horses
spring-rocking-horses.full: Spring horses (Wonder Horse) and painted wood rocking horses (Wonder Products, Hedstrom, Radio Flyer, Mobo, Ayres, Collinson)
spring-rocking-horses.money: antique carved dapple-grey wood horses $800–3,000. All are bigger than a passenger seat and excluded by the size rule.
spring-rocking-horses.fakes: - Modern decorative reproduction dapple-grey horses (often made in Asia, or new UK makers like Stevenson Brothers, which are genuinely valuable new pieces) can be confused with antiques. Look at the wear, construction an
spring-rocking-horses.buy: Excluded by the size rule (bigger than a passenger seat). The only exception noted is a carved wood dapple-grey under $150 local.
tells: Wonder Horse (Wonder Products, Collierville TN, 1950s–80s): moulded plastic horse on four big coil springs in a tubular steel frame, with "Wonder Horse" moulded on the body or neck.
Same market: Radio Flyer and Hedstrom spring horses, Blazon.
A separate, higher market: carved and painted wood dapple-grey horses on bow rockers or a "safety" stand (English Ayres and Collinson, $800–3,000), and 1950s Mobo (pressed steel, UK, $150–400).

stamp-collections.title: Stamp collections and albums
stamp-collections.full: Stamp collections and albums (Scott, Harris, Minkus, White Ace, generic albums, stock books, kiloware)
stamp-collections.fakes: Forgeries mostly affect classic high-value stamps (needs expertising — professional authentication, which Dylan avoids).
stamp-collections.buy: pass unless photos show pre-1930 US/British Commonwealth on album pages, a Scott Specialty/White Ace/Minkus album that is well filled, or mint US sheets bought below ~50% of face.

steiff-teddy-bears.title: Steiff teddy bears and animals
steiff-teddy-bears.full: Steiff teddy bears and animals (Margarete Steiff GmbH, Giengen, Germany)
steiff-teddy-bears.fakes: - Fake buttons are added to non-Steiff bears; check that the button era matches the construction. - Steiff's own replicas (white tag) are legitimate reissues of early designs. They are not antiques, so don't pay antique
steiff-teddy-bears.buy: Mohair, felt paws, raised-script or earlier button ≤ $60, or boxed white-tag limited edition ≤ $50; pass synthetic yellow-tag plush over $15.
tells: "Knopf im Ohr": a metal button in the left ear, usually with a yellow cloth tag (standard line) or a white one (limited edition). Post-1950s pieces also have a chest tag.
Button chronology (era tells):
elephant button: 1904–05

sterling-candlesticks.title: Sterling silver candlesticks
sterling-candlesticks.full: Sterling silver candlesticks (Gorham, Towle, Duchin, Web Silver, Fisher, Empire, International, Frank M. Whiting, Tiffany, English hallmarked)
sterling-candlesticks.money: Georgian/Tiffany/Georg Jensen $1,000–20,000+ (general knowledge, verify). Terapeak "weighted sterling candlesticks": median $49.95.
sterling-candlesticks.fakes: - Silverplate passed off as sterling; check mark. Fake English hallmarks on Asian silver. - "Sheffield" alone is a place name and usually means plate (old Sheffield plate or modern EPNS) unless lion passant and date lett
sterling-candlesticks.buy: Weighted pairs: pay ≤ $15; scrap silver content is tiny. Look for unweighted solid sterling, Georg Jensen, Tiffany, Kirk repoussé, or English Georgian hallmarks.
tells: Valuable versions: solid unweighted sticks (heavy for size without felt base), hallmarked English (lion passant, date letter, maker), Georg Jensen (Denmark, "925S" and Jensen mark), Tiffany ("Tiffany & Co. Makers Sterling"), Arts & Crafts hand-hammered (Kalo,
Title words: "sterling weighted", "reinforced", "Duchin", "Gorham", "Towle", "Shabbat", "console candlesticks", "hallmarked", "Georgian", "Jensen".

Where marks sit: US pieces on the base edge or the underside rim next to the "weighted" wording; English pieces on the base flange and often again on the nozzle/bobeche; Jensen on the underside of the foot with the design number.

sterling-silver-jewelry.title: Sterling silver jewelry
sterling-silver-jewelry.full: Sterling silver jewelry (Taxco Mexican silver, Georg Jensen, Navajo/Zuni/Hopi, Danecraft/Beau/Coro sterling, Modernist studio, Indian/Thai export, mall sterling)
sterling-silver-jewelry.money: Georg Jensen, William Spratling, Hector Aguilar, Los Castillo, early Navajo ingot $400–5,000+.
sterling-silver-jewelry.fakes: - Fake Taxco marks on silver-plate "Alpaca" pieces; fake "925" stamps on base-metal Chinese jewelry (test with magnet — sterling isn't magnetic — and acid test). - Fake Navajo silver made in the Philippines/Mexico with f
sterling-silver-jewelry.buy: Weigh it first: never pay above ~80% of melt for unsigned silver; pay more only for a readable premium mark (Taxco eagle/assay + maker, Jensen, Spratling, signed Native, Scandinavian 925S designer) where the sold median clears profit ≥ max($50, price).
tells: Scandinavian / modernist (1940s–70s): clean sculptural shapes, enamel, "925S" or "STERLING DENMARK," maker marks (Georg Jensen in dotted oval, N.E. From, Hans Hansen, David-Andersen Norway with enamel, Sigurd Persen). American modernist studio jewelers (Ed Wie

Navajo/Zuni/Hopi (1900s–present): stamped and hand-cut silver, turquoise and coral bezels, Zuni needlepoint/inlay, Hopi overlay (two layers, oxidized background). Early (pre-1940) pieces are thin, coin or ingot silver, often unmarked, with hand stamping.

Mexican Taxco (1930s–present): heavy, chunky, repoussé or geometric, often with inlaid stones/obsidian/abalone; marked "STERLING MEXICO," "TAXCO," maker's name and after 1948 the spread-eagle assay with a number; 1979 on, "TS-##" or "TL-##" alphanumeric regist

steuben-glass.title: Steuben glass
steuben-glass.full: Steuben glass (post-1933 colourless crystal and Carder-era colour, Corning NY)
steuben-glass.money: Carder Aurene, engraved and sculptural pieces $600–5,000.
steuben-glass.fakes: - Forged diamond-point "Steuben" signatures on unsigned crystal exist; compare the handwriting. - Fake Aurene and "Aurene"-signed iridescent pieces from the Czech Republic and the US circulate (general knowledge, verify)
steuben-glass.buy: Signed Carder colour under $100 or animals under $40; pass colourless vases and bowls at $75+.
tells: Pre-1933 Carder-era coloured Steuben (Aurene gold/blue iridescent, Rosaline, Jade) is a different and much higher market ($300–3,000+).
Corning NY, 1933–2011, colourless lead crystal. Heavy and optically perfect, often with a thick disc foot or a teardrop/"bubble" stem.
Signed "Steuben" in script on the base, acid-stamped or diamond-scribed. Ask for a base photo.

stiffel-brass-lamps.title: Stiffel and brass table lamps
stiffel-brass-lamps.full: Stiffel and brass table lamps (Stiffel, Frederick Cooper, Chapman, Westwood, Rembrandt, generic brass)
stiffel-brass-lamps.money: Stiffel/Frederick Cooper/Chapman designer forms (tole, faux bamboo, obelisk, pairs) $250–800+ (general knowledge, verify)
stiffel-brass-lamps.fakes: Post-2000 "Stiffel" under licence is lighter and cheaper. Many lamps are listed as Stiffel with no mark at all — the attribution is the seller's guess. Insist on the socket stamp or label.
stiffel-brass-lamps.buy: only buy a signed Stiffel/Chapman/F. Cooper pair or a designer form at ≤ $60; single generic brass lamps are a pass — shipping a 30" lamp eats the margin.

stoneware-jugs-crocks.title: Stoneware crocks, jugs and salt crocks
stoneware-jugs-crocks.full: Stoneware crocks, jugs and salt crocks (Red Wing, Western/Monmouth, Greensboro/New Geneva PA, decorated salt-glaze, Albany slip, blue-band)
stoneware-jugs-crocks.money: elaborate cobalt scenes, signed potters, 30+ gal $500–10,000+ (auction).
stoneware-jugs-crocks.fakes: - Modern "primitive" reproduction crocks and jugs with fake cobalt birds and artificial ageing are sold widely. Look for too-regular decoration, a light weight, and a clean base (general knowledge, verify). - Red Wing ha
stoneware-jugs-crocks.buy: Uncracked cobalt-decorated, Greensboro-stencilled or advertising piece well under value (≤ $40–100 depending on decoration) that can ship; pass plain, unmarked, cracked, pickup-only or over-5-gal pieces.
tells: Grey or tan stoneware, cylindrical crocks and shoulder jugs, with a gallon number and often a cobalt-blue mark. The money is in the mark and the decoration.

Red Wing (MN): red "wing" stamp plus an oval "Red Wing Union Stoneware" ink stamp. Earlier pieces have a hand-drawn cobalt "birch leaf" or "elephant ear" and a "Minnesota Stoneware" stamp. Wing size (small 4", 6", large wing) changes value.

Greensboro / New Geneva PA (Hamilton & Jones, Jas. Hamilton & Co., T.F. Reppert, Williams & Reppert): stencilled cobalt lettering, often with stencilled flowers or eagles and freehand stripes. Sellers copy the name off the pot ("TR Ruppert", "Jas Hamilton") wi

stopwatches-and-timers.title: Mechanical stopwatches and timers
stopwatches-and-timers.full: Mechanical stopwatches and timers (Heuer, Minerva, Hanhart, Gallet, Meylan, Breitling, Excelsior Park, Elgin, Waltham, Junghans, Smiths, Lemania; dashboard/rally timers; darkroom/kitchen timers)
stopwatches-and-timers.money: Heuer (Leonidas/Trackmaster), split-second/rattrapante, 1/100 second, regatta/yacht and Heuer dashboard timers (Monte Carlo, Master Time, Super Autavia) $200–1,500+ (general knowledge, verify)
stopwatches-and-timers.fakes: Low risk at stopwatch level; "Heuer" redials exist on dashboard timers and franken parts. Modern quartz "vintage-style" timers. Heuer dashboard timers above $500 can need authentication of dial/hands — treat as authentic
stopwatches-and-timers.buy: Buy running Swiss jewelled stopwatches (Heuer, Minerva, Hanhart, Gallet, Meylan, Lemania, Excelsior Park) at ≤ $40, split-second/regatta/Heuer dashboard timers at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on non-running, pin-lever, or Japanese/digital timers.

straight-razors.title: Straight razors
straight-razors.full: Straight razors (Solingen German: Henckels, Böker, Dovo, Puma, Wacker, Friodur; Sheffield English: Wade & Butcher, Joseph Rodgers, George Wostenholm I*XL, Joseph Elliot; American: Case, Robeson, Torrey, Geneva, Shumate, W.R. Case; retailer-branded German razors)
straight-razors.money: rare (Wade & Butcher "Celebrated Hollow Ground" big wedges, Frederick Reynolds, Dubl Duck, early Sheffield, ornate celluloid/ivory scales) $100–500+.
straight-razors.fakes: Fake Wade & Butcher etchings exist on cheap Pakistani razors; modern Pakistani "Damascus" razors flood eBay. Check for tang country stamp and real age.
straight-razors.buy: Buy razor lots ≤ $10 per razor when photos show clean blades (no pitting at the edge, no chips/cracks) and named makers; boxed NOS German razors are the fastest sellers.
tells: Blade: maker etching or stamp on tang/blade face, width (5/8" common, 6/8"+ more valuable), grind (full hollow = 20th c. Solingen; wedge/near-wedge = older Sheffield), spine profile, toe (round/square/spike/French).
Tang stamps: "Germany" (post-1891), "Solingen", "Sheffield", "Made in USA" (post-1914 country-of-origin era).
Scales: celluloid (often marbled, amber "faux ivory" yellowed), hard rubber/vulcanite (black, often "horn" pattern), bone, real horn (translucent), ivory (needs CITES caution), plastic (1950s+).

stressless-recliners.title: Stressless recliners
stressless-recliners.fakes: - No fakes, but "Stressless-style" chairs from other makers are mislabelled (general knowledge, verify).
stressless-recliners.buy: Excluded by the size rule. The old rule ("buy under $150 if it fits the car or profit ≥ $750") only applies if Dylan makes a size exception.
tells: A leather recliner on a swivel base (a round "classic" base or a cross/star base), usually with a matching ottoman.
Wraparound curved wood or upholstered arms, a high back with a separately adjusting headrest (the "Plus" system), and gliding recline set by body weight.
Badge: a small "Stressless" logo plate or embroidery on the side or back. Ekornes labels sit under the seat (general knowledge, verify). The entry note says to look for the Ekornes badge on the arm.

studio-pottery.title: Studio pottery , Noel Osheroff, Jerry Rothman, Peter Voulkos, Toshiko Takaezu, Edwin & Mary Scheier, Brother Thomas, Warren MacKenzie; Hans Hedberg , Berndt Friberg, Stig Lindberg, Lucie Rie, Hans Coper)
studio-pottery.full: Studio pottery (American, Scandinavian and European studio ceramics: Beatrice Wood, Otto & Gertrud Natzler, Harrison McIntosh, Laura Andreson, Glen Lukens, Robert Maxwell, David Cressey (Earthgender), Noel Osheroff, Jerry Rothman, Peter Voulkos, Toshiko Takaezu, Edwin & Mary Scheier, Brother Thomas, Warren MacKenzie; Hans Hedberg (Biot), Berndt Friberg, Stig Lindberg, Lucie Rie, Hans Coper)
studio-pottery.money: masters (Natzler, Wood, Voulkos, Rie, Coper, Takaezu) $1,000–50,000+.
studio-pottery.fakes: Forged signatures on high-end names (Natzler, Voulkos); attributed "style of" listings. - Lens or "similar to" matches to famous names are not attributions; insist on a legible signature that matches published examples.
studio-pottery.buy: Buy only signed, identifiable studio work where recent sold median ≥ 3× price; pass on unsigned or decorator vases even if Lens matches a famous name.
tells: Thrown pieces: spiral throwing rings inside the neck, a trimmed foot ring with tool chatter or a cut-off swirl, slight asymmetry, glaze that pools and breaks over edges.
Hand-built/sculptural: slab or coil joins, carved or combed texture, applied clay (e.g. extruded "hair"), often unglazed iron-rich clay contrasted with a glazed area.

Noel Osheroff / Robert Maxwell & David Cressey circle (1970s California): sculptural mother-and-child and figure groups in unglazed red/brown clay with textured hair, set on blue or earth-glazed cylindrical bases; incised signature on base (general knowledge,

surveying-instruments.title: Surveying transits, levels and drafting instruments
surveying-instruments.full: Surveying transits, levels and drafting instruments (K&E, Gurley, Dietzgen, Berger, Buff & Buff, Brunton)
surveying-instruments.fakes: - Decorative "nautical brass" reproduction transits and theodolites from India are common. They are light, crudely engraved, and carry fake names like "Stanley London" or "Keuffel & Esser" (general knowledge, verify).
surveying-instruments.buy: Brass Gurley/K&E/Young with box under $120, or Brunton under $50; pass black 1950s–70s K&E at $150+ and levels.
tells: A brass or black-crinkle instrument on a 3- or 4-screw levelling base, usually stored in a wooden dovetailed box.
The maker is on the horizontal circle or a plate: Keuffel & Esser (K&E), W. & L.E. Gurley (Troy NY), Dietzgen, Berger, Buff & Buff, Brunton (pocket transit).
The serial number dates it. K&E serials under ~50,000 = pre-1920, brass, higher value (verify against a K&E serial table).

swiss-silver-pocket-watches.title: Swiss silver pocket watches, 19th c.
swiss-silver-pocket-watches.full: Swiss silver pocket watches, 19th c. (cylinder/"Bijou" key-wind and stem-wind, coin silver/800/0.935 cases; Longines, Zenith, Omega, Patek-level rarities aside)
swiss-silver-pocket-watches.money: repeaters, chronographs, and high-grade makers $500–5,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
swiss-silver-pocket-watches.fakes: Modern Chinese "antique" mechanical watches with fake old dials; marriages (mismatched dial, case or movement).
swiss-silver-pocket-watches.buy: Buy only running, maker-named (Longines, Omega, Zenith, IWC) silver Swiss watches or enamelled decorative cases at ≤ 1/3 of resale; pass on generic cylinder fob watches above ~$40. High-grade/repeaters need professional authentication, so out of scope.

tantalus-decanter-sets.title: Tantalus decanter sets
tantalus-decanter-sets.full: Tantalus decanter sets (Betjemann's / G. Betjemann & Sons, Asprey, Mappin & Webb, Hukin & Heath, Walker & Hall, Edwardian oak and brass English makers; modern Mascagni, Godinger reproductions)
tantalus-decanter-sets.money: Betjemann patent, games-compendium tantaluses, silver-mounted or ebony/coromandel sets $500–2,500+.
tantalus-decanter-sets.fakes: Modern repro tantaluses; married decanters. Check stopper numbers match bottle numbers. - Modern pieces: lacquered bright brass, Phillips screws, machine-perfect veneers, pressed-glass decanters with mold seams, no stamp
tantalus-decanter-sets.buy: Buy only complete sets with original matched cut-glass decanters and stoppers (or Betjemann's/maker-marked lock) at ≤ 1/3 resale, and small enough to fit a passenger seat; pass on empty frames above $25.
tells: The Betjemann mechanism: on documented examples the key is pushed in and turned, then the key barrel is pressed down to free the swing arm, which folds away so the decanters lift out (Mark Goodger; Chairish).

Size: a full-size 3-bottle oak Betjemann measured 38.5 × 15 × 27 cm (Mark Goodger) and 14.5 × 6 × 12 in (Chairish); a coromandel miniature was 23.5 × 9.5 × 18.5 cm (LAPADA). Both fit a passenger seat.

Two construction types (Hemswell): the common open frame (bottles visible, bar over the stoppers, carry handle on top or each side) and the closed box (a case, often with a mirrored back, that opens to reveal the bottles). Most hold three bottles; one-, two- a

tattoo-equipment.title: Tattoo equipment
tattoo-equipment.full: Tattoo equipment (rotary pen machines, coil machines, power supplies, ink, flash; Cheyenne, FK Irons, Bishop, Dragonhawk, Mast; vintage Percy Waters, Spaulding & Rogers machines; Sailor Jerry/Bert Grimm/Percy Waters flash)
tattoo-equipment.money: vintage flash sheets $50–500, with original hand-painted 1920s–50s flash by known artists $1,000–10,000+ at auction (general knowledge, verify
tattoo-equipment.fakes: - Counterfeit Cheyenne/FK cartridges and pens are widespread on AliExpress. Vintage machine replicas exist. - Vintage-style flash is widely copied by modern tattooers and reprinted in books; reprints are printed, on mode
tattoo-equipment.buy: Pass on beginner kits and opened inks; consider only pro-brand pens (logo visible) tested on video at ≤ 40% of used price, or vintage hand-built coil machines / original flash.
tells: Modern kits: black or coloured aluminium pen-style rotary machines, cartridge needle boxes, small ink bottles, transfer paper, practice skins — beginner bundles sold on Amazon for $40–120 new. Pro pens show logos (Cheyenne "C", FK Irons, Bishop wand shape).
Vintage coil machines: iron/brass frame with two coils, springs, binding posts, often maker-stamped on the frame or coil caps; some sold as kits by supply houses.

Flash: sheets of tattoo designs displayed in shops; originals are pen-and-ink with watercolour or acrylic on heavy paper or card, often with pinholes from wall display; some early flash was distributed as blueprints/printed sheets by supply houses (e.g. Percy

teddy-bears.title: Teddy bears, collectible
teddy-bears.full: Teddy bears, collectible (Steiff, Raikes/Applause, Merrythought, Hermann, Schuco, Chad Valley, Ideal, Gund, Boyds, Dakin)
teddy-bears.money: pre-1920 Steiff with blank/elephant/FF-underscored button, "Teddy Girl"-era $2,000-50,000+.
teddy-bears.fakes: Steiff replicas (1980s-2020s) of early bears are legitimate but priced far below originals — the white tag/brass or gold button and certificate identify them. Fake Steiff buttons (pewter copies, stitched-on buttons on Ch
teddy-bears.buy: Buy only mohair bears with a visible maker's button/tag (Steiff script button + chest tag, Merrythought label, Hermann tag) or Raikes first-edition sets at ≤ 30% of sold; pass on tagless, synthetic and "antique?" bears.

telephone-collectibles.title: Telephone collectibles
telephone-collectibles.full: Telephone collectibles (Western Electric 302/500/554/Princess, candlesticks; Automatic Electric, Kellogg, Stromberg-Carlson; reproductions)
telephone-collectibles.fakes: - **Candlestick repros** (1970s–90s, Hong Kong/Taiwan/China; brands like "Crosley", "Radio Shack", "GPX"): lightweight, brass-plated plastic or thin brass, modular jack, push-button or fake dial, ringer inside the base.
telephone-collectibles.buy: Buy Western Electric 302s ≤ $40, original WE candlesticks ≤ $60, colored 500/554 in rare colors ≤ $20; pass all repros, black 500s and anything "for decor" without WE markings.
tells: WE 302 (1937–1955, Henry Dreyfuss design): heavy die-cast metal (later some thermoplastic) body, sloped front with a dial set in a recess, F1 handset with round ends, bell inside the base. Black most common; ivory, red, green, gray, burgundy are rarer.

WE 500 (1950–1980s): plastic body, rounder, dial with letters/numbers on the outer ring under a clear finger wheel; date code stamped on base and handset (e.g., "8-62"). 2500 = touch-tone version. Colors: black, beige, ivory, pink, turquoise, light blue, green
WE 554 wall phone (1950s–80s) and 354 (1950s), Princess (1959–), Trimline (1965–).

telescopes.title: Telescopes
telescopes.full: Telescopes (Edmund Astroscan, Celestron, Meade, Questar, Unitron, Criterion)
telescopes.fakes: - No fakes to speak of. Look out for decorative brass "nautical" telescopes sold as antiques and for rebranded Chinese optics (general knowledge, verify).
telescopes.buy: Astroscan complete ≤ $70, Questar/Unitron/C8 under $200; pass department-store refractors and Astroscans over $100.
tells: Questar 3.5": a small chrome and black Maksutov on a built-in fork, with a leather case. $1,500+.
Edmund Astroscan: a red plastic, bowling-ball-shaped 4¼" reflector that sits in a three-point base, 1976–2010s. Complete means the base, RKE eyepiece, peep sight, strap and cap.
Celestron C5/C8 orange tube: Schmidt-Cassegrains from the 1970s–80s with an orange tube on a fork mount. $250–500.

terracotta-sun-plaques.title: Terracotta and ceramic sun-face plaques
terracotta-sun-plaques.full: Terracotta and ceramic sun-face plaques (Mexican Talavera/barro, Southwest studio, Italian, garden decor)
terracotta-sun-plaques.money: named folk artists (e.g. Metepec masters) or large mid-century pieces $100–400
terracotta-sun-plaques.fakes: Mass-produced "aged" finish imports sold as antique. Rarely worth faking. New "Talavera-style" suns are sold widely by importers; Metepec trees of life face Chinese copies (Wikipedia), and the same risk applies loosely t
terracotta-sun-plaques.buy: Pass by default; only signed mid-century studio or known Metepec maker pieces under $25.

thermos-bottles.title: Vacuum bottles
thermos-bottles.full: Vacuum bottles (King-Seeley Thermos, Aladdin, Stanley, Universal Landers Frary & Clark, American Thermos Bottle Co.)
thermos-bottles.money: early Stanley Super Vac / Aladdin and 1910s–20s nickel/brass Thermos $40–150 (general knowledge, verify)
thermos-bottles.fakes: Thermos reissued retro ribbed and character designs; Stanley classic is still made. Fakes not a concern.
thermos-bottles.buy: Pass on generic ribbed or plain thermoses; only buy pre-1930 nickel/leather or early Stanley/Landers with box at ≤ $25.

tiffany-style-lamps.title: Tiffany-style and slag glass lamps and shades , Bradley & Hubbard, Miller, Salem, Duffner & Kimberly, Meyda Tiffany, Dale Tiffany, Quoizel, hobbyist leaded shades)
tiffany-style-lamps.full: Tiffany-style and slag glass lamps and shades (Tiffany Studios, Handel, Pairpoint (reverse-painted), Bradley & Hubbard, Miller, Salem, Duffner & Kimberly, Meyda Tiffany, Dale Tiffany, Quoizel, hobbyist leaded shades)
tiffany-style-lamps.fakes: Fake Tiffany Studios tags on Chinese reproductions are rampant; any "Tiffany" signature on a <$500 lamp is almost certainly fake. Handel reproduction tags too. Requires professional authentication for real Tiffany/Handel
tiffany-style-lamps.buy: Pass on leaded "Tiffany style" shades and modern lamps; look only for antique bent-panel slag lamps with cast-metal overlay or signed Handel bases/shade rims under $150 that fit in a seat.
tells: Real Tiffany Studios (1893–1932): small irregular pieces following natural forms (dragonfly, wisteria, peony), "TIFFANY STUDIOS NEW YORK" stamped tag on the shade rim and base numbered; bronze base with rich patina. Almost never on Craigslist for under $200.

Hobbyist and 1970s copper-foil shades: geometric grids of squares and rectangles, thick lumpy silver solder beads, swag ("Tiffany swag hanging lamp") shapes from 1970s kits and Dale Tiffany/Quoizel imports.
Antique panel lamps (1900–1930): Miller, Bradley & Hubbard, Salem, Moe Bridges, Handel: bent caramel/green slag panels behind cast white-metal or bronze filigree overlay, often marked on the base.

tin-litho-plates.title: Tin lithograph plates and trays
tin-litho-plates.full: Tin lithograph plates and trays (Ohio Art, J. Chein, Elite/Daher, Worcester Ware, Cheinco, Bristolware, advertising "tip trays")
tin-litho-plates.money: pre-1930 advertising tip trays and beer/soda trays $40–400+.
tin-litho-plates.fakes: Reproduction Coca-Cola, beer and Moxie trays since the 1970s (often marked "reproduction" small on the rim, or modern even lithography, light gauge). Modern "vintage style" tin signs and trays are everywhere. Decorative
tin-litho-plates.buy: Pass on all decorative 1960s–80s art-print tin plates; only buy pre-1930 advertising tip trays or serving trays (brand name lithographed in the design, US maker credit on the rim) at ≤ 25% of sold value.

tin-robot-toys.title: Tin robot toys , Alps, Linemar, Marx, Cragstan , Ichida, Yoshiya , Bandai; modern Schylling/Ha Ha Toy/China reproductions)
tin-robot-toys.full: Tin robot toys (Horikawa/SH, Yonezawa, Masudaya/Modern Toys, Nomura (TN), Alps, Linemar, Marx, Cragstan (importer), Ichida, Yoshiya (KO), Bandai; modern Schylling/Ha Ha Toy/China reproductions)
tin-robot-toys.money: classic 1950s rare (Robby, Mr. Atomic, Machine Man, Robert the Robot Ideal) $500–10,000+
tin-robot-toys.fakes: Extensive; reproduction boxes too. Japanese 1990s reissues (e.g. Osaka Tin Toy Institute) are legitimate collectibles but lower. - **Robot Lilliput:** original has a fan-shaped "KT" logo and "Made in Japan"/"Japan"; the
tin-robot-toys.buy: Buy Japanese-made tin robots (TN, SH, KO, Yonezawa marks; "Made in Japan" lithographed) with intact parts and box at ≤ 1/3 resale; skip battery-operated if untested (rule: no untested electronics) unless priced as non-working; pass on posters and Chinese repro
tells: Title words sellers use: "space robot", "tin toy", "battery op", "Made in Japan", "with box", "works", "Horikawa", "SH".

Construction: printed (lithographed) sheet tin folded and held with tabs through slots, not screws or glue; battery robots have a battery door in the back or feet and a remote or on/off switch; wind-ups have a key in the side or back.
Sizes: wind-ups are typically 5–9"; the big battery robots of 1957–64 run to ~15" (Masudaya Gang of Five).

tin-wind-up-and-battery-toys.title: Tin wind-up and battery-operated toys
tin-wind-up-and-battery-toys.full: Tin wind-up and battery-operated toys (Marx, Chein, Unique Art, Japan 1950s–60s, Schuco, Lehmann)
tin-wind-up-and-battery-toys.money: robots, rare Schuco and boxed pre-war Marx $1,000–10,000+.
tin-wind-up-and-battery-toys.fakes: - Schylling and other modern reissues of Marx and Lehmann designs; Chinese reproduction robots (Robby, Planet robots). - Fake boxes (colour-copied) for rare robots (general knowledge, verify).
tin-wind-up-and-battery-toys.buy: Japan/Marx/Schuco marked and working at ≤ 35% of sold, or any robot/space toy ≤ $100; pass Taiwan/China 1970s+ and non-working battery toys.
tells: US: MARX ("Louis Marx & Co", 1930s–70s), Chein, Unique Art, Wolverine.
Japan 1950s–60s: Alps, Masudaya (TM), Nomura (TN), Yonezawa (Y), Horikawa (SH), Bandai, and Linemar (Marx's Japan line).
Germany: Schuco, Lehmann, Arnold.

tobacco-cutters.title: Tobacco cutters
tobacco-cutters.full: Tobacco cutters (Enterprise, Reading Hardware, T. C. Johnson, P. Lorillard "Climax", Star, Scotten-Dillon; cast-iron plug cutters and rotary shredders)
tobacco-cutters.fakes: Many cast iron reproductions — mostly decorative "general store" pieces sold in the 1970s onward (general knowledge). Spot them by soft lettering, sand-cast grain, crude fit of the knife, and modern fasteners. The sweep
tobacco-cutters.buy: Buy only advertising-marked plug cutters under ~$40; unmarked or unidentified cast pieces are a pass.

tobacco-tins.title: Tobacco tins
tobacco-tins.full: Tobacco tins (pocket tins and flat tins: Prince Albert, Velvet, Sir Walter Raleigh, Edgeworth, Union Leader, Tuxedo, Kentucky Club, Half and Half, Granger; scarce: Forest & Stream, Dixie Queen, Hiawatha, Bagdad, Big Ben, Hi-Plane, Buckingham, Lucky Strike roll cut, Mayo's roly-poly; makers American Can, Tindeco, Heekin)
tobacco-tins.fakes: Chinese reproduction pocket tins of scarce brands (Forest & Stream, Hiawatha, Dixie Queen) since the 2000s – too-bright colours, no maker imprint, crude seams. 1980s "Collector's" reissue canisters (Sir Walter Raleigh, P
tobacco-tins.buy: Buy only scarce vertical pocket tins (Forest & Stream, Dixie Queen, Hiawatha, Bagdad short, Big Ben, Hi-Plane, Buckingham) at ≤ $30 each or lots containing them; pass Prince Albert/Velvet/Sir Walter Raleigh/Edgeworth lots above ~$4 per tin.
tells: Vertical pocket tins (hinged lid, curved to fit a pocket) – most collected; "Push up" or "Open other side" embossed on the lid edge; net weight (1½ oz, 1⅝ oz) printed on the base front.
Flat/box tins (Edgeworth rectangular with hinged lid, example 7955504538; "Larus & Bro. Co. Richmond VA").
Round canisters (Sir Walter Raleigh 14 oz, Prince Albert 1 lb) – 1960s–80s "Collector's" reissue canisters (example 7935473224) are $5–15.

tokusatsu-and-anime-vintage-tees.title: Tokusatsu and anime vintage tees
tokusatsu-and-anime-vintage-tees.full: Tokusatsu and anime vintage tees (Tsuburaya/Ultraman, Akira, Ghost in the Shell, Evangelion, Sailor Moon, Dragon Ball, Pokémon)
tokusatsu-and-anime-vintage-tees.money: grails (Akira 1988 Fashion Victim, Ghost in the Shell 1995–96, early Evangelion) $500–2,500+ (general knowledge, verify)
tokusatsu-and-anime-vintage-tees.fakes: Very high risk for Akira, GITS, Evangelion, Sailor Moon: bootlegs printed on genuine vintage blank tags (old Giant/Screen Stars tags) and modern "vintage-style" reprints (Hot Topic, Uniqlo UT, Crunchyroll, official retro
tokusatsu-and-anime-vintage-tees.buy: Buy ≤ $40 only when the tag, print and copyright line are visible and date it to 1999 or earlier; never buy a grail title without tag/copyright photos – bootlegs dominate.

toy-and-figure-marks.title: Toy and figure marks — reading guide
toy-and-figure-marks.full: Toy and figure marks — reading guide (Hot Wheels, Matchbox/Lesney, Kenner Star Wars, G.I. Joe, Barbie, Steiff, Schuco, Märklin, Lionel, Marx, Japanese tin makers, Fisher-Price, LEGO, Funko, Breyer, Hummel TMK, Precious Moments, Royal Doulton HN)
toy-and-figure-marks.money: The mark on the base, leg, foot, ear, stud or bottom is the date and often the whole value: redline Hot Wheels $8–5,000+ vs $1 for post-1977
toy-and-figure-marks.fakes: - **Hot Wheels:** reissues with redline-style wheels (1993 anniversary, later "vintage" lines); customs; repainted spectraflame; fake STH customs. - **Matchbox:** Lesney-style reissues marked China; wheel swaps. - **Star
toy-and-figure-marks.buy: Read the base/leg/foot/ear/bottom mark first and price from that mark's tier, not the toy's look. Pay ≤ ~40% of the sold comp for the marked tier so profit ≥ max($50, price) after ~13% fees and shipping both ways. Pass on China/Malaysia-base "vintage" claims,
tells: A copyright date is the date of the design or mould, not the production year. Hot Wheels "©1967", Kenner "© LFL 1977", Barbie "© MCMLVIII"/"©1966", Fisher-Price "©" dates and Breyer moulds all run for years after the date shown (Muncle Mike's; This Old Toy; ge
Reissues reuse the old marks plus a new date or maker. Look for a second, later date or a "Hasbro", "China", "Reproduction" line.
Country of origin (COO) is a period tell. Hong Kong / USA / England / Japan / West or US-Zone Germany = original period; China, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia = later, except where noted.

toy-animal-figures.title: Toy animal figures
toy-animal-figures.full: Toy animal figures (Britains, Elastolin, Lineol, Marx, Timpo, Starlux, Schleich, Safari Ltd, Papo, Bullyland, Hong Kong generics)
toy-animal-figures.money: Britains hollow-cast lead and Elastolin/Lineol composition $15–150+ each.
toy-animal-figures.fakes: Britains reissued some lead designs as "Britains Collectors' Edition" metal figures (1990s–2000s, marked with modern dates). Recast lead figures (white metal, solid, heavier) sold as Britains – check for hollow cast and
toy-animal-figures.buy: Buy only lead (Britains) or composition (Elastolin/Lineol) animals or marked retired Schleich lots at ≤ $3 per figure; pass all bags of unmarked soft plastic animals.
tells: Composition (Elastolin, Lineol, 1904–1960s): sawdust/glue body over wire armature, matte painted, cracks and chips show a brown-grey core; "Elastolin" or "Lineol" stamped under the base; often on a small integral base.

Hollow-cast lead (Britains, Johillco, Crescent, Taylor & Barrett, 1900–1966): heavy, dull painted surface with paint chips revealing grey metal, often a small round hole (casting vent), "Britains Ltd" + "Made in England" cast under the base.
Hard polystyrene/painted plastic 1950s–70s (Britains "Herald", Starlux France, Timpo, Crescent): crisp detail, hand-painted, marked.

toy-train-accessories.title: Toy train accessories
toy-train-accessories.full: Toy train accessories (Lionel / Marx / Noma postwar O-gauge, Plasticville, transformers)
toy-train-accessories.fakes: - Lionel's own modern reissues of postwar accessories, and aftermarket reproduction parts and boxes (general knowledge, verify).
toy-train-accessories.buy: Lots ≤ $4/piece with at least one 394 / water tower / operating accessory visible, or Lionel 313/350/97/164 under $80; pass all-Marx/plastic lots and transformer-only lots.
tells: Tinplate and bakelite trackside pieces:
silver lattice tower with a red/orange top (Lionel 394/494 rotary beacon)
black semaphores with red/green lenses (Lionel 151)

trade-bead-necklaces.title: Trade Bead Necklaces
trade-bead-necklaces.full: Trade Bead Necklaces (Venetian millefiori/chevron African trade beads, Bohemian glass, Nepalese/Tibetan metal beads, amber/copal, Bakelite)
trade-bead-necklaces.money: chevron 6–7 layer, large old beads, Baltic amber, Bakelite $80–500+ (general knowledge, verify)
trade-bead-necklaces.fakes: Modern Indonesian/Indian "trade beads", fake Bakelite ("fakelite"), fake amber resin. Chevrons are still made in Italy, India and China (Bead Chest); dealers list "faux chevron" beads openly (Africa Direct), and these of
trade-bead-necklaces.buy: Buy full strands of genuine old Venetian chevron/millefiori or tested Bakelite/amber under ~$25; pass assembled ethnic-look necklaces.

trade-violins.title: Trade violins
trade-violins.full: Trade violins (German/Czech "Stradivarius copy" fiddles, student outfits, Roth, Juzek, Pfretzschner, Mirecourt)
trade-violins.money: genuine Italian/French/English makers $2,500+ and good pernambuco bows $300–2,000.
trade-violins.fakes: - Every "Stradivarius" label is a copy, by design, not fraud. Fake labels of good German makers also exist; branded stamps are more reliable than paper labels (general knowledge, verify). - Bows: fake stamps on cheap Bra
trade-violins.buy: Roth/Juzek/Pfretzschner/French labelled and playable ≤ $150, or a stamped silver-mounted bow ≤ $50; pass "needs repair" and unlabelled trade copies.
tells: A paper label inside the f-hole reading "Antonius Stradivarius Cremonensis 1713", "Nicolaus Amatus" or "Jacobus Stainer" marks a Markneukirchen/Schönbach factory copy, 1880–1930. Millions were made.

Tells of a better instrument: a one-piece flamed maple back, a hand-cut scroll with crisp turns, inlaid (not painted) purfling, and a shop label "Made in Germany/Czechoslovakia" (E.R. Pfretzschner, Roth, Heberlein, Juzek, Wurlitzer).
Modern Chinese and Romanian student outfits (Cremona, Stentor, Euro-Standard) cost $80–200 new.

transferware.title: Transferware
transferware.full: Transferware (Spode, Copeland, Enoch Wood, Clews, Ridgway, Adams, Wedgwood, Johnson Bros, Enoch Wedgwood/Royal Staffordshire, Mason's, Churchill, Salem "Olde Staffordshire", Masons/Myott)
transferware.money: early (1815–1840) historical blue Staffordshire with American views $200–2,000+.
transferware.fakes: - Spode Blue Italian has been in continuous production; most vases and jars are late 20th-century; Spode/Portmeirion still sell new. Back-stamp variants date them (Copeland Spode, Spode England, Spode Portmeirion). - Chi
transferware.buy: Buy only pre-1850 dark-blue historical Staffordshire (American scenes, impressed maker marks, no back-stamp "England") or rare Spode shapes at ≤ $50; pass on all modern dinnerware sets.
tells: Early historical blue (c. 1815–1840): deep cobalt, scenes of American cities, ships, landmarks; irregular backs, stilt marks (three tiny marks on the base from kiln stilts), impressed makers' marks (WOOD, CLEWS, ADAMS, RIDGWAY), no "England" (added after 1891)

Earthenware/ironstone decorated by transfer printing: an engraved copper plate is printed onto tissue and transferred to the ware before glazing. Look for tiny dot/line engraving texture, repeat seams where borders meet.
Romantic period (1830–1860): lighter blues, pinks, browns, purples, greens; fanciful scenes.

transformers-g1.title: Transformers Generation 1
transformers-g1.money: boxed/MISB and giants (Fortress Maximus, Metroplex, Omega Supreme, Scorponok) $300–3,000+.
transformers-g1.fakes: - Chinese knock-offs (KOs) of Fortress Maximus, Metroplex, Jetfire, Optimus — off colours, blurry stamps, cheap plastic, no Hasbro/Takara stamp or a fake one. - Reproduction accessories (3D-printed or injection-moulded)
transformers-g1.buy: Buy loose figures only when complete or near-complete with weapons, unbroken, and ≤ 30% of sold; lots of 1984–86 figures with weapons at ≤ $10 per figure; check for reissue copyright dates.
tells: 1987: Headmasters, Targetmasters (small partner figures), Fortress Maximus, Scorponok.
1984–85: cars and planes (Optimus Prime, Jazz, Megatron gun, Soundwave tape deck, Jetfire), die-cast metal parts, "Made in Japan", chromed parts, rubber tyres.
1985–86: Dinobots, Constructicons (Devastator), Insecticons, rubsigns (heat-sensitive faction symbols from late 1985).

transit-tokens.title: Transit tokens
transit-tokens.full: Transit tokens (US bus, streetcar and subway fare tokens; makers Scovill, Osborne, Meyer & Wenthe, Ingle System, Patrick & Co.)
transit-tokens.fakes: Rarely faked; some fantasy pieces and modern restrikes exist (NYC). Not a concern at this price level. Error tokens (missing cut-outs or holes) are the one place to be careful: a filled cut-out or plugged hole would fake
transit-tokens.buy: Buy only large mixed lots with many different small-town/early tokens under ~$0.50 each; single common tokens are always pass.
tells: Read the legend: company name (e.g. "Tucson Transit System", "Capital Transit Co."), city, and the denomination wording ("Good for one fare", "Good for one ride", "School fare", "Half fare"). The company name dates the token, since transit companies changed na
Typical size reference: the NYC Diamond Jubilee is 22.8 mm, 1.6 mm thick, 4.3 g brass (Numista).
Look-alikes in "token jars": arcade, car wash, parking, casino and trade ("good for 5¢ in trade") tokens. Trade tokens are not transit tokens but can be worth more (see below).

tribal-area-rugs.title: Tribal and village area rugs , Turkish Anatolian , Caucasian , Moroccan Beni Ourain/Boucherouite, Navajo, Indian Agra/Jaipur copies, machine-made look-alikes)
tribal-area-rugs.full: Tribal and village area rugs (Pakistani Bokhara/Jaldar, Afghan Turkoman, Persian tribal (Qashqai, Baluch, Hamadan, Shiraz), Turkish Anatolian (Konya, Yahyali, Milas), Caucasian (Kazak, Shirvan), Moroccan Beni Ourain/Boucherouite, Navajo, Indian Agra/Jaipur copies, machine-made look-alikes)
tribal-area-rugs.fakes: Chemically aged and "antique washed" new rugs presented as old; painted-in wear; tea-washed Indian/Pakistani copies; machine-made rugs with sewn fringe sold as handmade.
tribal-area-rugs.buy: Small (≤ 4x6, rolled fits passenger seat) hand-knotted rugs only; pass on Pakistani Bokharas and Indian copies; target older tribal rugs with natural-dye abrash, wool foundation and asymmetric drawing, at ≤ 1/4 resale and only with back photos.
tells: Pakistani "Bokhara" / Jaldar (1960s–2000s): rows of repeated octagonal Tekke-style guls on salmon, rust, red, ivory, or taupe grounds, very even and clipped short, soft lustrous wool, cotton foundation, white cotton fringe; extremely common; $20–80 small.
Afghan Turkoman (Ersari, Tekke, Yomut): deep red guls, coarser older wool, sometimes wool warps; older ones collectible.
Persian tribal: Baluch (dark blues/aubergine, small), Qashqai/Shiraz (geometric, animals), Hamadan villages; wool warps and wefts in many tribal pieces.

trophies-and-awards.title: Trophies and Awards
trophies-and-awards.full: Trophies and Awards (Telly, Emmy, Clio, Grammy-type statuettes; sports trophies; sterling loving cups)
trophies-and-awards.fakes: Replica statuettes (Emmy/Oscar novelty) common and worth $10–40. Fake hallmarks on plated cups exist; English "pseudo-hallmarks" on American plate (look for "EP" or company names in imitation-hallmark boxes) (general kno
trophies-and-awards.buy: Pass on industry statuettes and sports trophies; only buy sterling cups (hallmarks visible) under melt or Art Deco figural trophies under ~$30.
tells: Telly Awards: founded 1979 for video and television; awarded in Gold, Silver and Bronze tiers; over 12,000 entries a year, and each credited team member can receive a statue, so supply is large (marjennings.com).

Restricted awards (cllct; Variety): Oscars awarded after 1951 must first be offered back to the Academy (for $1 per cllct, $10 per Variety) — a rule binding heirs, upheld in a 2015 Los Angeles ruling. Emmys may not be sold at all and are to be returned to the
Sterling presentation cups: often 6–10" tall, 2–3 handles (sometimes antler/horn handles), engraved with event, date and names; marks under the foot or on the side near the base.

truck-and-auto-emblems.title: Truck and auto emblems
truck-and-auto-emblems.full: Truck and auto emblems (hood, grille and fender badges; White Freightliner, Peterbilt, Kenworth, Mack bulldog, Diamond T, GMC, Ford, Chevrolet, Studebaker, International)
truck-and-auto-emblems.money: chrome Mack bulldogs, enamelled pre-war badges and radiator mascots $100–500+ (general knowledge, verify).
truck-and-auto-emblems.fakes: Restoration suppliers sell reproduction emblems for popular cars (Chevy, Ford, Mopar) and for some trucks (Mack, Peterbilt). Decorative "sign" reproductions are also sold as wall art. Look for part numbers and genuine we
truck-and-auto-emblems.buy: Buy original heavy-truck or pre-war enamel/cast emblems with intact mounting studs at ≤ 30% of verified sold; pass on modern badges, reproductions and anything over ~24" or over $40 without a Terapeak check.
tells: Mack bulldog hood ornaments: chrome (later) or gold-tone (for 'B' and later trucks), marked "Mack" and patent number.

Heavy-truck nameplates: large (15–30" long) cast pot-metal or aluminium plates with raised letters, often chrome-plated with painted recessed backgrounds. Example: "WHITE FREIGHTLINER" plate on a chrome loop surround, used on cab-overs in the 1950s–70s.
Car emblems/scripts: smaller pot-metal chrome scripts (Chevrolet, Bel Air, Impala), crests with enamel or plastic inserts.

tube-radios.title: Tube radios
tube-radios.full: Tube radios (Zenith, Philco, RCA, GE, Emerson, Fada; bakelite and catalin table radios)
tube-radios.fakes: - Reproduction catalin cabinets and knobs exist, and modern "retro" radios (Crosley, Thomas) are sold as vintage (general knowledge, verify). - Repro knobs, handles and bezels in contrasting colours are fitted to make a
tube-radios.buy: Pass on brown bakelite over $40 and anything untested; stop everything for coloured catalin.
tells: Catalin (swirled or marbled, translucent: Fada 1000 "Bullet", Addison, Emerson AU-190) is $800+. It never looks flat brown.

Catalin shapes: Fada "Bullet" (streamlined, round end, handle, 1940–47 across five Fada models; Model 1000 introduced 1945); Emerson AU-190 (c. 1938, cathedral/tombstone shape in catalin); Motorola 50XC; RCA 66X8 "Tuna Boat" (c. 1948) (WSHU, antiqueradio.org).
Zenith H725/K725/Y723 (1951–55): maroon or brown bakelite, a big round gold dial with "Zenith" below, a carry handle. Working $70–130; untested $30–60.

turkey-and-game-calls.title: Turkey and game calls
turkey-and-game-calls.full: Turkey and game calls (collectible box, pot and duck calls: Lynch, Neil Cost, Turpin, Ashby, Olt, Reelfoot)
turkey-and-game-calls.money: Lynch Squirrel Chatter Box mostly >$6,000 at auction.
turkey-and-game-calls.fakes: - Forged signatures on unsigned boxes in the style of Cost or Lynch exist. Collectors rely on provenance and the maker's handwriting (general knowledge, verify). - Lynch reissued its classic models (commemorative box set
turkey-and-game-calls.buy: Signed Cost/Turpin/Lee/early Lynch under $100, or any signed call lot under $40; pass Quaker Boy/Primos and seller-aware pieces.
tells: Wooden box calls (a lidded box with a paddle), pot/slate calls (a round pot with a striker), and duck/goose calls (wood or plastic barrels). The pivoted-lid box call was patented by Henry C. Gibson of Arkansas in 1897, and the basic design is unchanged (onX).
Mass-market makers (Quaker Boy, Primos, Knight & Hale, Lynch pre-2000) are worth $10–30.
M.L. Lynch early (Birmingham AL, pre-1960s)

turntables.title: Turntables
turntables.full: Turntables (Technics, Pioneer, Dual, Thorens, Garrard, Kenwood, Sansui, Stanton, Audio-Technica, Marantz, Yamaha, Denon)
turntables.money: high-end vintage (Thorens TD-125/160, Garrard 301/401, Pioneer PL-570/L1000, Technics SP-10, Kenwood KP-9010/L-07D) $300–1,500+.
turntables.fakes: - No real fakes, but beware Chinese "Technics-style" clones (Reloop, Audio-Technica LP1240, Hanpin OEM like Stanton STR8, Numark TTX, Pyle). They look like a 1200 but sell for a fraction. - Lens matches anything silver w
turntables.buy: Only buy a tested (seller demonstrates it plays on video) Technics SL-1200/1210 or a named high-end deck at ≤ 35% of sold median; everything else is too heavy and too fragile to ship for the margin.
tells: Technics SL-1200/1210: heavy silver (1200) or black (1210) die-cast/rubber plinth, big strobe dots around platter edge, a red/orange pop-up target light at front-left, pitch slider on the right, "Technics" in the lower left, rectangular start/stop button lower
Pioneer PL-: PL-12D, PL-15, PL-514, PL-518 (belt, common), PL-530/570/630 (quartz direct drive, better).
Thorens: TD-145/160/166 (Swiss/German, suspended sub-chassis, wood plinth), TD-124/125 (premium).

tv-lamps.title: TV lamps , Claes Originals, Maddux of California, Royal Haeger, Haeger, Metro Ware/Metropolitan, Royal Fleet, Premco, Moss)
tv-lamps.full: TV lamps (mid-century figural and planter TV lamps; Lane & Co., Kron (Texans Inc.), Claes Originals, Maddux of California, Royal Haeger, Haeger, Metro Ware/Metropolitan, Royal Fleet, Premco, Moss)
tv-lamps.fakes: Some modern ceramic reproductions of panthers; Chinese "MCM-style" lamps. Fiberglass shades reproduced. Texans Inc. kept producing into the 1970s–80s, so late pieces ("B edition", c.1971) exist alongside 1950s originals
tv-lamps.buy: Buy only glazed-ceramic Kron/Haeger/Lane/Maddux lamps with intact shade under $40; pass chalkware.
tells: Period: TV sets reached the market in 1946 and TV lamps followed; the heyday ended by the 1960s as picture quality improved (Journal of Antiques). Sold as a dime-store item for about $5–15 new, with new designs every year; at least 75–100 US makers plus some J
Size: typically 8–14" (JoA). Bulb ≤ 40 W behind a figural or scenic panel, giving indirect backlight; figures cast a silhouette on the wall.

Forms: panthers (the most popular, crouching/stalking), Siamese cats (one Texans Inc. cat-with-kitten design sold over 30,000 in a year), roosters, horses, deer, gazelles, dogs, swans, mallards, swordfish, ships/junks, shells, mermaids, covered wagons, locomot

ukelins-and-zithers.title: Ukelins, chord zithers, lap harps and psalteries
ukelins-and-zithers.full: Ukelins, chord zithers, lap harps and psalteries (International Musical Corp/Oahu Publishing ukelin, Marxochime, Phonoharp, Columbia, Bell Harp Co., Menzenhauer, Oscar Schmidt "Guitar-Zither", Hawaiian Art Co. violin-uke)
ukelins-and-zithers.fakes: - No meaningful fakes. Modern lap harps (Music Maker, Hearthsong) and Chinese-made zithers are new products, sold cheaply. - Autoharps (Oscar Schmidt, with chord-bar buttons) are a different, more playable instrument wit
ukelins-and-zithers.buy: Almost always a pass: buy only complete, crack-free ukelins or Bell Harps with case/bow at ≤ $30.
tells: Concert zither (Alpine): fretboard on one side with metal frets, 30–40 open strings, guitar-shaped or rounded body, German/Austrian makers.

Chord zither ("guitar-zither", "mandolin-harp"): flat trapezoidal box with a slanted pin row, a round soundhole with a paper rosette, chord string groups on the left, melody strings across, and a paper note chart under the strings. Usually an eagle, landscape

Ukelin (1920s–1960s): long narrow coffin-shaped box, two soundholes, 16 melody strings bowed with a violin bow plus 4 groups of chord strings strummed; sold door-to-door by International Musical Corp. (Hoboken/Jersey City NJ) and later Oahu Publishing (Clevela

underground-comix.title: Underground comix
underground-comix.full: Underground comix (Zap Comix, Apex Novelties, Print Mint, Rip Off Press, Last Gasp, Kitchen Sink; R. Crumb, Gilbert Shelton, S. Clay Wilson, Spain, Rick Griffin, Victor Moscoso, Robert Williams)
underground-comix.money: Zap #1 first printing ("Printed by Charles Plymell", 25¢) $4,000–7,000 raw VG/FN, $10,000–26,000+ CGC 8.0–9.4.
underground-comix.fakes: - The dominant "fake" is a misdescribed later printing sold as "1968 first print" — intentionally or not. Any seller who won't show the back cover and cover price is hiding a 3rd+ printing. - Counterfeit Zap #1 2nd print
underground-comix.buy: Buy only printing-verified first (or Zap #1 second) printings of 1968–72 keys at ≤ 35% of raw sold; a 25¢ Zap #1 or any "Printed by Don Donahue" Zap #1 at ≤ $200 is an immediate buy; pass on every later printing (cover price 50¢ or higher on a 1968 title is a
tells: Title words sellers use: "Zap Comix", "R. Crumb", "underground comic", "head shop", "hippie comic", "1960s", "Freak Brothers", "Mr Natural", "Print Mint", "Last Gasp", "adult comic".
