Small-press, adult, counterculture comic books 1968–c.1980 (the "comix" era; "newave" mini-comix after ~1978), mostly San Francisco/Berkeley (Apex Novelties, Print Mint, Rip Off Press, Last Gasp, Company & Sons) plus Kitchen Sink (Wisconsin). Standard comic si

Tells of the genre: hand-lettered covers, drug/sex/politics content, "Adults Only"/"For Adult Intellectuals Only" boxes, no Comics Code seal, cover prices 25¢–$1.50, a publisher name from the list above in the indicia (inside front cover or page 1, bottom).

vanity-dresser-sets.title: Vanity dresser sets , Celluloid Co. and other French ivory celluloid, sterling silver , Art Deco enamel/guilloché, Nippon/Bavaria/Limoges hand-painted porcelain, Apollo Studios, Matson ormolu)
vanity-dresser-sets.full: Vanity dresser sets (DuPont Pyralin / Ivory Pyralin and DuBarry pattern (ex-Arlington Co.), Celluloid Co. and other French ivory celluloid, sterling silver (Gorham, Unger Bros, Kerr, International), Art Deco enamel/guilloché, Nippon/Bavaria/Limoges hand-painted porcelain, Apollo Studios, Matson ormolu)
vanity-dresser-sets.money: Art Nouveau sterling (Unger, Kerr) and guilloché enamel sets $150–600+.
vanity-dresser-sets.fakes: Reproduction Art Nouveau sterling-look sets in plate; new "Victorian" painted porcelain from China; celluloid is rarely faked.
vanity-dresser-sets.buy: Buy sterling repoussé/Art Nouveau dresser pieces at ≤ 30% of comps and complete guilloché enamel sets at ≤ $40; pass on single celluloid items, cracked or amateur-painted porcelain and plated sets.
tells: Sterling: "Sterling" mark, maker hallmarks, repoussé florals, cherubs or Art Nouveau maidens (Unger Bros., William B. Kerr), monograms; hollow handles, often dented.
Celluloid/French ivory (1910s–40s): cream with faux grain lines, often monogrammed; "Ivory Pyralin" or "Du Pont Pyralin" stamped near the handle; smells of camphor when rubbed.
Guilloché enamel (1920s–30s): translucent enamel over engine-turned silver-plate or sterling, often pink, blue, green with painted roses.

victorian-photo-albums.title: Victorian photo albums
victorian-photo-albums.full: Victorian photo albums (celluloid, velvet and musical, 1880–1910)
victorian-photo-albums.money: identified Civil War/occupational/tintype albums, stand-top musicals and mint celluloid $300–800.
victorian-photo-albums.fakes: - Few reproduction albums. Modern prints of tintypes and post-mortem photos are inserted into old albums to raise prices. Check for paper stock, dot-screen printing and magnetic iron in tintypes (general knowledge, verif
victorian-photo-albums.buy: ≤ $40 with a working music box or a clean celluloid cover, or ≤ $50 with ≥ 20 period photos inside; pass worn, torn or empty albums over $50.
tells: Value drivers: the celluloid cover art's condition (no cracks or lifting), a working music box, an intact clasp, and above all the photos still inside. Tintypes, identified people, occupational images, post-mortem, Black Americana and Civil War soldiers add $5
Thick book-form albums with gilt-edged card pages cut to hold cabinet cards and CDVs.
Covers:

vintage-advertising-coolers.title: Vintage advertising coolers
vintage-advertising-coolers.full: Vintage advertising coolers (Coca-Cola, Pepsi, 7Up, Hamm's, Budweiser, Coors, Miller, Snap-on, Mac Tools, Matco, John Deere, NAPA; makers Progress Refrigerator, Cavalier, Hemp, Action Mfg, Poloron, Coleman, Gott, Igloo, Thermos)
vintage-advertising-coolers.money: Cavalier/Westinghouse chest coolers and machines $400–3,000+ (bigger, local).
vintage-advertising-coolers.fakes: Coca-Cola licensed reproduction coolers (1990s–2000s) and modern "retro" coolers. Check for maker stamps, wear, period construction.
vintage-advertising-coolers.buy: Only buy small embossed-metal soda/beer coolers in original paint ≤ 30% of median; plastic tool-truck coolers are too bulky to ship for their value — pass.
tells: 1950s metal soda coolers: embossed "Drink Coca-Cola in Bottles" sides, red paint, galvanized interior, bottle opener on the side, makers Progress Refrigerator (Louisville), Action Mfg, Cronstroms, Acton, Hemp. Small "6-pack" or "picnic" sizes.
Coleman/Thermos/Poloron metal (1950s–70s): painted/plaid, often with brand names.

Plastic promotional (1970s–2000s): Gott, Igloo, Coleman bodies printed with Snap-on, Mac Tools, Matco, Budweiser etc.; Gott made many Snap-on coolers (rounded lid, white top, red body). Fades to pink.

vintage-alarm-clocks.title: Vintage mechanical alarm clocks
vintage-alarm-clocks.full: Vintage mechanical alarm clocks (Westclox, Big Ben, Ingraham, Seth Thomas, Gilbert, New Haven, Lux, Telechron electric, Junghans, Kienzle)
vintage-alarm-clocks.money: novelty/animated (Lux, Mastercrafters, Oswald, Mickey) and early twin-bell $75–300+.
vintage-alarm-clocks.fakes: Modern Chinese "retro" twin-bell alarms; reproduction Mickey Mouse/character clocks, especially Bayard and Ingersoll; replacement printed dials.
vintage-alarm-clocks.buy: Buy only animated/character/novelty alarms or pre-1935 Big Ben variants with clean dials at ≤ 25% of resale; pass on plain 1950s–70s wind-ups and anything not running.

vintage-art-posters.title: Vintage art and event posters
vintage-art-posters.full: Vintage art and event posters (lithographs, screenprints, offset event posters; Mucha/Cappiello-era originals, mid-century travel, Fillmore/rock, museum exhibition, local festival posters)
vintage-art-posters.fakes: Huge: reprints of Mucha, travel posters, rock posters (second/third printings, bootlegs). Reprints often slightly smaller than originals and on bright paper.
vintage-art-posters.buy: Buy only original pre-1970 stone/offset lithographs (linen-backed or with printer credits and folds), first-print concert posters, or travel/airline posters at ≤ 25% of resale; pass on framed modern museum and local festival posters.

vintage-ashtrays.title: Vintage ashtrays
vintage-ashtrays.full: Vintage ashtrays (Snuf-A-Rette/National Porcelain, Shawnee, Fostoria, Higgins, Murano, Bitossi, Fornasetti, Georges Briard, Royal Haeger, Blenko, Lalique, Baccarat, casino/hotel/advertising glass)
vintage-ashtrays.money: Fornasetti, Bitossi Rimini Blu, Lalique, Baccarat, Tiffany silver, Gucci/Hermès $150–1,000+.
vintage-ashtrays.fakes: - Fornasetti is still made today. Modern pieces are marked "Fornasetti Milano Made in Italy" with a current-style label and sell at retail ($150–250 new), so vintage carries only a modest premium. Knock-off "Fornasetti-s
vintage-ashtrays.buy: Buy only designer/maker-signed art ashtrays (Fornasetti print, Higgins gold-signature, large Murano Sommerso, Lalique/Baccarat acid mark) at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on lots of common ceramic, glass, souvenir and onyx ashtrays.
tells: Bitossi / Aldo Londi (Italy): "Rimini Blu" deep blue glaze with incised geometric or fish and face motifs. $100–400.
Lalique: frosted crystal, acid-etched "Lalique France". $150–500. Baccarat: crystal, acid stamp of a circle with decanter, glass and goblet. $100–400+.
Fornasetti (Milan): porcelain with black-and-white transfer prints (Lina Cavalieri face, suns, playing cards, architecture), gold rims, "FORNASETTI MILANO" on the back. $150–600.

vintage-axes.title: Vintage axes
vintage-axes.full: Vintage axes (Plumb, Kelly Works/True Temper, Collins, Mann Edge, Warren Axe, Snow & Nealley, Hults Bruk, Gränsfors, Council Tool, Marbles, Keen Kutter, Winchester)
vintage-axes.money: embossed Kelly "Perfect"/Flint Edge, Keen Kutter, Winchester, Marbles, Snow & Nealley and Hudson Bay axes $80–300+ (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-axes.fakes: Fake etched logos on old heads; ground-in counterfeit "Winchester" stamps. Also (Appraisily): re-stamped heads sold as rare lines; stamp font, order and placement that do not match documented originals; cast heads with m
vintage-axes.buy: Buy only when a maker stamp or embossed logo is visible (Keen Kutter, Winchester, Kelly embossed, Marbles) and price ≤ ~$30 per axe; unmarked rusty heads are a pass.
tells: Pattern shapes: Dayton (flared bit, rounded), Michigan (straighter, squarer cheeks), Jersey (scalloped/lipped edge corners), Hudson Bay (small single-bit "half axe" with a narrow poll and flared bit), boys/cruiser (smaller, 2–2.5 lb heads on 28 in handles, cru

Parts: bit (cutting edge), cheeks (flat sides — where embossed logos and paper labels sit), eye (handle hole — stamps are usually just below or beside it), poll (back/butt; on single bits), haft/handle, wedge in the top of the eye.
Head weight is often stamped (e.g. "3½") and is what buyers ask for first.

vintage-barbie-playsets.title: Vintage Barbie playsets, furniture, cases and accessories
vintage-barbie-playsets.full: Vintage Barbie playsets, furniture, cases and accessories (Mattel, Suzy Goose, SPP/Standard Plastic Products, Arco)
vintage-barbie-playsets.money: boxed 1960s Dream House/Kitchen-Dinette/Cafe/Fashion Shop and cases full of 1959–66 dolls and outfits $200–1,000+
vintage-barbie-playsets.fakes: - Mattel's own "reproduction" vintage dolls and outfits (1990s–2000s collector issues) look vintage — boxes say "reproduction" or have later dates. - Aftermarket reproduction accessories and cases are common; loose piece
vintage-barbie-playsets.buy: Pass on 1980s+ playsets and empty cases; buy cases and lots only when the contents include 1959–67 dolls/outfits, or boxed 1960s playsets, where the sold median clears profit ≥ max($50, price) — and the item fits the passenger seat.
tells: 1959–1967 ("vintage" to collectors): pastel cardboard playsets (Barbie's Dream House 1962, Fashion Shop 1962, Cafe Today), Suzy Goose wooden-look plastic furniture (1962–64: wardrobe, canopy bed, vanity, piano), black or colored vinyl cases with printed art of

1965–1972 ("mod"): Francie, Twist 'N Turn Barbie, Skipper, Tutti; vinyl trunks by SPP (Standard Plastic Products) with mod graphics; Barbie Family House, Country Living House, Barbie's Dream Kitchen-Dinette (1964).

1973–1989 ("superstar"/80s): molded pink/peach plastic: Townhouse (1974), Dream House (1979), Beauty Salon #4839 (1983), Dream Store, Glamour Home, Arco brand playsets (Arco was Mattel-owned, 1980s). Large, bulky, common.

vintage-bicycle-parts.title: Vintage bicycle parts
vintage-bicycle-parts.full: Vintage bicycle parts (Schwinn, Mesinger, Persons, Troxel, Bendix, Stewart-Warner, Campagnolo, Brooks; cruiser, middleweight, Sting-Ray/muscle and road parts)
vintage-bicycle-parts.money: Campagnolo Record groupsets, prewar balloon-tire tanks, lights and horns $150–1,000+.
vintage-bicycle-parts.fakes: - Reproduction Sting-Ray seats, sissy bars, Krate springers, Slik tyres, decals and grips are made in Taiwan and China. They are lighter, with sharper vinyl graphics and no Schwinn date codes. - Schwinn itself reissued t
vintage-bicycle-parts.buy: Buy only Schwinn-marked Krate/Sting-Ray/Phantom parts, Persons/Mesinger springer saddles, Bendix 2-speed hubs, 1950s speedos/tanks and Campagnolo Record, small enough to ship, at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on generic bars, saddles, speedometers and anything needing r
tells: Road bike: Campagnolo Nuovo/Super Record derailleurs, hubs and cranks (the "Campagnolo" script, patent numbers), Brooks Professional saddles (copper rivets, "Brooks Professional" stamp), Cinelli bars and stems, Mafac and Universal brakes.

Schwinn stamps and dates: Schwinn-approved parts carry "Schwinn" on chainrings, cranks, stems, bars, rims ("Schwinn S-7", "S-2") and fenders (some). Handlebars and stems have a two-letter or number date code. Saddles: "Schwinn Approved" with Persons or Mesinge

Sting-Ray / Krate parts (1963–79): "Slik" rear tyre, Solo Polo or "Bucket" banana seats with a Schwinn script, springer forks with a chrome spring, Stik shifter (Shift-Stik) with an orange/red knob, sissy bars, high-rise "ape hanger" bars stamped Schwinn with

vintage-board-games.title: Vintage board games
vintage-board-games.full: Vintage board games (Parker Brothers, Milton Bradley, Selchow & Righter, Ideal, Cadaco, Invicta, Pressman, 3M Bookshelf, Avalon Hill, SPI, TSR, Waddingtons)
vintage-board-games.money: rare (Victorian McLoughlin, early Monopoly, sealed Star Wars/Beatles) $150–1,000+.
vintage-board-games.fakes: Retro reissues (Winning Moves, Target "vintage edition") of Monopoly, Clue, Operation, Mastermind; replica early Monopoly sets; re-shrinkwrapped "sealed" games. Check copyright dates and manufacturer addresses.
vintage-board-games.buy: Buy only complete, unpunched or sealed TV/movie/monster/space games of 1955–85, 3M bookshelf games, early wargames and pre-1940 lithographed games at ≤ $15; pass on Mastermind, Monopoly, Scrabble, Clue, Checkers/travel-game lots and anything missing pieces.

vintage-books.title: Vintage books
vintage-books.full: Vintage books (first editions, illustrated children's books, cookbooks, counterculture paperbacks; publishers incl. Shambhala, World Publishing Rainbow Classics, Grosset & Dunlap, Golden Books, Reilly & Lee)
vintage-books.money: true first editions of key titles, signed copies, early Oz/Big Little Books, rare cookbooks $100–5,000+.
vintage-books.fakes: - Facsimile dust jackets on real firsts, and book-club copies with a real-looking jacket. - Publisher facsimile editions (e.g., Hemingway, Tolkien, Little Golden Books 50th anniversary reprints with "A" in the code). - F
vintage-books.buy: Buy only with a copyright-page photo proving a first printing (or a signature/ inscription) of a title that sells ≥ $100; pass on reprints, book-club editions and anything priced for its age alone.
tells: Book-club editions (BCE): smaller, thinner boards, no price on jacket flap, "Book Club Edition" on flap, a blind-stamped dot or square on the back board. Worth little.
Dust jacket present, with the price on the front flap (not clipped) — required for most modern firsts.
Copyright page — "First Edition", "First Printing", a number line ending in "1", or no later-printing statement. Ask for this photo every time.

vintage-box-and-bakelite-cameras.title: Vintage box and Bakelite cameras
vintage-box-and-bakelite-cameras.full: Vintage box and Bakelite cameras (Kodak Brownie family, Argus, Utility Mfg Falcon/Spartus, Birdseye/Herbert George, Coronet, Purma, Ansco, Agfa, Imperial)
vintage-box-and-bakelite-cameras.money: colored Art Deco Kodaks (Beau Brownie, Petite, Bantam Special), Coronet Midget colors, Kodak Super Six-20 $150–2,500.
vintage-box-and-bakelite-cameras.fakes: - Few fakes in this category. Novelty "Bakelite-look" decor cameras and Lomography/Holga plastic cameras (modern, labeled) are not vintage. - Repainted/recovered cameras sold as original colors — check for overspray in l
vintage-box-and-bakelite-cameras.buy: Almost all box/Bakelite cameras sell under $40 — pass unless the photo shows a colored Art Deco model (Beau Brownie, Coronet Midget color, Kodak Petite/Vanity, Bantam Special, Ensign Midget) priced so the sold median clears profit ≥ max($50, price).
tells: Bakelite is glossy black or brown, heavy for size, with a molded textured pattern and art-deco ribs (Falcon/Spartus/Utility, Kodak Baby Brownie, Purma, Coronet). Colored Bakelite/plastic (green, blue, red, mottled brown) is the valuable exception.

Lens panel text gives the maker: "UTILITY MFG. CO. NEW YORK" (Falcon/Spartus), "BIRDSEYE Flash" (Birdseye Camera Corp./Herbert George, Chicago), "argus" plate + "argoflex" (Argus, Ann Arbor MI), "Brownie"/"Kodak" on the strap or faceplate.

TLR (twin lens) cameras: Argoflex E/EF/EM have two lenses geared together with toothed rings (focusing models); the Argoflex Seventy-Five (1949–58) is a box-shaped TLR with fixed focus; Argoflex Forty (1950–58) similar with flash.

vintage-calendars.title: Vintage calendars
vintage-calendars.full: Vintage calendars (advertising, pin-up, art and gas-station calendars; Brown & Bigelow, Shaw-Barton, Gerlach-Barklow, Thomas D. Murphy Co., Osborne, Hallmark/Coutts)
vintage-calendars.money: Maxfield Parrish Edison-Mazda, Coca-Cola, Hood's and Winchester calendars $400–5,000.
vintage-calendars.fakes: - **Matching-year reissues** (1915/1971, 1931/1987, 1959/2015, and so on). They are sold sealed with poems about the year returning, like the Sybil "1915" reprint. - Coca-Cola, pin-up (Elvgren, Monroe) and Parrish calend
vintage-calendars.buy: Buy only pre-1930 chromolithographed or embossed calendars, or Elvgren/Vargas/Petty/Moran pin-ups, with a complete pad or a clean image, at ≤ 25% of sold value; pass on 1950s+ local-store and greeting-card calendars and on reprints.
tells: 1920s–40s: halftone colour printing, oil-painting prints by named calendar artists (Maxfield Parrish, R. Atkinson Fox, Hy Hintermeister, Philip R. Goodwin, Frances Hook) with the artist's name in the margin.
Pre-1920: chromolithography (rich, grainless colour), embossed die-cut cardboard, a ribbon hanger, often a small pad, ornate Victorian or Art Nouveau framing. The year is printed on the pad.

1950s–60s: photo-litho landscapes and children, the store's name and phone exchange ("Phone 40", "TE 8-") in a block under the picture, and a stapled tear pad. Calendar-maker credit in tiny print: Brown & Bigelow, Shaw-Barton (Coshocton OH), Osborne, Thos. D.

vintage-camera-straps.title: Vintage camera straps
vintage-camera-straps.full: Vintage camera straps (1970s woven hippie straps, Nikon/Canon/Olympus/Leica/Hasselblad OEM, leather makers; Ace = guitar-strap brand)
vintage-camera-straps.money: Leica/Hasselblad leather and rare logos $40–150 (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-camera-straps.fakes: Modern reproductions sold as "vintage style" on Etsy/Amazon; D'Andrea Ace reissue guitar straps; Leica's own new "vintage" straps; aftermarket "for Hasselblad" leather straps.
vintage-camera-straps.buy: pass on single straps; only buy boxes of OEM camera-brand straps (Leica/Hasselblad/Nikon F era) at ≤ $3 each.

vintage-casting-reels.title: Vintage casting reels and tackle lots
vintage-casting-reels.full: Vintage casting reels and tackle lots (level-wind baitcasters, Kentucky reels, glass minnow traps: Pflueger, Shakespeare, Langley, South Bend, Heddon, Meek, Talbot)
vintage-casting-reels.money: early Ambassadeur, Shakespeare President, Kentucky reels (Meek, Milam, Talbot) $150–1,000+.
vintage-casting-reels.fakes: - Reproduction glass minnow traps with "Orvis" embossing exist, and modern Asian casting reels are styled as vintage (general knowledge, verify). - Married parts are common in lots.
vintage-casting-reels.buy: Lots ≤ $6/reel with at least one Pflueger Supreme / Ambassadeur / Heddon visible, or a glass minnow trap ≤ $25; pass modern-lure tackle boxes and sellers who already name the good reels.
tells: The maker is stamped on the foot or end plate: Pflueger (Supreme, Akron, Nobby), Shakespeare (Criterion, Tournament), Langley, South Bend, Penn, Heddon, Ocean City, Bronson.
1930s–70s round-sided metal casting reels with a level-wind bar across the front, knurled end plates, and pearl or black handle knobs.
The Great Lakes Products "Great Lakes" single-action trolling reel is a big spoked aluminium reel.

vintage-cell-phones.title: Vintage cell phones
vintage-cell-phones.full: Vintage cell phones (Motorola DynaTAC/StarTAC/MicroTAC/RAZR, Nokia 8xxx/3310, early Samsung/LG flips, BlackBerry, early iPhone)
vintage-cell-phones.fakes: Refurb/new-housing Nokia 8800 and Vertu fakes; re-housed RAZRs.
vintage-cell-phones.buy: buy only DynaTAC/early Motorola bricks, Nokia 88xx chrome sliders or sealed early iPhones at ≤ $50; common flip lots are untested electronics → pass.

vintage-childrens-clothing.title: Vintage children's clothing
vintage-childrens-clothing.full: Vintage children's clothing (Health-tex, Carter's, OshKosh B'gosh Vestbak, Polly Flinders smocked, Florence Eiseman, Feltman Brothers, Sears Winnie-the-Pooh, Disney/character, handmade crochet and knit)
vintage-childrens-clothing.money: Florence Eiseman, Feltman Bros, Victorian christening gowns $40–200. (Terapeak 365d generic "vintage childrens clothing" median $6.97.)
vintage-childrens-clothing.fakes: Not significant. Brands still in business (OshKosh, Carter's, Florence Eiseman) sell new clothes in classic styles; date by label and origin, not by look.
vintage-childrens-clothing.buy: Pass on handmade crochet and generic kids clothes; buy only lots of labeled Florence Eiseman/Polly Flinders, OshKosh Vestbak, or 1970s character graphics at ≤ $5/piece.

vintage-christmas-decorations.title: Vintage Christmas decorations
vintage-christmas-decorations.full: Vintage Christmas decorations (Shiny Brite, German/Polish blown glass, Dresden, Bradford/Paramount/Noma lights, Union Products and Empire blow molds, Atlantic Mold/Holland Mold ceramic trees, Holt Howard, Hallmark Keepsake)
vintage-christmas-decorations.money: pre-WWII German Dresden, figural glass, Belsnickles, feather trees and candy containers $150–2,000+.
vintage-christmas-decorations.fakes: - Christopher Radko, Inge-Glas and Old World Christmas (1980s–present) make faithful-looking German-style figurals. Read the cap and the box. - Reproduction Belsnickles and feather trees (Bethany Lowe, others) are heavie
vintage-christmas-decorations.buy: Buy only pre-1960 German/Japanese/US glass, Dresden, papier-mâché, feather trees or ceramic trees, at ≤ 25% of sold and in Sep–Nov; pass on 1980s+ craft and resin "Victorian-style" décor, clings, trivets and wreaths.
tells: Belsnickles and papier-mâché Santas, candy containers: chalk/compo faces, mica-flecked coats, German. $200–2,000+.
Pre-1940 German blown-glass figurals (Lauscha): birds with spun-glass tails, fruit, Santas, clip-ons. Paper-thin glass, silvering inside, a pressed metal cap stamped "Germany". $20–300 each.
Dresden ornaments (embossed gilded or silvered cardboard, 1880–1910): $100–1,000+.

vintage-cigarette-lighters.title: Vintage cigarette lighters
vintage-cigarette-lighters.full: Vintage cigarette lighters (Ronson, Dunhill, S.T. Dupont, Evans, Thorens, Zippo, Colibri, Japanese makers)
vintage-cigarette-lighters.money: Dunhill Unique/Sports-Watch, silver or gold-cased pieces $300–1,500+
vintage-cigarette-lighters.fakes: - Japanese copies of Dunhill Rollagas and Dupont sold as "Dunhill-style"; check base marks. - Fake Dupont and Dunhill (Chinese, 2000s) with wrong fonts and no "ping". - Ronson reissue Banjos (Japan, 1980s–90s, gold plate
vintage-cigarette-lighters.buy: Buy only hallmarked silver/gold cases, Dunhill Unique/Dupont/Ronson Banjo at ≤ 30% of sold; pass on chrome Ronson Standards, Evans and Japanese copies unless ≤ $8.
tells: Lift-arm / semi-automatic petrol (1926–1950s): a hinged arm with a snuffer cap that lifts and strikes the flint in one push. Ronson (Art Metal Works, Newark NJ): Banjo (1926, banjo-shaped arm on top), De-Light, Princess, Standard (rectangular body, arm with a

Flip-top gas/petrol (1950s–80s): Dunhill Rollagas (roller wheel, lozenge or barley pattern), S.T. Dupont Ligne 1/2 (a "ping" when opened, lacquer or Chinese lacquer), Colibri, Cartier oval, and many Japanese copies (Gladys, Maruman, Zaima, Crown, Prince) that
Zippo: dated by bottom stamps (dots/slashes, year codes); pre-1950s and military/advertising Zippos are the valuable ones.

vintage-clock-radios.title: Vintage Clock Radios
vintage-clock-radios.full: Vintage Clock Radios (GE, Zenith, Sony, Panasonic, Westclox, Telechron, Magnavox/Philips, Braun, Bang & Olufsen)
vintage-clock-radios.money: space-age flip/digital (Sony Digimatic 8FC, Braun ABR, Panasonic RC-6025 "Groundhog Day" now often $200+) $60–300 (general knowledge, verify). Correction: the Panasonic Toot-a-Loop named in the first version is a bracelet radio, not a clock radio.
vintage-clock-radios.fakes: Retro-styled reissues (Crosley). Fake "world's first flip clock radio" listings exist: one 8FC-59 asked $750 but sold for $3.25 + $34.19 shipping in May 2018 (Flip Clock Fans).
vintage-clock-radios.buy: Buy only tested space-age flip/cube designs and colored 1950s tube sets under ~$30; pass travel clock radios and anything untested.
tells: Flip-number (digital mechanical), 1968–1980 — Copal (Japan) supplied cheap compact flip mechanisms that set off the craze: Copal 201 (1966) started the US flip-clock trend; most makers advertised flip clock radios around 1969 (Flip Clock Fans). Sony 8FC-59 (19
Design pieces, 1970s–80s — Braun ABR 21 "signal radio" (1978, Dieter Rams and Dietrich Lubs; ABS and metal; 11.4 × 18 × 6.5 cm; held by Museum Boijmans), Bang & Olufsen.

Early transistor, mid-1960s — Sony 8RC-44 / 8RC-54 / 8RC-74: solid-state, Telechron movement marked at lower left, walnut-veneer plywood case with acrylic front and chrome trim (8RC-54 from c.1965; 8RC-44 identical but wood-grain face; 8RC-74 more modern facep

vintage-comic-books.title: Vintage comic books
vintage-comic-books.full: Vintage comic books (Golden Age 1938–55, Silver Age 1956–70, Bronze Age 1970–85: Marvel, DC, Dell/Gold Key, Archie, Harvey, Charlton, Classics Illustrated)
vintage-comic-books.money: Silver Age keys and Golden Age books $100–10,000+
vintage-comic-books.fakes: Facsimile editions (2019+ Marvel/DC facsimiles carry "Facsimile Edition" and modern barcodes); Marvel Milestone reprints; 1966 Golden Record ASM #1 reprint; Famous First Edition tabloids; Toys "R" Us/Kellogg's giveaway r
vintage-comic-books.buy: Buy pre-1975 lots at ≤ $2–3 per book when photos show 10¢/12¢ cover prices and DC/Marvel superhero titles, or any lot with an identifiable key at ≤ 30% of raw value; pass on 1985+ commons, dealer stock with placeholder prices, and any key needing a CGC grade t

vintage-denim.title: Vintage denim
vintage-denim.full: Vintage denim (Levi's, Lee, Wrangler, Big Yank, Sears Roebucks/Hercules, JCPenney Big Mac/Foremost, Montgomery Ward Powr House, Big E, Carhartt, Osh Kosh)
vintage-denim.money: Big E (pre-1971) Levi's jeans and type 1–3 jackets, 1950s chore/work denim $250–3,000+.
vintage-denim.fakes: Levi's Vintage Clothing (LVC) and Japanese repro brands (Warehouse, Studio D'Artisan) copy Big E details; they are legitimately valuable but must not be sold as vintage. LVC tags read "Levi's Vintage Clothing" and have m
vintage-denim.buy: Buy jeans/jackets with a capital-E red tab, selvedge (redline) outseam, single-stitch back pockets or a "Made in USA" care tag from the 1960s–80s at ≤ $25; pass on paper-patch 2000s 501s, women's, stretch and modern "vintage-style" pieces.
tells: Red tab: "LEVI'S" with capital E = pre-1971 ("Big E"). Small "e" = 1971 onward.
Selvedge: turn up a cuff; a clean white edge with a red line ("redline") on the outseam = pre-~1985 Levi's.

Jackets: Levi's type 1 (one pocket, cinch back, 506XX), type 2 (two pleated pockets, 507XX), type 3 (V-shaped seams, 557XX, 70505 with small e); Lee 101-J (zig-zag stitch, side pleats), Wrangler 11MJ/24MJZ.

vintage-disney-collectibles.title: Vintage Disney collectibles
vintage-disney-collectibles.full: Vintage Disney collectibles (Walt Disney Productions-era toys and souvenirs: Gund, Knickerbocker, Hasbro, Marx, Ingersoll/US Time, Disneyland park souvenirs; later Disney Store, Poliwoggs, WDCC; Disney purses/bags)
vintage-disney-collectibles.money: 1930s–50s toys, early park ephemera and production cels $100–50,000.
vintage-disney-collectibles.fakes: - 1970s–90s reproductions of 1930s Mickey toys (Schmid music boxes, Mickey "vintage style" tin) and Chinese pie-eyed fakes. - Disney Store "vintage style" re-releases (e.g., 2000s Mickey retro plush). - Fake Dooney & Bou
vintage-disney-collectibles.buy: Buy only items marked "Walt Disney Productions" or "© Walt Disney" (pre-1986) or 1930s–50s licensed toys, in good condition, at ≤ 20% of sold median; pass on all "The Walt Disney Company"/Disney Store-era goods.
tells: "© Walt Disney Enterprises" (1930s–1939) and "© Walt Disney Productions" (1939–1986) = vintage. "WDP" on small items.
"© Disney" and "The Walt Disney Company" (1986–) = modern; mostly retail-or-less.

vintage-electric-clocks.title: Vintage electric clocks
vintage-electric-clocks.full: Vintage electric clocks (General Electric/Telechron, Westclox, Sessions, United Clock, Lanshire, Hamilton, Seth Thomas, Herman Miller/George Nelson, Spartus, Mastercrafters, Kirsch, Lux/Robertshaw)
vintage-electric-clocks.money: MCM designer (George Nelson/Howard Miller ball, sunburst, Eye, Spike) $250–1,500.
vintage-electric-clocks.fakes: George Nelson designs are reissued (Vitra) and knocked off (cheap Chinese copies on Amazon). Originals: Howard Miller label, wooden ball tips painted, brass/steel spokes, AC motor. Kit-Cat reissued continuously since 196
vintage-electric-clocks.buy: Buy working Nelson/Howard Miller designs and working motion clocks ≤ 30% of median; pass on plastic kitchen clocks and common figural clocks unless ≤ $10.
tells: Howard Miller / George Nelson designs (1949–1960s): Ball clock, Sunburst, Asterisk, Spike, Eye, Kite. Paper/foil Howard Miller label and Kienzle or GE movements. Vitra reissues since 1999.
MCM starburst (Welby, Elgin, Verichron, Syroco): wood/brass starburst wall clocks, many battery-converted.
Telechron / GE: "Telechron" or "GE" logo on dial, red second hand (Telechron trademark), Bakelite or Catalin cases (Deco), later plastic. Model numbers on bottom/back (e.g. 2H07, 7H241, 2130KA).

vintage-electric-fans.title: Vintage electric fans
vintage-electric-fans.full: Vintage electric fans (Vornado, Emerson, GE, Westinghouse, Robbins & Myers, Hunter/Century, Manning Bowman, Lasko)
vintage-electric-fans.money: restored colour Vornado, Emerson 6-blade brass, Westinghouse "Tank", Marelli/Jandus $300–800.
vintage-electric-fans.fakes: - Modern "retro" brass-look fans and Vornado reissues are sold as vintage. The tells are plastic parts, UL labels and a light weight (general knowledge, verify). - Vornado's own reproduction "vintage" circulators and Sil
vintage-electric-fans.buy: Working Vornado ≤ $40 or working brass-blade Emerson/GE ≤ $60; pass "doesn't work" (repair) and steel 1950s+ fans over $15.
tells: Emerson/GE/Westinghouse 1910s–30s: brass blades, brass cage, cast-iron base. Six-blade brass Emersons are the top tier; read the blade count from the model number (see below), not from the seller's title.
Westinghouse "Tank": a heavy, rounded cast-iron motor housing with brass blades and cage on a cast-iron foot (e.g. 12" style 60677 sold as a brass-blade "Tank").

1930s–50s Art Deco fans: stamped-steel bases, aluminum or Micarta blades, concentric-ring steel cages (Westinghouse, GE Vortalex, Emerson 77 series, Hunter Zephair, Wade-Youman Chrom-Ever bullet-back 1948–52).

vintage-eyeglasses.title: Vintage eyeglasses and spectacles
vintage-eyeglasses.full: Vintage eyeglasses and spectacles (American Optical, Bausch & Lomb, Shuron, Ray-Ban, Algha, Bonschott)
vintage-eyeglasses.money: 18th–19th c. coin-silver/solid gold or rare scissors/lorgnettes $100–600
vintage-eyeglasses.fakes: Modern repro "vintage" round frames (Chinese wire frames, Savile Row reissues, AO reissues) look similar; tell by modern hinges, laser engraving, clean screws. Stamped 12K GF is period-consistent. Further: red flags (App
vintage-eyeglasses.buy: Buy solid-gold (10k/14k stamped), coin-silver, early B&L Ray-Ban, or round 12K GF frames with 46–48mm eyes ≤ $20; typical gold-filled pairs are pass above $25.
tells: Sliding/telescopic temples (inner rod adjusts length): early 19th century.
Riding-bow (cable) temples: strongest 1890s–1930s; their presence rules out an 18th-century date.
Pince-nez: 1870s–1890s rise; C-bridge types c. 1880–1910, fingerpiece types c. 1890–1915.

vintage-fire-helmets.title: Vintage fire helmets
vintage-fire-helmets.full: Vintage fire helmets (Cairns & Brother leather "New Yorker"/"Senior", Cairns aluminum and composite; E.D. Bullard "Hard Boiled" fiberglass and aluminum; MSA Topgard/Cairns; Morning Pride; leather fronts/shields)
vintage-fire-helmets.money: 19th-c. leather parade/eagle helmets and named-company provenance $500–3,000.
vintage-fire-helmets.fakes: - Reproduction parade helmets, decorative frontpieces and fake "FDNY" shields exist; brass eagles reproduced. - Married pieces: genuine helmet with a reproduction or later eagle/shield; check fasteners and patina match.
vintage-fire-helmets.buy: Buy only leather Cairns/early leather helmets with eagle and shield at ≤ $100 (resale ≥ $300); pass on fiberglass Bullards above ~$20.
tells: Leather (Cairns & Brother; Gratacap design, 1836 onward): 4, 8, 12, 14 or 16 combs (ribs) on the crown, long rear brim ("duck tail"), brass eagle or beaver frontpiece holder, leather shield with company number. Inside: Cairns stamped label or maker's plate. Ha
"Solid top" leather (1940s Cairns): smooth crown, short brim all round instead of the long tail; frontpiece fixed with nails.
Aluminum (1930s–60s): pressed metal with combs; Cairns, Bullard, MSA; conductive (discontinued).

vintage-fishing-lures.title: Vintage fishing lures
vintage-fishing-lures.full: Vintage fishing lures (Creek Chub, Heddon, Pflueger, South Bend, Shakespeare, Paw Paw, Arbogast)
vintage-fishing-lures.money: Boxed Creek Chub / Heddon / Pflueger $30–150 each
vintage-fishing-lures.fakes: - Heddon and Creek Chub reissued classic lures (including "Classic" lines). Modern repaints and "folk art" reproductions with aged finishes exist. Reproduction boxes too (general knowledge, verify). - Repaint/fake tells
vintage-fishing-lures.buy: Lots only if boxes or glass-eye wooden lures are visible.
tells: Look-alikes: modern "folk art" carved decor lures and resin decorative lures sold in home-decor shops; modern "Classic" reissues by Heddon/Creek Chub.

Painted wooden plugs (1900s–1950s) with glass eyes, cup-and-screw hook hardware, and maker boxes (two-piece cardboard, sometimes with the lure's catalogue number). Later lures are plastic (1950s+) with painted or tack eyes (general knowledge, verify).
Tackle-box lots: most contents are modern plastic (Rapala, Rebel, Beetle Spin) at $1–3 each.

vintage-fishing-reels.title: Vintage fishing reels and bamboo rods
vintage-fishing-reels.full: Vintage fishing reels (casting, spinning, saltwater) and bamboo rods (Pflueger, ABU Ambassadeur, Penn, Newell, Shimano, Tiburon, Vom Hofe, Meek, Montague, South Bend, Heddon)
vintage-fishing-reels.money: Vom Hofe, Meek, Talbot, Hardy Perfect, Penn International 130 $500–3,000.
vintage-fishing-reels.fakes: - ABU reissued "Record" and "Classic" Ambassadeurs. Asian-made rods carry fake decals. Married reel parts are common (general knowledge, verify).
vintage-fishing-reels.buy: Lots with a visible Ambassadeur/Penn Senator/Newell under $30; complete Montague/South Bend bamboo in tube under $40; pass per-reel market pricing and rod "ends".
tells: Antique brass and German-silver reels (pre-1910: Meek, Milam, Talbot, Vom Hofe) are the top tier ($300–3,000).
Penn (Senator 4/0–12/0 $60–200; International gold lever drags $150–500)
Casting (level-wind) reels:

vintage-football-helmets.title: Vintage football helmets
vintage-football-helmets.full: Vintage football helmets (Spalding, Rawlings, Wilson, MacGregor/Goldsmith, Riddell, Hutch, Reach, Draper-Maynard, Nokona)
vintage-football-helmets.money: documented pro/college game-used or team-decaled pro shells $1,000–5,000+.
vintage-football-helmets.fakes: - Modern Chinese and Pakistani "vintage leather football helmets" sold as decor: perfectly even stitching, bright tan or brown leather, polyester lining, no or crude stamp, no wear inside. - Riddell and others make throw
vintage-football-helmets.buy: Buy maker-stamped ADULT leather helmets or pre-1960 plastic suspension shells at ≤ $40 (≤ $75 for dog-ear/flat-top); pass youth sizes, Sears/Ward's store brands, repros and anything cracked.
tells: Leather era (c.1895–1949). Flat-top / "beehive" (1910s–early 20s: soft leather segments meeting in a flat or pinched crown, no ear holes); dog-ear (1920s: leather ear flaps that stick out sideways, often with a separate chin strap); wing / winged-front (1930s:

Early plastic (1939–early 1960s). Riddell patented the first plastic suspension helmet in 1939; wartime shortages kept leather alive until c.1949. 1940s–early 50s plastic shells often have a leather or vinyl edge binding stitched around the rim, a rolled leath
Facemask era (1955+). Single or double bar masks bolted through the shell. Holes at the front sides or brow = mask was fitted at some point.

vintage-fountain-pens.title: Vintage Fountain Pens
vintage-fountain-pens.full: Vintage Fountain Pens (Parker, Sheaffer, Waterman, Conway Stewart, Montblanc, Pelikan, Wahl-Eversharp, Esterbrook)
vintage-fountain-pens.money: gold-filled/solid gold, celluloid jade/pearl, restored Sheaffer Balance oversize (~$250), Montblanc 149 $150–600+
vintage-fountain-pens.fakes: Montblanc fakes common; Chinese 51 clones (Hero 616) — check "PARKER 51 MADE IN USA" on barrel. 2001 Parker 51 Special Edition is a legitimate reissue that differs from originals. Married caps and barrels are common.
vintage-fountain-pens.buy: Buy Parker 51/Vacumatic, Sheaffer Snorkel/Balance, Wahl Doric and gold/celluloid pens under ~$15–30; pass cartridge pens; Montblanc requires authentication (excluded).

vintage-fur-coats.title: Vintage fur coats and stoles
vintage-fur-coats.full: Vintage fur coats and stoles (mink, fox, sable, marten, Persian lamb, beaver, raccoon, chinchilla; faux fur by Borgana, Glenoit, Collins & Aikman, Tissavel, Sasson, Dan Coma)
vintage-fur-coats.fakes: Faux sold as real (and vice-versa): check backing with a pin — real fur has leather; faux has fabric. Dyed rabbit sold as mink/chinchilla; dyed muskrat sold as "Hudson seal". Use the FTC-required label (post-1952) that n
vintage-fur-coats.buy: Only buy full-length female mink (light ranch, pastel, blackglama) or sable/lynx/chinchilla in good leather at ≤ $60 with seller confirmation the hide is supple; pass on stoles, Persian lamb, rabbit and most faux.
tells: Mink: short dense glossy guard hair, visible vertical "let-out" stripes on full coats (narrow strips sewn diagonally). Colors: ranch (dark brown), mahogany, pastel (light brown), tourmaline/silver-blue, black (Blackglama). Female pelts are softer and lighter.
Critter/animal stoles: whole pelts with heads, feet and tails, clip-mouths joined in a chain (usually 2–6 mink, marten or sable), 1930s–50s.

Fox: long fluffy guard hair (red, silver, blue, white, crystal). Sable: long, silky, brown with silver hairs. Marten: like sable but coarser, slightly longer, often with buff throat patch. Persian lamb (karakul): tight curled black or brown, low value. Raccoon

vintage-globes.title: Vintage globes
vintage-globes.full: Vintage globes (George F. Cram, Replogle, Rand McNally, Weber Costello, Hammond, Denoyer-Geppert, Nystrom, C.S. Hammond, Chad Valley/J. Chein tin globes, Ohio Art; 19th c. Schedler, Merriam Moore, Gilman Joslin)
vintage-globes.fakes: "Antique-look" modern globes (Replogle Heirloom, imports) with parchment ocean and old-style typography look antique but contain modern borders. Reproduction 18th c. globes (Smith's, Cary) sold as decor. Over-labelled gl
vintage-globes.buy: Pass on post-1960 12 in. desk globes; buy only pre-1940 globes (check borders: "Persia", "Siam", "Indo-China", "Austria-Hungary") or tin globes ≤ $30 that fit the seat.

vintage-handkerchiefs.title: Vintage handkerchiefs
vintage-handkerchiefs.full: Vintage handkerchiefs (Tammis Keefe / "Peg Thomas" for J.H. Kimball, Burmel, Pat Prichard, Carol Stanley, Faith Austin, Franshaw, Jeanne Hamm; souvenir World's Fair hankies; Irish/Swiss linen and lace; Appenzell embroidery; Marghab Madeira linens)
vintage-handkerchiefs.fakes: - Few; modern Chinese reprints of 1950s designs exist. - Keefe prints were reissued as fabric yardage (Michael Miller, 2013); items cut and hemmed from yardage are not period hankies (machine hems, no aged fold lines). -
vintage-handkerchiefs.buy: Buy only large lots with signed designer prints, souvenir/World's Fair or fine lace at ≤ $2/hanky, or single standouts at ≤ 1/3 resale; small mixed lots of 5 never clear $50.
tells: Whitework/lace: white or ecru linen with drawn-thread work, embroidered initials, needle or bobbin lace borders (Brussels/Belgian, Irish, Appenzell from Switzerland), often a wedding hanky.

Marghab: very fine hand-embroidered Irish linen or "Margandie" (Swiss organdy) worked on Madeira, 1933–1980 (Wikipedia). Look for minute, dense satin stitch and shadow-work; Marghab pieces are often found with paper labels or stamped tags (marking method not c
Cotton, linen or silk squares, 10–16 in. Collectible eras: 1930s–1960s printed cottons and linens, plus earlier (pre-1930) fine whitework and lace.

vintage-hat-boxes.title: Vintage hat boxes – milliner, luggage and travel hat cases
vintage-hat-boxes.full: Vintage hat boxes – milliner, luggage and travel hat cases (Lady Baltimore, Samsonite, Amelia Earhart, Hartmann, Oshkosh, Neiman Marcus/Stetson/Dobbs/Knox store boxes)
vintage-hat-boxes.money: 19th-century wallpaper bandboxes and Hermès/Louis Vuitton/Goyard hat boxes $300–5,000+ (authentication).
vintage-hat-boxes.fakes: Modern decorative hat boxes (Lierys, home-decor nesting boxes) are common and cheap. Luxury-brand hat boxes are faked; never buy without authentication.
vintage-hat-boxes.buy: Buy only 19th-c. wallpaper bandboxes or early leather cases under $40; ordinary 1950s–60s vinyl round cases are pass above ~$15.

vintage-home-computers.title: Vintage home computers
vintage-home-computers.full: Vintage home computers (Apple, Commodore, Radio Shack/Tandy TRS-80, Atari, TI, Amiga, IBM)
vintage-home-computers.fakes: Few outright fakes for common machines. Modern reissues/remakes exist (TheC64, Commodore 64 Ultimate-style reproductions, Apple-1 replicas) — check model labels and date codes. Married boxes (a box from a different unit)
vintage-home-computers.buy: Buy Apple II family, Amiga, SX-64 or Model 100 shown working under $100; pass MC-10, TI-99, Atari 400/800XL, VIC-20 and anything untested.

vintage-kitchen-gadgets.title: Vintage kitchen gadgets
vintage-kitchen-gadgets.full: Vintage kitchen gadgets (Androck, A&J / Ekco, Foley, Edlund, Taylor, Robinson Knife Co., Tupperware, Pyrex accessories, Nutbrown, Bromwell, Wear-Ever, Mirro, Rival, Vaughan, Dazey)
vintage-kitchen-gadgets.money: patent-era 1850s–1900 apple parers and rare cast iron $100–400.
vintage-kitchen-gadgets.fakes: Cast-iron apple parers and cherry pitters have been reproduced (lighter, rough casting, no patent dates). Retro "Bakelite-look" plastic utensils sold at craft stores (2000s). Modern "farmhouse" enamel/wood utensils marke
vintage-kitchen-gadgets.buy: Pass carded modern gadgets and mixed utensil drawers; buy only matched 1930s–50s Bakelite/painted-handle sets in original box, or 19th-century cast-iron patent parers/pitters/beaters with legible patent dates, at ≤ 25% of the ladder.
tells: Bakelite/catalin handles (1930s–50s): red, green, butterscotch, cream; slightly translucent edges, heavier; often with a painted "stripe" (Androck, A&J). Plastic 1960s+ handles are lighter, uniform colour, moulded seams.
Painted wood handles (1920s–50s): red/green/blue/yellow paint with a cream band, often chipped.

Cast iron mechanisms (1850–1920): apple parers (Reading Hardware, Goodell "White Mountain", Lockey & Howland), cherry stoners (Enterprise Mfg Philadelphia), Dover egg beaters ("Dover Stamping Co. Boston, Pat. May 31 1870") – raised patent dates in the casting.

vintage-kitchen-glassware.title: Vintage kitchen glassware
vintage-kitchen-glassware.full: Vintage kitchen glassware (Pyrex, Fire-King, Glasbake, Anchor Hocking, Federal, Hazel-Atlas, Jeannette, Indiana Glass/Tiara, Jadeite, Depression glass)
vintage-kitchen-glassware.money: rare Pyrex promos (Lucky in Love, Atomic Eyes turquoise, Pink Daisy promos), Jadeite rarities, Depression glass rarities $200–6,000.
vintage-kitchen-glassware.fakes: - Jadeite is heavily reproduced (1990s–present Chinese "Jadeite" and Martha Stewart/Fire-King reissues). Old Fire-King has the anchor-and-"Fire-King Oven Ware" mark. Modern reissues say "Fire-King" in new fonts or nothin
vintage-kitchen-glassware.buy: Buy only rare Pyrex patterns and promos, complete primary-colour or pink Pyrex sets, Jadeite (genuine, Fire-King/Jeannette marked or restaurant-ware), and Depression-glass rarities at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on clear pressed glass, Glasbake, amber Tiara/Indiana an
tells: Rare promos: Lucky in Love (hearts and shamrocks, 1959 promo, $1,000–6,000), Atomic Eyes 1950s promos, Pink Gooseberry with gold, "Hex Signs", the turquoise Cinderella "Star" promos.
Good: Primary colours (blue/red/green/yellow) bowls set, Butterprint (turquoise Amish), Gooseberry (pink/black), Pink Daisy, Snowflake Garland, Pink Stems, Atomic Eyes, Friendship.

Depression glass (1920s–40s): pressed, thin, mould-made colours (pink, green, amber, cobalt). Makers Hazel-Atlas, Federal, Jeannette, Anchor Hocking, Indiana, Hocking, U.S. Glass. Rare patterns and colours (Royal Lace cobalt, Mayfair blue) sell high. Most piec

vintage-kites.title: Vintage Kites
vintage-kites.full: Vintage Kites (Hi-Flier, Gayla, TopFlite, Alox, Go Fly a Kite, Spectra Star, Peter Powell, Hayes, Shaw Creations; advertising paper kites)
vintage-kites.money: TopFlite "Man in the Moon" cited at $300+ (Junkbox, anecdotal) (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-kites.fakes: Hi-Flier reproductions are said to exist (old entry; not confirmed by the sources consulted — verify). Post-1981 licensed "Hi-Flier"-branded toys and Estes-era kites are not Decatur production. Modern "vintage style" pap
vintage-kites.buy: Buy unopened 1950s–70s Hi-Flier paper advertising/character kites (or barn-door/box kites) under ~$20; pass modern nylon kites.

vintage-luggage.title: Vintage luggage
vintage-luggage.full: Vintage luggage (Samsonite/Shwayder Bros, Hartmann, Lady Baltimore, American Tourister, Amelia Earhart, Skyway, Herculyte, Mark Cross, Crouch & Fitzgerald, Louis Vuitton, Goyard, genuine alligator cases)
vintage-luggage.money: genuine alligator, LV/Goyard/Hermès and rare sets $200–2,500.
vintage-luggage.fakes: - Embossed "faux alligator" cowhide and leatherette is far more common than genuine alligator (underpricedai: faux-gator train cases median $41). - Louis Vuitton and Goyard fakes are everywhere: a reason to stay out. - M
vintage-luggage.buy: Only genuine alligator, Hartmann belting-leather, or luxury-maker luggage at ≤ 30% of sold median, small enough (≤ 24") for a sensible shipping box; pass on all vinyl hardshells, decorated or altered cases and soft floral bags.
tells: Vinyl over board: textured basket-weave or "cross-hatch" vinyl, piping on the edges, script metal nameplates (Lady Baltimore, Amelia Earhart), satin or pleated linings.
Samsonite (Shwayder Bros, Denver): tan, brown or two-tone, with "Samsonite" logo plates and pleated rayon linings. A wardrobe hanger bar in the lid = 1940s–50s Streamlite-era.
Hartmann: tweed with leather trim, or belting leather (thick saddle-tan leather, heavy brass, white-stitched corners).

vintage-lunch-boxes.title: Lunch boxes
vintage-lunch-boxes.full: Lunch boxes (metal 1950s–80s, vinyl, 1990s character) (Aladdin, Thermos/King-Seeley Thermos, ADCO Liberty, Ohio Art)
vintage-lunch-boxes.fakes: Licensed reproductions and later reissues exist (e.g. 1990s–2000s retro tin boxes of Star Wars, Beatles, Hopalong Cassidy; Vandor and similar novelty tins) — they lack the period maker mark and have modern copyright line
vintage-lunch-boxes.buy: Buy 1950s–60s metal with thermos under $60 or 1960s vinyl under $25; pass 1990s boxes at any price.

vintage-magazines.title: Vintage magazines
vintage-magazines.full: Vintage magazines (Life, Look, Saturday Evening Post, Playboy, National Geographic, TV Guide, Rolling Stone, Mad, Highlights, Barbie, Seventeen, Vogue, Harper's Bazaar, Popular Mechanics, pulp and comic-adjacent titles)
vintage-magazines.money: pulps, Playboy Dec 1953 and true first issues $100–5,000+.
vintage-magazines.fakes: Facsimile reprints of Playboy #1, Life moon issues, Action/Superman-related magazines; "commemorative" reissues.
vintage-magazines.buy: Buy only key-cover issues (first issues, celebrity/event covers, Famous Monsters, early Rolling Stone, 1940s–60s fashion with Avedon/Penn, pulps) at ≤ $10 each or big lots at ≤ $1 per issue with keys; pass on National Geographic, Reader's Digest, Highlights an

vintage-marbles.title: Vintage marbles
vintage-marbles.full: Vintage marbles (jar lots, machine-made and handmade) (Akro Agate, Peltier, Christensen Agate, Marble King, Vitro, Master, German handmade)
vintage-marbles.fakes: Modern contemporary handmade marbles and Chinese reproductions of German swirls/sulphides exist; reproduction sulphides often have crude figures and bubbles; new Akro-colour repros exist (general knowledge, verify).
vintage-marbles.buy: Buy pre-1970 machine-made ≤ $15/quart or visible pontil/sulphide lots ≤ $50; pass cat's-eye lots and $30+/quart.

vintage-medical-charts.title: Vintage medical, anatomical and acupuncture charts
vintage-medical-charts.full: Vintage medical, anatomical and acupuncture charts (Denoyer-Geppert, A.J. Nystrom / Frohse, Jung-Koch-Quentell, Hagemann, Iokai Shiatsu/Masunaga, Chinese acupuncture charts, pharma posters)
vintage-medical-charts.money: 19th-c. lithographed charts and German Jung-Koch-Quentell $200–800 (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-medical-charts.fakes: Many reprint posters of vintage anatomical art; check for halftone dots and modern paper. Also: canvas giclée prints of JKQ and Frohse images sold as "vintage school chart"; publishers' own later reissues (Nystrom and D-
vintage-medical-charts.buy: buy only canvas/linen-backed pull-down school charts or pre-1950 lithographs at ≤ $60; paper posters and 1970s shiatsu charts are a pass.

vintage-medical-equipment.title: Vintage medical equipment
vintage-medical-equipment.full: Vintage medical equipment (resuscitators, quack/electro-therapy devices, instruments, sterilizers, apothecary items; Hudson, Stephenson Minuteman, E&J, Burdick, Welch Allyn, Bausch & Lomb, Sharp & Smith, Kny-Scheerer, Violet Ray makers)
vintage-medical-equipment.fakes: "Civil War surgeon's kits" are assembled and faked frequently; cases from India with new instruments. Mid-century resuscitators are not faked. Married sets: compare fonts, handles and ferrules across instruments; matchin
vintage-medical-equipment.buy: Pass empty mid-century cases; buy only complete cased pre-1900 instrument sets with ebony/ivory handles or boxed violet-ray kits under 25% of comps; no electrical testing promises.
tells: Portable resuscitators: a case (often red, green or grey) with one or two small oxygen cylinders, a regulator/gauge, hoses, face masks and airways. The Stephenson Minuteman Mk 2 in Museum Wales is a 1970s red-cased unit about 24 × 63 × 19 cm and 7.65 kg (made

Violet ray kits: a fitted box (often leatherette) with a bakelite or hard-rubber hand unit holding the high-voltage coil, and several evacuated glass electrodes of different shapes (comb, surface, nasal, rectal/throat); some have a separate control box.

Surgical sets: brass-bound mahogany (or rosewood) case with fitted, velvet- or plush-lined compartments, often a brass cartouche on the lid and a maker's label inside; instruments include saws, amputation knives, tourniquet, bone forceps, trephines.

vintage-microphones.title: Vintage microphones
vintage-microphones.full: Vintage microphones (Shure, Electro-Voice, Turner, Astatic, RCA, American, Altec)
vintage-microphones.money: RCA 44/77 ribbons and Shure 55 "fatboy" $300–3,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-microphones.fakes: Decorative "vintage-style" chrome mics (Chinese prop microphones shaped like Shure 55 or RCA 77) sell $15–40; Shure's current 55SH Series II is a modern reissue ($100). Check for real nameplate, weight, and connector. -
vintage-microphones.buy: Pass on chipped common ham/PA mics; buy Shure 55/556/5575, EV 630/950/951 or RCA ribbon shapes at ≤ $60 where the shape is unmistakable.
tells: Look-alikes: decorative chrome "vintage-style" prop mics (Shure 55 and RCA 77 shapes), theatre props built as RCA 44 shells (plastic, hiding a wireless transmitter; VCU prop article), Bakelite telephone mouthpieces on rods, Kellogg candlestick telephone transm

Correction/nuance on the Shure 55 nicknames: the large original Model 55 (1939–1952) is the "Fatboy"; the smaller 55S (from 1951) is the one called the "Elvis" mic (ProSoundWeb). The head shape is similar; size and base differ. The Fatboy 55B is about 7.7 × 3.

Connector tells for age: early Shure 55s use a three-pin Amphenol-type connector; later bases have a built-in XLR (ProSoundWeb). Early JT-30s use the 5/8" Amphenol/Switchcraft screw-on "button" connector; later ones XLR (BluesHarmonica).

vintage-microscopes.title: Vintage microscopes
vintage-microscopes.full: Vintage microscopes (Bausch & Lomb, Spencer / American Optical, Leitz, Zeiss, Nikon, Olympus, Swift, Unitron, Japanese student scopes)
vintage-microscopes.money: named-maker brass in fitted box $500–3,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-microscopes.fakes: Indian/Pakistani polished-brass decorator microscopes ("antique brass microscope with wooden box") are everywhere; tell: no maker/serial, crude threads, 1 non-working lens, very shiny brass, case with brass corners and r
vintage-microscopes.buy: Buy only brass/lacquered pre-1920 stands or Leitz/Zeiss/B&L black-enamel stands with fitted wood case at ≤ $60; black-crackle student scopes are a pass.

vintage-minnow-buckets.title: Vintage minnow buckets
vintage-minnow-buckets.full: Vintage minnow buckets (bait buckets; Old Pal / Woodstream, Frabill, Falls City, Planet, Bill DeWitt, Thermos "Stay-Alive")
vintage-minnow-buckets.fakes: Decorative "vintage-style" galvanized buckets are sold as decor. Not common fakes. Converted buckets (hanging lights, planters) are sometimes listed as vintage — drill holes reduce collector value.
vintage-minnow-buckets.buy: Pass on 1960s+ Old Pal/Frabill; buy only pre-war buckets with bright original paint graphics at ≤ $20.
tells: Old Pal (Woodstream Corp., Lititz PA): red/orange "OLD PAL" lettering on galvanized steel, 1950s–80s; sizes 6, 8, 10 qt; "Floating Minnow Bucket".
Frabill (Milwaukee): green or galvanized buckets with "Frabill" logo, 1940s–80s.
Falls City (Louisville) and Planet: early, often painted green with gold stencilling.

vintage-nerf-toys.title: Vintage Nerf Toys
vintage-nerf-toys.full: Vintage Nerf Toys (Parker Brothers 1969–c.1987, Kenner c.1987–1990s, OddzOn/Larami 1990s, Hasbro)
vintage-nerf-toys.money: early blasters (1989–93 Blast-a-Ball, Bow 'n' Arrow, Sharpshooter, Arrowstorm) $50–250 (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-nerf-toys.fakes: Hasbro retro reissues (2010s–2020s "Nerf Retro" boomerang) — check date/box. Hasbro Pulse has sold retro reissues of early blasters (e.g. a listing titled "Nerf Sharp92 Retro Blaster", a nod to the 1992 Sharpshooter); re
vintage-nerf-toys.buy: Buy boxed/sealed Parker Brothers Nerf and complete early-1990s blasters under ~$25; pass loose foam.
tells: Blasters (1989 onward) — 1989 Blast-a-Ball (a two-player ball-blaster game set, invented by Reyn Guyer), 1990 Blast-a-Matic, 1991 Bow 'n' Arrow, 1992 Sharpshooter (the first dart blaster), Master Blaster, Missilestorm, Missile Launcher, NB-1 Missile Blaster, S

Foam balls and sports toys (1970–1980s) — the 1970 Nerf ball (sold as the "world's first official indoor ball"), Super Nerf Ball, 1972 Nerfoop indoor basketball and the Nerf football, later the boomerang (1983) and Turbo football. Sold in boxes or blister card

vintage-paperbacks.title: Vintage paperbacks
vintage-paperbacks.full: Vintage paperbacks (Signet, Bantam, Pocket Books, Ace, Avon, Dell, Popular Library, Perma Books — 1940s–60s)
vintage-paperbacks.money: Pocket Books #1–10, fine Dell mapbacks $200+ (Fleming UK hardcover firsts reach $5,000+).
vintage-paperbacks.fakes: Facsimile reprints and later printings with the same cover art are the main issue — check the printing line and cover price rather than the artwork (general knowledge, verify).
vintage-paperbacks.buy: Buy 1st-printing or pre-1955 pulps in VG at ≤ $3/book; pass 1960s reprint runs priced ≥ $50.

vintage-patches.title: Vintage patches
vintage-patches.full: Vintage patches (Boy Scouts of America / Scouts Canada, Order of the Arrow, military and NASA mission patches, snowmobile/motorcycle brands, Presidential Physical Fitness, Cub Scouts, oil company, gas station, rock band)
vintage-patches.money: rare OA and WWII Disney-designed squadron patches $200–2,000+.
vintage-patches.fakes: Rampant for WWII squadron, NASA, OA and Harley patches; reissues of jamboree patches. Military and OA rarities require collector authentication: outside Dylan's rules.
vintage-patches.buy: Buy large mixed lots (50+) at ≤ $0.50 each, or single early OA flaps, pre-1960 jamboree, WWII squadron and 1960s snowmobile/racing brand patches at ≤ 25% of comps; pass on small lots of common scout and Presidential Fitness patches.
tells: Twill/felt base with fully embroidered surface: 1960s onward (fully embroidered = 1970s+ mostly).
Cut edge vs rolled (merrowed) edge: cut-edge twill = generally pre-1970; merrowed (overlocked) edge = 1970s+.
Back: plastic/glue backing = 1980s+; gauze/cheesecloth = older; no backing on chain-stitch felt = 1930s–50s.

vintage-perfume-bottles.title: Vintage perfume bottles
vintage-perfume-bottles.full: Vintage perfume bottles (Lanvin, Guerlain, Chanel, Caron, Schiaparelli, Lalique, Baccarat, DeVilbiss, Irice, Matson, Stylebuilt, Czech Bohemian)
vintage-perfume-bottles.money: Lalique/Baccarat signed flacons and large factices $150–1,000+.
vintage-perfume-bottles.fakes: - Counterfeit Chanel No.5 and modern "vintage-style" bottles exist; check old-style box and label typography. - Czech-style jewelled bottles are reproduced in quantity (2000s, often unmarked or with new foil labels). Rea
vintage-perfume-bottles.buy: Buy only sealed or near-full boxed pre-1980 extraits at ≤ 1/3 of sold comps, signed Czech/Lalique/Baccarat glass with intact stopper and dauber at ≤ $60, or giant store factices; pass on empty common bottles, ormolu vanity bottles over $25 and Egyptian souveni

vintage-photographs.title: Vintage photographs
vintage-photographs.full: Vintage photographs (cabinet cards, CDVs, tintypes, daguerreotypes, real-photo postcards, panoramic/"yard-long" group photos)
vintage-photographs.money: cased images with subject interest, Civil War, Black history, early sports/aviation $200–5,000+.
vintage-photographs.fakes: Inkjet/laser copies of famous images; reprinted panoramas from LOC files; "Old West" fakes and invented captions; fake Civil War tintypes. Check paper, tones, and mount. - Modern tintypes are being made again (wet-plate
vintage-photographs.buy: Buy subject-driven images (occupational, military, sports, street scenes, ethnic/Black history, early technology) at ≤ 25% of resale; pass on anonymous portraits and ordinary church/school panoramas over $25.
tells: Ambrotype (1854–1865; PSAP gives c. 1854–1880s for the full span): glass negative backed with black, in a case. No mirror effect; warm chocolate-to-grey tone with milky highlights, low contrast. Look for flaking black varnish that reveals a negative image behi

Tintype (1856–1920s; PSAP: c. 1853–1930s): dark iron plate, often in paper sleeve. A magnet sticks (the plate is iron, not tin). Usually loose or in a paper sleeve/card; also cased in the 1860s. "Gem" tintypes are 1.5 in or smaller. Back is black/brown lacquer

Daguerreotype (1839–1860): mirror-like silver plate in a hinged case; image flips negative/positive with angle. Per PSAP: silver-mercury image on silver-plated copper, cool grey tone, sometimes lightly hand-tinted; cased in leather/paper/cloth-covered wood or

vintage-pinball-and-tabletop-games.title: Vintage tabletop pinball and marble games
vintage-pinball-and-tabletop-games.full: Vintage tabletop pinball and marble games (Northwestern Products Poosh-M-Up, Wolverine, Marx, Durable Toy, Lindstrom, Bagatelle boards)
vintage-pinball-and-tabletop-games.money: boxed/scarce themes (space, baseball, Big 4) $80–150+ (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-pinball-and-tabletop-games.fakes: Few fakes. Modern "nostalgia" tin pinballs (Schylling, Made in China, 1990s–present) mimic Wolverine – look for "Schylling" or modern safety warnings. Bagatelle reproductions sold as decor.
vintage-pinball-and-tabletop-games.buy: Buy only complete (glass/plunger/marbles present) graphic-rich pieces ≤ $20, or boxed scarce versions ≤ $40; pass on plain wood bagatelles and full-size boards.
tells: Poosh-M-Up (Northwestern Products Co., St. Louis, 1930s–1960s): wood frame, bright printed paper/masonite playfield, glass cover, name in big letters ("Poosh-M-Up Jr.", "Big 4", "Slugger", "Double Track", "3-in-1"). Some had a "pin-ball" scoring dial.

Wolverine Supply & Mfg. Co. (Pittsburgh, 1903–): lithographed tin pinballs, 1930s–1970s, colorful themes (space, cowboys, sports, "Pin Ball No. 99"-type numbering), wire legs, plastic covers on later ones.
Bagatelle: older English/American parlor game, wooden board with pins and cups; tabletop versions 12–24 in; Victorian full-length boards are furniture-sized (pass).

vintage-playboy-magazines.title: Vintage Playboy magazines
vintage-playboy-magazines.fakes: Facsimile/reprint of Issue #1 (1970s–2000s reproductions, "Collector's Edition") often mistaken for the 1953 original — real #1 has no date on the cover and is 44 pages; reprints usually say "reprint" or have modern pape
vintage-playboy-magazines.buy: Only buy large 1950s–early-60s lots or bulk 70s lots at ≤ $2/issue; single 1970s issues are pass.

vintage-portable-radios.title: Vintage portable radios
vintage-portable-radios.full: Vintage portable radios (Regency, Zenith, Sony, Motorola, RCA, Panasonic/National, GE, Philco, Toshiba, Reader's Digest-branded Japanese sets)
vintage-portable-radios.money: first-gen 1954–58 pocket sets in colors and big 1980s "boomboxes" (JVC RC-M90, Sharp GF-777, Conion C-100F) $300–2,000+.
vintage-portable-radios.fakes: - Regency TR-1 reproductions and replica cases have been sold; check for a correct back label and period components. - "Bluetooth-converted" vintage radios (gutted chassis) are sold as decor — collectors pay less for the
vintage-portable-radios.buy: Untested electronics are out — buy only a seller-tested working set whose sold median clears profit ≥ max($50, price); in practice only early pocket transistors (1954–60, colored cases, 4–7 transistors) and top-tier boomboxes ever qualify.
tells: Boomboxes (1978–1990): twin speakers, chrome, VU meters, often detachable speakers. The high-value ones are large (JVC RC-M90, Sharp GF-777, Conion C-100F, Crown CSC-950) — check the size rule.

Early pocket transistors (1954–1962, the money tier): shirt-pocket size, a round thumbwheel dial, molded plastic case in colors (red, turquoise, ivory, pink, black), metal or plastic grille with a big brand logo, often "TRANSISTOR" or "6 TRANSISTOR" spelled ou

1960s "all transistor" portables: book-size sets with chrome trim, a slide-rule or vertical dial with "KC" scale, leather or leatherette wrap (Motorola, Zenith Royal series, GE, RCA, Philco). The "KC" (kilocycles) dial is pre-1970s; "kHz" suggests later.

vintage-postcards.title: Vintage postcards
vintage-postcards.full: Vintage postcards (view cards, linen, real-photo RPPC, Tuck, Detroit Publishing, Curt Teich)
vintage-postcards.fakes: - Modern reprints of RPPCs: glossy, with no stamp box or modern paper. - Reproduction Halloween cards: flat (not embossed), modern bright-white stock, a halftone dot pattern where the original was chromolithographed, and
vintage-postcards.buy: Never pay more than ~$0.25/card for tourist-view lots; look only for RPPCs of small towns/people at work and Halloween holiday cards.
tells: Pioneer era (1893–98): government printed 1¢ cards and privately printed souvenir cards; no message allowed on the address side.
Private Mailing Card era (1898–1901): "Private Mailing Card / Authorized by Act of Congress May 19, 1898" on the back.

Undivided back, "Post Card" (Dec 24, 1901 – March 1, 1907): back is address only, so messages are written across the picture side. The entry's earlier summary "undivided back (1898–1907)" covers both of these eras.

vintage-power-tools.title: Vintage power tools
vintage-power-tools.full: Vintage power tools (Sears Craftsman, Porter-Cable, Delta/Rockwell, Milwaukee, Skil, Black & Decker, Stanley Electric, Walker-Turner, Thor)
vintage-power-tools.money: collectible early Porter-Cable (503, 100 router "Speedmatic"), Stanley Electric, Walker-Turner, art-deco drills, rare Delta Homecraft $150–600.
vintage-power-tools.fakes: Not faked. Reissue confusion: Porter-Cable/Delta/Craftsman names were sold to Stanley Black & Decker (Craftsman 2017) and later tools are China-made with the same names – value is in USA-made vintage only.
vintage-power-tools.buy: Buy only professional-grade USA-made portable tools (Porter-Cable, Milwaukee, Skil 77/HD77, Delta/Rockwell portable, Stanley router) shown running, at ≤ 30% of sold; pass every Craftsman consumer portable, every stationary machine (weight), and anything untest
tells: Nameplates: Sears "Craftsman" red/black or silver/black badge with a model number "xxx.yyyy" – the prefix identifies the contract maker (e.g. 103 = King-Seeley stationary 1930s–60s; 113 = Emerson Electric stationary; 315 = Singer then Ryobi portables; others v
Era: cast-iron or cast-aluminium housings, cloth/rubber cords, two-prong plugs, toggle switches = 1940s–60s; grey/black plastic clamshells = 1970s+; double-insulated symbols = 1970s+.

Examples: 7952618137 Craftsman 3×21 belt sander (1970s–80s, plastic case, two-prong plug); 7981213827 Craftsman 4 in belt / 6 in disc motorized benchtop sander (113-series, Emerson, 1980s, yellow lock key, 4 A); 7951383449 Craftsman 207.2561 sander/polisher (1

vintage-pyrex.title: Vintage Pyrex and Corning kitchenware
vintage-pyrex.full: Vintage Pyrex and Corning kitchenware (Corning Glass Works Pyrex opal and clear glass; Corning Ware; JAJ Pyrex UK; Agee Pyrex Australia)
vintage-pyrex.money: rare (Lucky in Love, Atomic Eye full sets, rare promos and colour variants) $400–3,000+.
vintage-pyrex.fakes: Post-1998 "pyrex" reissues of vintage patterns (2016 Pyrex "Vintage Charm" line by World Kitchen/Corelle: Pink Daisy, Butterprint etc. reproductions, marked with modern lowercase logo). Fake "promotional" patterns create
vintage-pyrex.buy: Buy only scarce 1950s–60s promotional patterns or complete primary/rare-colour bowl sets in bright, unscratched condition at ≤ 1/3 sold median; pass 1970s patterns, carafes, and anything with dishwasher dulling.
tells: Promotional/limited patterns: often sold as a single casserole in a cradle or with a lid as a give-away/limited release (e.g., Lucky in Love 1959, Atomic Eye/Atomic Stars, Golden Hearts, Starburst, Balloons, Bluebelle, Golden Honeysuckle, Golden Branch). Examp
Logo: embossed "PYREX" in capitals (often with "Corning N.Y.", "Made in U.S.A.", shape number such as 024, 444, 473, 475-B) on the base. Lowercase "pyrex" = post-1998 soda-lime glass, not vintage.

Shapes: nesting mixing bowls (401–404), Cinderella bowls with spout tabs (441–444), round casseroles (471–475), oval casseroles (043, 045), refrigerator dishes (501–503), Hostess/Space Saver casseroles, divided dishes (1063), butter dishes, carafes.

vintage-quilts.title: Vintage quilts
vintage-quilts.full: Vintage quilts (hand-pieced American quilts — Amish, Mennonite, African American, feed-sack, crazy quilts, tied comforters)
vintage-quilts.money: Amish, African American, 19th-c. and fine crazy quilts $300–3,000+ (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-quilts.fakes: Chinese/Indian imported "hand-quilted" quilts since the 1990s (uniform, larger stitches, new cotton). - **Arch quilts** (QuiltHistory): imported from China by Arch Associates, Inc. (founded c. 1987, Elmsford then Hawthor
vintage-quilts.buy: Buy only hand-quilted (small even stitches) pre-1950 quilts in clean condition at ≤ $60; tied polyester/flannel utility quilts are a pass.
tells: Title words: "antique quilt", "hand quilted", "hand stitched", "feed sack", "tied", "Amish", "Double Wedding Ring", "Grandmother's Flower Garden".
A quilt has three layers (top, batting, backing) held by stitching or ties; a "summer spread" or coverlet has no batting.

Pieced (patchwork of cut shapes), appliqué (shapes sewn onto a background), whole-cloth (one fabric, all quilting), crazy (random silk/velvet/wool shapes with embroidery over the seams, mostly Victorian), embroidered (redwork, Sunbonnet Sue, state birds).

vintage-ray-ban-sunglasses.title: Vintage Ray-Ban sunglasses — plus Vuarnet Pouilloux, Persol, Carrera, Serengeti as lot companions
vintage-ray-ban-sunglasses.full: Vintage Ray-Ban sunglasses (Bausch & Lomb USA 1937–1999: Aviator, Outdoorsman, Shooter, General, Wayfarer 5022, Clubmaster, Olympian, Caravan, Cats, Wings, Ambermatic, Chromax, 1990s W-series; vs Luxottica 1999–) — plus Vuarnet Pouilloux, Persol, Carrera, Serengeti as lot companions
vintage-ray-ban-sunglasses.money: Ambermatic, Chromax, The General (50th anniversary, "50" lens), Olympic Games editions, NOS with case/box $300–800+. Vuarnet Pouilloux 002/027/085 Skilynx $100–250 (est), dealer asks $325.
vintage-ray-ban-sunglasses.fakes: - Fake Ray-Bans are everywhere (1980s–now), including fake "B&L" marks on cheap aviators and Wayfarers. Authenticate every pair: etch precision, hinge quality, glass lenses, correct model code on the temple, correct typo
vintage-ray-ban-sunglasses.buy: Buy only B&L pairs ("BL" lens etch and/or "B&L Ray-Ban U.S.A." on the temple) in a named premium model, scratch-free glass lenses, straight frames, at ≤ 30% of the est. sold price; pass on Luxottica-era, scratched lenses, bent/re-plated frames, missing nose pa
tells: Ray-Ban was a Bausch & Lomb (Rochester NY) brand from 1937 until Luxottica bought it in 1999. B&L pairs were US-made with mineral glass lenses (G-15 grey-green, B-15 brown, RB-3 "Tru Green" early, Ambermatic photochromic, Chromax, Diamond Hard, mirror). The wh

Models by silhouette: Aviator (teardrop wire, "L0205" 58mm / "L2823" 62mm), Outdoorsman (aviator with a plastic "sweat bar"/brow bar and cable or plastic temple tips), Shooter (aviator with a round "cigarette holder" ring at the bridge), General (aviator with

B&L tells in a photo: a tiny laser-etched "BL" in a corner of one lens (from ~1982; earlier B&L lenses have no etch — then the frame marks date it); the other lens may carry an etched or painted "Ray-Ban" script (1990s); the temple inside reads "B&L Ray-Ban U.

vintage-recurve-bows.title: Vintage recurve & longbows
vintage-recurve-bows.full: Vintage recurve & longbows (Bear, Damon Howatt, Wing, Browning, Pearson, Shakespeare, Indian Archery)
vintage-recurve-bows.money: coin-era Kodiaks, Bear takedowns, Wing Presentation II, Tamerlane $350–1,000+.
vintage-recurve-bows.fakes: Bear has reissued classic models (e.g. "Kodiak", "Super Kodiak", "Grizzly" in later production) — check the coin or medallion type and serial to date it (general knowledge, verify). Coins can be swapped in refinished ris
vintage-recurve-bows.buy: Buy Bear coin-riser Kodiak/Super Kodiak/Grizzly under $90, Howatt/Wing/Condor/Palomino under $70; pass unbranded, >60 lb draw, LH, or seller-priced over $100.

vintage-saxophones.title: Vintage saxophones
vintage-saxophones.full: Vintage saxophones (Buescher, Conn, King, Martin, Selmer)
vintage-saxophones.fakes: Chinese/Taiwanese "Mark VI-style" horns and stencil horns with fake engravings exist; check serial numbers against the maker's chart and engraving quality. Some horns are re-engraved (general knowledge, verify). Document
vintage-saxophones.buy: Buy pro-tier (Conn 6M/10M, King Super 20, Martin, Selmer Paris) under $200 with keys complete; pass untested student/mid tier.

vintage-sewing-machines.title: Vintage sewing machines
vintage-sewing-machines.full: Vintage sewing machines (Singer, Kenmore/Sears, Montgomery Ward/Signature, White, Necchi, Pfaff, Bernina, Elna, Viking Husqvarna, National, Free, New Home)
vintage-sewing-machines.fakes: Chinese "Featherweight" lookalikes exist mainly as toys/miniatures and decor replicas; check Singer serial plate on the bed. Singer reissued no Featherweights; Japanese clones (Brother, Pinnock, "Deluxe") copy Singer 15
vintage-sewing-machines.buy: Only Singer Featherweight 221/222 (black, tiny, ~11 lb) or Singer 301 at ≤ $150 that the seller shows sewing; everything else is too heavy for its value.

vintage-shaving-brushes.title: Vintage shaving brushes
vintage-shaving-brushes.full: Vintage shaving brushes (Ever-Ready, Rubberset, Made Rite, Erskine, Simms, Kent, Vulfix, catalin/bakelite handles)
vintage-shaving-brushes.money: marbled/two-tone catalin, large "400" sizes, boxed NOS $60–200 (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-shaving-brushes.fakes: Modern "vintage-style" red/cream brushes sold on Amazon/Temu imitate Ever-Ready; check the stamp and the handle weight. Re-knotted vintage handles are honest restorations but should be sold as re-knotted, not original.
vintage-shaving-brushes.buy: buy lots of 4+ with catalin (translucent butterscotch, marbled, cherry red) handles or NOS boxed brushes at ≤ $8 per brush; pairs of common brushes are a pass.
tells: Title words: "catalin", "butterscotch", "bakelite", "Ever-Ready", "Rubberset", "Made Rite", "sterilized", "badger", "NOS", "barber".

"Sterilized" stamp: belongs to the WWI-era anthrax scare. Outbreak summaries for 1915–24 counted 149 US military and 17 US civilian cases tied to brushes, and almost all medical case reports fall in 1917–23. Wartime makers had substituted horsehair shipped str
