vintage-skateboards.title: Vintage skateboards and collectible decks
vintage-skateboards.full: Vintage skateboards and collectible decks (Powell Peralta, Santa Cruz, Vision, G&S Fibreflex, Alva, Sims, Dogtown, Z-Flex)
vintage-skateboards.fakes: Reissues are the main issue: most "rare limited edition" CL listings are reissues — check the © date under the graphic and any "reissue" text. Counterfeit Powell/Santa Cruz decks from overseas exist (general knowledge, v
vintage-skateboards.buy: Buy confirmed 1980s originals ≤ $60–150 (see full rule), NOS reissue ≤ $40, 70s Fibreflex/Tracker/Kryptonics complete under $120; pass reissues ≥ $60 and sellers quoting eBay.
tells: 1970s fibreglass / early urethane: Gordon & Smith Fibreflex (1964–80s): laminated maple/fibreglass deck, reddish-brown
1980s decks: wide (10"), fish tail, concave with a nose kick, rails/tail bone screw holes, "pig" shape with a short
Reissues (Powell Bones Brigade series, Santa Cruz reissues, Vision reissues 2000s+): glossy, crisp print, the word

vintage-ski-apparel.title: Vintage ski apparel
vintage-ski-apparel.full: Vintage ski apparel (Bogner, Ellesse, Fila, Obermeyer, Head, Descente, Spyder, The North Face, Columbia, Roffe, Skyr, Marker, Gerry, Demetre)
vintage-ski-apparel.money: Bogner, Ellesse, Fila Italy, Descente, early Spyder, TNF Extreme/Steep Tech and wild 80s one-pieces $80–300
vintage-ski-apparel.fakes: Fila and Ellesse reissue retro styles (made in Asia, newer tags). TNF reissued Steep Tech in 2010s–2020s. Check tag style and country. More: TNF Steep Tech returned in 2000 (urban relaunch), again via Supreme in 2016, an
vintage-ski-apparel.buy: Pass on fleece, resort souvenirs and plain shells; only one-piece 80s suits, Bogner/Ellesse/Fila/Descente/TNF Steep Tech pieces in clean condition at ≤ $25.
tells: Logos on chest, sleeve or leg: Ellesse half-ball, Fila "F", Descente arrows, TNF half-dome.
Zip pulls are branded on good pieces (Bogner "B", Descente, TNF), and the zip maker (YKK, Riri, Lampo, Opti) is stamped on the slider.

Era tells from the cut: 1970s — quilted down/poly-fill jackets with snap storm flaps, narrower fit, stretch "warm-up" pants. 1980s — one-piece suits with padded shoulders, elastic waists, stirrup or gaiter cuffs, neon/pastel colour-blocking, diagonal zips. 199

vintage-snare-drums.title: Vintage snare drums
vintage-snare-drums.full: Vintage snare drums (Ludwig, Slingerland, Rogers, Gretsch, Leedy, MIJ Pearl/Star/Tama)
vintage-snare-drums.money: Dynasonic, Black Beauty, pre-war Radio King, COB Supra $600–2,000.
vintage-snare-drums.fakes: Ludwig has reissued Black Beauty and Supraphonic (modern ones have modern badges and serials); badge swaps onto generic shells exist (general knowledge, verify).
vintage-snare-drums.buy: Buy Ludwig/Slingerland/Rogers/Gretsch with badge visible at ≤ $100; pass no-badge or MIJ tapered-nut-lug snares.
tells: Slingerland: "Sound King" / Radio King badge; Stick Saver hoops; streamlined "beavertail" lugs.
Rogers: Dynasonic (brass, with snare cradle frame) or Powertone; "beavertail" lugs; script badge.
Ludwig: Keystone (pre-1970) or Blue/Olive oval badge; "Imperial" bow-tie lugs. Supraphonic LM400/402 =

vintage-snowshoes.title: Vintage snowshoes
vintage-snowshoes.full: Vintage snowshoes (Tubbs, Snocraft, Iverson, Faber, Chestnut Canoe Co., C.A. Lund, Westover, Northland, Sherpa; Native-made)
vintage-snowshoes.money: early or unusual (babiche, Native-made, early stamped Tubbs) $200–600 (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-snowshoes.fakes: Modern décor snowshoes; "made to look older" modern pairs (Journal of Antiques); restored pairs presented as original. No known faked Tubbs stamps (general knowledge).
vintage-snowshoes.buy: Buy only labelled Tubbs/Snocraft, Army-marked or Native-made pairs under ~$40; common pairs at $90 are a pass.

vintage-sports-caps.title: Vintage sports and racing caps , Drew Pearson, Competitor, Twins Enterprise; racing/F1 and NASCAR caps; Mitchell & Ness and New Era reissues)
vintage-sports-caps.full: Vintage sports and racing caps (Sports Specialties, Starter, AJD, American Needle, Annco, Logo 7, New Era (pre-2000), Drew Pearson, Competitor, Twins Enterprise; racing/F1 and NASCAR caps; Mitchell & Ness and New Era reissues)
vintage-sports-caps.money: deadstock with tags, rare teams/events, 1970s wool caps $150–600+.
vintage-sports-caps.fakes: Mitchell & Ness reissues closely copy Sports Specialties Bulls/Lakers/Raiders scripts; counterfeit modern "vintage" caps from China with fake SS tags; bootleg Ferrari caps with printed shields; fake "deadstock" with repr
vintage-sports-caps.buy: Inside tag decides: Sports Specialties, Starter (with 1990s tags), AJD, Annco, American Needle "Blockhead" = buy at ≤ 1/3 resale; Mitchell & Ness, New Era 2000s+, '47 = pass; F1/Ferrari caps need official-sponsor and era tells, mostly pass.
tells: Sports Specialties (LA, 1950s–1993; Nike to ~1997): wool/acrylic, green undervisor, big embroidered script team names ("Script"), "Grid", "Shadow", "Wave", "Laser"; inside: "Sports Specialties" woven tag and "Pro" sweatband; snap often embossed. Bulls, Raiders
Starter (1980s–1999): "Starter" logo on back strap/snap, tri-power, arch, splash designs; tags "Made in Korea/Taiwan".
AJD, Annco, Logo 7, American Needle (Blockhead), Drew Pearson, Competitor, Twins Enterprise: 1980s–90s.

vintage-squeak-toys.title: Vintage squeak toys
vintage-squeak-toys.full: Vintage squeak toys (Sun Rubber, Rempel, Edward Mobley/Arrow, Sanitoy, Irwin, Knickerbocker, Hong Kong vinyl)
vintage-squeak-toys.fakes: "Repro-1955 Sun Rubber" items exist (Terapeak shows one at $10.59, Feb 2026). Modern pet-store latex squeakers in retro shapes are sometimes titled "vintage"; they lack moulded maker marks.
vintage-squeak-toys.buy: pass under almost all circumstances; only Disney/licensed character Sun Rubber or Rempel lots of 5+ at ≤ $5 each.

vintage-star-wars-figures.title: Vintage Star Wars action figures
vintage-star-wars-figures.full: Vintage Star Wars action figures (Kenner 3¾" 1977–1985; Palitoy, Meccano, Lili Ledy, Glasslite, Toltoys, Takara; vs Hasbro 1995+ reissues)
vintage-star-wars-figures.money: rare variants (vinyl-cape Jawa, double-telescoping sabers, Blue Snaggletooth, Yak Face) $750–30,000+ and need authentication
vintage-star-wars-figures.fakes: Reproduction weapons, capes and Jawa vinyl capes are everywhere; fake COOs and fake double-telescoping sabers on high-end variants; resealed cards. Hasbro Vintage/Retro reissues imitate Kenner packaging ("updated version
vintage-star-wars-figures.buy: Buy loose Kenner lots at ≤ $3–5 per figure (≤ $8 with weapons), or when photos show Boba Fett, Last 17/Droids figures or original weapons; pass on Hasbro-era lots; never pay for "rare variant" claims without authentication.

vintage-stereo-receivers.title: Vintage stereo receivers
vintage-stereo-receivers.full: Vintage stereo receivers (Sansui, Pioneer, Marantz, Kenwood, Technics, Lafayette, Realistic)
vintage-stereo-receivers.fakes: No real fakes; watch for faceplate/knob swaps, LED lamp conversions (some buyers dislike) and units sold "serviced" without proof (general knowledge, verify). Replacement (non-original) wood cabinets are sold new and sho
vintage-stereo-receivers.buy: Buy tested Marantz 22xx, Pioneer SX-1050+, Sansui 8080/9090/G ≤ $200; pass untested/"in storage", slim 1980s, Lafayette/Realistic.
tells: Marantz: 20xx = smaller, 22xx = the main 1970s two-channel line, 23xx = bigger; within a series the last digits roughly equal watts per channel (2245 = 45 W, 2270 = 70 W, 2285B = 85 W, 2385 = 185 W; 2010 = 10 W, 2015 = 15 W) (Gear Patrol). A "B" suffix is a la

Pioneer: SX-x50 series (1976–77) is the classic silver-face generation; SX-x80 (1978–79, e.g. SX-980, SX-1980) is the top silver generation; higher number = more power (SX-980 = 80 W per channel; SX-1250 large, heavy with big transformer — Gear Patrol). Earlie

Sansui: three/four-digit numbers (771, 881, 8080, 9090); "DB" suffix (8080DB, 9090DB, about 1977) adds Dolby FM; G-series (G-7700, G-9700, G-33000; ~1978–80) are the last big silver receivers; R-series are the slim 1980s units.

vintage-telephones.title: Vintage telephones
vintage-telephones.full: Vintage telephones (Western Electric/Bell System, Automatic Electric/GTE, Kellogg, Stromberg-Carlson, ITT, North Electric, novelty phones: Coca-Cola, Mickey Mouse, Snoopy, Garfield, hamburger)
vintage-telephones.fakes: Modern "retro" reproductions (Crosley, Mid-Century Modern) look like 302s and 500s but are light and have push-buttons hidden in rotary-style dials; China-made "candlestick" phones abound. Look for the Western Electric/B
vintage-telephones.buy: Buy Western Electric 302s, candlesticks, wood crank wall phones and rare colors (pink/turquoise/aqua/red 500s, ivory 302s) ≤ 30% of median; pass on beige/black/brown 500s, GTE 80s and 1990s novelty phones.
tells: Western Electric 500 (1949–1980s): rounded desk set, finger-wheel dial with letters under clear holes; date stamped under base and inside handset ("10-63"). Bell System property.
Western Electric 302 (1937–1954): smaller, taller "Lucy" phone, metal (early) or thermoplastic body, dial on a sloped front; values rise for metal, ivory, red, green.
WE 554/2554 wall, Princess (701/2702), Trimline, 2500 Touch-Tone.

vintage-tennis-ball-cans.title: Vintage tennis ball cans
vintage-tennis-ball-cans.full: Vintage tennis ball cans (Wilson, Spalding, Penn, Dunlop, Slazenger, Pennsylvania, Bancroft, Davis, Wright & Ditson, Tretorn, Court/Continental UK)
vintage-tennis-ball-cans.money: pre-1960 graphic tins, key-wind sealed cans and rare brands $75–300+ (general knowledge, verify)
vintage-tennis-ball-cans.fakes: Little faking. Brands have reissued "retro" cans (e.g., Wilson/Penn retro tins) — modern construction and barcodes give them away.
vintage-tennis-ball-cans.buy: Buy only sealed (unopened, still pressurised) key-open or pre-1970 graphic cans under ~$25; empty common 1970s+ tins are a pass.
tells: Before ~1930: balls sold in paper bags or cardboard boxes (12-ball boxes are common), occasionally metal boxes.
Late 1920s: first pressurised metal cans, by Thomas E. Wilson & Co. and the Pennsylvania Rubber Company. Early examples have flat tops and a solder spot where the gas was injected.

Key-wind / key-open cans (late 1920s–1972): opened by winding a thin metal strip on a key; the key was attached to the lid, recessed into the bottom, or fixed to the side. British tins had reusable lids; American cans left sharp edges and could not be reused u

vintage-test-equipment.title: Vintage test equipment
vintage-test-equipment.full: Vintage test equipment (Simpson, Triplett, Weston, Marion Electrical Instrument Co., Hickok, Heathkit, Eico, Precision, Supreme, General Radio, Tektronix, Hewlett-Packard, Fluke)
vintage-test-equipment.fakes: None significant; decor "steampunk" meters. Reproduction roll charts and manuals are sold separately and are fine if disclosed.
vintage-test-equipment.buy: Only buy tube testers (Hickok 6000/539/600A, Sencore) and named lab gear that the seller demonstrates working, at ≤ 1/3 resale; pass on untested VOMs and generic meters (rule: no untested electronics).
tells: Oscilloscope / signal generator / lab gear: heavy steel cabinets with front-panel knobs; Tektronix (blue-grey cabinets, round CRT), HP (grey, "hp" logo), General Radio (black crackle).

VOM / multimeter: hand-held box with one large meter, a big central range-selector knob and banana jacks. Simpson 260: tall brown/black Bakelite case, meter on top half, knob and jacks below. Triplett 630: wider case, large rotary knob in the centre of the low
Panel meter: round or square meter with a flange and studs on the back, made to mount in a panel; single scale (volts, amps or milliamps).

vintage-toasters.title: Vintage chrome toasters
vintage-toasters.full: Vintage chrome toasters (Sunbeam Radiant Control, Toastmaster, GE, Universal, Manning-Bowman, flip-side 1920s–30s)
vintage-toasters.fakes: No significant fakes. Modern retro-styled toasters (Smeg, Dualit, Sunbeam retro lines) are not collectible (general knowledge, verify).
vintage-toasters.buy: Buy Sunbeam Radiant Control (no lever) under $40, deco Toastmaster/GE under $20; pass lever toasters over $20 and untested $35+ lots.

vintage-tool-bags.title: Vintage tool bags
vintage-tool-bags.full: Vintage tool bags (lineman's/electrician's canvas and leather bags; Klein Tools, Mathias Klein & Sons, Buckingham, Bashlin, Kunz, Plumb, railroad/telephone company bags)
vintage-tool-bags.money: leather tool bags and early Mathias Klein $80–200 (all general knowledge, verify
vintage-tool-bags.fakes: None meaningful; modern Klein bags look similar but cleaner and with modern tags. Buckingham Heritage bags are new production in a vintage style.
vintage-tool-bags.buy: Buy only clean, maker-stamped (Mathias Klein, Bell System, railroad) bags ≤ $25; pass rotted unmarked canvas.
tells: Zippered canvas tool bag (Klein 5102-20 larger, 5139 smaller): rectangular, leather or vinyl bottom, zipper top.

Lineman's nut-and-bolt bag: round or rectangular leather bucket bag with a stiff rim, hung from the belt or a handline; Buckingham and Bashlin make these (Buckingham still sells a "Heritage" leather line, so check for modern tags).
Carpenter's/plumber's bag: open tote, canvas or leather, wooden or leather handles.

vintage-tote-bags.title: Vintage tote bags
vintage-tote-bags.full: Vintage tote bags (L.L.Bean Boat and Tote, conference/promo canvas totes, USPS/NALC union totes, museum/bookstore totes, Coach/Lands' End canvas)
vintage-tote-bags.money: vintage L.L.Bean Boat and Tote (made in USA, pre-2000 "Maine" label) $30–90, with worn 1970s–80s examples listed (asking, not sold) at $248–650
vintage-tote-bags.fakes: L.L.Bean reissues (current production) look similar; label details date them. The "1944 Boat and Tote" is a current reissue, not a 1944 bag. Generic heavy canvas totes in Bean colours exist; no label = not Bean.
vintage-tote-bags.buy: Pass promo totes; buy only pre-1990 L.L.Bean, real leather-trim USPS carrier satchels or sought graphic totes at ≤ $15.

vintage-toy-luggage.title: Vintage toy and character luggage
vintage-toy-luggage.full: Vintage toy and character luggage (child-size suitcases and train cases; Cabbage Patch Kids, Barbie, Holly Hobbie, Strawberry Shortcake, Disney, Ponytail, Neevel)
vintage-toy-luggage.money: early Barbie 1961–64 cases and rare characters in near-mint $50–150 (general knowledge, verify).
vintage-toy-luggage.fakes: Not faked. Some characters were reissued (Barbie retro cases, 2000s) — reissues are newer-looking and marked with later dates. - Hand-made miniature vinyl copies of Barbie cases exist for doll displays (Fashion Doll Guid
vintage-toy-luggage.buy: Pass on 1980s character cases above $10; buy only clean 1950s–60s Barbie/Disney/cowboy vinyl cases at ≤ $15.
tells: Barbie cases: black or coloured vinyl with Barbie art and "© Mattel" date (1961–64 most collected).

Two kinds of "case": a child's suitcase (for the child's clothes, 12–18") vs a doll case (sized for an 11½" Barbie, often with a clothes rail and drawers inside). Vintage Barbie doll cases are the larger collector market; open the case in the photos to tell.

Ponytail: a 1950s–60s girls' brand built on a stylised ponytailed-girl graphic, used on vinyl cases, diaries, eyeglass cases, record totes and a 1959 Thermos lunch kit ("Ponytail Tid-Bid-Kit", American Thermos, pink vinyl). A c.1960 Ken doll set with carrying

vintage-tracing-stencils.title: Vintage tracing stencils and templates
vintage-tracing-stencils.full: Vintage tracing stencils and templates (Westland Plastics, Spirograph-era kids' plastic, Hong Kong/Japan imports, Rapidesign/Pickett drafting templates, Hallmark/Disney sets)
vintage-tracing-stencils.fakes: Not a reproduction target; modern dollar-store stencils exist but are flat sheets, not molded figural tracers.
vintage-tracing-stencils.buy: Pass almost always; only boxed licensed-character sets under $10, never loose generic animal tracers.

vintage-tupperware.title: Vintage Tupperware
vintage-tupperware.full: Vintage Tupperware (Servalier canisters, Wonderlier bowls, Millionaire line, Fix-N-Mix, pitchers, Ice Tups; Tupperware Home Parties)
vintage-tupperware.money: full 1950s–60s pastel or Millionaire-line sets and rare pieces $60–150 (general knowledge, verify).
vintage-tupperware.fakes: Tupperware reissued retro colours and Servalier-style canisters in the 2000s–2010s. Newer pieces have different mould numbers and brighter colours. Not a fake risk, but "vintage" is used loosely.
vintage-tupperware.buy: Buy only complete matched 1950s–60s pastel or Millionaire-line sets with all lids at ≤ $25; pass on 1970s harvest/orange sets above $15.
tells: Servalier (1970s–80s): round canisters with a sunburst (starburst) lid and a push-button lid seal. Colours: harvest gold, orange, avocado green, brown. The example listing is a four-piece orange Servalier canister set.
Wonderlier (1950s on): bowls with flat or "bell" lids, often in pastels (pink, yellow, aqua, mint).
Millionaire line (late 1950s–60s): frosted pastel ribbed pieces with a sleek, mid-century look. Most collected.

vintage-typewriters.title: Vintage typewriters
vintage-typewriters.full: Vintage typewriters (Royal, Underwood, Smith-Corona, Olympia, Hermes, Olivetti, Remington)
vintage-typewriters.money: Hermes 3000, Olympia SG1, Corona 3, Blickensderfer, Oliver $300–1,000+.
vintage-typewriters.fakes: Few fakes; repainted machines sold as "colour" and Frankenstein machines (parts swapped) are the risk. Modern decorative "typewriter-look" items are not typewriters (general knowledge, verify).
vintage-typewriters.buy: Buy Olympia SM/Hermes/colour Royal ≤ $60, Royal QDL/Smith-Corona ≤ $35 with a type sample; pass standards, repainted machines and sellers quoting online prices.
tells: Portable vs standard: a portable sits low (about 4–6 in. tall), comes with a fitted case or lid and weighs 10–20 lb; a standard (desktop) is tall, open-framed or boxy, 25–35 lb and has no case.

Reading a photo: the model name is on the paper table, the front panel or the top cover; the maker's decal is on the front or the paper table; the serial is on a frame rail under the carriage (move the carriage to one side), on the right or left of the frame,
Typeface: shown only by a type sample. Pica (larger, 10 per inch) and elite (12 per inch) are standard; script or cursive is the premium.

vintage-ukuleles.title: Ukuleles, 1920s–50s
vintage-ukuleles.full: Ukuleles, 1920s–50s (Martin, Gibson, Kamaka, Kumalae, Harmony, Regal, Favilla, banjo ukes)
vintage-ukuleles.fakes: Martin and Kamaka still make ukes — modern ones have serial numbers and modern labels (current US-made Martin 5K and "Daisy" models are serialised, per UMGF); "Martin-style" copies and modern Asian koa-look laminates are
vintage-ukuleles.buy: Lots under $150 only if a Martin or Gibson headstock is visible
tells: Martin: "C.F. Martin & Co" stamp on the back of the headstock (with "Nazareth PA" on the 1K listing) and a stamp
Gibson: logo on the front of the headstock — silver paint stencil "The Gibson" on 1920s ukes (Retrofret Uke-2);
Kamaka: interior labels and headstock "KK" decal (from 1958, per Kamaka); the oval "pineapple" body is a Kamaka

vintage-vacuum-cleaners.title: Vintage vacuum cleaners
vintage-vacuum-cleaners.full: Vintage vacuum cleaners (Hoover, Electrolux, Kirby, Royal, Eureka, Lewyt, Air-Way, Rexair/Rainbow, Filter Queen, General Electric; non-electric Bissell carpet sweepers)
vintage-vacuum-cleaners.money: rare early uprights/hand-pumped vacuums and boxed examples $200–800.
vintage-vacuum-cleaners.fakes: No significant fakes. Reproduction parts (belts, bags) available.
vintage-vacuum-cleaners.buy: Pass almost always – electric, bulky, untested; only consider complete Art Deco/1950s Hoover Constellation or Electrolux shown running in a video at ≤ $30.
tells: Hoover Portable (1960s): green or tan metal suitcase holding a canister motor, hose and wands (example 7939923970, with bags in packaging).
Hoover Constellation: spherical "flying saucer" canister that floats on its exhaust (1950s–70s).
Kirby: polished aluminium upright with brown cloth bag; model name on bag ("Classic", "Dual Sanitronic", example 7965739707 "Kirby Classic" c.1960s).

vintage-vinyl-dolls.title: Vintage vinyl dolls
vintage-vinyl-dolls.full: Vintage vinyl dolls (Horsman, Effanbee, Ideal, Madame Alexander, Vogue, Uneeda, Mattel, Kenner, Remco, Eegee, American Character, Arranbee)
vintage-vinyl-dolls.money: Madame Alexander Cissy, Ideal Patti Playpal, American Character Tressy $60–300
vintage-vinyl-dolls.fakes: Reissues by Effanbee, Ideal (Shirley Temple, Patti Playpal 1980s Ideal reissue), Madame Alexander; check neck mark years. Not commonly faked.
vintage-vinyl-dolls.buy: Only boxed, complete, working mechanical dolls or Patti Playpal/Cissy-type collector dolls at ≤ $20; loose play dolls are a pass.

vintage-wool-coats.title: Vintage wool coats , department-store labels)
vintage-wool-coats.full: Vintage wool coats (Lilli Ann, Forstmann wool, Pauline Trigère, Bonnie Cashin, Christian Dior, Hattie Carnegie, Mr. Blackwell, Mackintosh, Lassie, Fairfield/Fashionbilt, Sophie Gimbel, Marvin Richards (modern), department-store labels)
vintage-wool-coats.money: designer couture and dramatic Lilli Ann 1940s–50s $400–1,500+.
vintage-wool-coats.fakes: Modern "vintage style"; check labels/union tags. Label swaps (a designer label sewn into a plain coat) occur; check that the label stitching matches the other interior stitching.
vintage-wool-coats.buy: Buy only labeled better makers or dramatic 1940s–50s cuts in great condition, at ≤ 1/3 resale; ask the seller for label, fiber tag and moth-damage photos; pass otherwise.
tells: Label photo (neck or inside front facing): maker name, plus city ("San Francisco", "Paris" on post-war Lilli Ann).
Label reading "AFL" without "CIO": before 1955.
"AFL-CIO": 1955 or later (1958: small blue imprinted outerwear label).

vintage-wristwatches.title: Vintage & fashion wristwatches
vintage-wristwatches.full: Vintage & fashion wristwatches (Elgin, Bulova, Hamilton, Gruen, Benrus, Omega, Longines, Tissot, Seiko, Citizen, Rolex, Invicta, Swatch)
vintage-wristwatches.fakes: Rolex, Omega, Heuer and Seiko fakes and "Frankenwatches" (mixed parts, redialed Seikos) are widespread; homage brands (Steeldive, Pagani) copy famous designs. Authenticate reference/serial, movement and dial before any p
vintage-wristwatches.buy: Buy Accutron/Hamilton Electric/Seiko chrono/Omega/Longines/military running at ≤ 30% of tier (≤ $75), solid 14K under melt, A-11 under $60; pass GF dress watches over $40–60, non-running, fashion brands.
tells: American mid-century (Elgin, Bulova, Hamilton, Gruen, Benrus, Waltham, Wittnauer) 1940s–60s: 10K gold-filled or
Swiss: Tissot PR50/PR100 quartz $50–100; Tissot/Omega/Longines mechanical 1950s–60s $150–600 (Omega
Japanese: Seiko 6139/6138 chronographs ($250–600), 6105/6309 divers ($400–1,500), Seiko 5 ($30–80), Grand

vintage-yo-yos.title: Vintage yo-yos
vintage-yo-yos.full: Vintage yo-yos (Duncan, Cheerio, Royal, Festival, Hummingbird, Flambeau-made Duncan, Yomega, Playmaxx, ProYo, Spintastics, YoYoJam, Duncan Freehand, Tom Kuhn, Henrys)
vintage-yo-yos.money: rare wood (Duncan "Gold Seal", Cheerio Beginner/Tournament jeweled, Flores), sealed 1960s blister cards, and early 2000s boutique metal (YoYoFactory, One Drop, CLYW, Spyy) $60–400.
vintage-yo-yos.fakes: Duncan reissued wooden "Throwback"/"Retro" Butterflies and Tournaments (2000s–2010s) – look for modern packaging or a © date. Chinese counterfeits of One Drop/YoYoFactory exist (cheap anodising, no engraving depth). Soda
vintage-yo-yos.buy: Pass plastic 1990s lots (Yomega Fireball/Brain/X-Brain/Raider, Duncan Imperial glow) above ~$1.50/yo-yo; only buy pre-1965 wooden yo-yos with legible stamped/goldleaf logos or jewels, sealed vintage carded yo-yos, or machined aluminum boutique yo-yos at ≤ 25%
tells: Boutique metal (2003 on): one-piece machined aluminium/titanium, anodised, engraved logos (YoYoFactory, One Drop, CLYW, Spyy, YoYoJam, Duncan "Metal Drifter", General Yo, Turning Point). Recognised by bright anodised metal and wide "H" or "W" profiles.

Wooden (1928–c.1965): one-piece turned maple or two halves on a wooden axle; logo hot-stamped in gold or silver foil ("Duncan O-Boy", "Duncan Gold Seal", "Cheerio 77", "Royal Tournament", "Hi-Ker", "Festival"). Rhinestone/"jeweled" sides on 1950s Duncan Tourna

Early plastic (c.1955–1985): Duncan Imperial (solid colour, foil-stamped "Duncan Imperial" with the "sunburst", 1955 on; glow-in-the-dark "Glow Imperial" 1970s–90s), Duncan Butterfly (1957 on, flared halves), Duncan "Wheels" (tyre graphic, 1980s–90s), Festival

vinyl-record-lots.title: Vinyl record lots
vinyl-record-lots.full: Vinyl record lots (LP and 45 collections: rock, jazz, soul, punk, classical; labels Blue Note, Prestige, Impulse!, Riverside, Columbia, RCA, Atlantic, Motown, Stax, Capitol, Vertigo, Harvest, Sub Pop, SST)
vinyl-record-lots.money: rare originals (Blue Note NY pressings, private-press psych, early punk) $200–3,000.
vinyl-record-lots.fakes: Counterfeit pressings of rare titles (Beatles, Elvis Sun, Velvet Underground, punk rarities), bootlegs, and unofficial European reissues. Check matrix numbers and label typography against Discogs.
vinyl-record-lots.buy: Buy lots only when photos/spines show ≥ 3 identifiable valuable originals (original-label jazz, 60s–70s psych/prog, punk, soul, rare rock first pressings) at ≤ $1–2 per record overall; never buy a box blind.
tells: Jazz: Blue Note (address on label: 47 West 63rd/767 Lexington = early; "Liberty" or "A Division of United Artists" = later), Prestige (NJ/Bergenfield yellow), Riverside, Impulse! (orange/black), Contemporary, Pacific Jazz. "Deep groove" ring on label, "RVG" or

Rock: original first pressings of Beatles (Vee-Jay, Capitol rainbow), Led Zeppelin (Atlantic plum/red), Pink Floyd (Harvest), Velvet Underground (Verve), Nirvana Bleach (Sub Pop), Bowie, Stones (London), psych/prog on Vertigo swirl, private press.
Soul/funk: Motown/Tamla/Stax/Atlantic originals, Northern Soul 45s, Blaxploitation soundtracks.

vinyl-records.title: Vinyl records — single LPs where one pressing is worth a multiple
vinyl-records.full: Vinyl records — single LPs where one pressing is worth a multiple (Led Zeppelin, Beatles, punk/hardcore originals)
vinyl-records.money: Ordinary 1965-85 classic-rock LPs sell $5-25 each, $13-33 as small lots. The money is a handful of specific pressings of common titles: Led Zeppelin II "RL/SS" Robert Ludwig cut $150-500 (VG-VG+) to $1,000-1,800 (NM, Presswell), Beatles "Yesterday and Today" butcher cover $2,000-20,000 (second/third
vinyl-records.fakes: Counterfeits exist for Vee-Jay Introducing the Beatles (the most common fake LP), the butcher cover (printed "butcher" covers sold as novelties, and faked third states with a photo pasted on), Led Zeppelin bootlegs, Nirv
vinyl-records.buy: Never buy a record lot on cover photos; buy single titles only when the seller confirms the dead-wax/label tell (RL etch, butcher image, original label/catalog number) and the price leaves ≥ max($50, price) after Media Mail both ways.

violin-bows.title: Violin bows
violin-bows.full: Violin bows (antique / trade bows) (Mirecourt workshops: Bazin, Ouchard, Cuniot-Hury, Morizot, Husson; German: Nürnberger, Pfretzschner, Knopf; student: Glasser)
violin-bows.money: Ouchard, Sartory, Voirin, Peccatte, real Tourte $5,000–100,000+.
violin-bows.fakes: False stamps of famous makers (Tourte, Vuillaume, Sartory) on trade bows are very common; only certificates from recognised experts count for top-tier bows (general knowledge, verify).
violin-bows.buy: Buy a legible maker stamp (Bazin, Morizot, Cuniot-Hury, Nürnberger, Pfretzschner, Knopf), straight stick, ≤ $150; lead on good frogs without a stamp photo; pass unstamped/brazilwood/plastic/warped.

wade-whimsies-and-miniatures.title: Wade Whimsies and miniatures
wade-whimsies-and-miniatures.full: Wade Whimsies and miniatures (George Wade & Son / Wade Ceramics; Red Rose Tea premiums; Tom Smith crackers)
wade-whimsies-and-miniatures.money: boxed 1950s sets, Wade Blow-Ups and rare early figures $75–300+ (general knowledge, verify)
wade-whimsies-and-miniatures.fakes: Not heavily faked (too cheap). Confusion comes from Wade's own reissues (Red Rose reusing English Whimsies moulds) and from other makers' look-alikes: Sylvac, Szeiler, Goebel minis, Japanese bone-china miniatures, "Whims
wade-whimsies-and-miniatures.buy: Only buy loose lots at ≤ $0.50–1 per figure or 1950s first-series/Hat Box/Blow-Up pieces at a fraction of resale; a plain common lot rarely clears $50 profit.

walking-canes.title: Walking canes and sticks
walking-canes.full: Walking canes and sticks (crook canes, gadget canes, folk-art carved, silver/gold-topped, malacca, Brigg, Swaine Adeney, shillelagh)
walking-canes.money: gadget/system canes (sword, flask, gun) $300–5,000 (general knowledge, verify)
walking-canes.fakes: Indian-made sword canes and "antique" brass-handle canes (dog head, duck head) sold in the $20 range flood the market. Brass animal-head and skull handles are sold new as separate parts on eBay (ebay.de listings; "3 part
walking-canes.buy: Pass on plain crooks; buy only metal-handled (sterling/gold-filled marked), carved figural, or gadget canes ≤ $40. Note full-length canes do fit diagonally in a car but cost $25–40 to ship.

wall-clocks.title: Wall clocks
wall-clocks.full: Wall clocks (antique American regulators; MCM Howard Miller/George Nelson, Welby, Elgin, Syroco starbursts; Lux and Kit-Cat novelty; Telechron/GE electric; décor reproductions Ren-Wil, Howard Miller, Sterling & Noble, Casablanca-dial station clocks)
wall-clocks.money: Lux pendulettes, early Kit-Cat, George Nelson originals, Vienna regulators $150–2,000+.
wall-clocks.fakes: Décor reproductions of schoolhouse and station clocks with quartz movements; Asian-made "Nelson style" clocks; reissued Kit-Cats (modern battery); fake Vienna regulators assembled from parts.
wall-clocks.buy: Buy only Lux/Keebler pendulettes, original 1950s–60s George Nelson/Howard Miller pieces, and working spring-wound American wall clocks that fit a passenger seat, at ≤ 30% of sold; pass on quartz décor clocks.
tells: MCM: George Nelson for Howard Miller (1949–60s: Ball, Sunflower, Asterisk, Spike; Vitra reissues since 1999), Howard Miller starbursts; Welby and Elgin starbursts with 8-day spring or battery movements; Syroco wood-composition sunbursts.

Novelty: Lux Clock Co. (Waterbury CT) pendulette clocks (1930s–50s; animated figures — dogs, birds, Woody Woodpecker), Keebler; Kit-Cat Klock (1930s–present; early ones with a wind-up or electric motor).

Antique mechanical (1860s–1930s): schoolhouse (octagonal top, short drop), regulators (long case, pendulum window; Seth Thomas, Ansonia, Waterbury, E. Ingraham, Gilbert, Sessions, New Haven), Vienna regulators (German/Austrian, glass case, often large). Key-wo

wall-tapestries.title: Wall tapestries
wall-tapestries.full: Wall tapestries (Aubusson and Flemish antique weavings; Belgian/French machine jacquard tapestries; Manual Woodworkers & Weavers; Italian/Turkish velvet wall rugs; 1970s needlepoint/crewel hangings; Hines of Oxford)
wall-tapestries.money: hand-woven Aubusson/Flemish (18th–19th c) fragments and panels $300–10,000+ (needs specialist).
wall-tapestries.fakes: Machine jacquards are often sold as "Aubusson" or "antique French tapestry". Velvet souvenirs are often called "antique Persian". Lens matched a modern floral jacquard throw to $795 listings: unreliable.
wall-tapestries.buy: Pass on throws, velvet souvenirs and modern jacquards; buy only labelled Belgian jacquards with figural classical scenes ≤ 4 ft at ≤ $20, and never pay for "Aubusson" claims without visible hand-woven slits and age (specialist territory).
tells: Hand-woven tapestry (Aubusson, Flemish): weft-faced, slits between colour areas, wool/silk, colour shading by hatching, faded, often reduced or patched. Rare on Craigslist.
Machine jacquard tapestry (Belgium, France, 1950s–today): uniform weave, cotton/poly, the back shows a reversed image with floats; usually a label "Made in Belgium" or "Tapisserie" and a rod pocket.
Tapestry throws (Manual Woodworkers & Weavers, Goodwin Weavers, Pure Country): fringe on two or four sides, cotton, 50×60" or 50×70" size; a blanket, not a wall piece.

wallace-nutting-prints.title: Wallace Nutting and hand-colored photographs
wallace-nutting-prints.full: Wallace Nutting and hand-colored photographs (Wallace Nutting, David Davidson, Charles Sawyer / Sawyer Pictures, Fred Thompson, Charles Higgins, Lake Placid, Harrison, Bicknell, Gardner)
wallace-nutting-prints.money: rare titles, snow scenes, animals, men, seascapes $300–2,000
wallace-nutting-prints.fakes: 1930s Nutting "process prints" (machine printed) sold as hand-coloured; modern scans/inkjets of popular titles; added fake pencil signatures on other studios' prints.
wallace-nutting-prints.buy: Pass on common blossom/lane exteriors over $15; buy only interiors, snow scenes, animals, seascapes or men-in-scene Nuttings, or large sizes (≥ 13x16) at ≤ $40 with the signature and title on the mat.

watch-case-marks.title: Watch case precious-metal marks
watch-case-marks.full: Watch case precious-metal marks (Swiss Helvetia, squirrel, bear, grouse, duck, Morgenstern, chamois/ibex, St Bernard; US solid vs gold-filled: Keystone, J. Boss, Crescent, Fahys, Dueber, Wadsworth, Star; British Dennison and assay marks; French eagle's head, horse's head, owl, swan, dog's head; platinum)
watch-case-marks.money: solid 9k cases ≈ $50/g of case gold, 14k ≈ $78/g, 18k ≈ $100/g at $4,144/oz gold, so a typical 14k hunting case (20–40 g of case gold) holds about $1,550–3,100 melt
watch-case-marks.fakes: - Engraved or stamped fake "14K"/"18K" on base-metal cases are rare but exist (american-pocket-watches entry); acid-test or XRF before paying gold money. - Modern Chinese-made "antique" pocket watches with fake Swiss hal
watch-case-marks.buy: Never price a "gold" watch until you have seen the inside of the back lid: a Swiss Helvetia head or squirrel, a British crown with 18 or "9 .375" and a date letter, a French eagle's head, or a plain "14K"/"18K"/"0.585"/"0.750" with no years and no "filled" mea
tells: Inside the back lid (most common): karat or fineness, hallmark animal or head, case maker's trademark, case serial number.
Inner dust cover / cuvette: often a second set of marks, or "Métal"/"Cuvette métal"/"Cuvette or" — the cuvette may be gilt brass inside a gold case, so it does not decide the case metal by itself.

Inside the front lid of a hunter, on the bezel and on the bow and pendant (the ring and stem at 12 o'clock): Swiss and French bows often carry a tiny head or animal mark. The 1914 Swiss decree placed marks on the middle part of the case, the case back and beze

watch-dealer-lots.title: Watch dealer lots and showcase watches
watch-dealer-lots.full: Watch dealer lots and showcase watches (Bulova, Elgin, Hamilton, Waltham, Timex, Benrus, Gruen, Westclox, Seiko, Swiss "pin-lever" brands)
watch-dealer-lots.fakes: Fake Rolex/Omega/Cartier common in lots; Franken-watches (case of one, movement of another, redial). Any luxury brand in a lot needs authentication: outside Dylan's rules — do not buy for the luxury piece. Bulova Accutro
watch-dealer-lots.buy: Pass on individually priced showcase watches; buy only mixed lots of 10+ mechanical watches at ≤ $4 each or any lot with solid 10K/14K cases (stamped "10K"/"14K", not "10K GF/RGP") under melt.
tells: Desirable makers/models: Hamilton (Ventura asymmetrical, Electric 500, early rectangular "Piping Rock", military), Bulova Accutron (tuning fork, open dial "Spaceview"), Omega, Longines, Universal Geneve, Gruen Curvex, Benrus military (DTU-2A/P), Elgin/Waltham

Low tier: Timex (Marlin, Viscount, mechanical 1950s–80s), Westclox, Ingersoll, Swiss pin-lever brands (Chalet, Caravelle by Bulova, Waltham post-1957 Swiss, Sheffield), Japanese/Hong Kong "17 jewels" novelties.

Solid gold cases: rich even yellow colour with no brassing at lugs/edges; 14K/18K stamps inside the caseback (needs a photo). Gold-filled (GF, RGP, "10K gold filled", "rolled gold plate") shows brass at edges when worn — worth $1–5 scrap only.

watt-pottery.title: Watt Pottery
watt-pottery.full: Watt Pottery (Watt Pottery Co., Crooksville, Ohio, 1922–1965: Apple, Starflower, Rooster, Cherry, Tulip, Dutch Tulip, Autumn Foliage, Morning Glory, advertising pieces)
watt-pottery.money: rare forms — Apple canister sets $1,500–2,500+, Apple grease jar ~$500–700, cookie/goodies jars, ice buckets, Apple divided dinner plates, small-town advertising pieces $100–150 — are the multiples.
watt-pottery.fakes: - **Four Rivers Stoneware, Hazel, Kentucky (mid-1994)** made Watt-look pieces; **spring 1995** a line of reproductions was sold at auctions and shows, cast from moulds taken off originals and carrying the impressed Watt
watt-pottery.buy: Buy only the scarce patterns (Tulip, Dutch Tulip, Rooster, Morning Glory, Cherry, Eagle) or scarce forms (canisters, grease jar, cookie jar, ice bucket, #17 ice-lip, shakers, advertising) at ≤ 35% of estimated sold; pass on all Apple/Starflower bowls and #15/#
tells: Yellowware/cream-bodied kitchen stoneware (not white ironstone): mixing bowls, pitchers, casseroles, bean pots, cookie jars, pie plates, spaghetti bowls, platters, shakers, canisters. Hand-painted with 3–5 quick brush strokes in deep red, green (two greens on
Title words sellers use: "Watt", "Watt Ware", "Oven Ware USA", "yellowware apple pitcher", "farmhouse", "Crooksville".

Mark: impressed in the base, usually in concentric rings: "WATT / OVEN WARE / U.S.A." with a shape number, or just the shape number plus "U.S.A." (as on our #16 pitcher and #31 platter photos — number in the inner ring, U.S.A. in the outer). Early (pre-1949) o

wedding-cake-toppers.title: Wedding cake toppers
wedding-cake-toppers.full: Wedding cake toppers (chalkware, bisque, celluloid and plastic bride-and-groom figures; Wilton, Coast Novelty, Japanese and German bisque makers)
wedding-cake-toppers.money: rare figural pieces (military groom, ethnic couples, German bisque with original box) $100–250 (general knowledge, verify).
wedding-cake-toppers.fakes: Little faking. Retro-style reproductions of Art Deco couples (resin) are sold as wedding decor today. Resin is heavier and glossier than composition and has no crazing. Bisque reproductions exist from the 1980s–2000s.
wedding-cake-toppers.buy: Buy only pre-1945 bisque or composition couples with original veil/flowers or a military groom, at ≤ $20; pass on 1950s chalkware and all plastic toppers.
tells: 1900s–1920s: German or Japanese bisque couples (matte, unglazed porcelain with fine painted faces). Groom often in a tailcoat. Bases are plaster or wire with wax flowers. Brides have long cloth veils.
1920s–30s Art Deco: slim, elongated composition or chalkware figures with bob-cut brides, standing under a wire-and-tulle arch or a satin bell. These are the most collected.
1940s war era: groom in Army, Navy or Marine uniform. Military grooms carry a premium.

wedgwood-jasperware.title: Wedgwood Jasperware
wedgwood-jasperware.full: Wedgwood Jasperware (Josiah Wedgwood & Sons, Etruria/Barlaston, England 1775–present; plus Adams, Dudson and German/Japanese imitators)
wedgwood-jasperware.money: 19th-century dip jasper, rare colours, tricolour and Portland vase copies $150–5,000+ (a tricolour Britannia vase made £4,100 at auction in Nov 2021).
wedgwood-jasperware.fakes: Fake "Wedgwood" marks are rare; many imitators are unmarked. Wedgwood itself has copied the Portland vase across eras, so the mark era decides value. Watch for "Wedgewood" (with an extra e) marks on non-Wedgwood wares, a
wedgwood-jasperware.buy: Pass on pale blue trinket dishes and plates; buy black basalt/dark blue/lilac/tricolour or 19th-c. pieces with impressed "WEDGWOOD" (no "England") under ~$40.
tells: History: Josiah Wedgwood made his first jasper bas-reliefs in November 1774. The Portland Vase copy was completed in 1790 after four years of trials.
Title words: "Wedgwood jasperware", "jasper dip", "Portland blue", "lilac", "sage", "crimson", "tricolour", "Dancing Hours", "Wedgewood" (misspelled).
Production waned after 1811 and had virtually ceased by 1829. It resumed in 1844 as a jasper dip on a new body, and solid jasper was made again from 1860.

weltron-radios.title: Weltron space-ball radios / 8-tracks
weltron-radios.fakes: No known Weltron reproductions; modern "retro sphere" Bluetooth speakers are not Weltrons (general knowledge, verify).
weltron-radios.buy: Buy working coloured units under $150 (white only far under $90 — see note); pass white at $150+.

west-point-cadet-uniforms.title: West Point cadet uniforms
west-point-cadet-uniforms.full: West Point cadet uniforms (full-dress coats, 1900s–1950s) (Cadet Store, USMA)
west-point-cadet-uniforms.fakes: Costume and theatrical reproductions exist; they lack the Cadet Store label and use lighter wool and stamped buttons. Labels can be transferred, so check that wear on the label matches the coat (general knowledge, verify
west-point-cadet-uniforms.buy: Buy a complete tailcoat (all buttons, braid intact, label legible) under $75; pass missing buttons, moth damage, or $150+ asks.

western-hats.title: Vintage western / cowboy hats
western-hats.full: Vintage western / cowboy hats (John B. Stetson Co., Resistol, Bailey, American Hat Co., Charlie 1 Horse, Champion, custom hatters such as Rand's, Greeley and Baron)
western-hats.money: 20X–100X beaver, pre-war wide-brim/tall-crown Stetsons and custom-hatter beaver $250–1,000+ (estimates).
western-hats.fakes: Fake Stetson labels sewn into cheap wool hats; "Stetson" licensed wool hats sold as fur; modern hats with "vintage" liners. Check the sweatband stamping and felt quality. Not a heavy-fake market.
western-hats.buy: Buy fur-felt westerns showing pre-1970 tells (Philadelphia/union label, no printed scenic liner, Resistol Self-Conforming 5X+) or 10X+ beaver in sizes 7–7⅝ at ≤ $40; pass straw, wool, 1980s+ 4X with scenic liners above ~$30, and stained or moth-eaten hats.
tells: X ratings: a fur-content/quality grade per maker; on old Stetsons 3X–5X were mid-grade and "100X", "Clear Beaver", "Royal Deluxe" were top. Modern X numbers aren't comparable across eras or makers.
Fur-felt (beaver, rabbit/hare or blends) or wool-felt hat with a tall creased crown and a wide brim; also palm and shantung straw.
Inside the hat tells you almost everything: the leather sweatband (stamped maker, size, X rating), the satin liner (logo, scenes, union label), and size tags.

whiskey-decanters.title: Whiskey decanters
whiskey-decanters.full: Whiskey decanters (Jim Beam / Regal China, Ezra Brooks, Ski Country, Wild Turkey, Old Fitzgerald, Lionstone, McCormick, Bell's / Wade)
whiskey-decanters.fakes: Not faked: values are too low. Confusion pieces exist (a 1971 Masonic decanter is often mistaken for Beam, ~$30). Club "convention" pieces were made in small runs; check numbering and documentation.
whiskey-decanters.buy: Pass on empty mass-production figurals at any price over ~$5 each; only a documented rare club/convention piece or a Ski Country/Jim Beam car under $15 is worth a look.
tells: Jim Beam: shaped like animals, cars, trains, states, political donkeys/elephants, sports, clubs. Paper label near the base reading "Beam ... Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey", proof, and often "Regal China" on the base or label. 1950s–60s glass "Beam's Choice
Ezra Brooks: heavier, glossier figurals (Shriners, sports, Indian chiefs) with an "Ezra Brooks" label; generally lower value than Beam.
Ski Country (Colorado, 1973–90s): the best-made: finely modelled birds, owls, eagles, Indian figures, with crisp painting. Base reads "Ski Country Limited Edition".

wicker-fishing-creels.title: Wicker fishing creels & tackle baskets
wicker-fishing-creels.full: Wicker fishing creels & tackle baskets (George Lawrence, McMonies, Turtle, Peters, ARCA/Eurosporta, Brady)
wicker-fishing-creels.fakes: Decor reproductions are common (see junk tier); faked maker stamps on leather are possible on high-value Lawrence creels — compare stamp style to known examples (general knowledge, verify).
wicker-fishing-creels.buy: Buy leather-bound American creels with any maker stamp ≤ $80; pass Hong Kong/Japan creels and European seat-baskets over $30.

wildlife-art-prints.title: Wildlife / rural art prints
wildlife-art-prints.full: Wildlife / rural art prints (Terry Redlin, Bev Doolittle, Thomas Kinkade, Frank Massa etc.)
wildlife-art-prints.fakes: Open-edition reprints and posters of the same images are everywhere; licensed products (plates, calendars, puzzles) carry the images too. Only the pencil signature + number distinguishes the edition print.
wildlife-art-prints.buy: Buy pencil-signed & numbered (confirmed in photo) ≤ $40, local or driveable; pass open editions and sellers quoting eBay asks.

wire-baskets.title: Wire baskets
wire-baskets.full: Wire baskets (French wire, egg baskets, aluminum woven bread baskets, Kalo / Arts & Crafts silver, farmhouse decor)
wire-baskets.money: antique French wire and hand-made ornate wire $60-200 (general knowledge, verify)
wire-baskets.fakes: Huge decor-market reproduction of "French farmhouse" egg baskets and painted chicken baskets (2000s-present). Fresh, even rust is a sign of a repro. - Repro tells: spot welds, identical wire gauge everywhere, uniform fak
wire-baskets.buy: Pass on modern/aluminum; only antique hand-twisted French or primitive pieces under $20.
tells: French pedestal / compote egg basket (c. 1890–1910): a bowl of concentric wire rings on a wheel-form or splayed foot, twisted-wire rim; typical ~9" diameter × 6" high (1stdibs example). Often slightly off-round from age.
French tiered egg stands: two or three stacked wire tiers on a central stem or legs, usually painted black or left dark iron.
Heavy-gauge steel gathering/potato baskets: thick wire, bail handle, flat or rounded bottom; French, German and American.

wood-cased-telephones.title: Wood-cased telephones
wood-cased-telephones.full: Wood-cased telephones (Western Electric/Bell, Kellogg, Stromberg-Carlson, Northern Electric, American Electric, Leich, Chicago Telephone Supply; 1890s–1930s oak wall sets, wood desk/cabinet sets, 1930s art-deco wood handset sets)
wood-cased-telephones.money: cathedral-top, walnut, long-box 3-box, and small-maker 1880s–90s sets $400–2,000+
wood-cased-telephones.fakes: - 1970s–2000s **reproduction oak wall phones** (Crosley CR91, "Country Kitchen" style, Taiwan/China): pine or thin oak with orange stain, a working push-button keypad inside the transmitter or on the front, a fake crank,
wood-cased-telephones.buy: Buy a complete, original oak magneto wall set or 1930s deco desk set at ≤ $75 only if the maker tag, crank/magneto (or dial), receiver, transmitter and ringer are all present and the wood is uncracked; pass on repros, incomplete "restoration projects", anythin
tells: Oak magneto wall telephone (1895–1930): vertical quarter-sawn oak box 18–24" tall with a sloped writing shelf, a crank on the right side (magneto), two nickel bells on top or a bell under the shelf, a black transmitter on an adjustable arm in the middle of the

Three-box ("long box") wall sets (1880s–1900): three stacked boxes — bells top, transmitter middle, battery bottom — the oldest and most valuable; cathedral-top (arched or pointed top boxes) and picture-frame front sets are also early.
Wood "vanity"/cabinet desk phones (1890s–1910s): telephone circuitry on a flat oak desktop, magneto and bells behind a glass door; hotel lobbies and offices; rare.

wooden-crates.title: Wooden crates and boxes
wooden-crates.full: Wooden crates and boxes (ammunition: Winchester, Remington UMC, Peters, Western, US military; explosives: Hercules, Atlas, DuPont; liquor: Drambuie, Johnnie Walker, Old Grand-Dad; soda: Coca-Cola, Pepsi, Nehi, Dr Pepper; dairy, fruit, cheese, egg and poultry crates)
wooden-crates.money: rare early two-piece ammo/powder boxes with paper labels and military WWI/early crates $150–600.
wooden-crates.fakes: Large volume of reproduction Winchester, Remington, Coca-Cola and dynamite boxes since the 1980s – often pine with laser-crisp stencils, brad nails and no wear inside. Craft-store "vintage-style" crates (Hobby Lobby, Tar
wooden-crates.buy: Buy only small branded ammo/powder/explosives boxes with dovetailed or finger-jointed corners, intact stencils and sliding lids at ≤ $30; pass liquor, soda, poultry and plain crates.
tells: Stencilled ink lettering (Winchester "Small Arms Ammunition – Loaded Shot Shells – Made in U.S.A.", example 7967804574) vs paper labels (fruit crates, early ammo) vs branded/burned lettering.
Construction: finger (box) joints or dovetails = better quality (ammo/powder 1890s–1950s); butt joints with cut nails = 1880s–1920s; wire nails and staples = 1920s+; plywood = post-1940s.
Sliding lid in a groove = ammo/powder/cheese/cigar; nailed lid = shipping.

wooden-cutting-boards.title: Vintage wooden cutting boards and breadboards
wooden-cutting-boards.full: Vintage wooden cutting boards and breadboards (Dansk/Jens Quistgaard, Digsmed, Goodwood, Catskill Craftsmen, Snow River, John Boos, unbranded primitive and animal-shaped boards)
wooden-cutting-boards.money: 19th-c. carved bread boards, large primitive dough bowls and folk-art pig boards with old surface $80–300.
wooden-cutting-boards.fakes: - Distressed "farmhouse" boards made new (Hobby Lobby/Etsy) mimic primitives; check tool marks and wear location. - Dansk reissued some Quistgaard designs in the 2000s–2010s (general knowledge, verify); reissues carry mo
wooden-cutting-boards.buy: Buy only antique primitives with real wear/patina or signed Danish teak (Dansk/Digsmed) under ~$25; anything modern or homemade is pass.
tells: Hardwood (maple, walnut, teak, oak, sycamore) boards. Collectible types:
Animal-shaped boards (pigs, fish, chickens, mice — 1950s–70s); Digsmed made a "mouse" charcuterie board with button eyes.

Mid-century Danish teak boards with stamps (Dansk Designs by Jens Quistgaard, Digsmed, Kalmar). Often staved (strips of teak glued edge to edge, visible as parallel stripes), sometimes with a slanted/canted edge, juice groove, or a carved well.

wooden-desk-organizers.title: Wooden desk organizers , Thomas Webb-era mahogany desk sets)
wooden-desk-organizers.full: Wooden desk organizers (letter boxes, roll-top/tambour desk caddies, cubby organizers, stationery boxes; Shaker-style, Victorian walnut, 1970s–80s oak tambour "The Byte Box"/Rolodex/Eldon; Danish teak (Dansk, Digsmed), Thomas Webb-era mahogany desk sets)
wooden-desk-organizers.money: Arts & Crafts/Shaker signed or tiger-oak pieces $100–400.
wooden-desk-organizers.fakes: Bombay Company and Pier 1 "antique-style" stationery boxes look Victorian but are 1990s Asian-made (MDF or rubberwood).
wooden-desk-organizers.buy: Buy only Victorian/Edwardian stationery cabinets, Danish teak and signed Arts & Crafts pieces at ≤ 30% of median; pass on 1980s oak-veneer tambour and pine mail organizers (Terapeak median $23.57).
tells: 1980s tambour organizers: oak-veneer particleboard ends with a roll-top tambour of wood slats glued on fabric; built for floppy disks, CDs or cassettes (e.g. "The Byte Box" 2101 dual rolltop CD/disk holder). Low value.
Pine/maple mail organizers and cubbies (1980s–2000s): clear-lacquered knotty pine, small knob drawers, cork boards. Low value.
Victorian/Edwardian stationery boxes: walnut, oak or mahogany with slanted fronts, pigeonholes for envelopes, brass hinges and plaques.

wooden-hand-planes.title: Wooden hand planes & moulding planes
wooden-hand-planes.full: Wooden (woodie) hand planes & moulding planes (Ohio Tool, Sandusky, Auburn, Greenfield, Union Factory/Chapin, Scioto, Marples/Mathieson, Nicholson, Chelor)
wooden-hand-planes.fakes: Modern decor reproductions and "fake-aged" planes exist; faked 18th-c. maker stamps are a risk at the top end — stamp style should match reference books (Pollak's "A Guide to the Makers of American Wooden Planes") (gener
wooden-hand-planes.buy: Buy screw-arm plow planes ≤ $60, H&R sets ≤ $100, named 18th-c. makers ≤ $200; pass unmarked bench-plane lots over $20/plane.

wooden-shoe-trees.title: Wooden shoe trees, stretchers and shoe lasts
wooden-shoe-trees.full: Wooden shoe trees, stretchers and shoe lasts (Rochester, Woodlore, Florsheim, Allen Edmonds, Alden, Johnston & Murphy, Church's, John Lobb; cobbler's lasts)
wooden-shoe-trees.money: bespoke lasted trees (John Lobb, Lobb Paris, Edward Green with brass plates) $100–400.
wooden-shoe-trees.fakes: Not faked meaningfully. Beware "antique" decorative lasts made in India for décor shops (2000s–present), with cast handles and aged finish.
wooden-shoe-trees.buy: Buy only bespoke or named-maker lasted trees with brass plates or stamped makers, or Victorian tall boot trees, at ≤ $15 a pair; lots of generic trees fail on shipping weight.
tells: Split-toe spring trees (1930s–present): toe block split down the middle, a coiled spring or metal tube to a heel knob. Cedar (reddish, aromatic) or beech/maple (pale).

Lasted / one-piece trees (1900s–60s, and bespoke makers today): a solid carved forefoot with a hinged or separate heel block and turned knob, shaped like the shoe's last; often stamped with a size ("7½") and sometimes a maker.
Stretchers: a forefoot form with a screw handle that widens it (metal T-handle, like the single one in our sweep).

wooden-train-sets.title: Wooden train sets
wooden-train-sets.full: Wooden train sets (Thomas Wooden Railway/Learning Curve, BRIO, KidKraft, Melissa & Doug, IKEA Lillabo, Imaginarium)
wooden-train-sets.fakes: - Chinese knock-offs ("Thomas" wooden fakes), re-releases of popular engines. - Fisher-Price-era re-releases of Learning Curve characters look similar; check stamps.
wooden-train-sets.buy: buy only big lots (100+ pcs) at ≤ $40 or lots with visible retired Learning Curve (pre-2012, flat-magnet, painted face) rarities; small lots are a pass.
tells: Wooden track-compatible trains (peg-and-hole "jigsaw" track, ~1.5 in. wide, grooved both sides).

Thomas Wooden Railway (TWR): Learning Curve (Chicago, founded 1992 by John W. Lee; Thomas line developed by Roy Wilson; made Thomas toys 1993–2012) — wooden bodies with magnets, painted faces. RC2 (2002/03 onward) owned Learning Curve; Mattel/Fisher-Price took
Copyright stamps on the underside help date Thomas pieces: "©Britt Allcroft" (earliest), "©Gullane", "©HIT", then Mattel/Fisher-Price (general knowledge, verify).

woodworking-clamps.title: Woodworking clamps
woodworking-clamps.full: Woodworking clamps (Jorgensen / Adjustable Clamp Co., Pony, Bessey, Stanley, Record, Brink & Cotton, Hargrave, Wetzler, Cincinnati Tool, Columbian)
woodworking-clamps.money: Record/Stanley/Bessey cast quick-release bar clamps and sets of matched parallel clamps $80–300 per set.
woodworking-clamps.fakes: None meaningful. Decorative "antique" hand screws are sometimes new import décor; new wood is pale and sharp-edged with machine threads.
woodworking-clamps.buy: Buy only matched sets of Bessey K-body/Jorgensen Cabinet Master parallel clamps or short (≤ 36") lots at ≤ 25% of resale; pass on pipe clamps, long bar clamps, single hand screws over $15 and rusty mixed lots.
tells: Bar clamps / F-clamps: steel bar with a sliding jaw (Jorgensen, Pony, Bessey "GZ", Stanley, Record).
Parallel jaw clamps: Bessey K-Body (red/black), Jorgensen Cabinet Master (orange), Jet. Sold new $50–80 each; used sets are the best value in this category.
Pipe clamps: cast fixtures (Pony/Jorgensen "No. 50", orange or red) that slide on 1/2" or 3/4" black/galvanised pipe. Value is in the fixtures, not the pipe.

world-banknotes.title: World banknotes
world-banknotes.full: World banknotes (foreign paper money: Austria-Hungary, Germany inflation, Brazil, Mexico, China, Japan invasion money, military payment certificates)
world-banknotes.money: scarce PMG-graded notes, early colonial, pre-1949 Chinese in top grade $100–5,000+.
world-banknotes.fakes: - Chinese counterfeit pre-1949 notes, Confederate-style copy notes, fake overprints and stamps on Austro-Hungarian notes, "souvenir" replica sets (Zimbabwe trillion copies, "COPY" printed), and modern Chinese fantasy not
world-banknotes.buy: Buy only crisp uncirculated or rare-issue notes identified by Pick number with sold ≥ $100 at ≤ 25% of sold; pass on circulated foreign currency and inflation notes, which are almost worthless.
tells: Grade from the photo: folds, creases, soft corners, tears, stains, pinholes, tape → circulated (VG–VF). Crisp, flat, sharp corners, bright paper → UNC.
Overprints, signatures and serial prefixes change Pick numbers and value.

yamaha-acoustic-guitars.title: Yamaha acoustic guitars
yamaha-acoustic-guitars.full: Yamaha acoustic guitars (FG / A-series / L-series / APX / classical)
yamaha-acoustic-guitars.fakes: Counterfeits are rare at this price; mislabelled models (a later FG sold as "red label") are the risk — confirm the label colour and text (general knowledge, verify). - A Taiwan red label (without "Nippon Gakki") sold as
yamaha-acoustic-guitars.buy: Buy A-series with case under $120, A3/A5 or L-series under $200, red-label FG under $120; pass current-retail F/FG models and cracked/"needs work".
tells: Where the identifiers are: the soundhole label carries the model and often the serial. Serial numbers may also be stamped on the neck block (visible through the soundhole) or on the back of the headstock. Taiwan-made guitars sometimes say "Made in Taiwan" on t

A-series model code (Bananas): A = A-series; C = concert body (no C means dreadnought, e.g. AC3M vs A3M); 1/3/5 = tier; M = mahogany back and sides; R = rosewood. The A4K/AC4K was a limited edition in all-solid Hawaiian koa.

Red-label FG: a red label reading "Nippon Gakki" in the soundhole, a plain dreadnought with no cutaway, and a simple headstock with the tuning-fork logo. Models seen include FG-75, FG-110, FG-140, FG-150, FG-180, FG-230 (12-string) and FG-300 (TDPRI; Reverb).

zildjian-cymbals.title: Cymbals
zildjian-cymbals.money: Istanbul K, Paiste Giant Beat/602 vintage, large trans-stamp A's $400–2,500.
zildjian-cymbals.fakes: Counterfeit Zildjian/Sabian/Paiste cymbals (often sold cheaply online from overseas) exist; tells are wrong logo fonts, missing trademark stamp and very light weight. Logos can also be re-inked or a budget cymbal relabel
zildjian-cymbals.buy: Buy uncracked pro-series (cast B20) at ≤ 40–50% of sold (20" A ride under $50, K/K Custom/2002 ≤ $80, vintage trans-stamp A/Istanbul K/602 ≤ $100–120); pass B8/sheet lines, any crack/keyhole/repair, sellers already at market.
